Title: Presentation of the Annual Report 2014 to the National Assembly, June 3, 2015
text: PRESENTATION OF THE 2014 ANNUAL REPORT TO THE NATIONAL ASSEMBLY, PRESIDENT OF THE BCN OVIDIO REYES RAMiREZ R" JUNE 3, 2015 PRESENTATION OF THE 2014 ANNUAL REPORT TO THE NATIONAL ASSEMBLY, PRESIDENT OF THE BCN OVIDIO REYES RAMiREZ R" JUNE 3, 2015 03/06/2015 Good morning, Honorable Deputy Iris Montenegro, President of the National Assembly by Law, Honorable Members of the Board of Directors, Honorable Deputies before this National Assembly, Representatives of the Media, invited all. I am pleased to write to you to present the Annual Report of the Central Bank of Nicaragua for the year 2014. During 2014, the Nicaraguan economy continued to perform positively, characterized by economic and employment growth, price stability, consolidation of public finances and a sustainable level of public debt. All of the above took place in a favourable international context, particularly due to the dynamism in most of the main trading partners, although with a mixed result in the recovery of export prices. The world economy was distinguished by stable economic growth but with marked divergence among the main countries, highlighting the acceleration of the United States, the fragile recovery of the Eurozone, and the slowdown of emerging economies. Overall, according to the International Monetary Fund, the global growth rate in 2014 remained constant from 2013 and stood at 3.3 percent. On the other hand, the behavior of world prices was distinguished by the reduction in commodity prices, highlighting the decrease in gold and oil prices. The evolution of these external prices affected the results of the country's balance of payments, as we will see later. GDP growth in 2014 is estimated at 4.7 percent, driven by stronger demand and aggregate supply. Regarding the former, both domestic and external demand contributed positively to economic activity, mainly due to the boost in household consumption. On the supply side, most economic activities showed increases in their value added, mainly trade and services, due to higher transactions and imports of durable and non-durable consumer goods, and manufacturing due to increases in the production of meat and fish and other foods, as well as machinery and transport equipment. The Nicaraguan economy has registered sustained growth with an average rate of 4.8 percent during the years 2010-2014, higher than the average growth of 3.9 percent for Central America and the Dominican Republic and the growth of 3.5 percent for Latin America and the Caribbean. In particular, GDP measured on the supply side, recorded a higher contribution of services and trade with 3.0 percentage points, followed by manufacturing, which contributed 0.6 percentage points, and agriculture and fishing activities with 0.6 percentage points. Consistent with the above, employment showed a positive evolution. Affiliation to the INSS behaved in line with Nicaraguan economic activity, registering a growth of 5.4 percent year-on-year. According to data from the INI DE continuous household survey, the unemployment rate opened in the third quarter reached 6.8 percent. (Open unemployed population / Economically active population). Nominal wages, on the other hand, grew driven by adjustments to both the minimum wage approved by the Ministry of Labor and the average wage of Central Government workers. In particular, the average nominal salary of INSS members registered a growth of 7.8 percent. On the side of real wages for workers, the Central Government and members of the INSS, these grew 2.6 and 1.7 percent, respectively, with the increase in the purchasing power of INSS members being the largest in the last 4 years. In the area of purchasing power, the price dynamics of 2014, although higher than that of the previous year, remained below the average of the last four years, which shows a trend of stability. Thus, the accumulated inflation to December 2014 closed at 6.48 percent (5.67% to December 2013), a result that was influenced by the irregular behavior of the rainy season, which caused the reduction in the domestic supply of basic grains and certain perishable and related goods and services. This was offset by the fall in international prices of oil and its derivatives during the last quarter of the year, in addition to the permanence of the policies of subsidies and price stabilization in basic grains promoted by the Government. In terms of divisions of the consumer price index, food and non-alcoholic beverages contributed the most to inflation, while transport accounted for the most negative contribution. In particular, the food and non-alcoholic beverages division showed an accumulated inflation of 11.74 percent (5.98% in 2013), representing a contribution of 4.20 percentage points to national inflation. The most significant case in this division was the increase in the price of red beans with a contribution of 0.87 percentage points to inflation. In 2014, the performance of the National Financial System was robust, exhibiting an accelerated deposit growth rate and a stable expansion of credit, which led to a convergence in both rates. Thus, the dynamism in deposit deposits was 19.0 percent, while the gross portfolio showed a growth of 19.4 percent. By institutional sector, the household portfolio was the most dynamic, while by type of debtor the highest growth corresponded to livestock credit, and commercial credit was the one with the highest participation. Additionally, indicators of profitability, liquidity and risk of the national financial system continued to reflect the health of the system. The Non-Financial Public Sector ended 2014 with a deficit after donations of 1.5 percent of GDP. This deficit mainly reflected higher capital spending, mostly from the rest of the non-financial public sector. However, the Central Government showed a better performance than planned, with a deficit after donations of 0.3 percent, while its projection in the Economic and Financial Program was 0.5% of GDP. This improved performance was in line with a positive evolution in tax collection and a prudent spending policy. As for the total public debt, it reached the figure of 5,800 million dollars, equivalent to 49.1 percent of GDP in 2014, reflecting a reduction of 4.2 percentage points compared to 2013. This evolution of debt reflects a policy of responsible external and domestic public debt. The export sector showed a recovery by growing 9.6 percent in 2014 (-10.1% in 2013), which was driven by the increase in demand from most of our main trading partners, combined with the productive expansion particularly of the manufacturing (meat, sugar and dairy) and agricultural (coffee, peanuts and beans) sectors. Mining and fishing were affected by falls in international prices of both gold and shrimp, which reduced the export value of these items. Free zone exports, meanwhile, grew 7.2 percent, as a result of higher exports of textiles and fishery products and footwear. Merchandise imports showed a growth of 3.9 percent (-3.4% in 2013), mainly determined by higher imports of capital goods, especially industry, and consumer goods, which was consistent with the dynamics of the country's economic activity. However, there was a lower oil bill by 4.1 percent, as a result of the fall in international oil prices. In this way, the exchange with the rest of the world was positively influenced by the recovery of the US economy and its impact on related economies, the reduction in international oil prices and the dynamism of the national productive sectors, which was partially offset by the fall in the price of gold. The final result was a reduction in the current account deficit of the Balance of Payments as a percentage of GDP of 4 percentage points compared to 2013, reaching an amount of 838.1 million dollars, equivalent to 7.1 percent of GDP. The conduct of monetary policy in coordination with fiscal policy allowed reaching a record balance of gross international reserves (RIB) of 2,276.2 million dollars (14.2% higher than 2013). This result was mainly determined by a greater absorption of internal resources and inflow of external resources. Thus, a coverage of IMF on a monetary basis of 2.6 times and 4.7 months of imports were achieved, levels that reinforce the credibility of the exchange rate regime. In this context of the end of 2014, the economic outlook for 2015 also remains positive. For this year, the expected growth range between 4.5-5 percent is maintained, which will be supported by a better international context in terms of growth of our main trading partners and commodity prices. However, risks such as changes in oil prices and upward pressures on international interest rates would remain. Internally, we also remain vulnerable to climate change events. Thus, it is expected that the macroeconomic and sectoral policies that are being implemented will promote an inflation rate in a range between 6.0 and 7.0 percent, maintain financial stability, and continue with the path of strengthening the country's fiscal and external sustainability. Finally, I would like to reflect on the macroeconomic results of 2014 and the future prospects. Although the national economy has been evolving positively, we cannot ignore the fact that our GDP per capita is still very low, reaching 1,905 dollars per inhabitant, in comparison, the average GDP per capita of Central America is 5,260 dollars per inhabitant. While progress and good dynamics are recorded in the macroeconomic field, significant challenges remain. The labor market has a high percentage of informal employment, while 42% of our population continues to live in poverty. These people will find it difficult to understand macroeconomic outcomes because they do not yet translate into a significant improvement in their standard of living. Most importantly, however, the macroeconomic stability that we have achieved in a model of dialogue, alliances and broad consensus between the Government and the main productive forces creates opportunities to continue increasing the pace of production and attract investments that generate new jobs and gradually enable us to escape poverty. This is what all Nicaraguans must continue to bet on to achieve ever higher levels of well-being and prosperity. Thanks a lot.

Me complace dirigirme a ustedes para presentarles el Informe Anual del Banco Central de Nicaragua correspondiente al a<96>o 2014. Durante 2014, la econom<92>a nicarag<9f>ense continu<97> desempe<96><87>ndose de forma positiva, caracterizada por crecimiento econ<97>mico y del empleo, estabilidad de precios, consolidaci<97>n de las finanzas p<9c>blicas y un nivel de deuda p<9c>blica sostenible. Todo lo anterior se desenvolvi<97> en un contexto internacional favorable, particularmente por el dinamismo en la mayor<92>a de los principales socios comerciales, aunque con un resultado mixto en la recuperaci<97>n de los precios de los productos de exportaci<97>n. La econom<92>a mundial se distingui<97> por un crecimiento econ<97>mico estable pero con marcada divergencia entre los principales pa<92>ses, sobresaliendo la aceleraci<97>n de Estados Unidos, la fr<87>gil recuperaci<97>n de la Zona Euro, y la desaceleraci<97>n de las econom<92>as emergentes. En general, seg<9c>n el Fondo Monetario Internacional, la tasa de crecimiento mundial en 2014 se mantuvo constante con respecto a 2013 y se ubic<97> en 3.3 por ciento. Por su parte, el comportamiento de los precios mundiales se distingui<97> por la reducci<97>n de los precios de materias primas, resaltando la disminuci<97>n de los precios del oro y del petr<97>leo. La evoluci<97>n de estos precios externos incidi<97> en los resultados de la balanza de pagos del pa<92>s, como veremos m<87>s adelante. Se estima que el crecimiento del PIB en 2014 fue de 4.7 por ciento, impulsado por un mayor dinamismo de la demanda y de la oferta agregada. Respecto a la primera, tanto la demanda interna como la externa contribuyeron positivamente a la actividad econ<97>mica, principalmente por el impulso del consumo de los hogares. Por el lado de la oferta, la mayor<92>a de las actividades econ<97>micas mostraron incrementos en su valor agregado, principalmente comercio y servicios, debido a mayores transacciones e importaciones de bienes de consumo duradero y no duradero, y manufactura por aumentos en la producci<97>n de carnes y pescados y otros alimentos, as<92> como maquinaria y equipos de transporte. La econom<92>a nicarag<9f>ense ha registrado un crecimiento sostenido con una tasa promedio de 4.8 por ciento durante los a<96>os 2010-2014, superior al crecimiento promedio de 3.9% para Centroam<8e>rica y Rep<9c>blica Dominicana y al crecimiento de 3.5% para Latinoam<8e>rica y el Caribe. En particular, el PIB medido por el lado de la oferta, registr<97> un mayor aporte de servicios y comercio con 3.0 puntos porcentuales, seguido de manufactura que contribuy<97> con 0.6 puntos porcentuales, y las actividades agricultura y pesca con 0.6 puntos porcentuales. Consistente con lo anterior, el empleo mostr<97> una evoluci<97>n positiva. La afiliaci<97>n al INSS se comport<97> en l<92>nea con la actividad econ<97>mica nicarag<9f>ense, registrando un crecimiento de 5.4 por ciento interanual. Seg<9c>n datos de la encuesta continua de hogares del INI DE, la tasa de desempleo abierto al tercer trimestre se alcanz<97> 6.8 por ciento. (Poblaci<97>n desocupada abierta / Poblaci<97>n econ<97>micamente activa). Por su parte, los salarios nominales crecieron impulsados por los ajustes tanto del salario m<92>nimo aprobado por el Ministerio del Trabajo, como del salario promedio de los trabajadores del Gobierno Central. En particular, el salario promedio nominal de los afiliados al INSS registr<97> un crecimiento de 7.8 por ciento. Por el lado de los salarios reales para los trabajadores el Gobierno Central y afiliados al INSS, <8e>stos crecieron 2.6 y 1.7 por ciento, respectivamente, siendo el incremento del poder adquisitivo de afiliados al INSS el mayor en los <9c>ltimos 4 a<96>os. En el <87>mbito del poder adquisitivo, la din<87>mica de precios de 2014, aunque mayor que la del a<96>o anterior, se mantuvo por debajo del promedio de los <9c>ltimos cuatro a<96>os, lo que muestra una tendencia de estabilidad. As<92>, la inflaci<97>n acumulada a diciembre 2014 cerr<97> en 6.48 por ciento (5.67% a diciembre 2013), resultado que se vio influenciado por el comportamiento irregular de la temporada de lluvia, lo que provoc<97> la reducci<97>n en la oferta dom<8e>stica de granos b<87>sicos y ciertos perecederos y bienes y servicios relacionados. Esto fue contrarrestado por la ca<92>da en los precios internacionales del petr<97>leo y sus derivados durante el <9c>ltimo trimestre del a<96>o, adem<87>s de la permanencia de las pol<92>ticas de subsidios y de estabilizaci<97>n de precios en los granos b<87>sicos impulsadas por el Gobierno. En t<8e>rmino de divisiones del <92>ndice de precios al consumidor, la que m<87>s aport<97> a la inflaci<97>n fue la de alimentos y bebidas no alcoh<97>licas, mientras que la de transporte reflej<97> la contribuci<97>n m<87>s negativa. En particular, la divisi<97>n alimentos y bebidas no alcoh<97>licas mostr<97> una inflaci<97>n acumulada de 11.74 por ciento (5.98% en 2013), representando un aporte de 4.20 puntos porcentuales a la inflaci<97>n nacional. El caso m<87>s significativo en esta divisi<97>n fue el aumento del precio del frijol rojo con una contribuci<97>n de 0.87 puntos porcentuales a la inflaci<97>n. En 2014 el desempe<96>o del Sistema Financiero Nacional fue robusto, exhibiendo una tasa de crecimiento de los dep<97>sitos acelerada y una expansi<97>n estable del cr<8e>dito, lo cual dio lugar a una convergencia en ambas tasas. As<92>, el dinamismo en las captaciones de dep<97>sitos fue de 19.0 por ciento, mientras que la cartera bruta mostr<97> un crecimiento de 19.4 por ciento. Por sectores institucionales, la cartera de los hogares fue la m<87>s din<87>mica, mientras que por tipo de deudor el mayor crecimiento correspondi<97> al cr<8e>dito ganadero, y el comercial fue el de mayor participaci<97>n. Adicionalmente, indicadores de rentabilidad, liquidez y riesgo del sistema financiero nacional continuaron reflejando la sanidad del sistema. El Sector P<9c>blico No Financiero finaliz<97> 2014 con un d<8e>ficit despu<8e>s de donaciones de 1.5 por ciento del PIB. Este d<8e>ficit reflej<97> principalmente el mayor gasto de capital, en su mayor<92>a del resto del sector p<9c>blico no financiero. No obstante, el Gobierno Central mostr<97> un mejor desempe<96>o respecto a lo planificado, con un d<8e>ficit despu<8e>s de donaciones de 0.3 por ciento, siendo que su proyecci<97>n en el Programa Econ<97>mico y Financiero fue de 0.5% del PIB. Este mejor desempe<96>o estuvo en l<92>nea con una evoluci<97>n positiva de la recaudaci<97>n tributaria y una pol<92>tica de gasto prudente. En cuanto a la deuda p<9c>blica total, <8e>sta alcanz<97> la cifra de 5,800 millones de d<97>lares, equivalentes al 49.1 por ciento del PIB de 2014, reflejando una reducci<97>n de 4.2 puntos porcentuales con respecto a 2013. Esta evoluci<97>n de la deuda refleja una pol<92>tica de endeudamiento p<9c>blico externo e interno responsable. El sector exportador mostr<97> una recuperaci<97>n al crecer 9.6 por ciento en 2014 (-10.1% en 2013), la cual fue impulsada por el aumento en la demanda de la mayor<92>a de nuestros principales socios comerciales, combinado con la expansi<97>n productiva particularmente de los sectores manufactura (carne, az<9c>car y l<87>cteos) y agr<92>cola (caf<8e>, man<92> y frijoles). La miner<92>a y la pesca se vieron afectadas por las ca<92>das en los precios internacionales tanto del oro como del camar<97>n, lo que redujo el valor exportado de dichos rubros. Las exportaciones de zona franca por su parte crecieron 7.2 por ciento, como resultado de mayores exportaciones de textiles y productos pesqueros y calzado. Las importaciones de mercanc<92>as mostraron un crecimiento de 3.9 por ciento (-3.4% en 2013), determinadas principalmente por mayores importaciones de bienes de capital, especialmente de industria, y bienes de consumo, lo cual fue congruente con la din<87>mica de la actividad econ<97>mica del pa<92>s. No obstante, se registr<97> una menor factura petrolera por 4.1 por ciento, producto de la ca<92>da de los precios internacionales del petr<97>leo. De esta forma, el intercambio con el resto del mundo estuvo positivamente influenciado por la recuperaci<97>n de la econom<92>a estadounidense y su impacto en econom<92>as relacionadas, la reducci<97>n en los precios internacionales del petr<97>leo y el dinamismo de los sectores productivos nacionales, lo cual fue parcialmente contrarrestado por la ca<92>da del precio del oro. El resultado final fue una reducci<97>n en el d<8e>ficit de cuenta corriente de la Balanza de Pagos como porcentaje del PIB de 4 puntos porcentuales respecto a 2013, alcanzando un monto de 838.1 millones de d<97>lares, equivalente a 7.1 por ciento del PIB. La conducci<97>n de pol<92>tica monetaria en coordinaci<97>n con la pol<92>tica fiscal permiti<97> alcanzar un saldo r<8e>cord de reservas internacionales brutas (RIB) de 2,276.2 millones de d<97>lares (14.2% superior a 2013). Este resultado estuvo determinado principalmente por una mayor absorci<97>n de recursos internos y entrada de recursos externos. As<92>, se logr<97> una cobertura de RIB a base monetaria de 2.6 veces y de 4.7 meses de importaciones, niveles que refuerzan la credibilidad en el r<8e>gimen cambiario. En este contexto de cierre de 2014, las perspectivas econ<97>micas para 2015 tambi<8e>n se mantienen positivas. Para el presente a<96>o se mantiene el rango de crecimiento esperado entre 4.5-5 por ciento, lo que estar<87> respaldado por un mejor contexto internacional en t<8e>rminos de crecimiento de nuestros principales socios comerciales y de precios de materias primas. No obstante, persistir<92>an riesgos como las variaciones en el precio del petr<97>leo y presiones al alza en las tasas de inter<8e>s internacionales. Desde el punto de vista interno, tambi<8e>n continuamos vulnerables a eventos relacionados al cambio clim<87>tico. As<92>, se espera que las pol<92>ticas macroecon<97>micas y sectoriales que se est<87>n implementando propicien una tasa de inflaci<97>n en un rango entre 6.0 y 7.0 por ciento, se mantenga la estabilidad financiera, y se contin<9c>e con la senda de fortalecimiento de la sostenibilidad fiscal y externa del pa<92>s. Para finalizar, quisiera hacer una reflexi<97>n en torno a los resultados macroecon<97>micos 2014 y las perspectivas de futuro. Si bien la econom<92>a nacional ha venido evolucionando positivamente, no podemos dejar a un lado el hecho que nuestro PIB por habitante es a<9c>n muy bajo, alcanzando 1,905 d<97>lares por habitante, en comparaci<97>n, el PIB por habitante promedio de Centroam<8e>rica es de 5,260 d<97>lares por habitante. Si bien se registran avances y buena din<87>mica en el campo macroecon<97>mico, permanecen desaf<92>os importantes. El mercado laboral presenta un alto porcentaje de empleo Informal, mientras que el 42% de nuestra poblaci<97>n contin<9c>a viviendo en condiciones de pobreza. A estas personas les resultar<87> dif<92>cil entender los resultados macroecon<97>micos porque a<9c>n no se traducen en una mejora significativa de su nivel de vida. Sin embargo, lo m<87>s importante, es que la estabilidad macroecon<97>mica que hemos alcanzado en un modelo de di<87>logo, alianzas y consenso amplio entre el Gobierno y las principales fuerzas productivas, crea oportunidades para continuar aumentando el ritmo de producci<97>n y atraer inversiones que generen nuevos empleos y nos permitan poco a poco salir de la pobreza. A esto es lo que debemos continuar apostando todos los nicarag<9f>enses para alcanzar cada vez mayores niveles de bienestar y prosperidad. Muchas Gracias.

Title: Seminar Mechanisms of Transmission of Monetary Policy Opening speech, September 24, 2015
text: SEMINAR MONETARY POLICY TRANSMISSION MECHANISMS OPENING SPEECH BY THE PRESIDENT OF THE CENTRAL BANK OF NICARAGUA SEPTEMBER 24, 2015 24/09/2015 Good morning. I welcome you all to the Monetary Policy Transmission Mechanisms Seminar. I would like to thank you for your presence today and in a very particular way Mr. Herberth Solorzano of the Central Bank of Guatemala, Mr. Joel Gonzalez of the Central Bank of the Dominican Republic, Mr. Adolfo Cobo of the Central Bank of Colombia, Mr. Juan Sebastian Chamorro of FUNIDES and Mr. Jean Francois Clevy of the Central Bank of Nicaragua, who will be the speakers of this Seminar and who kindly accepted our invitation to participate. In the case of foreign guests, please convey, through your media, our thanks to the presidents of your respective Central Banks for allowing you to share with us your experiences. Before inaugurating this event, I would like to share and share with you our joy as Nicaraguans for being September the month of freedom and independence of our nation. In addition to our greatest national holiday, we are also proudly celebrating the 55th anniversary of the founding of the Central Bank of Nicaragua, and this seminar is a special way to commemorate it. Since its creation in 1960, our institution has ensured that the country has macroeconomic stability, for the benefit of Nicaraguan society. In this regard, it was logical to highlight the issue of monetary policy transmission mechanisms. After all, the Central Bank is the authority in charge of issuance, payment systems, and good policy design lies in understanding, at the highest level, how transmission mechanisms are transmitted to the main macroeconomic variables. Unfortunately, we have to be humble and recognize that it is not easy to fully understand these transmission mechanisms. Economics is a social science and as such is riddled with inaccuracies and oddities, often not captured by theoretical and mathematical models. Thus, in the design of monetary policy, pragmatism and common sense must prevail over theoretical considerations. For some, this may be debatable, and for this type of discussions that allow us to approach the understanding of reality is that these types of events take place. Today we seek to establish a space for the study of international and national experience related to the channels through which monetary policy operates at the macroeconomic level, in order to improve the work and mandate of central banks. That is, to formulate and execute effectively and efficiently a monetary policy that favors the development and welfare of the population. During the seminar, we will hear the experiences of the central banks of Guatemala and the Dominican Republic, countries that are part of the Central American Monetary Council. We will also have the opportunity to learn about the experience of Colombia, a country that has an important financial integration with Central America. The experience of these three central banks in monetary policy has led them to establish inflation-targeting regimes, which are mandatory for all. In the case of Nicaragua, we will know the opinion of one of the most important think tanks in the country, such as FUNIDES. Likewise, our institution will present the technical analysis that we have been carrying out in this field. I trust then that today we will have a productive event that will leave us with a rich agenda of experiences and ideas to improve the policies of the Central Bank's work. I invite you then to make the most of this Seminar, which I consider to have been opened. Thanks a lot.

La econom<92>a es una ciencia social y como tal est<87> plagada de imprecisiones y rarezas, muchas veces no capturadas por los modelos te<97>ricos y matem<87>ticos. Para algunos, esto puede ser discutible, y para este tipo de discusiones que permitan acercarnos al entendimiento de la realidad es que se realizan este tipo de eventos. El d<92>a de hoy buscamos establecer un espacio para el estudio de la experiencia internacional y nacional relacionada con los canales a trav<8e>s de los cuales la pol<92>tica monetaria opera a nivel macroecon<97>mico, a fin de mejorar la labor y el mandato de los bancos centrales. Es decir, formular y ejecutar efectiva y eficientemente una pol<92>tica monetaria que favorezca al desarrollo y bienestar de la poblaci<97>n. Durante el seminario, escucharemos las experiencias de los bancos centrales de Guatemala y Rep<9c>blica Dominicana, pa<92>ses que forman parte del Consejo Monetario Centroamericano. Tambi<8e>n tendremos la oportunidad de conocer la experiencia de Colombia, pa<92>s que tiene una importante integraci<97>n a nivel financiero con Centroam<8e>rica. La experiencia de estos tres bancos centrales en pol<92>tica monetaria los ha conducido a establecer reg<92>menes de metas de inflaci<97>n, que resultan de obligatorio estudio para todos. Para el caso de Nicaragua, conoceremos la opini<97>n de uno de los centros de pensamientos m<87>s importantes del pa<92>s, como lo es FUNIDES. Asimismo, nuestra instituci<97>n presentar<87> el an<87>lisis t<8e>cnico que hemos venido realizando en este campo. Conf<92>o entonces que el d<92>a de hoy tendremos un evento productivo que nos dejar<87> una rica agenda de experiencias e ideas para ir mejorando las pol<92>ticas del quehacer del Banco Central. Title: Launch of new bills 2015
text: LAUNCH OF NEW BANKNOTES 2015, WORDS OF THE PRESIDENT OF THE CENTRAL BANK OF NICARAGUA, OVIDIO REYES R., OCTOBER 2015 12/10/2015 Good morning friends journalists and Nicaraguan people. The Central Bank of Nicaragua announces the issuance of the new 2015 banknotes, approved by the Board of Directors of the BCN in March 2014. The issuance of the new banknotes is carried out to supply the demand of the period 2015-2017, replace the banknotes that the central bank withdraws from circulation due to their deterioration and improve the security characteristics of the banknote in circulation, taking into account advances in technology and international best practices. The new banknotes will begin to circulate from October 26, 2015. It is worth mentioning that the banknotes currently in circulation will retain their liberatory value and will continue to circulate until they are gradually replaced, as they deteriorate. This process of modernization of our banknotes was used to make changes in their design that will make them, in addition to being safer, colorful and attractive, incorporating new images of buildings, landscapes and traditions that promote the identity, culture and beauty of our country. This new banknote issue comprises the following main aspects: 1. It has a denomination printed on cotton paper substrate -that of 500 cordobas- and five denominations printed on polymer substrate, which are 10.20, 50.100 and 200 cordobas. 2. The existing denominations will be maintained, each of which will have colors and sizes similar to the current ones. 3. In the length, the banknotes have a difference of 5 mm between each denomination, while the width is the same for all banknotes, this is 67mm. Designation Material or substrate Length (mm) Width (mm) 500 cordobas Paper 156 67 200 cordobas Polymer 151 67 100 cordobas Polymer 146 67 50 cordobas Polymer 141 67 20 cordobas Polymer 136 67 10 cordobas Polymer 131 67 4. It was decided to print banknotes of different sizes to facilitate their identification and reduce the risk of counterfeiting. 5. For the denominations of 10, 20, 50, 100 and 200 cordobas, polymer material, or plastic, was used to achieve greater durability, since these banknotes have high circulation. It also seeks to issue cleaner banknotes and protect the environment. 6. The new banknotes are signed by the President of the Central Bank and the Minister of Finance and Public Credit, as established by the Organic Law of the Central Bank of Nicaragua. The designs and main security features of the banknotes are the following: 500 cordobas banknote: It is red and the design highlights the western region of the country, showing on the obverse the image of the cathedral of Leon and on the reverse to the Momotombo volcano. The main security measures of this denomination are an ink stamp with dynamic effect in the form of a hexagon and with the number of the denomination printed, which shows the figure of a circle that moves when tilting the banknote, this being the first banknote in the world with this technology. In addition, it presents a security thread with color change effect, from red to gold and the watermark with the image of the sacuanjoche flower. On the reverse it has a band that shines when tilted with the denomination of 500. 200 cordobas banknote: It is brown, and the design represents national art, with the image on the obverse of the Ruben Dario National Theater and on the reverse, a representation of the dance comedy "El Gueguense". The main security measures of this banknote are the complex window with variable optical effect depending on the angle of light, with the image of the guard, this being the second banknote in the world with this technology, as well as the transparent window with color change effect with the number of the denomination printed. 100 cordobas banknote: It is blue, and the design pays homage to the city of Granada, presenting on the obverse the image of the cathedral of Granada and on the reverse the image of a horse carriage, alluding to this historic city. In this denomination, the main security measures are the complex window with color change effect, from purple to green and from purple to gold, with image of two atabales and transparent window with color change effect with the number of the denomination printed. Ticket of 50 cordobas: It is purple, and the design represents the craftsmanship and national folklore, presenting on the obverse the image of the handicraft market of Masaya and on the reverse an image of the Nicaraguan folkloric ballet. The main security measures of this banknote are the complex window with color change effect, from purple to green, with image of two marimbas and transparent window with color change effect with the number of the denomination printed. 20 cordobas banknote: It is orange, and the design pays homage to the Caribbean region of Nicaragua, showing on the obverse the image of the Moravian church of Laguna de Perlas and on the reverse a representative image of the Mayo Ya festival. The main security measures are the complex window with color change effect, from purple to brown, with image of two turtles and transparent window with color change effect with the number of the denomination printed. 10 cordobas banknote: It is light green, and the design represents the city of Managua, showing on the obverse an image of Puerto Salvador Allende and on the reverse the image of the dance of La Vaquita, in homage to the patron saint festivities of Managua. The main security measures are the window complex with color change effect, from golden to green, with images of two palm trees and transparent window with Color change effect with the printed denomination number. The Central Bank of Nicaragua hopes that with this new issuance of banknotes, the population will carry out their transactions in an agile and safe manner. Thanks a lot.

Title: Transcription of Press Conference: Conclusions on Review of Economic Performance and Perspectives, and Mr. Gerardo Peraza, Head of the IMF Delegation
text: TRANSCRIPT PRESS CONFERENCE CONCLUSIONS REVIEW OF ECONOMIC PERFORMANCE AND OUTLOOK BCN PRESIDENT OVIDIO REYES AND MR. GERARDO PERAZA, IMF DELEGATION CHIEF OCTOBER 29, 2015 Master of Ceremony: The President of the Central Bank of Nicaragua, Comparo Ovidio Reyes and the Head of Delegation of the International Monetary Fund, Mr. Gerardo Peraza will offer statements at the conclusion of the meeting between the Government of Nicaragua and the International Monetary Fund to review the economic performance and prospects of the country. The President of the Central Bank of Nicaragua will give statements initially. Ovidio Reyes: Good morning, my friends, journalists and the Nicaraguan people. Today the International Monetary Fund is concluding a visit to our country that aimed to carry out an evaluation of the Macroeconomic Performance and Outlook. In this assessment, the IMF met with the economic team. We have also recently completed a meeting between the IMF staff and the economic team to see the results of their mission. The IMF also held meetings with all the institutions involved in national financial and macroeconomic work. In general, the IMF has told us at the meeting that our economy is robust and that the set of economic policies aimed at strengthening financial and macroeconomic security are adequate. This coincides with the analysis that we have been carrying out throughout this time and that also strengthens our medium-term macroeconomic projections aimed at increasing growth and maintaining stable inflation. I therefore leave it to the Representative of the International Monetary Fund, Mr. Gerardo Peraza, who will make the final statement of his visit. Gerardo Peraza: First of all, I would like to thank the Nicaraguan authorities, especially here the Governor of the Central Bank of Nicaragua, for their kind hospitality, excellent cooperation and frank discussions in these two weeks. In particular, to the President of the Bank for his kindness to take care of us and attend to us in these two weeks, especially me. As the Governor stated, we have had formal meetings with members of the Production and Budget, also a group of trade unions, academic groups, representatives of Analytics centers and business leaders. The macroeconomic outlook, as we see them, is positive. By 2015, GDP growth is estimated to be about 4%. Obviously the figures can be revised once we have more information and, mainly, due to the result of inflation and the price of petreo. We have inflation projected at around 3.5%. We also estimate that the deficit of the consolidated sector will rise by approximately 2.7% of GDP. In addition, we project a moderate increase in the external account deficit to 8%, but we estimate that reserve coverage remains stable compared to the previous year. For the medium term, we see issues of potential growth and we have had very frank discussions with officials that perhaps, in the medium term, it would be growth of about 4%, with stable inflation of 7%. As the Governor said, what we perceive is that the combination of current policies is conducive to maintaining macroeconomic stability. So, that's what he means is that there is a good prompt for the rest of the a. So with that, I remain at the service for your questions. Master of Ceremonies: Next we will enter a question and answer period. Libeth Gonzalez of Radio La Primerisima begins. Libeth Gonzalez: It is determined that 4% could be true growth, with the reduction in the price of petreo, the more you consider that this could contribute, I want to ask Dr. Ovidio Reyes, how much could this contribute let's say to achieve a greater dynamism of the economy in the country? Ovidio Reyes: Our estimates are already made with all the changes incorporated, in prices of the Petreo. Let us remember that we already have a first semester observed, even some months too and on the basis of the return that already incorporates the new prices of petreo, is that we have made our estimates. I must clarify that we have a little more growth than what the IMF is projecting, we have not changed our estimate of 4.3% at least and up to 4.8% maximum. However, in the light of the information, as it ends month by month, and Arriving, we could make some adjustment towards Go ahead, but at this moment we We maintain at 4.3%. Master of Ceremony: Blanca Morel, AFP Agency. Blanca Morel: I wanted to ask you if the drought affecting the entire Central American Dry Corridor will affect Nicaragua's economic growth projections, specifically if you plan to take some measures, given that the phenomenon is expected to also affect the beginning of cousin a? Ovidio Reyes: Like the previous question, we have incorporated all the changes that have already occurred to date, more or less until August we have approximate information, and that is already incorporated into the estimate of 4% that the IMF has and the 4.3% that we continue to sustain with all the new information. Let us remember that, yet, the winter is not over and we need to hold meetings with the productive sectors, to carry out the final evaluation. Master of Ceremony: Journalist Ricardo Guerrero, El Nuevo Diario. Ricardo Guerrero: As Peraza is, apart from all the findings that you found in our economy in the discussions and conversations you had with the different actors, I would like to know what are the main recommendations that you leave to the government, as trusted advisors, as the government now has for you. What are the main recommendations left to the Government after this visit? Gerardo Peraza: I'll explain the process a little bit. We have a preliminary evaluation with the Information that the authorities have given us, we went back to Washington, finalized our report and took it to the IMF board, where we elaborated in more detail the specific recommendations. What I can tell you is that there has been a consensus, a full consensus with the authorities that there is a need to strengthen macro policies in general and that is the fundamental thing. So, in terms of specific recommendations, as I mentioned, we will have more details in the report that will be published in a moment. Master of Ceremony: Journalist Nestor Tellez, Canal 14. Nestor Tellez: Doctor, what sectors would be pushing this growth that you project for cousin a of the country's economy, projecting that the main commodities such as coffee, gold would be lowering their prices, I would also like to know your appreciation of this study presented by the World Bank and that COSEP does not agree. in what does the business climate in Nicaragua range 125 to 123? Ovidio Reyes: Well, as we have explained before, we have seen that as a result of the fall in the price of oil, there has been a greater internal dynamic in the economy, mainly in terms of consumption, services and even the construction sector. It is not surprising that the release of resources left by the lower oil bill and the lower expenditure of fuel, is then destined by the population towards other spending activities. So, we expect that dynamic, the dynamics of construction, the dynamics of the service sector, will continue for cousin a. The export sector, as we also agree on that with the IMF, because it maintains a not so positive expectation, because international prices really tend downward and the world economy has not been able to get out of the problems it presents. Yesterday, for example, the US Federal Reserve kept monetary policy interest rates unchanged. It is a clear indication that the conditions are not in place for the world economy to fully reactivate. Regarding what I ask about the work of the World Bank, we are studying it. Well, I don't know, I have to study the document. Jonathan Castro-100% News: But you don't know where those figures come from? Ovidio Reyes: Well, I don't know, I have to study the document. Master of Ceremony: We have the tima intervenci with the journalist Wendy alvarez of La Prensa. Wendy Alvarez: Good morning. Being from the IMF. In the scams you have celebrated the macroeconomic stability of Nicaragua and I would like to know, because so far there has not been a more open debate, for example, on the issue of informality that in Nicaragua affects almost 75% of the market; Productivity has been falling. The exchange rate, for example, although you project inflation at 3.5%, remember that we have a slippage rate of 5% per year. Practically already that is an elevated floor. The issue of the INSS also, this for the second consecutive time the INSS will close with a deficit of almost 600 million cdobas, despite the fact that in 2013 a reform was discussed, enter into force and it had been promised that in 2014 it would generate a surplus, despite this the INSS closed a deficit of 800 million cdobas. Even prime a is expected to generate a surplus. And apart from that, in the case of purchasing power that remains below 2006. I would like to know what recommendations you have given to the government to solve these problems. And in the case of Mr. Ovidio Reyes, I would like you to explain: on August 6 you promised that the methodology used for the revision of the National Accounts and the balance of payments would be published in October. Remember that this opened a gap that had to adjust different sectors to prevent GDP from falling a little more than 800 million dollars in 2013. I would also like you to explain to me why the National Accounts report has not yet been published in the second quarter of this year. It is almost a month late. Thanks a lot. Gerardo Peraza: With regard to macroeconomic stability, let's think about it from this perspective: The sectors that do not have protection when there is no macroeconomic stability are the most vulnerable. So, from that perspective, maintaining macroeconomic stability is important to maintain the living conditions of the most vulnerable. With regard to informality, it is a relevant issue, and we have discussed some issues about it. We will have more specific recommendations in our report. But it is an issue that really has to be discussed, thought about and worked on, precisely that can lead to greater growth. With the theme of the INSS. Indeed, the 2013 reform increases contributions, there is an issue of expenses, we must see it and especially the long-term projections of the INSS. We still need to increase contributions by 1% in the 2 ace primes, so once we have a better picture of what the financial situation is that can be reviewed. Ovidio Reyes: We did an exhibition, as Wendy says. In that presentation we clarified what all the adjustments we had made, adjustments we made in coordination and the technical assistance of the Monetary Fund were about. Indeed, we have been working on that from that date until now and the IMF has additional considerations that once we incorporate them we will finish it. These issues are issues that take time, they are issues that lead to a review and lead to an improvement of the statistical system and as such they have made recommendations to us and we will continue working on that. With regard to the issues of the cycle, I have told you that we also see these issues at the production table with the productive sectors, when we have completed that review, then we will proceed to make the respective explanations and projections. Let us remember that all this results from the model of dialogue and consensus that the government has with the sectors. We ask them how to see the progress of production and how they see the future, and on that basis we make our adjustments and corrections. Wendy alvarez: Dr. Ovidio I was not referring to the production cycle, what I meant was that in the anticipated publication calendar you said a month ago that the National Accounts were going to be published for the second quarter and you have not published that. Ovidio Reyes: It has to do with the same thing, Wendy. Wendy alvarez: This quarterly accounts report does not necessarily include the issue of production, but rather advances growth in different sectors. Ovidio Reyes: It's the same. Master of Ceremony: We have concluded the press conference, we appreciate your valuable presence.

Title: Delivery of Awards of the Contest: Award for Economics, Finance and Development Dr. Vicente Vita Rodrguez 2015, December 10, 2015
text: AWARDS CEREMONY OF THE CONTEST: PRIZE OF ECONOMY, FINANCE AND DEVELOPMENT DR. VICENTE VITA RODRiGUEZ 2015, PRESIDENT OF THE CENTRAL BANK OF NICARAGUA, OVIDIO REYES R., DECEMBER 10, 2015 10/12/2015 Good afternoon. Thank you all for your presence at this award ceremony where, through the "Dr. Vicente Vita Rodriguez 2015 Economics, Finance and Development Award", we recognize the efforts of researchers and academics who have provided valuable contributions to the understanding of the economy and social sciences of our country. For the Central Bank of Nicaragua it is in the interest of promoting scientific research that generates value, so that it serves as an input in the elaboration and implementation of the country's economic policies. We promote this initiative under the premise that there are researchers, national and foreign, trained to make significant advances in the frontier of knowledge about the Nicaraguan economy. This year, within the framework of the Contest, 12 research papers were received on various topics of monetary and exchange policy, fiscal policy, labor market, tourism, migration, education, among others. Additionally, as in the last two years, we have the participation of national and foreign researchers. Particularly, in 2015, we had contributions from researchers from Mexico, El Salvador, Colombia and Ecuador. The Qualifying Jury had an arduous task when choosing the winners. Presentation criteria, originality, quality of the argument, theoretical and methodological rigor were used. It is worth mentioning that the process of choosing the winners is anonymous so as not to bias the selection. The Jury, made up of officials of the Central Bank of Nicaragua, unanimously decided to award two prizes and a special mention. The first place corresponded to the research: "Do we all educate ourselves equally? Analysis of the determinants of educational inequality in Nicaragua" by Lelys lleana Dinarte and Alan Rico. This paper proposes a methodology to analyze inequality in educational quality in Nicaragua, measured from the variability in the results of standardized tests. The authors found that the determinants that generate the greatest contribution to explain educational inequality until 2006 are: first, an index of the socioeconomic level of the family, constructed as a combination of various socioeconomic variables and, second, the characteristics of schools. In particular, of the total variance, 96 percent for mathematics and 85 percent for language is determined by the joint effects of the Socioeconomic Level index and effects of school characteristics. The second place was awarded to a research written in English that we could translate as: "Living standards, multidimensional poverty, and intergenerational transmission of income: Comparative analysis between different family arrangements in Nicaragua" by Alvaro Jose Altamirano Montoya. This research examines, comparatively, the socioeconomic conditions of Nicaraguan families. The study finds that male-headed two-parent families have a higher incidence of poverty than those of single mothers or two-parent families headed by women. And finally, a special mention is given to the work: "Migration and Welfare: An analysis of Nicaraguan households" by Alvaro Anibal Lopez Espinoza. This paper analyzes the impact of migration on the well-being of Nicaraguan households. The results show that migration processes do improve the well-being of Nicaraguan families, so that a proportion of households that are not considered poor in the sample used would be below the poverty line if they did not receive remittances. As we can see, this year's winning research measures important issues of development and living standards and poverty in our country. I must mention that the BCN is committed to the promotion of research, and that the Vicente Vita 2016 Contest is soon to open its call, and I invite those present to participate in this new edition and also to distribute the message among their fellow researchers. In closing, let me extend my congratulations to the winners, their families and friends who are with us today. I also thank everyone present for accepting our invitation to attend this award. I take this opportunity to wish you on behalf of the Central Bank of Nicaragua, and myself, our best wishes for a happy Christmas and New Year holidays in the company of your loved ones. Thanks a lot.

Como podemos observar, las investigaciones ganadoras de este a<96>o realizan mediciones en temas importantes del desarrollo y los niveles de vida y pobreza en nuestro pa<92>s. Debo mencionar que el BCN se encuentra comprometido con la promoci<97>n de la investigaci<97>n, y que el Certamen Vicente Vita 2016 ya est<87> pronto a abrir su convocatoria, e invito a los presentes a participar en esta nueva edici<97>n y tambi<8e>n a distribuir el mensaje entre sus colegas investigadores. Title: Presentation of Commemorative Postal Stamp: Centenary of the Death of Poet Rubn Daro, December 16, 2015
text: PRESENTATION OF COMMEMORATIVE POSTAGE STAMP: CENTENARY OF THE DEATH OF POET RUBeN DARiO, PRESIDENT OF THE CENTRAL BANK OF NICARAGUA OVIDIO REYES R., DECEMBER 16, 2015 16/12/2015 Good morning to everyone present at this event. The Central Bank of Nicaragua and our entire country recognizes in Ruben Dario the highest representative of our Nicaraguanness. Throughout the world he is also recognized as the Prince of Castilian letters. The Bank has reflected this recognition of our Poet in a number of works that he has published, on our banknotes, in authentic poems that we guard and in a set of artistic works from our collection. Scholars have praised Ruben Dario as the literary Bolivar of Latin America, transatlantic leader of modernism, rooted cosmopolitan, and emblematic singer and forger of Latin American identity. Essential facets of his that Nicaraguans share with pride to remember him always. As part of the commemoration of the centenary of his death, or rather of his entry into immortality, the Central Bank of Nicaragua in coordination with the Correos de Nicaragua company, we have had the initiative to present a commemorative stamp to honor our great universal poet. It is a stamp that contains an oil portrait of the Poet, whose original work is in our gallery and which was executed by the artist Julio Martinez. The issue is composed of ten thousand stamps, whose unit size is 35 x 45 mm, at a face value of C60 (Sesenta Cordobas), with the legend: "Centenary of the Death of the Poet Ruben Dario 1916-2016. This seal will begin to circulate nationally from the date and we hope that everyone enjoys it with respect and affection. Let us celebrate, then, the official opening of this stamp: the first of many that will surely be issued in other countries to commemorate the transcendent value of Hispanic letters of all times that is our Ruben Dario. Thanks a lot.

Title: Commemoration of the Centenary of the Death of Rubn Daro
text: COMMEMORATION OF THE CENTENARY OF THE DEATH OF RUBeN DARiO GENERAL MANAGER OF BCN SARA AMELIA ROSALES CASTELLoN FRIDAY, FEBRUARY 5, 2016 05/02/2016 Good morning, the President of the Central Bank of Nicaragua, Companero Ovidio Reyes Ramirez, has delegated me to preside over this act, and excuses himself from not being present for reasons of force majeure, so welcome Directors of the Board of Directors of the Central Bank of Nicaragua; Directors of the Board of Directors of the Superintendency of Banks and Other Financial Institutions; Ambassadors and representatives of the Diplomatic Corps in Nicaragua; Members of the Academy of Geography and History of Nicaragua; Members of the Nicaraguan Academy of Language; Mr. Pablo Kraudy Medina, Professor of Philosophy at the UNAN-Managua and other Nicaraguan universities, Member of the Academy of Geography and History of Nicaragua (AGHN), Order of Cultural Independence Ruben Dario, 2008; Mr. Erick Aguirre Aragon, Writer and Member of the Nicaraguan Academy of Language; Mr. Ruben Dario Lacayo, great-grandson of Ruben Dario; Special Guests; officials of the Central Bank; media representatives. It is an honor on behalf of the Central Bank of Nicaragua to address these words, in this act, where once again our institution exalts the greatest Nicaraguan, Ruben Dario, as is known, on the centenary of his death  that is, of his entry into the glory of immortality  is the anniversary that motivates him. In December 2015, the Bank officially inaugurated the issuance of a postage stamp with an oil portrait of our great man of letters, belonging to the artistic heritage of the institution. Today we continue to pay tribute to him, announcing the issuance of commemorative coins, "Centenary of the Death of the Poet Ruben Dario", minted in gold and silver materials, with a representative design of this anniversary. Presenting the first issue of the Nicaraguan Journal of Culture, devoted to his life and work. A Dariano Catalogue has been published, amply illustrated, which contains the cultural heritage of Dario existing in our institution and renaming our library with the name of Ruben Dario, for the transcendence that means the legacy of the Prince of Castilian Letters to Nicaraguan culture and universal culture, and for being this a center of knowledge, development of reading, educational, research and with a wide collection of the literary work of Dario, original manuscripts and other artistic expressions in which numismatics, painting and sculpture excel. It is appropriate to mention that the Bank's Executive Building will be named after Dr. Roberto Incer Barquero. These announcements are four different expressions with a single objective: to recognize Dario as the maximum cultural creator of Nicaragua, one of the founding managers of Latin American identity and the most transcendent revolutionary of poetry in the Spanish language. For something it has been said that after Miguel de Cervantes he has been our inevitable countryman, the author of the Hispanic letters that has most aroused interpretations, having translated his works into sixteen languages: German, Arabic, Bulgarian, Croatian, Chinese, Czech, Danish, French, Hungarian, English, Italian, Japanese, Portuguese, Romanian, Russian and Swedish, which until now we know. As an intellectual builder of the country, we must remember his book El viaje a Nicaragua e Intermezzo tropical (1909), in which he traces our history, describes our geography and our natural resources, praises our women and investigates for the first time the idiosyncrasy of the Nicaraguan, describing our people as cheerful, brave, haughty, passionate, cunning, adventurous and vibrant. To conclude, I wish to transcribe two quotes about Dario and his experiences. The first is authored by the Spaniard Jorge Guillen, who said: "No one has been emperor as absolute as he, who became a poet of all Spain. Only in the verses of Ruben does the sun not set." And the other belongs to the universal Argentine Jorge Luis Borges, who said: "Dario renewed everything, the matter, the vocabulary, the meter, the peculiar magic of certain words, the sensitivity of the poet and his readers. Their work has not ceased and will not cease. Those of us who once fought it understand today that we continue it. And we can call him The Liberator." Thanks a lot.

Title: Presentation of the Annual Report 2015 to the National Assembly, April 5, 2016
text: PRESENTATION OF THE 2015 ANNUAL REPORT TO THE NATIONAL ASSEMBLY, PRESIDENT OF THE BCN OVIDIO REYES R., APRIL 5, 2016 05/04/2016 Good morning, Engineer Rene Nunez Tellez, President of the National Assembly and members of the Board of Directors, Deputies. I am pleased to write to you, in accordance with the mandate of the Law, the Annual Report of the Central Bank of Nicaragua for the year 2015. The Nicaraguan economy performed favorably in 2015. Thus, GDP growth was 4.9 percent, 0.3 percentage points above the growth registered in 2014, thus maintaining the good dynamics of the last five years, a period during which economic growth averaged 5.2 percent. By the production approach, the largest contributions to economic growth came from the services and trade sectors with 2.7 percentage points, followed by construction activity with 1.3 percentage points, and agriculture, livestock and forestry activities with 0.6 percentage points. By the expenditure approach, growth was determined by Gross Capital Formation, which grew 29.5 percent and for Consumption that grew 5.2 percent. Imports grew 11.6 percent and exports decreased 2.0 percent. Consistent with the performance of the national economy, both employment and wages continued to show a positive and sustained evolution. Affiliation to the INSS registered a growth in formal employment of 8.9 percent, the highest in the last five years. The sectors that attracted the most affiliates on average were commerce, hotels, restaurants; and the financial sector. Likewise, the average nominal salary of INSS affiliates grew 6.3 percent, while in real terms the growth was 2.2 percent. On the part of the Central Government, the increase in the average nominal wage was 7.0 percent and 2.8 percent in real terms. As for price dynamics, inflation during 2015 was low and stable, registering the lowest level in the last five years, standing at 3.05 percent as of December 2015 (6.48 percent in December 2014). This behavior was mainly the result of the transfer of low international oil and food prices to the rest of the prices of the domestic economy. In addition, the continuity of the government's subsidy policy, the adequate food supply in the country and the changed scheme contributed to price stability. In terms of contribution to inflation, the Restaurants and hotels sector was the one with the greatest contribution with 0.82 percentage points, followed by Education with 0.46 percentage points and Recreation and Culture with 0.33 percentage points. As for the Non-Financial Public Sector, it closed 2015 with a deficit after donations equivalent to 1.6 percent of GDP, with its deficit in 2014 of 1.5 percent of GDP. The slight increase in the deficit was mainly due to the marked emphasis of fiscal policy on public investment, evidenced by the 30.6 percent growth in capital spending. The balance of public debt reached a level of 5,753.5 million dollars, equivalent to 45.3 percent of GDP, lower by 3.9 percentage points compared to December 2014. This evolution of debt reflects a policy of sustainable public debt. In 2015 the performance of the National Financial System was positive, highlighting an expansion and stable behavior of credit, coupled with a growth in deposits. Thus, the gross portfolio registered a growth of 23.0 percent and deposits increased by 13.9 percent. The performance of credit and deposits occurred in a context of stable levels of profitability, solvency and capital adequacy. The conduct of monetary policy in coordination with fiscal policy made it possible to achieve adequate levels of International Reserves with respect to the Monetary Base and adequate liquidity conditions. This allowed an accumulation of Gross International Reserves for an amount of 2,492.3 million dollars, 9.5 percent above the level observed in 2014, for a year-end coverage of RIB to WB of 2.3 times, thus safeguarding the stability of the current changed regime. The world economy was distinguished by a moderate performance of developed economies, among which the United States and the Eurozone stand out, and a slowdown in emerging and developing economies, highlighting the slowdown of the Chinese economy, as well as the recession of Brazil and Russia. Overall, according to the International Monetary Fund, the global growth rate in 2015 was 3.1 percent, 0.3 percentage points lower than the growth recorded in 2014, while growth in Latin America was negative at 0.4 percent. Likewise, the international context was determined by the low prices of raw materials, highlighting the marked fall in the price of oil. In addition, tighter financial conditions and lower capital flows were observed due to expectations of the increase in the monetary policy rate in the United States. The export sector was influenced by the international context of low commodity prices. Thus, in 2015 there was a contraction of 8.0 percent in the total value exported, which was determined by lower volumes exported by 6.5 percent and lower contracted prices by 1.5 percent. The products that registered the greatest contraction were gold, sugar and peanuts, however, the export dynamism of dairy products, lobster, shrimp, meat and raw tobacco stood out. For its part, the total export value of the free zone regime registered a contraction of 1.4 percent, significantly lower than the contraction in fob exports. The drop in value was mainly due to lower sales of fishery products and textiles, the latter as a result of the expiration of TPLs. However, this result was partially offset by the dynamism in exports of tobacco, footwear and harnesses. In fob terms, merchandise imports registered a contraction of 0.3 percent, as a result of a 32.3 percent decrease in oil, due to lower international prices. However, non-oil imports, consistent with the dynamism of the economy, registered a growth rate of 8.4 percent, mainly as a result of the dynamism shown by the acquisitions of transport equipment, medicine and pharmaceutical products, construction materials, and industrial machinery. As a result of external factors and domestic demand and supply balances, the current account deficit was 1,045.2 million dollars, equivalent to 8.2 percent of GDP, 0.5 percent higher than in 2014. In short. During 2015, the Nicaraguan economy continued to show vigorous economic and employment growth and low inflation. Public finances remained stable and public debt continued to decline. Monetary policy ensured the stability of the currency reflected in a significant increase in international reserves. The financial system also continued to see growth in credit and deposits, as well as strength in its main indicators. The international context was characterized by a reduction in international fuel prices that increased national disposable income, thus increasing consumption and investment. Meanwhile, the greater internal dynamics allowed to compensate for the higher imports and lower exports resulting from the fall in international prices of primary export products. The economic outlook for 2016 remains positive. For this year, the expected growth range between 4.5 and 5 percent is maintained. Likewise, it is estimated that the macroeconomic and sectoral policies that are being implemented will promote an inflation rate in a range between 5 and 6 percent, a deficit of the Non-Financial Public Sector of 2.1 percent of GDP and a level of Gross International Reserves of 2,551.8 million dollars, which will allow ending the year with a coverage of RIB to Monetary Base of 2.5 times. All of the above while maintaining a slippage rate of 5 percent. However, external risks, such as changes in oil prices and upward pressures on international interest rates, remain. While at the domestic level we continue to be vulnerable to events related to climate change and rainfall regime. I would like to conclude by pointing out that the macroeconomic stability that we have achieved in a model of dialogue, alliances and broad consensus between the Government and the main productive forces creates opportunities to continue increasing the pace of production and attract investments that generate new jobs and gradually allow us to escape poverty. Growth must continue to reach everyone, for the well-being of all, but mainly to the poorest. In this great objective we must continue working all Nicaraguans to achieve higher levels of well-being and prosperity. Thanks a lot.

Mientras que, la mayor din<87>mica interna permiti<97> compensar las mayores importaciones y menores exportaciones resultantes de la baja en los precios internacionales de los productos primarios de exportaci<97>n. Title: V Conference with Companies "The participation of companies in the generation of macroeconomic statistics" Opening speech
text: V CONFERENCE WITH COMPANIES "THE PARTICIPATION OF THE COMPANIES IN THE GENERATION OF MACROECONOMICS" INAUGURAL SPEECH BY THE PRESIDENT OF THE BCN 29/08/2016 Mr. Jose Adan Aguerri, President of the Superior Council of Private Enterprise COSEP, Mr. Michael Healy, President of the Union of Agricultural Producers of Nicaragua, UPANIC, Cra. Sara Amelia Rosales, General Manager of the Central Bank of Nicaragua, Dear representatives of companies, international organizations, media, Central Bank officials and public servants. I am pleased to begin this fifth annual conference with companies, in which the Central Bank of Nicaragua exchanges experiences with entrepreneurs, business managers and representatives who contribute their statistics to the base of the national information prepared by our institution. Since its foundation, the BCN has participated in the design, conceptualization and execution of economic surveys and in the statistical compilation of administrative records. The goal is to obtain information for analysis and decision-making at all levels. The public sector uses these indicators to formulate and evaluate the performance of its policies for the benefit of the population. They also use indicators to analyze economic behavior and make projections. For companies, this information is useful to analyze the context of their activity, the prospects and the situation of their company within the industry to which they belong. Investors take these indicators to find opportunities and undertake new projects. Analysts and academics carry out their evaluations and studies to contrast their hypotheses with facts. Hence the relevance of holding these meetings to review how we are doing our statistics and present the different methodologies and uses. In this fifth conference we are pleased to have the presence of Jose Adan Aguerri, President of the Superior Council of Private Enterprise, COSER who is also a member of the Board of Directors of the BCN. Mr. Aguerri will put into context the business assessment of the statistical work carried out in the Bank. We will also have a presentation on the current situation and outlook for oil, which will be given by Mr. Hector Valdivieso, Energy Specialist at the Inter-American Development Bank, IDB. Finally, Ms Lisbeth Laguna, Manager of National Accounts of the BCN, will present the results of the Digital Cartography of the city of Granada. Before proceeding with the scheduled presentations, I would like to give you the assessment that the Central Bank has on the state of the Nicaraguan economy. In the first half of 2016, economic activity continued to perform solidly. Quarterly GDP registered a year-on-year growth of 4.1 percent in the first quarter of the year, supported by trade, agriculture, financial intermediation services and hotels and restaurants. While the Monthly Index of Economic Activity reflected a higher pace, presenting an accumulated growth of 4.6 per cent determined by the trade, agriculture, livestock and manufacturing sectors, and to a lesser extent by construction. On the demand side, low oil prices continued to boost disposable income and boost consumption and investment, although the weakening of exports offset this. The labour market remained dynamic. The INSS employment growth rate grew year-on-year by 11.4 percent, reaching 819,436 the number of insured. Electric power generation, which is another indicator correlated with GDP, grew by 6.2 percent, with a 51.2 percent share in renewable generation. The dynamism of economic activity was accompanied by a stable performance of prices. During the first half of the year, inflation remained relatively low, presenting a cumulative rate of 2.1 percent as of June. As of July, the year-on-year rate stands at 4.1 percent, below the range initially projected for 2016 that was between 5.0 percent and 6.0 percent. Core inflation, which measures the structural or long-term trend, shows a downward trend, standing at 4.0 percent, being determined by the lower growth in the prices of non-tradable goods. The evolution of domestic prices has been influenced by low international oil prices that lower transport costs, low international inflation that has a downward impact on the prices of imported goods and an adequate food supply that keeps prices stable. Economic performance continued to be supported by prudent macroeconomic policies in both fiscal and monetary areas. The cumulative results of the Central Government to June 2016 reflected a prudent and balanced public finances. Central Government revenues grew by 18.0 percent, a higher rate than expected, while total spending grew by 17.1 percent, resulting in a larger surplus compared to the same period in 2015. The greater fiscal savings have favored the reduction of the public debt balance, which stood at 45.0 percent of GDP. Monetary policy was present in the liquidity markets to stabilize the surpluses originated in the first part of the year, which were induced by the redemptions of BIS, causing greater sales of foreign currency in the foreign exchange market. The open market operations of the BCN led to a net placement of 1,603.5 million cordobas, thus contributing to an adequate position of Gross International Reserves (RIB), which as of June stood at 2,458.9 million dollars, guaranteeing a coverage of 2.7 times the monetary base and 4.9 months of imports. As of July, gross international reserves stood at 2,460.2 million dollars, keeping the correspondence with the Monetary Program. For its part, the activity of the financial sector to June continued its robust and positive trend. In this sense, the loan portfolio maintained a favorable dynamism, growing year-on-year by 23.2 percent. While deposits grew by 11.2 percent, although slowly. Additionally, the profitability and solvency indicators of financial institutions remained robust, with a return on equity of 20.9 percent, a return on assets of 2.3 percent and a non-performing loan portfolio of 1.0 percent. The performance of sectors linked to merchandise exports continued to be affected by a less favourable international environment in terms of prices and external demand. Merchandise exports stood at 1,172.1 million dollars, presenting a year-on-year reduction of 12.5 percent. However, Free Trade Zone exports stood at 1,288.9 million dollars, presenting a year-on-year growth of 12.6 percent, highlighting the participation of textiles, harnesses for vehicles and tobacco, mainly. Merchandise imports, although growing slightly, reflected the dynamism of economic activity. Merchandise imports totaled 2,902.2 million dollars, with a year-on-year growth of 1.6 percent. The determining factor has been the growth of imports of consumption, intermediate goods and capital that grew by 6.9 percent. While oil imports stood at 294.7 million dollars, presenting a reduction of 29.3 percent. On the other hand, the flows of remittances received by Nicaraguans from abroad continued to grow, accumulating 608.4 million dollars, 4.7% higher. The overall context indicates that economic and employment growth continues. The country now has greater capacity to face environmental problems, such as the slowdown in the world economy, low commodity prices or particular problems in domestic sectors. A determining factor for higher economic growth in 2016 will be the regularization of the rainfall regime, which seems to be happening. A good winter will produce significant increases in the agricultural, livestock and fisheries sectors, which will increase the supply of food and exports, thus favoring greater stability in supply and prices. However, the international environment still looms adverse. International commodity prices remain depressed, although recoveries have been observed in gold, coffee and sugar, which, if sustained, could favour our exports. However, the recovery of the United States has not yet been fully consolidated, China is experiencing a slowdown in its growth, Europe is engaged in active policies to get out of recession and Latin America will decrease by 0.8% Due to the above elements, the Central Bank has decided to maintain its GDP growth projection for 2016 between 4.5 and 5.0 percent. This dynamism will continue to be supported by trade, agriculture, services and industry activities, the latter derived from the recovery of exports from Free Trade Zones. Also, based on the lower evolution of international and domestic inflation, and because oil prices have been below the initial projection of 56 dollars average per barrel, the estimate of inflation was revised downwards, which is now projected between 4.5 and 5.5 percent. On the other hand, the Central Government deficit is expected to be close to 1.0 percent of GDP. At the level of the Non-Financial Public Sector, the deficit after grants will be around 2.0 percent of GDP, in which the activation of capital spending is decisive. In conclusion, I would like to thank you once again for joining us this morning, but, above all, to invite you to continue to support this effort to develop national statistics. Thanks a lot.

La pol<92>tica monetaria ejerci<97> presencia en los mercados de liquidez para estabilizar los excedentes originados en la primera parte del a<96>o, los cuales estuvieron inducidos por las redenciones de BPI's, ocasionando mayores ventas de divisas en el mercado cambiario. Las operaciones de mercado abierto del BCN conllevaron a una colocaci<97>n neta por 1,603.5 millones de c<97>rdobas, contribuyendo as<92> a una adecuada posici<97>n de Reservas Internacionales Brutas (RIB), las que al mes de junio se ubicaron en 2,458.9 millones de d<97>lares, garantizando una cobertura de 2.7 veces la base monetaria y de 4.9 meses de importaciones. El desempe<96>o de los sectores vinculados a las exportaciones de mercanc<92>as continu<97> afectado por un entorno internacional menos favorable en t<8e>rminos de precios y de demanda externa. Las exportaciones de mercanc<92>as se ubicaron en 1,172.1 millones de d<97>lares, presentando una reducci<97>n interanual de 12.5 por ciento. Por su parte, los flujos de remesas recibidas por nicarag<9f>enses del exterior continuaron creciendo, acumulando 608.4 millones de d<97>lares, un 4.7% superior.
