Un factor determinante de un mayor crecimiento econ<97>mico en 2016 ser<87> la regularizaci<97>n del r<8e>gimen de lluvias, lo que parece estar ocurriendo. Un buen invierno producir<87> aumentos importantes en el sector agr<92>cola, pecuario y pesca, que aumentar<87>n la oferta de alimentos y de exportaci<97>n, favoreciendo as<92> una mayor estabilidad en el abastecimiento y los precios. No obstante, el entorno internacional a<9c>n se vislumbra adverso. Los precios internacionales de las materias primas contin<9c>an deprimidos, aunque se han observado recuperaciones en el oro, caf<8e> y az<9c>car, que, de sostenerse, podr<92>an favorecer nuestras exportaciones. Sin embargo, la recuperaci<97>n de Estados Unidos a<9c>n no se ha terminado de consolidar, China est<87> experimentando una desaceleraci<97>n en su crecimiento, Europa est<87> enfrascada en pol<92>ticas activas para salir de la recesi<97>n y Am<8e>rica Latina decrecer<87> en 0.8% Por los anteriores elementos, el Banco Central ha decidido mantener su proyecci<97>n de crecimiento del PIB para 2016 entre 4.5 y 5.0 por ciento. Este dinamismo continuar<87> soportado por las actividades de comercio, agropecuario, servicios e industria, este <9c>ltimo derivado de la recuperaci<97>n de las exportaciones de Zonas Francas. Asimismo, con base en la menor evoluci<97>n de la inflaci<97>n internacional e interna, y debido a que los precios del petr<97>leo han estado por debajo de la proyecci<97>n inicial de 56 d<97>lares promedio por barril, se revis<97> hacia la baja la estimaci<97>n de la inflaci<97>n, la que ahora se proyecta entre 4.5 y 5.5 por ciento. Por otro lado, se espera que el d<8e>ficit del Gobierno Central se ubique cercano al 1.0 por ciento del PIB. A nivel del Sector P<9c>blico no Financiero, el d<8e>ficit despu<8e>s de donaciones se ubicar<87> en alrededor del 2.0 por ciento del PIB, en el que resulta determinante la activaci<97>n del gasto de capital. Para finalizar, quisiera agradecerles una vez m<87>s por acompa<96>arnos esta ma<96>ana, pero, sobre todo, invitarlos a continuar apoyando este esfuerzo por desarrollar las estad<92>sticas nacionales. Muchas Gracias.

Title: Signing of the credit line contract with CABEI, 7th renewal
text: ACT OF SIGNING THE CREDIT LINE AGREEMENT WITH CABEI, 7TH RENEWAL WORDS OF THE PRESIDENT OF THE BCN, OVIDIO REYES R. 02/09/2016 Good morning Dr. Silvio Conrado, Director for Nicaragua before the Central American Bank for Economic Integration (CABEI), Ms. Edda Magaly Melendez, CABEI Country Manager, CABEI officials accompanying Dr. Conrado, Cra. Sara Amelia Rosales Castellon, General Manager of the Central Bank of Nicaragua, officials of our institution and fellow journalists. I am pleased to welcome you on the occasion of celebrating the seventh renewal of the Credit Line to support liquidity management, granted by CABEI to the Central Bank of Nicaragua. This Line of Credit for an amount of 200 million dollars is intended to solve contingencies and safeguard the financial position of our country, if required. Seven years ago, CABEI's Board of Executive Directors, in the midst of the 2009 international financial crisis, approved the initiative "Credit Program to Support the Liquidity Management of the Central Banks of CABEI's Founding Countries," consisting of the provision of contingent financing of 200 million for each country. This credit line constitutes an important precautionary measure that commits Nicaragua to developing a coherent economic policy that safeguards macroeconomic and financial stability. I would like to express my gratitude to Dr. Silvio Conrado, whose work has facilitated Nicaragua's continued financial support from this multilateral organization, and I ask you to convey to CABEI's Board of Directors and Executive Presidency our gratitude for this renewal. Thanks a lot.

Title: Presentation of Rubn Daro's Poetic Anthology Book
text: PRESENTATION OF BOOK POETIC ANTHOLOGY OF RUBeN DARiO WORDS OF THE PRESIDENT OF THE BCN, OVIDIO REYES R" SEPTEMBER 5, 2016 05/09/2016 Gold. Telemaco Talavera, rector of the National Agrarian University and the National Council of Universities. Cro. Luis Morales, Director of the Nicaraguan Institute of Culture. Cra. Sara Amelia Rosales, General Manager of the Central Bank of Nicaragua. Poets, writers, public officials of the BCN, journalists who accompany us in this event. The Central Bank of Nicaragua, responding to the guidance of our President, Commander Daniel Ortega, to promote the study and dissemination of our great poet and Prince of Castilian Letters Ruben Dario, in this year that commemorates the centenary of his death, has the honor of presenting the work Antologia Poetica de Ruben Dario. This work is based on a selection that Dario himself made during his maturity, in a poetic self-anthology published for the first time in the Corona Library, Madrid, in three volumes, entitled: Muy siglo XVIII (1914), Muy antiguo y muy moderno (1915) and Y una sed de ilusiones infinitas (1916). Little known, this self-anthology was published for the first time in 1967, within the framework of Dario's birth centenary, with a complementary anthology of 30 Darian poems selected by Pablo Antonio Cuadra and Eduardo Zepeda Henriquez. Three more times, already in the XXI century it was disseminated in Nicaragua by the UNO Foundation (Dario por Dario) in 2001; in Barcelona by Editorial Lumen (Y una sed de ilusiones infinita) in 2011 and in Mexico City by Joaquin Mortiz (Antologia personal) in 2013. Apparently, Darius proposed a fourth volume, entitled Audaz, cosmopolitan, or With Hugo strong and with Verlaine ambiguous; but the imminence of the First World War surely prevented it. For this occasion, Ruben's self-anthology also integrates a selection of 60 poems by Dario made by Dr. Jorge Eduardo Arellano, which contains enduring poems such as "A Colon", "A Roosevelt", "Retorno" and "Pax". As a novel contribution, the Darian self-anthology that we present today is preceded by an unknown and unpublished manuscript: "Hultzilopox-tli", Aztec god, whose manuscript treasures the Central Bank of Nicaragua in its literary collection, and which will be declaimed in his honor today. The date of writing of the unpublished poem must be placed around 1914. With this publication, the Central Bank of Nicaragua pays tribute to the universal Nicaraguan and makes available to the public a wide selection of Darian poems, to contribute to their dissemination for the benefit, above all, of the new generations. Thanks a lot.

Esta obra se basa en una selecci<97>n que el propio Dar<92>o realiz<97> durante su madurez, en una auto antolog<92>a po<8e>tica publicada por primera vez en la Biblioteca Corona, de Madrid, en tres tomos, titulados: Muy siglo XVIII (1914), Muy antiguo y muy moderno (1915) e Y una sed de ilusiones infinitas (1916). Poco conocida, esta auto antolog<92>a se edit<97> por primera vez en 1967, en el marco del centenario natal de Dar<92>o, con una antolog<92>a complementaria de 30 poemas darianos seleccionados por Pablo Antonio Cuadra y de Eduardo ZepedaHenr<92>quez. Tres veces m<87>s, ya en el siglo XXI fue difundida en Nicaragua por la Fundaci<97>n UNO (Dar<92>o por Dar<92>o) en 2001; en Barcelona por la Editorial Lumen (Y una sed de ilusiones infinita) en 2011 y en M<8e>xico, D.F. por Joaqu<92>n Mortiz (Antolog<92>a personal) en 2013. Al parecer, Dar<92>o planteaba un cuarto tomo, titulado Audaz, cosmopolita, o Con Hugo fuerte y con Verlaine ambiguo; mas la inminencia de la Primera Guerra Mundial seguramente lo impidi<97>. Para esta ocasi<97>n, la auto antolog<92>a de Rub<8e>n adem<87>s integra, una selecci<97>n de 60 poemas de Dar<92>o realizada por el Dr. Jorge Eduardo Arellano, que contiene poemas perdurables como "A Col<97>n", "A Roosevelt<d3>, "Retorno<d3> y "Pax". Como aporte novedoso, la auto antolog<92>a dariana que hoy presentamos est<87> precedida por un manuscrito desconocido e in<8e>dito: "Hultzilopox-tli", dios azteca, cuyo manuscrito atesora el Banco Central de Nicaragua en su colecci<97>n literaria, y que ser<87> declamado en su honor el d<92>a de hoy. La fecha de redacci<97>n del poema in<8e>dito debe ubicarse hacia 1914. Con esta publicaci<97>n, el Banco Central de Nicaragua rinde homenaje al nicarag<9f>ense universal y pone al alcance del p<9c>blico una amplia selecci<97>n de poemas darianos, para contribuir a su difusi<97>n en beneficio, sobre todo, de las nuevas generaciones. Muchas Gracias.

Title: International Seminar: "Developing the country's financial infrastructure: The importance of payment systems" September 29, 2016
text: INTERNATIONAL SEMINAR: "DEVELOPING THE COUNTRY'S FINANCIAL INFRASTRUCTURE: THE IMPORTANCE OF PAYMENT SYSTEMS" SEPTEMBER 29, 2016 29/09/2016 Good morning to all, on behalf of the Central Bank of Nicaragua and on my own behalf, it is a pleasure to welcome you to the International Seminar: "Developing the country's financial infrastructure: the importance of payment systems". I would like to extend a special welcome to our members of the Board of Directors, members of the private sector, public officials, think tanks, students and the media who are with us this morning. I would also like to thank the people who accepted our invitation to participate in this event today, especially our international guests, Ms. Clara Machado of the Bank of the Republic of Colombia; Mr. Enrique Garcia, of the Executive Secretariat of the Central American Monetary Council; Mr. Wagner Fonseca of the Central Bank of Costa Rica; Mr. angel Gonzalez of the Central Bank of the Dominican Republic; and Mr. Eduardo Lerete of the Central Bank of Uruguay. To our foreign guests, please convey our thanks to the presidents of their respective Central Banks for allowing them to share with us their experiences. I also thank our guests from national institutions: Ms. Teresa Montealegre of the Association of Private Banks of Nicaragua: Ms. Elsie Rivas of Unired ACH; Ms. Ana Chamorro from BAC and Mr. Luis Rivas from Banpro, who will also share with us their experiences on this issue. We are on the eve of closing this month of September, where we commemorate our national holidays and also the anniversary of the Central Bank of Nicaragua, which makes it even more propitious to discuss this issue of national and institutional significance. There are many reasons why it is important to ensure proper functioning of the payment system. This system is part of the infrastructure through which money is mobilized in the economy, allowing people to carry out their transactions quickly and safely, therefore, its efficiency entails significant savings. It is also an essential vehicle for the proper implementation of monetary policy. Its soundness is fundamental for the development and stability of the financial system. In addition, it is a key pillar of financial inclusion. Significant developments in payment systems are taking place worldwide, mainly in the field of electronic payments. The high degree of penetration of cellular telephony, new technologies and innovations in payment services and instruments, are creating conditions conducive to people, as never before, having access to innovative means of payment, constituting an obvious opportunity to significantly expand access and use of financial services. At the regional level, several central banks have developed specialized platforms to promote electronic transfers, through internet banking or mobile banking. Changes have also been made to laws and regulatory frameworks to boost financial inclusion. I would venture to say that in the near future, the most impactful innovations in financial terms, with great potential to change the lives of millions of people in the world, will come from payment systems. In Nicaragua there have been significant advances in the payment system in recent years. Thus, the services of electronic channels of banks have proliferated, with various options to make electronic transfers. However, despite these advances, much remains to be done. Hence the importance that we occupy this discussion space to learn about the experience of other countries on different areas of action that allow us a good development of payment systems at the national level. During the morning session of this seminar, we will hear the experiences of various countries in the region that have achieved innovative developments in their payment systems in terms of technology, services, uses and surveillance. For the afternoon session, we will talk about the development of the payment system in our country and we will have the opportunity to reflect on possible lines of action to be developed together during the coming years. I am confident then that today we will have a productive event that will leave us with a rich agenda of experiences and ideas to improve our payment systems. I invite you, then, to make the most of this Seminar. Thanks a lot.

Title: Closing Remarks for the XIV Regional Conference for Central America, Panama and Dominican Republic Antigua, Guatemala, November 18, 2016
text: REMARKS BY THE PRESIDENT OF THE CENTRAL BANK OF NICARAGUA, MR. OVIDIO REYES RAMiREZ, FOR THE CLOSING OF THE XIV REGIONAL CONFERENCE FOR CENTRAL AMERICA, PANAMA AND THE REPUBLIC DOMINICANA ANTIGUA, GUATEMALA, NOVEMBER 18, 2016 18/11/2016 On behalf of the Central American Monetary Council and on my own behalf, I would like to thank President Jimmy Morales for his kindness in facilitating the holding of this event and for having addressed the opening remarks to the Bank of Guatemala, in particular its Acting President, Mr. Sergio Recinos, and to the International Monetary Fund for organizing this Regional Conference. I would also like to thank the speakers, who have shared their vision on various topics of relevance to the region. These conferences provide an opportunity for the exchange of ideas between regional economic authorities and the International Monetary Fund. On this occasion, during these two days, we have addressed different aspects related to global and regional economic developments and the importance of investment in infrastructure to support growth. Also noteworthy was the intervention of the Deputy Managing Director of the International Monetary Fund, Mr. Mitsuhiro Furusawa, on financial inclusion. These issues are relevant to the economic development of our countries. On the subject of integration, it must be recognized that policy actions must be undertaken in conjunction with promoting the dynamism of the private sector. An example of this is in our financial system, where there is an increase in the operations of regional groups. Along with efforts to facilitate and promote integration, we have the challenges of supervision and regulation of financial activity. For the above reason, the Plan of Activities of the Central American Monetary Council for 2017, approved yesterday, contemplates actions aimed at strengthening the surveillance of financial systems and consolidating the Payment Interconnection System. These efforts should be coordinated with the respective regional councils of superintendents and finance ministers of each of our countries. With regard to infrastructure, we must anticipate key requirements in order to prevent its lack from becoming a brake on development. If we want to promote integration, we must pay special attention to all the infrastructure that connects us. Thus, regional initiatives such as the "Master Plan for Investment and Economic Development Projects of the Gulf of Fonseca" deserve to be promoted with the financial support of regional banks. On financial inclusion, it will also be essential to launch programs for its promotion. On the one hand, there is the challenge of increasing the financial education of our population, and on the other, facilitating that technology and new developments in payment systems and financial products are also available to groups usually excluded. Boosting the efforts of integration, infrastructure and financial inclusion, discussed at this Conference, we have no doubt will contribute to strengthening economic growth and regional stability. Once again, I reiterate my gratitude to the Bank of Guatemala for its fine attention and to the IMF for promoting these mutually beneficial conferences. Thanks a lot.

Title: Launch of 1000 cordobas note
text: LAUNCH OF 1000 CoRDOBAS BANKNOTE, WORDS OF THE PRESIDENT OF THE BCN, OVIDIO REYES R" NOVEMBER 22, 2016 22/11/2016 Good morning friends journalists and Nicaraguan people. The Central Bank of Nicaragua announces the issuance of new banknotes of the denomination of 1000 cordobas. This issue is made to supply the demand for banknotes in the economy and make it easier for the public to carry out their transactions in cash. The issuance of a higher denomination banknote will allow the use of fewer banknotes in high-value transactions, derived from the greater demand for circulating. The stability of prices and the period of festivities at the end of the year, are conducive to the issuance of the 1000 cordobas banknote. This issue comprises the following main aspects: 1. The 1000 note has two different designs, which will be put into circulation on the following dates: The first design corresponds to the 1000 cordobas banknote commemorating the centenary of the death of the poet Ruben Dario. This ticket will have a limited issue and will start circulating from December 1, 2016. The second design corresponds to the 1000 cordobas banknote of regular circulation, which completes the issuance of the series of banknotes that began circulating in October 2015. This ticket will start circulating from January 02, 2017. 2. A new denomination of higher value is added to the banknotes that are in circulation, therefore, there will now be seven different denominations: 10.20, 50, 100, 200, 500 and 1000 cordobas. 3. The 1000 cordobas banknote, both the commemorative to the centenary of the death of the poet Ruben Dario and the 2015 series banknote, is printed on paper substrate and is dark green. 4. They have the following dimensions: 161 millimeters wide by 67 high, which implies that it is 5 millimeters longer than the 500 cordobas note. 5. Present the signature of the President of the Central Bank and the Minister of Finance and Public Credit. The design and main security features of the 1000 cordobas banknote commemorating the centenary of the death of the poet Ruben Dario are: the design of this banknote commemorates the 100th anniversary of the death of the poet Ruben Dario, showing on the obverse the portrait of the poet, an image of a daisy flower and a verse of the poem "Pax"; on the reverse, the image of a dove of peace and a verse from the same poem "Pax" are shown. The main security measures are: a security thread with a three-dimensional image that moves when the note is tilted; an ink stamp with dynamic effect, showing a line moving when the banknote is tilted, with the figure of a pen; a watermark with the image of the strawberry tree and the denomination number 1000; and perfect registration with the number 1000. The design and main security features of the 1000 cordobas banknote of the 2015 series are the following: the design of this banknote is allusive to the sovereignty of Nicaragua, highlighting on the obverse the image of the Hacienda San Jacinto and on the reverse to the San Juan River. The main security measures are: on the obverse a security thread with a three-dimensional image that moves when the ticket is tilted; an ink stamp, which changes color from green to blue when you tilt the note; a watermark with the image of the strawberry tree and the denomination number 1000; and perfect registration with the number 1000. On the obverse, a band that shines when tilted with the denomination number crossed vertically. The Central Bank of Nicaragua hopes that, with this new issuance of 1000 cordobas banknotes, the population will carry out its transactions in an agile and safe manner. Thanks a lot.

Title: Presentation of Journal of Economics and Finance, November 24, 2016
text: PRESENTATION OF THE ECONOMY AND FINANCE MAGAZINE, REMARKS BY THE PRESIDENT OF THE BCN, OVIDIO REYES R., NOVEMBER 24, 2016 24/11/2016 Good morning everyone, I would like to warmly welcome our guests, public sector officials, students of the engineering career in economics and business of the National University of Engineering, media and the people who join us this morning in the presentation of the third volume of the Journal of Economics and Finance of the Central Bank of Nicaragua. With this publication and event, the BCN promotes the exchange of knowledge on topics related to economic sciences. This year, in addition to this initiative, we have continued with the publications of Working Papers, we have held an international seminar on payment systems and we also carried out the Economy, Finance and Development contest. In addition, our officials have participated in various international forums of a regional nature, where research is also promoted. In this volume, the Journal of Economics and Finance includes five investigations on very varied topics, such as: financial intermediation, credit growth, tourism, productivity and informality. These investigations were developed by officials of the Central Bank of Nicaragua within the framework of our work agenda. Thus, this morning, we will know from the researchers a summary of the methodology and results of the 5 investigations included in the Journal. The first research: "Financial intermediation conditions and the real economy", as its name implies, builds an index of Financial Intermediation Conditions to measure its impact on the real economy. The researcher concludes that policy measures aimed at boosting looser financial conditions have a positive impact on economic activity, although they could lead to inflationary pressures. The second research: "Expenses and perceptions of tourists about Nicaragua as a tourist destination", analyzes the expenditure made and the willingness to spend more by tourists visiting Nicaragua, while inquiring about the perception of the quality of the country's tourist offer. The third research, "Can growth affect productivity?", presents an alternative theoretical and methodological framework in which the relationship between output and productivity is reversed, with respect to conventional knowledge. The researcher concludes that, in the case of Nicaragua, the null hypothesis of causality relationship from product to productivity cannot be rejected. The fourth research: "Credit growth in Nicaragua: Natural growth or credit boom?", presents an analysis of the evolution of credit in Nicaragua focused on the detection of credit boom for the period 1995-2014. The results conclude that, during the period under study, there has been no credit boom. Instead, sustained credit growth corresponds to economic growth. Finally, the fifth research: "Determinants of informality in Nicaragua", characterizes labor informality in the country, identifying its determinants and proposing policy options for its reduction. The researchers conclude that it is more likely to be informal in the strata with low levels of education, affecting more women, young people and the elderly. Likewise, informality generates lower incomes than formal employment and is concentrated in agricultural and commercial activities. Finally, I thank everyone for their participation in this event. The BCN will continue to promote applied research to quantify and understand the socioeconomic processes that arise in our country and the region. Thanks a lot.

Title: Presentation of results of the Measurement of Poverty and Inequality of the National Living Standards Measurement Survey 2016
text: PRESENTATION OF THE RESULTS OF THE MEASUREMENT OF POVERTY AND INEQUALITY OF THE NATIONAL SURVEY OF MEASUREMENT OF LIVING STANDARDS 2016. REMARKS BY THE PRESIDENT OF THE BCN, CRO. OVID REYES R. 03/07/2017 Good morning fellow representatives of the Government, Diplomatic Corps, public officials, guests and Nicaraguan people who see and hear us through the media. Today we are pleased to present the results of the Measurement of Poverty and Inequality of the National Survey for the Measurement of Living Standards carried out during 2016. Nicaragua has been making significant progress in the economic and social fields. Sustained economic growth has been accompanied by significant progress in social indicators. Different surveys of living standards have been conducted with the World Bank every four years. The last one was held in 2014. To give continuity to this effort with closer series, INIDE, with the technical and financial support of the Central Bank of Nicaragua, carried out a survey of Measurement of the Standard of Living raised in October 2016. The study used the same methodology that has been adopted during all these years and was conducted by the same team of professionals that INIDE has been accompanying the World Bank in previous years. As an overall result, the survey indicates that both Poverty and Inequality continue to decline nationally. General poverty went from 29.6% to 24.9%, while extreme poverty went from 8.3% to 6.9%. The inequality coefficient, known as the Gini coefficient, improved from 0.38 to 0.33. The above result is good news for everyone, and shows that the model adopted and the economic and social policies that are being implemented are achieving their objectives. The sustained improvement in the living standards of our population is demonstrating this. We know that we face a great challenge and that there is still a long way to go. The country needs to improve even more its per capita income, which can be achieved through higher rates of economic growth that allow the generation of employment and the constitution of income for families. The results we are achieving motivate us to continue moving decisively along this path. We thank you all for your presence. The survey and its results will be available to the public on the website of INIDE and the Central Bank of Nicaragua. Thanks a lot.

Title: VI Meeting with Companies "New statistical challenges, utility and perspectives"
text: VI MEETING WITH COMPANIES "NEW STATISTICAL CHALLENGES, USEFULNESS AND PERSPECTIVES". REMARKS BY THE PRESIDENT OF THE BCN, CRO. OVID REYES R. 15/08/2017 Mr. Jose Angel Buitrago, representing the Superior Council of Private Enterprise COSEP, Dear representatives of companies, international organizations, media, Central Bank officials and public servants. Since 2012, the Central Bank of Nicaragua has been holding meetings with companies that provide economic information for the survey of the macroeconomic statistics system. Today we are holding the VI Meeting with Companies, which we have called "New statistical challenges, usefulness and perspectives". Challenges that, with the help of you and Nicaraguan households, will generate updated information useful for the different sectors of the national economy. The statistics of the Central Bank of Nicaragua contribute to the formulation of monetary and exchange rate policy, as well as to the elaboration of economic policy analyses and recommendations. They also serve for business decision-making, market research and proper monitoring of the behavior of the economy. The NCB compiles, through surveys, financial reports of enterprises and reports of public institutions, monetary, financial, exchange rate, balance of payments and national accounts statistics already known to all. It also supports public institutions, in collaboration with the Institute for Information and Development, INIDE, to collect and publish relevant information on the scope of production, employment, prices, consumption and expenditure of households, as well as the population, among others. As part of the Economic Statistics Improvement Program that we released in 2014, the BCN published the reports of the Digital Cartography and the Urban Economic Directory, which includes all 153 municipal capitals. Currently, the NCB is working on two relevant statistical improvement projects: the survey of household income and expenditure and the change of reference year of the System of National Accounts. The development of the Household Income and Expenditure Survey 2017/2018 started in April 2017 and aims to obtain information on the structure of income and expenditure that will redefine a new weighting base for the CPI and an integrated household economic account. For its survey, the BCN will conduct continuous interviews of 8,000 households for a full year. To explain the scope of this survey, Ms. Ernestina Perez will make a presentation emphasizing the use that companies can use it and how the survey connects in the international arena. Ms. Perez is an expert from the Statistics Division of the Commission for Latin America and the Caribbean of ECLAC who is providing technical assistance to the NCB in the methodological and conceptual aspects of the baseline survey. For its part, the Change of Reference Year of the National Accounts that is currently located in 2006, will be updated to 2018, which will entail a measurement effort that will take at least three years to incorporate the new economic activities, cost structures, incomes and added value that now occur in our economy. To explain what the change of reference year consists of, Ms Lisbeth Laguna, Manager of National Accounts of the NCB, will present the progress in the collection of information and the main challenges to be able to complete it. I take this opportunity to greet Ms. Martha Tovar, who is visiting us from the IMF's regional training office in Guatemala, known as CAPTAC-DR, who is providing technical assistance in this process. Finally, we thank you for your support in generating economic statistics for our country. We also thank everyone for their presence, as well as the panelists, hoping that this Meeting will be useful. Good morning.

Title: Signing of the Credit Line Contract with CABEI, Eighth Renewal
text: ACT OF SIGNING THE CREDIT LINE AGREEMENT WITH CABEI, EIGHTH RENEWAL. REMARKS BY THE PRESIDENT OF THE BCN, CRO. OVID REYES R. 01/09/2017 Good afternoon Dr. Silvio Conrado Gomez, Director for Nicaragua before the Central American Bank for Economic Integration (CABEI); CABEI officials accompanying Dr. Conrado; Comrade Sara Amelia Rosales Castellon, General Manager of the Central Bank of Nicaragua; officials of our institution and fellow journalists. We have summoned you to join us in the subscription of the Credit Line granted by CABEI to support the liquidity management of the Central Bank of Nicaragua. Through this Line, CABEI makes available to the BCN up to 200 million dollars as a liquidity assistance line, if required. Eight years ago, CABEI's Board of Executive Directors, in the midst of the international financial crisis of 2007-2008, approved the initiative called "Credit Program to Support the Liquidity Management of the Central Banks of CABEI's Founding Countries," consisting of the provision of contingent financing of 200 million dollars for each of the Central American countries. This Credit Line, which will have a new term of one year, counted from August 21, 2017, constitutes an important precautionary measure that contributes to strengthening the financial safety net, safeguarding financial stability and strengthening the stability of the exchange regime. Over the years, CABEI has established itself as one of the strategic allies of the Government of Nicaragua in the task of promoting sustainable and balanced economic and social development. For this reason, I wish to express my gratitude to Dr. Silvio Conrado, whose work has facilitated Nicaragua's continued strong support from this international financial organization, and I ask him to convey to the Board of Directors and the Executive Presidency of CABEI our gratitude for the renewal of this Credit Line. Thanks a lot

Title: Award Ceremony of the Central Bank of Nicaragua Painting Contest 2017
text: AWARDS PAINTING CONTEST BCN 2017. REMARKS BY THE PRESIDENT OF THE BCN, CRO. OVID REYES R. 12/09/2017 Dear attendees of this ceremony, esteemed artists, art critics, journalists; Friends all: I thank all of you for your presence at this ceremony held especially to formally deliver the Awards of the Painting Contest "Pride of my country", convened this year 2017 by the Central Bank of Nicaragua. It should be recalled on this occasion that, as a public entity, the BCN has maintained, continues to maintain and will always maintain as an important part of its institutional policies, the contribution, in an effective and constructive manner, the promotion and preservation of the most important values that stand out in Nicaraguan society. Among them, Art and Culture. Consequently, for many years now, the NCB has been committed to the systematic and permanent development of its Cultural Programme; in active cooperation and coordination with our Government and national cultural authorities. This has been one of our most important forms of social projection. It is also a fundamental part of our legal powers, but it is also the reflection of our firm will to promote these high values in present and future Nicaragua. As in recent years, in 2017 we call on all national artists residing in the country or abroad to participate in our Painting Contest, this time under the slogan "Pride of my country", as a way to stimulate the theme of the participating works towards pride and promotion of our own values. The technique in which it was convened was as always of free choice. Each artist participates, as every year, with an original and unpublished work, not awarded in other BCN contests. In accordance with the Rules of the contest, the members of the Qualifying Jury met to deliberate, who, after a careful review of the 14 works submitted to the competition, announced their conclusions. The Jury decided to award Second Place to the painting entitled "Comedia Bailete El Gueguense" for recreating the universal work El Gueguense, respecting the technique of the pen combined with other techniques, making a work of dynamic and narrative composition, which proudly reflects our identity as Nicaraguans. The Nicaraguan artist Renal Marcel Montiel was the author of this work. Likewise, the Jury designated the Third Place to the painting entitled "Warrior of Love", a work that according to the Jury stands out for its technical skill, both in the achievement of the character, Salvador Cardenal, icon of national music and defender of the environment, as well as for the expression of the ideals of the artist portrayed; with excellent use of color, cleanliness in the finish and a dynamic composition. The Nicaraguan artist Ledis Osman Gonzalez Flores was the author of this work. Today we are pleased to make the formal presentation of these awards before you. We congratulate the winning artists and thank the participation of the rest of the participating artists who with their participation make this contest one of the most important of our arts nationwide. We take this opportunity to reiterate the commitment of the Central Bank of Nicaragua to the development of Nicaraguan art and culture. Title: Act in celebration of the 38th Anniversary of National Police
text: ACT IN CELEBRATION OF THE 38TH ANNIVERSARY OF THE NATIONAL POLICE WORDS OF THE PRESIDENT OF THE BCN, CRO. Title: International Seminar: "Inclusion and financial education: International experience and challenges in Nicaragua", closing remarks
text: INTERNATIONAL SEMINAR: "INCLUSION AND FINANCIAL EDUCATION: INTERNATIONAL EXPERIENCE AND CHALLENGES IN NICARAGUA", CLOSING REMARKS BY THE PRESIDENT OF THE BCN, CRO. OVID REYES R. 28/09/2017 This has been a very fruitful morning for the exhibitions and interest of the public in this relevant topic such as Inclusion and Financial Education. I want to highlight and thank the international exhibitors for having shared their experience and enlighten us the advances in the subject at hand and the national exhibitors who have shown us the work that has been done from the Financial Services Commission. I also want to thank the people who accompanied us today at this table, Mr. Jose Adan Aguerri, President of COSER, the General Manager of the BCN Mrs. Sara Amelia Rosales, the moderators, the people from the private sector, representatives of organizations, academics, students, think tanks and media who accompanied us. The call and interest in interventions and concerns demonstrates its interest in this type of dialogue and encourages the NCB to continue promoting these rapprochement forums. From the experiences of this morning we learned that there is no single organizational or strategy scheme for financial inclusion and education that is applied in all countries, and that although there is progress in some countries, at the regional level we have a long way to go. We learned that this is not an effort that can be carried out by a single institution, but that achieving results in this area requires an inter-institutional effort that encompasses both the public and private sectors, but also requires decisive action by users. We learned that the involvement of private providers of financial services and education for youth and children is key and that we must direct efforts to incorporate them into our financial inclusion system. In the case of Nicaragua, we saw this afternoon that there are many areas in which we can work together, which include aspects of education, regulation, new instruments of the payment system, among others. While the challenges seem great, it is clear that the benefits contribute to the well-being of the population in general, to the competitiveness of companies, to the deepening of the financial system and to the development of our economy. In this regard, I can only reiterate the BCN's commitment to continue promoting policies and actions aimed at financial inclusion and education. Have a good afternoon. Thanks a lot.

Title: The Art of Nicaraguan Ceramics
text: THE ART OF NICARAGUAN CERAMICS. REMARKS BY THE PRESIDENT OF THE BCN, CRO. OVID REYES R. 29/09/2017 Good afternoon friends present. Dear artists, cultural scholars, BCN officials, journalists and friends all, I appreciate your presence at the inauguration of this beautiful exhibition that we have called "The Art of Nicaraguan Ceramics," which we made to highlight the national ceramics and in particular the one produced in San Juan de Oriente, with which the BCN has been linked for many years. This exhibition is part of the effort that the BCN makes permanently through our Cultural Program. Today, our artisans heirs of all the knowledge and experience bequeathed by our ancestors continue to work with the techniques of their ancestors, but also help with modern techniques and materials to create beautiful and unique decorative and utilitarian pieces. The three artisans who exhibit here now, are originally from San Juan de Oriente, municipality of the department of Masaya, known for its beautiful and useful crafts made of clay; Famous nationally for the originality and multiple shapes of its ceramic pieces. Works by artists such as Jose Ortiz Bracamonte, Helio Gutierrez and Jose Bernardo Carballo are exhibited here. In these ceramic works it is remarkable the variety of forms, including some versions of pre-Columbian art, but also other pieces product of the free creation of the artist. Jose Ortiz Bracamonte is known for having made the integral proposal of formats and color that inspired the book El jaguar y la luna, by the poet Pablo Antonio Cuadra. Few know that as a child he cut coffee on the farms of San Marcos and that outside the harvest season he helped his mother in the artisanal tasks; But he was also a student of technical drawing. His talent surprises and impresses. His achievements are admired by nationals and foreigners. Helio Gutierrez; He grew up watching his mother create functional clay pots. He worked for three years in the ceramics of Gregorio Bracamonte, until he founded his own workshop. Now he makes and models very original pieces, with dynamic and innovative designs, splendid colors, fine decorative finish and exquisite plastic beauty. For his part, Jose Bernardo Carballo began making handmade pieces, with religious, ancestral and environmental motifs. Animal-shaped piggy banks, citadels, church repairs, Noah's arks, chickens, deer and others. In its pieces you can appreciate the beauty and color of our birds, the filigree in the decoration of their plumages, the simplicity of the houses of our villages. We invite you to appreciate the work of these three master craftsmen. The pieces exhibited here today are just part of that chromatic joy that characterizes Nicaraguan craftsmanship today. The works of these artists recover the ancestral permanence of mystery and beauty in our culture. Let's appreciate them, admire them and feel proud to be Nicaraguans. Our most sincere congratulations to our master craftsmen. Thanks a lot

text: AWARD CEREMONY OF THE PRESIDENT OF THE BCN LITERATURE CONTEST. REMARKS BY THE PRESIDENT OF THE BCN, CRO. OVID REYES R. 09/10/2017 Good morning to everyone here. Dear writers and poets, officials of the Central Bank of Nicaragua (BCN), journalists and friends all: As part of its interest in promoting art and literature in Nicaragua, the BCN has permanently implemented its Cultural Program; conceived as one of our most important forms of social projection at the national level. In 2017 we summon, as every year, Nicaraguans interested in enriching and strengthening the literary tradition of the country, to participate in our Maria Teresa Sanchez Literature Contest, which aims to contribute to the dissemination and creation of the literary arts. The genre for this year was Poetry; with free theme, metre and composition form. The authorship of the work corresponded to Danilo Enrique Aguirre Sequeira. Finally, as Third Place was selected the work entitled: "Dark Matter", the beauty of his metaphors was valued in this work, as well as the emotion and intensity of his writings, which take the reader to a kind of journey to the universe. The work corresponded to the author Ornar Ali Moya Garcia. Today we are pleased to make the formal presentation of these awards. We congratulate the winning authors and appreciate the participation of all the writers who with their contributions make this contest a tribute to Nicaraguan letters. We take this opportunity to reiterate here the commitment of the Central Bank of Nicaragua to the development of Nicaraguan art and culture. We thank everyone for their presence at this ceremony and call on the award-winning writers to come and receive their awards. Thanks a lot.

Title: Journal of Economics and Finance 2017
text: JOURNAL OF ECONOMICS AND FINANCE 2017. REMARKS BY THE PRESIDENT OF THE BCN, CRO. OVID REYES R. 27/11/2017 Good morning. I would like to warmly welcome you all to the presentation of Volume 4 of the "Journal of Economics and Finance" 2017 edition. For the Central Bank it is very gratifying to have the presence today of researchers, public officials, representatives of the private sector, students, media, and special guests. With the publication of the fourth Journal of Economics and Finance, the Central Bank of Nicaragua promotes research and dissemination of rigorous studies on issues relevant to the national economy, especially those related to the formulation and implementation of economic policies. The Central Bank of Nicaragua also promotes research through the Economy, Finance and Development Award, which recently won its awards this month. In this volume, the Journal of Economics and Finance includes four investigations on various topics, such as: Mechanisms of transmission of external and internal shocks, Projection and simulation models, Characterization of household income and Determinants of maize crop yield in Nicaragua. These investigations were developed by officials of the Central Bank of Nicaragua within the framework of our research agenda. In this activity we will know from the researchers a summary of the methodology and the results of the four investigations included in the journal. The first research "A medium-scale Bayesian VAR for the Nicaraguan economy" analyzes the advantages of using a large dataset to forecast key variables such as growth and inflation. In addition, through the analysis of impulse response functions, the transmission mechanisms present in the Nicaraguan economy, related to oil price shocks and fiscal expenditure, are analyzed. The analysis provides arguments to debate the short- and long-term position of fiscal policy in Nicaragua. The second research "External shocks and economic cycles in Nicaragua" presents a short-term macroeconometric model, which allows us to appreciate the effects of external shocks on the main macroeconomic variables, especially on GDP, inflation, international reserves and interest rates. The study compares differences in income between urban and rural areas, levels of education, sex of the head of household and socioeconomic levels. Finally, the fourth research "Analysis of the determinants of maize yield in Nicaragua" estimates a linear and a multinomial model of the determinants of maize crop yield, using agricultural surveys. The results suggest that any project aimed at increasing yields should be seen as an integral process to optimize crop management. Finally, I thank everyone present for their participation in this event. Inviting everyone to continue providing contributions with their knowledge and rigorous studies of the national economy. Thanks a lot

Title: Exhibition of Painting Nicaragua Linda, Nicaragua Natural
text: EXHIBITION OF PAINTING NICARAGUA LINDA, NICARAGUA NATURAL. REMARKS BY THE PRESIDENT OF THE BCN, CRO. OVID REYES R. 29/11/2017 I thank everyone for their presence at this event that we call: Nicaragua Linda, Nicaragua Natural, which reveals, once again, the commitment of the Central Bank for the sustained promotion of the artistic and cultural values of Nicaragua. Since 2002, our institution has held 16 painting contests, in homage to twentieth-century masters such as Rodrigo Penalba, Armando Morales, Alejandro Arostegui, Leoncio Saenz, Carlos Montenegro and Roger Perez de la Rocha, among others. Nicaraguans have been delighted with their magnificent works of art that represent a pride of our country. In these calls, new artists have been consecrated. In 2013, Mr. Marcelo Ampie one of the three participants in this exhibition was awarded the oil work "Metaphysical Thinker", an example of a heartbreakingly human portrait. In this exhibition, Mr. Ampie is inspired by social themes of great human content, in portraits masterfully drawn, in objects representative of the daily life of the people and in surprising landscapes of the natural environment of Nicaragua. Today we are summoned, in addition to Ampie, by Mrs. Rosario Ortiz de Chamorro, who starts from nature and transforms it by ordering the severity and purity of its forms. Its static and monumental flowers and fruits invite contemplation. Likewise, subtle graduations of tone, sensuality of his brushstrokes and graphite shading denote his patient craft and skill, merging real and imaginary motifs. For his part, Mr. Mauricio Rizo handles color in his canvases as an ode to nature bathed in twilight or exalted by artificial light. In his landscapes he presents the joy and joy for life in nature, the simplicity and serenity of the peasant house, banana plantations and coffee plantations. Nature constitutes the central character of the three, united by their original contemplation of our tropics, glimpsed through different ways. But with its palettes endowed with vibrant colors that orchestrate diaphanously games of light and shadow, master textures and dazzling visions. Let us appreciate, then, this representative sample of our Nicaragua Linda, Natural Nicaragua, and recognize the persevering work of its executors who are presented today with their paintings to highlight with their strokes the art that accompanies the heritage of Nicaraguans. Thanks a lot

Title: Presentation of Annual Report 2017 to the National Assembly
text: PRESENTATION OF ANNUAL REPORT 2017 TO THE NATIONAL ASSEMBLY PRESIDENT OF THE BCN, CRO. OVID REYES R. 10/04/2018 Good morning comrade Gustavo Porras, President of the National Assembly, comrade Loria Dixon, First Secretary, Members of the Board of Directors, Deputies, invited all. In compliance with Article 32 of Law No. 732, Organic Law of the Central Bank of Nicaragua, I have the honour to present to this plenary the 2017 Annual Report of the Central Bank of Nicaragua (BCN), which was presented on March 28, 2018 to the President of the Republic. The Report has been made available to the public on our institution's website. The Annual Report summarizes the country's economic performance and the BCN's operations during 2017, and summarizes as follows: For the eighth consecutive year, Nicaragua continued to record a positive macroeconomic performance. Economic activity and job creation continued to grow and inflation remained stable. The management of public finances remained prudent, international reserves strengthened, while the financial system remained healthy. The better international context and a good rainfall regime favored the growth of exports, as well as an increase in the flow of family remittances and tourism that contributed to the strengthening of the country's external position. The Gross Domestic Product (GDP) recorded a robust growth of 4.9 percent in 2017, in line with expectations. With this result, Nicaragua has managed to achieve an average growth of 5.2 percent in the period 2010-2017. This sustained pace of economic growth allowed reaching a GDP per capita of 2,161 dollars in 2017 and has favored an improvement in poverty indicators. Economic growth in 2017 was driven by an improvement in net external demand, which offset more moderate growth in domestic absorption. Consistent with the above, primary and industrial activities linked to the export sector experienced the highest growth, stimulated by favorable weather conditions and a recovery in the world economy that increased external demand. On the production side, the impulses came mainly from agriculture, manufacturing and livestock activity. Consistent with the performance of economic activity, the labor market presented positive indicators. The Continuous Household Survey (ECH) recorded a net employment rate of 96.7 percent in the fourth quarter, consistent with an unemployment rate of 3.3 percent. Likewise, underemployment stood at 42.7 percent. While formal employment grew 6.6 percent, registering the greatest dynamism in the affiliation to the INSS the sectors of commerce, hotels and restaurants and communal and personal services. On the other hand, the average nominal wage grew 5.5 percent, resulting in a growth of 1.5 percent in real terms. The favourable results in terms of economic growth and employment took place in a context of price stability. Thus, inflation remained low, reaching an accumulated variation of 5.68 percent, which was associated with the good rainfall regime and low international inflation. For its part, fiscal policy remained prudent, registering a Non-Financial Public Sector deficit of 1.9 percent of GDP, slightly lower than in 2016. Public debt with respect to GDP stood at 47.0 percent, 2.0 percentage points higher than in 2016, as a result of higher external disbursements linked to development projects aimed at increasing the productive capacity of the national economy. The conduct of monetary policy was favoured by the improvement in the external position, which allowed an accumulation of international reserves of 310 million dollars compared to 2016. Thus, at the end of 2017, gross international reserves (RIB) stood at 2,757.8 million dollars, reflecting a coverage of 2.6 times the monetary base and 5.4 months of imports of cif goods. The BCN's monetary policy was more active, seeking to reduce excess reserve requirements in national currency, through its monetary operations with short-term liquidity management instruments. In this way, the volume of bills payable in cordobas increased by 86.0 percent compared to 2016, mainly for placements in installments of 7 and 14 days, and 1 month. The financial sector continued to grow at a good pace, while its regulatory framework was strengthened. The loan portfolio continued to show dynamism, although with a slowdown growth rate (13.8%), while deposits accelerated their growth rate (10.7%). The indicators of the financial system showed a healthy performance in terms of portfolio quality, profitability, capital adequacy, liquidity and non-performing loans. The stability of the financial system continued to be underpinned by the implementation of new macroprudential policies, aimed at consolidating the management of systemic risks, and other changes in the regulatory framework. These policies include the establishment of countercyclical provisions and capital reserves. The current account of the balance of payments continued to reflect a strengthening of the country's external position. Thus, the current account deficit stood at 5.0 percent of GDP, showing a reduction for the second consecutive year. The most important component of the current account continued to be the balance of goods and services, reflecting a reduction in its deficit with respect to GDP, as a result of higher export values, driven especially by the country's good productive performance, and moderate growth in imports. Higher income from remittances and tourism also contributed to the improvement in the external position. The current account deficit improved despite the fact that in 2017 the country's terms of trade ended with a slight deterioration of 2.2 percent. Better international conditions had a positive impact on export prices (0.8%), although the rebound in the prices of oil and its derivatives caused import prices to increase further (3.1%). In this context, the value of merchandise exports totaled 2,548.3 million dollars in 2017, registering a growth of 14.5 percent compared to the value reached in 2016. This performance was mainly determined by higher traded volumes, which provided good dynamism to the economy during the year. On the other hand, free zone exports did not show similar performance, growing 1.0 percent compared to 2016, reaching 2,638.1 million dollars. On the side of cif imports, these amounted to 6,092.3 million dollars in 2017, registering a growth of 3.5 percent. This result was mainly driven by the increase in the oil bill (28.1%), as a result of the higher average price of oil, and by the greater demand for intermediate goods for industry and agriculture. The Nicaraguan economy developed in a favorable environment at the international level. The global economic upturn that began in mid-2016 continued during 2017, and was characterized by widespread and synchronized growth in most economies. The world economy registered a growth of 3.7 percent in 2017 (3.2% in 2016), as a result of the greater dynamism of developed economies, accompanied by an increase in industrial activity, a rebound in international trade and greater consumer confidence. Finally, with respect to the operations of the Central Bank of Nicaragua, in 2017 a result was presented in correspondence with the budget, reflecting the accumulated results of monetary, exchange and financial policies, implemented to preserve the stability of the national currency and the normal development of internal and external payments. The Bank's balance sheet highlights the increase in the balance of gross international reserves (RIB) and the decrease in the MHCP's obligations to the NCB. Likewise, actions related to: (i) the updating of the regulatory framework and automation of the payment system, specifically the Automated Clearing House; (ii) proper management to improve the performance of international reserves, through reform of the IMFN Administration Policy; (ii) the free convertibility of the currency through the operations of the exchange desk, and (iv) the active management of the treasury, including the circulation of a 1,000 cordobas banknote, completing the series of banknotes issued in 2015. Thank you for your attention and I am at your disposal for any inquiries you may wish to make. Thanks a lot

Title: Presentation of the Book Pride of My Country: Beauty of Nicaragua
text: PRESENTATION OF THE BOOK PRIDE OF MY COUNTRY: BEAUTY OF NICARAGUA WORDS OF THE PRESIDENT OF THE BCN, CRO. OVID REYES R. 27/06/2018 The Central Bank of Nicaragua is pleased to present the Illustrated Book Pride of my country: Beauty of Nicaragua, which was prepared from photographs taken during the national campaign that, with the same name, the Government of Nicaragua promoted since 2015 and in which elements of our Nicaraguanness were highlighted. This campaign sought to raise national pride and serve as a catalyst for our values for the promotion of good living and tourism. The original idea was to develop a book with an immediate content to identify and photographs easy to remember, both for those who already knew our country and for tourists, who should easily locate all its content, from a tour of our country. Thus, they are shown through beautiful photographs and brief but enlightening notes, our welcoming cities, tourist attractions often unique in their kind, religious temples of all denominations, suggestive folkloric manifestations, splendid crafts, succulent gastronomy, economic progress, great people of culture and sport and picturesque national celebrations. The book thus contains a journey of the whole of Nicaragua, with wide cultural, religious and artistic diversity, with an enviable potential for economic development and a population prospering and rejoicing in its achievements and future. We never imagined that this book would be presented at a difficult and painful time for our country. That Nicaragua that appears in these photographs has changed. The economy has been disrupted and some sites no longer look like in the photographs because they have been destroyed, damaging the cultural heritage of the Nation, particularly in the cities of Granada, Leon and Masaya. However, we have realized that the Book is of revealing importance because it serves as a photographic memory to recall the progress and beauty that we have been achieving in recent years and that is possible and we are obliged and in time to recover. Other aspects highlighted in the book maintain their value. The folkloric elements, gastronomic, crafts, celebrations, characters, temples and tourist sites continue in force, becoming an obligatory source of consultation for those who intend to know and remember Nicaragua. The book Pride of my Country is the contribution of public institutions to the promotion of our nationality and our patriotic pride, but also a way to show our joy of belonging to a small, beautiful, open and generous country. So let's enjoy this book to learn more about our culture and our pride in belonging to it. Thanks a lot.

Title: Opening of the Exhibition of Nicaraguan Folk Costumes
text: INAUGURATION OF THE EXHIBITION OF NICARAGUAN FOLKLORIC COSTUMES WORDS OF THE PRESIDENT OF THE BCN, CRO. OVID REYES R. 08/08/2018 In greeting to the patron saint festivities of Managua, whose oldest documentary reference dates back to 1845, the Central Bank of Nicaragua has organized a representative and identity exhibition. Representative because it offers a sample, never before performed, of the costumes that in the three regions of the country have been used in their dances for many years. And identity because they refer to that traditional expression rooted in our people and that expresses our most intimate joy and regional collective personality. I will not make a detailed description of these costumes, consistent with the theme, music and choreography of our most diverse dances or dances. I will limit myself to saying that, without them, without that typical clothing of women and men, with their ornaments and masks, the grace that characterizes our popular dances of the Pacific would diminish: that of the Mestizaje or Inditas, the Negras danced by men, the Gypsies or Hungarians, the Old and the Old, among others. The North-Central area, with its own characteristics, is also admired in this wide exhibition for its sobriety, as well as the colorful costumes of the Palo de Mayo, of British origin, but assimilated and recreated impetuously by the Afro-descendant population of Bluefields since the nineteenth century. Finally, three are the elements that represent these costumes: the primitive background of our indigenous ancestors, the elegant body language inherited from Europe and the rhythmic frenzy provided by Africa. Thanks a lot.
