Title: Presentation of the Annual Report 2018 at the National Assembly
text: PRESENTATION OF THE 2018 ANNUAL REPORT IN THE NATIONAL ASSEMBLY PRESIDENT OF THE BCN, CRO. OVID REYES R. 09/04/2019 Good morning Cro. Gustavo Porras, President of the Honorable National Assembly, members of the Board of Directors, Deputies, media, invited all. In compliance with Article 32 of Law No. 732, Organic Law of the Central Bank of Nicaragua, the Central Bank presented the 2018 Annual Report to the President of the Republic on March 29, 2019; and has been made available to the public on the website of our institution. This Annual Report summarizes the country's economic performance during 2018, which is summarized as follows: In 2018, Nicaragua experienced a series of socio-political events that affected various sectors of the economy, altering the trend of economic growth that had been observed since 2010, which was reflected in effects on economic activity estimated at 1,453.3 million dollars, reduction of employment until the third quarter in 154,512 workers and 139,918 additional who left the labor force. Additionally, damage to infrastructure was quantified for 204.6 million dollars. Despite the above, the macroeconomic consolidation achieved in recent years made it possible to face these developments from a position of relative economic and financial strength: greater diversification in the real sector, adequate level of international reserves, public finances characterized by low fiscal deficits, sustainable public debt ratios, and a healthy financial system, liquid and capitalized. The economic authorities took a number of coordinated measures to preserve economic stability. Thus, the Central Bank of Nicaragua (BCN) complemented the monetary policy conduct scheme with the introduction of daily monetary operations of absorption and injection of liquidity, made the legal reserve policy more flexible and simplified its line of financial assistance, among other measures. For its part, the Government carried out a reform to the General Budget of the Republic (PGR2018) aimed at safeguarding fiscal sustainability, the Superintendency of Banks and Other Financial Institutions (SIBOIF) issued the debtor relief rule, the Financial Stability Committee was created and the legal framework for the issuance of bonds to strengthen financial soundness, among others. These policies made it possible to preserve macroeconomic stability in key aspects such as exchange rate convertibility, financial stability and the proper functioning of payment systems. In this context, after a positive first quarter that pointed to the continuity of a good year in economic and social matters, during 2018, some activities were negatively affected, among them Hotels and Restaurants (-20.2%), Construction (-15.7%), Commerce (-11.4%), Livestock (-5.4%), Financial Intermediation (-5.4%) and Transport and Communications (-3.5%). Other activities showed good dynamism, such as: Fisheries and Aquaculture (14.7%), Agriculture (3.3%) and Mining (1.7%). However, in the aggregate, the Gross Domestic Product (GDP) registered a reduction of 3.8 percent, which imposed a brake on the average growth achieved in the period between 2010 and 2017 (5.1%). From the point of view of aggregate demand, domestic demand was the one that most felt the effects of the reduction in economic activity, with a decrease in gross capital formation (-23.6%) and consumption (-4.5%). On the other hand, external demand reflected a lower dynamism of exports (-2.6%) and the adjustment in import demand (-14%). The decline in economic activity had a significant impact on employment. The Continuous Household Survey (ECH) reflected an increase in the open unemployment rate that reached 6.2 percent in the third quarter (3.3% in the fourth quarter of 2017) and a reduction in the global labor participation rate that stood at 70.3 percent in the third quarter (73.0 percent in the third quarter of 2017). While the active insured to the Nicaraguan Institute of Social Security (INSS) totaled 755,874 workers, which represented a year-on-year reduction of 17.3 percent, equivalent to 157,923 fewer affiliates. The main reductions in insured persons were in trade (-69,318), communal, social and personal services (-36,590) and financial services (-16,266). The results in terms of economic activity and employment were presented in an environment of low inflation, despite the fact that between the months of May and July free movement was obstructed, which partially affected the production and supply of distribution centers. Inflation in 2018 stood at 3.89 percent (5.68% in 2017), a result that was mainly determined by lower prices in the food division given the favorable rainfall regime and low international inflation. Public finances were tightened by the negative impact on Non-Financial Public Sector (NFPS) revenues, so fiscal policy was tightened, reflecting a prudent approach to cost containment. In this context, the NFPS deficit after grants stood at 4.1 percent of GDP (2.0 percent of GDP in 2017), and public borrowing at 52.5 percent of GDP (46.9 percent of GDP in 2017). For its part, monetary policy was active, developing amid increased demand for liquidity and a reduction in monetary aggregates. Banks, as a precaution, increased their cash requirements, both in domestic and foreign currency. In addition, there was a use of government resources in the BCN. The above elements were reflected in net foreign exchange sales by the NCB to the financial system and decumulation of international reserves. However, at the end of 2018, gross international reserves (RIB) stood at 2,261.1 million dollars, reflecting a stability in the coverage indicators that represented 2.43 times the monetary base and 5.2 months of imports of CIF goods. The financial sector was stressed. Thus, deposits showed a reduction of 20.7 percent, while the loan portfolio registered a decrease of 9.2 percent year-on-year. However, liquidity indicators strengthened, while solvency and capitalization indicators continued to reflect levels above legal requirements. The adverse scenario suffered by the economy resulted in the reduction of some external flows such as tourism (-41.1%) and Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) (-63.2%). Thus, the current account of the balance of payments recorded a surplus of 0.6 per cent of GDP, a fact that had not been recorded in many years. This was mainly due to the effect of the reduction in import demand, coupled with the good performance of free zone exports, as well as the continued dynamism of remittance flows (7.9%). The value of total exports, including goods and free zones, reflected a growth of 3.9 per cent. percent with respect to total exports in 2017. This is mainly explained by the increase of free zone exports that registered a year-on-year growth of 8.8 percent (1.0% in 2017), while merchandise exports showed a reduction of 1.2 percent (14.5% in 2017), due to the fact that the effect of lower international prices on the value of exports could not be compensated in volume. Regarding imports, these reflected a reduction of 8.5 percent compared to 2017. The lower inflow of imports was due to a decline in domestic demand, which was reflected in lower purchases of capital goods, intermediate goods and consumer goods. This was presented despite the increase in the oil bill of 12.7 percent compared to 2017. The value of the invoice was affected by the largest purchases of crude oil, mainly due to an increase in the price, while the imported volume decreased. From the point of view of the international context, the Nicaraguan economy developed in a mixed environment. The global economic upturn that began in mid-2016 continued during 2018, although less vigorously than that observed in 2017. The world economy recorded 2018 Annual Report 3.7 percent growth in 2018 (3.8 percent in 2017), as a result of the good performance of both developed and emerging economies, although with a downward trend from the third quarter, mainly in the European and Asian economies. However, the terms of trade were negative, presenting a reduction of 8.2 percent. Finally, with respect to the operations of the Central Bank of Nicaragua, in 2018 a result was presented in correspondence with the elements of the monetary, exchange rate and financial policies implemented. The Bank's balance sheet highlights the decrease in the balance of gross international reserves (RIB) and the MHCP's obligations to the BCN, the disbursement received from the Central American Bank for Economic Integration (CABEI) and the liquidity-injection operations to the national financial system through the monetary reporting instrument. Also noteworthy is the increase in the return on investments of international reserves and the cash management of the Bank's Treasury. Thank you for your attention and I am at your disposal, Thank you very much. President of the National Assembly, Gustavo Porras We are going to give the clarifying questions, we have three deputies listed, we close with Deputy Walmaro Gutierrez Mercado. We give the floor to Deputy Alfredo Cesar Aguirre. Deputy Alfredo Cesar Aguirre Thank you, I had to preside over the Central Bank at a time of shortage of foreign currency like the one the country is currently experiencing. In the year 81, the country was governed by the Government Board of National Reconstruction and had begun to impose the first economic sanctions by the Republican government of President Ronald Reagan, little similar to what is happening now with the first sanctions that have been received by the Republican government of President Donald Trump. And I had to live through very difficult times because when currencies are scarce, the situation at the head of the Central Bank becomes very critical. In the report that we are receiving today, from the President of the Bank, Dr. Ovidio Reyes, it demonstrates several things that have been sustained during this first year of generalized crisis, including low inflation, a stable price of the currency, there have been no devaluations, more than the usual 5% per year that is already warned and that we have already been applying it in Nicaragua for a good number of years. That regime has not changed. But logically where the broken dishes of the crisis and sanctions have been paid is in the level of reserves of the Central Bank, that is, the amount of foreign currency that the country has to meet all its import needs for payment of external debt and other needs in services. In one year, the Central Bank has lost half of its Net International Reserves, I speak of the Netas, because, perhaps it is easier to understand for the ordinary citizen who is not specialists in these issues. The Net International Reserves are really the amount of foreign currency that belongs to the Central Bank and that can make use of them, because in the Gross International Reserves there is an additional amount of foreign currency that does not belong to the Central Bank and therefore cannot make use of them. It is easier for the ordinary ordinary citizen who does not have that specialty to talk about the Net International Reserves, which I repeat, is really the amount of foreign currency that the Central Bank has to meet the needs of the country. And in a year basically rounding up figures, Net International Reserves went from 2 billion to 1,000 million, which is what we currently have. And that did not happen, so that we have an idea of the magnitude of this fall, this did not happen since back in 2010, to have a level of net international reserves close to 1,000 million dollars instead of the two thousand that we had a year ago and, therefore, causes the first concern to which the first question refers and that is the following. It is public knowledge, and today it is indicated by the Annual Report of 2018, that the Central Bank, of that decrease of approximately 1,000 million in one year provided foreign currency to commercial banks, 840 of the 1,000 million, that is, the bulk, 843 to make specific according to the report, millions of dollars the Central Bank provided to commercial banks so that in turn commercial banks could face the Massive withdrawal of deposits from the public, which already totals more than 1,700 million dollars withdrawn by the public in its deposits in private commercial banks. And of those 1,700 withdrawals, I repeat 843, practically half were provided by the Central Bank, that is, they cause the main reason for the decrease in Net International Reserves, in supplying private commercial banks with those currencies to face the withdrawal of deposits. The question is: given that we are about to start the second year of economic crisis and realistic indicators indicate that deposits continue to and will continue to leave the public, therefore, Net International Reserves will continue to fall. What action does the Central Bank have prepared to avoid that in a few months we will not even have foreign currency to import the basics that the country needs? and it has to be linked in some way, an action linked to continuing to provide foreign currency to commercial banks that continue to face the outflow of deposits from the public. What action does the Central Bank plan in the coming months, days before entering the second year of open economic crisis and that sanctions continue the same to prevent us from running out of foreign currency for the fundamental causes that must be imported? The second, very briefly, has to do with the concern of the agricultural cycle that we are also about to start in Nicaragua. Private banks have faced the withdrawal of deposits from the public, decreasing credit, that is also public. The credit available to the productive sectors has been drastically reduced because banks preserve what they receive in customer payments and other income in order to have enough cash and satisfy any customers who withdraw their deposit. It is a logical defensive action of a private bank. But of course, the damage or the broken dishes in this case comes in the drastic decrease in credit to the productive sectors and I am particularly referring to the agricultural cycle that is already going to begin. Second and last question. What actions does the Central Bank plan to achieve at least some degree of financing for the new agricultural cycle that is presented and we do not have an agricultural cycle in the coming months that really depresses perhaps the only sector that so far has been less affected by the political and social crisis and, In particular, let us remember that a primary aspect for the life of all Nicaraguans is what is produced in the countryside and the financing of those producers is essential. Thank you. President of the National Assembly, Gustavo Porras We give the floor to Mr Douglas Aleman. Deputy Douglas Aleman Thank you, President. Well, what is usually referred to here as a political crisis was the period of the attempted coup d'etat that provoked a political crisis in the country. I remember when the so-called dialogue show was made last year, having seen the President of the Central Bank warning the opposition sectors involved in this attempt, warning them of the damage that this could cause and that it was already causing to the economy. I remember seeing and hearing the President of the Central Bank announce when we were already going for at least 2% of the growth that was expected. There were those who said that it was a cost they were willing to pay, the truth is that the cost has been paid by all Nicaraguans. I want to congratulate the Central Bank for the sound management it has made of the Nicaraguan economy over the past 11 years. A healthy management that has allowed us to maintain a stable exchange rate parity, an acceptable level of inflation and economic growth that has been an example in Latin America. I even dare say that the Central Bank also showed excellent capabilities in making a healthy management of the economy in times of crisis. I congratulate Ovid because if you have not done that management of the economy at that time, we would really be in an irreversible economic crisis. The International Reserves that were precisely increased in the time of fat cows really served us to face the crisis at a time when the cow was not that it was skinny but that they were wanting to kill it, which was the economy. Agricultural producers, much is said about this issue on all sides of the agricultural cycle, agricultural producers do not dismantle our work and that is why you saw last year that despite the crisis caused despite the internal obstacles to trade such as the barricades, agricultural activity was maintained and producers logically kept making an effort. Don't worry about financing the agricultural sector for this agricultural cycle because we've never had it. Private banking is not going to take away what it has never given us. Livestock has not been able to finance more than 2.3% of its portfolio. Therefore, do not worry, we are not going to stop producing because private banks do not lend to us, because we have not stopped doing so in all these years despite that absence of credit. The agricultural sector and the livestock sector are going to guarantee the feeding of our people, logically we are facing difficulties, but we come from a sector that is noble, is persevering, and we are going to see at the end of the year presenting positive figures of growth in the production of beans, corn, rice, meat and milk, Because we agricultural producers assume this responsibility of feeding our people seriously and efficiently. Thank you very much, President. President of the National Assembly, Gustavo Porras Thank you, we close the questions in the order of the floor with Mr Walmaro Gutierrez Mercado. Deputy Walmaro Gutierrez Thank you very much, Mr President, good morning, ladies and sisters. Good morning Nicaraguan people who follow the parliamentary debates in this National Assembly and to whom all the deputies owe ourselves as directly elected by the popular vote of the Nicaraguan people. And it is to that Nicaraguan people that we must address today, because now that we receive the Central Bank Report, obviously within the characteristics and technicality that corresponds to a financial and monetary entity such as the Central Bank, there are many elements of that Report that for the bulk of the Nicaraguan population is indigestible. it is incomprehensible, and I think it is imperative, that from this report, we subtract some elements that are important for the people of Nicaragua to assimilate and understand. First of all, this is not a Report to celebrate, it is not a Report to celebrate. Reports to celebrate were those that from 2008 to 2017, were presented on the state of the national economy, where Nicaraguans got used to growing an average of 5% per year and where we reduced poverty and extreme poverty rates as no government in the 153 years of republican history could do, those were Reports to celebrate! Today we are facing a report that reflects a harsh reality of what was the true objective of the coup attempt, which thank God the Nicaraguans were able to overcome, and that with the efforts of the Government of Reconciliation and National Unity, including in the current dialogue table, The conditions are being created to restore the fundamental right of Nicaraguans, which is to live in peace. When we lived in peace we were able to reduce poverty, we were able to generate employment, we were able to generate the best living conditions that Nicaraguans can remember in these last 153 years of republican history. However, today, we are facing a report that instead of informing us that we are growing at that rate of 4.8%, 5% annual average, is telling us that we had a negative growth of 3.8%, what does that mean for Nicaraguans? It means a sensitive, noticeable reduction in the well-being of the Nicaraguan family, in fewer resources, fewer resources to guarantee the restitution of the right to education, more children in our schools, more young people in secondary schools and universities, greater health care, greater investment in infrastructure to be more competitive. Those things did not happen as a consequence of the failed coup attempt, that is the reality that tells us, that means not having grown or grew negatively by 3.8%. And it still resonates in my ears because even Ovid was at that dialogue table, which was a real farce at that time, when the representatives of my government, came to say gentlemen to dialogue, but let's not affect the economy, because we are affecting the poorest in this country. They are wrong to think that a government or a President is the one they are affecting. Nicaragua already deserves a better political class, it is not through destroying the country that we are going to strengthen democracy. However, voices were raised so impertinent and obtuse that they came to say that what the Central Bank is presenting today is an economic cost that we were going to pay and that we Nicaraguans were willing to pay. And I ask the people of Nicaragua, are we really willing to pay for this barbarity that a few did? And that is why we have to take the lesson, here in this country, Peace and Dialogue is the only way to restore the right of Nicaraguans to live in well-being, to live in a better country, it is not through destruction. Gentlemen, what can we expect?, because it is important that we know: what can we expect when damage was caused to institutions so important to this country; only in infrastructure to the INSS 2.6 million dollars, to MIFAMILIA 1 million dollars, to MINED 229 thousand dollars, to the mayors 147.7 million dollars, to ENATREL 1.6 million dollars, to MTI 39.6 million dollars, to the National Police 5.7 million dollars, in other words, 204 million dollars in damages to the people of Nicaragua. Do you know what this represents according to the data of our General Budget of the Republic? Almost 28% of the annual public investment plan of 2018 in destruction, in burning of mayors, in destruction of hospitals, health centers, roads, roads to get production. That was the result, only the poorest in this country were affected. And that is why the people of Nicaragua, although they are peace-loving and committed to peace, do not forget. That is important that we have in our heads, because we cannot forget, because we have to take this lesson and to say never again, it is not possible, that sheltered in a blue and white flag, or using a blue and white flag of mountain passes, we are going to commit crimes and disrupt public goods that cost the Nicaraguan people so much sweat and tears. Un manejo sano que nos ha permitido mantener una paridad cambiar<92>a estable, un nivel de inflaci<97>n aceptable y un crecimiento econ<97>mico que ha sido un ejemplo en Am<8e>rica Latina. Incluso me atrevo a decir que tambi<8e>n el Banco Central dio muestras de excelentes capacidades al hacer un manejo sano de la econom<92>a en momentos de crisis. Lo felicito Ovidio porque si ustedes no han hecho ese manejo de la econom<92>a en esos momentos, realmente estuvi<8e>ramos en una crisis econ<97>mica irreversible. Las Reservas Internacionales que precisamente se vinieron aumentando en la <8e>poca de vacas gordas nos sirvieron realmente para hacer frente a la crisis en un momento en que la vaca no es que estaba flaca sino en que la estaban queriendo matar, que era la econom<92>a. Los productores agropecuarios, mucho se habla de este tema por todos lados del ciclo agr<92>cola, los productores agropecuarios no desmontamos nuestro trabajo y es por eso que ustedes vieron el a<96>o pasado que a pesar de la crisis provocada a pesar de los obst<87>culos internos al comercio como fueron los tranques, la actividad agropecuaria se mantuvo y los productores l<97>gicamente nos mantuvimos haciendo esfuerzo. No se preocupen por el financiamiento al sector agropecuario para este ciclo agr<92>cola porque nunca lo hemos tenido. La banca privada no nos va quitar lo que nunca nos ha dado. A la ganader<92>a no ha sido capaz de financiarle m<87>s del 2.3% de su cartera. Por lo tanto, no se preocupen, que nosotros no vamos a dejar de producir porque la banca privada no nos preste, porque no lo hemos dejado de hacer en todos estos a<96>os a pesar de esa ausencia de cr<8e>dito. El sector agr<92>cola y el sector ganadero vamos a garantizar la alimentaci<97>n de nuestro pueblo, l<97>gicamente estamos enfrentando dificultades, pero venimos de un sector que es noble, es perseverante, y nos vamos a ver al fin de a<96>o presentando cifras positivas de crecimiento en la producci<97>n de frijoles, de ma<92>z, de arroz, de carne y de leche, porque esa responsabilidad de alimentar a nuestro pueblo los productores agropecuarios la asumimos con seriedad y eficiencia. Muchas Gracias Presidente. Presidente de la Asamblea Nacional, Gustavo Porras Gracias, cerramos las preguntas en el orden de la palabra con el diputado W<87>lmaro Guti<8e>rrez Mercado. Diputado W<87>lmaro Guti<8e>rrez Muchas Gracias Sr. Presidente, muy buenos d<92>as, hermanas y hermanos diputadas y diputados. Buenos d<92>as pueblo nicarag<9f>ense que sigue los debates parlamentarios en esta Asamblea Nacional y al cual todos los diputados y diputadas nos debemos como electos directamente por el voto popular del pueblo nicarag<9f>ense. Y es a ese pueblo nicarag<9f>ense al que nosotros debemos de dirigirnos el d<92>a de hoy, porque ahora que nosotros recibimos el Informe del Banco Central, obviamente dentro de las caracter<92>sticas y el tecnicismo que le corresponde a una entidad financiera y monetaria como el Banco Central, hay muchos elementos de ese Informe que para el grueso de la poblaci<97>n nicarag<9f>ense es poco digerible, es poco entendible, y creo que es imperativo, que de ese informe, nosotros sustraigamos algunos elementos que son importantes que el pueblo de Nicaragua asimile y entienda. En primer lugar, este no es un Informe para celebrar, no es un Informe para celebrar. Informes para celebrar fueron los que desde el a<96>o 2008 y hasta el 2017, se presentaron sobre el estado de la econom<92>a nacional, donde los nicarag<9f>enses nos acostumbramos a crecer un promedio del 5% anual y donde redujimos las tasas de pobreza y pobreza extrema como ning<9c>n gobierno en los 153 a<96>os de historia republicana pudieron hacer, <c1>esos eran Informes para celebrar <c1>. El d<92>a de hoy estamos frente a un Informe que nos refleja una realidad cruda de lo que fue el verdadero objetivo del intento de golpe de estado, que gracias a Dios las y los nicarag<9f>enses pudimos superar, y que con los esfuerzos del Gobierno de Reconciliaci<97>n y Unidad Nacional, incluso en la actual mesa de di<87>logo, se est<87>n creando las condiciones para restituir el derecho fundamental de las y los nicarag<9f>enses que es vivir en paz. Cuando nosotros viv<92>amos en paz pudimos reducir pobreza, pudimos generar empleo, pudimos generar las mejores condiciones de vida que el nicarag<9f>ense puede recordar en estos <9c>ltimos 153 a<96>os de historia republicana. Sin embargo, el d<92>a de hoy, estamos frente a un Informe que en vez de informarnos que estamos creciendo a esa tasa de 4.8%, 5% promedio anual, nos est<87> diciendo que tuvimos un crecimiento negativo del 3.8%, <c0>Qu<8e> significa eso para las y los nicarag<9f>enses? significa una reducci<97>n sensible, sensible, en el bienestar de la familia nicarag<9f>ense, en menos recursos, menos recursos para garantizar la restituci<97>n del derecho a la educaci<97>n, m<87>s ni<96>os en nuestras escuelas, m<87>s j<97>venes en las escuelas secundarias y universidades, mayor atenci<97>n en salud, mayor inversi<97>n en infraestructura para ser m<87>s competitivo. Esas cosas no se dieron como consecuencia del intento fallido de golpe de estado, esa es la realidad que nos dice, eso significa no haber crecido o crecido negativamente en un 3.8%. Y todav<92>a me resuena en los o<92>dos porque incluso hasta Ovidio estuvo en esa mesa de di<87>logo, que fue un verdadero sainete en ese momento, cuando los personeros de mi Gobierno, llegaban a decir se<96>ores dialoguemos, pero no afectemos la econom<92>a, porque estamos afectando a los m<87>s pobres de este pa<92>s. Se equivocan pensando de que a un Gobierno o a un Presidente es al que est<87>n afectando. Ya Nicaragua merece una mejor clase pol<92>tica, no es a trav<8e>s de destruir al pa<92>s que vamos a fortalecer la democracia. Sin embargo, se alzaron voces tan impertinentes y obtusas que llegaron a decir que esto que est<87> presentando el Banco Central el d<92>a de hoy es un costo econ<97>mico que <92>bamos pagar y que est<87>bamos dispuestos a pagar las y los nicarag<9f>enses. Y le pregunto al pueblo de Nicaragua, <c0>Realmente nosotros estamos dispuestos a pagar por esta barbaridad que hicieron unos cuantos? Me parece que no. Y es por eso que tenemos que tomar la lecci<97>n, aqu<92> en este pa<92>s, la Paz y el Di<87>logo es el <9c>nico camino para restituir el derecho de las y los nicarag<9f>enses a vivir en bienestar, a vivir en un pa<92>s mejor, no es a trav<8e>s de la destrucci<97>n. Se<96>ores, <c0>qu<8e> podemos esperar nosotros?, porque es importante que lo sepamos: qu<8e> podemos esperar cuando se propiciaron da<96>os a instituciones tan importantes para este pa<92>s; solo en infraestructura al INSS 2.6 millones de d<97>lares, a MIFAMILIA 1 mill<97>n de d<97>lares, al MINED 229 mil d<97>lares, a las alcald<92>as 147.7 millones de d<97>lares, a ENATREL 1.6 millones de d<97>lares, al MTI 39.6 millones de d<97>lares, a la Polic<92>a Nacional 5.7 millones de d<97>lares, en otras palabras, 204 millones de d<97>lares en da<96>os al pueblo de Nicaragua. <c0>Saben que representa esto seg<9c>n los datos de nuestro Presupuesto General de la Rep<9c>blica? Casi el 28% del plan de inversi<97>n p<9c>blica anual del a<96>o 2018 en destrucci<97>n, en quema de alcald<92>as, en destrucci<97>n de hospitales, de centros de salud, de carreteras, de caminos para sacar la producci<97>n. Ese fue el resultado, s<97>lo se afect<97> a los m<87>s pobres de este pa<92>s. Y es por eso que el pueblo de Nicaragua, aunque es amante de la paz y est<87> comprometido con la paz, no olvida. Eso es importante que lo tengamos en la cabeza, porque no podemos olvidar, porque nosotros tenemos que tomar esta lecci<97>n y a decir nunca m<87>s, no es posible, que cobijados en una bandera azul y blanco, o utilizando una bandera azul y blanco de pasa monta<96>a, nosotros vayamos a cometer delitos y a desbaratar bienes p<9c>blicos que tanto sudor y l<87>grimas le cuesta al pueblo nicarag<9f>ense. Porque esas alcald<92>as, esos centros de salud, esas escuelas, esas carreteras, esos caminos, todo lo que se destruy<97> no es consecuencia del dinero del bolsillo de un mandatario, es de los impuestos que todos y todas las nicarag<9f>enses pagamos para tener un pa<92>s mejor. Por eso, lamentamos los resultados de este Informe. Lamentamos la situaci<97>n de hechos en materia econ<97>mica que nos han impuesto. Pero y empero aqu<92> esta es una lecci<97>n que el pueblo nicarag<9f>ense est<87> pagando caro pero que tambi<8e>n no olvidar<87>, y ah<92> es donde nosotros tenemos que revertir r<87>pidamente esto. Y qui<8e>n lo puede hacer, solamente el <9c>nico Gobierno que pudo reducir pobreza a los niveles que redujimos pobreza, que fue el Gobierno del Frente Sandinista de Liberaci<97>n Nacional que tiene un compromiso con los pobres en este pa<92>s, y que vamos a seguir trabajando por mejorar las condiciones de vida de la poblaci<97>n nicarag<9f>ense independiente del distingo, del color pol<92>tico ideol<97>gico que tengan. Porque la pobreza no distingue, porque cuando la pobreza patea las puertas de los hogares nicarag<9f>enses y les ense<96>a los dientes y las garras, no anda pregunt<87>ndole que si es Liberal, que si es Sandinista, Conservador o que si no tiene ning<9c>n partido pol<92>tico. Es al pueblo nicarag<9f>ense al que el Frente Sandinista se debe. Por lo tanto, hoy no es un motivo de celebraci<97>n, pero s<92> es un motivo de compromiso. Primero, no pudieron, ni podr<87>n, y segundo que este estado de cosas el Frente Sandinista de Liberaci<97>n Nacional lo va a revertir porque es un compromiso que tiene con el pueblo de Nicaragua. Muchas gracias Se<96>or Presidente. Presidente de la Asamblea Nacional, Gustavo Porras Gracias. <c0>Si tiene bien a responder Ovidio? Presidente del BCN, Ovidio Reyes R. Muchas Gracias Presidente. Me gustar<92>a referirme a los temas que aqu<92> se han expuesto. Primero, con respecto al tema econ<97>mico. En el Informe nosotros explicamos que la econom<92>a si bien recibi<97> un impacto en el segundo trimestre del a<96>o 2018, el an<87>lisis nuestro m<87>s bien era <c0>qu<8e> pasa despu<8e>s? Porque el impacto estaba dado y fue severo, fue grande. Y en el an<87>lisis de qu<8e> pasa despu<8e>s nos hemos encontrado que hay dos sectores de la econom<92>a que continuaron creciendo que es el sector primario y el sector secundario. <c0>Qu<8e> son estos sectores? La agricultura, la pesca, la miner<92>a, la manufactura, principalmente, motivado por el dinamismo de las exportaciones. Y es el sector terciario o el sector de bienes de servicios; el sector de hoteles, restaurantes, comercio, comunicaciones y servicios financieros, el que est<87> en mayor depresi<97>n. Consecuente a eso tambi<8e>n, y como hab<92>a un problema en el Sistema Financiero, es que frente al Shock las personas decidieron retirar dep<97>sitos, pero otras decidieron usar sus dep<97>sitos debido a que el cr<8e>dito se contuvo, despu<8e>s de todo los ahorros son para eso, para usarlos en malos momentos, entonces hab<92>a un componente tambi<8e>n de uso de los ahorros, entonces el Banco Central procedi<97>, en pol<92>tica coordinada con el resto de instituciones p<9c>blicas, tambi<8e>n a facilitar los ahorros y el uso de los mismos que el pa<92>s hab<92>a acumulado durante los a<96>os de bonanza. Y ten<92>amos cerca de 3,000 millones de d<97>lares cuando la crisis comenz<97>, en reservas l<92>quidas. Quiero aclarar que para nosotros el tema de la liquidez es principal y nosotros pensamos en ese momento que ten<92>amos que proveer liquidez al Sistema Financiero, porque de lo contrario pod<92>a venir una par<87>lisis general en la econom<92>a. Y lo hicimos. Desarrollamos Reportos Monetarios; que b<87>sicamente son cr<8e>ditos al Sistema Financiero con algo que en la econom<92>a se le llama colateral, pero b<87>sicamente es respaldo con T<92>tulos. Y alcanzamos una cifra de alrededor de los 11,000 millones de c<97>rdobas en el momento m<87>ximo de estos reportos. Hacia finales de a<96>o ya los Reportos Monetarios hab<92>an finalizado en cerca de los 7, 000 millones de c<97>rdobas, y esa es la l<92>nea de Reportos que m<87>s o menos el Banco Central mantiene con las instituciones financieras; un poco m<87>s de 200 millones de d<97>lares. <c0>En qu<8e> ayud<97> toda esta l<92>nea de Reportos? Bueno, colabor<97> en el ciclo productivo; puesto que dimos Reportos a m<87>s de seis meses y eso permiti<97> apalancar, adem<87>s el ciclo productivo, atender los requerimientos de dep<97>sitos. Y nosotros dispusimos las Reservas Internacionales que no bajaron en 1,000 millones, voy aclarar eso, sino que menos que esa cantidad. Por ejemplo, las Reservas Internacionales Brutas que nosotros se<96>alamos claramente, finalizaron en 2,261 millones, al inicio de 2017 estaban en 2,757 millones de d<97>lares. Las Reservas Internacionales Netas, que este es un c<87>lculo contable que se hace para ver de obligaciones cu<87>nto se puede deducir de esas brutas, pasaron de 2,716 millones de d<97>lares a 2,038. Las Reservas Internacionales Netas y las Reservas Internacionales Netas ajustadas pasaron de 1,802 a 1,145 millones, o sea unos 655 millones de d<97>lares. Nosotros creemos que, con ese nivel de Reservas Internacionales, m<87>s otras acciones que se adoptaron, se facilit<97> la liquidez en la econom<92>a, los bancos pudieron mantener coeficientes de liquidez de alrededor del 32 por ciento, pudieron atender los dep<97>sitos del p<9c>blico y pudieron darle curso a la actividad econ<97>mica. No obstante, aqu<92> hubo un cambio. Al inicio nosotros comenzamos con cr<8e>ditos de 6 meses, pero no nos corresponde al Banco Central realizar esa actividad, la actividad crediticia es privada, no es del Estado. El Estado no da pr<8e>stamos, el Banco Central no puede dar pr<8e>stamos. Lo que hacemos es apoyar en liquidez a las instituciones financieras y fungimos como agentes financieros del Gobierno. Ese es el mandato que tenemos por Ley, no tenemos un mandato de dar cr<8e>dito. No obstante, con los Reportos nosotros incidimos en que el cr<8e>dito fluyera, que es diferente. Y despu<8e>s que dimos Reportos de 6 meses, pasamos a los Reportos propios de Banca Central que son cr<8e>ditos de 1 hasta 7 d<92>as m<87>ximo y ahora todos nuestros Reportos est<87>n en ese mercado. Tratando de responder un poco la pregunta que hizo aqu<92> el Diputado Alfredo C<8e>sar sobre la continuidad del ciclo agr<92>cola, ese es un tema que creemos nosotros que es relevante. Relevante porque el sector exportador ha estado respondiendo positivamente y es un sector que continu<97> y contin<9c>a hasta el mes de enero en nuestras informaciones, contin<9c>a presentando un desempe<96>o positivo, entonces es necesario apoyar. Una de las cosas que el Banco Central podr<92>a hacer en este nuevo contexto es volver a otorgar los Reportos crediticios de 1 a 7 d<92>as, hasta 6 meses para que el Sistema Financiero tenga posibilidad tambi<8e>n de reactivar el cr<8e>dito agr<92>cola. Otra posibilidad es que el Banco Central permita la repatriaci<97>n de ciertos dep<97>sitos que han salido del pa<92>s o dep<97>sitos de la propia banca, o liquidez de la propia banca en el exterior, para dar una remuneraci<97>n y a trav<8e>s de esa remuneraci<97>n tambi<8e>n movilizar el cr<8e>dito. Todas esas son f<97>rmulas que nosotros hemos venido trabajando y que estar<92>amos a finales de este mes en la posici<97>n de poder decir que el Banco Central pudo haber apoyado la actividad. Pero nuevamente, no es nuestro mandato. Recordemos que la banca enteramente es privada, la banca comercial. Recordemos que la banca tambi<8e>n es la que mueve las divisas. El Banco Central por el sistema de libre convertibilidad no capta las divisas privadas a diferencia de otros bancos centrales. Las remesas familiares los 1,500 millones de d<97>lares que llegan al pa<92>s, llegan a la banca privada, es la banca privada la que las moviliza, no es el Banco Central. Los 5,300 millones de d<97>lares de exportaciones que llegan a Nicaragua, llegan a la banca privada no es al Banco Central. Incluso los ingresos por turismo llegan a la banca privada. El Banco Central lo que percibe en d<97>lares es los excedentes de d<97>lares que la banca comercial vende al Banco Central libremente y adem<87>s de eso los ingresos de operaciones de contrataciones de pr<8e>stamos internacionales que realiza la Tesorer<92>a General de la Rep<9c>blica, con esos fondos es que nosotros hemos venido operando y hasta ahora lo que hemos hecho es mantener los balances. Creemos que la Reforma Tributaria y la Reforma de Pensiones que realiz<97> el Gobierno vienen a apoyar la estabilidad tambi<8e>n del flujo de divisas ya que equilibra los balances del Sistema Financiero, y en la medida en que tambi<8e>n el Sistema Financiero logra mantener cierta estabilidad, tambi<8e>n eso apoya al mercado de divisas. Lo que s<92> es cierto es que nosotros continuamos manteniendo el sistema de libre convertibilidad cero control sobre las divisas, ellas operan libremente en el mercado. La gente compra y vende al Tipo de Cambio que resulte en el mercado. El Tipo de Cambio Oficial es una se<96>al, una referencia, pero a la larga las divisas se determinan libremente y creemos que ese sistema puede continuar y debe continuar operando tal y como est<87> formulado a la fecha. Obviamente, que nosotros no est<87>bamos preparados el a<96>o pasado para un shock de esa naturaleza de la que tuvimos. En el escenario m<87>s negativo nosotros apenas lleg<87>bamos a una ca<92>da del 5 por ciento de los dep<97>sitos, nunca esperamos que <92>bamos a poder tener una ca<92>da de casi el 30 por ciento en los dep<97>sitos. Sin embargo, la fortaleza que ten<92>a la econom<92>a al inicio de toda esta perturbaci<97>n le permiti<97> confrontar muy bien, incluso mejor que otros pa<92>ses que enfrentaron situaciones similares. La parte positiva que creo que se rescata de este Informe, es que la econom<92>a despu<8e>s de junio se ha venido reactivando en el sector primarlo y el sector secundario. Creemos que eso es algo que se debe continuar promoviendo y respaldando, y esperar<92>amos nosotros que este nuevo ciclo productivo cuente con los fondos suficientes para que el pa<92>s pueda tener la oportunidad que todos los nicarag<9f>enses nos merecemos. Muchas Gracias Presidente de la Asamblea Nacional, Gustavo Porras Gracias, Doctor, Ovidio Reyes, Presidente del Banco Central. Le agradecemos a usted la presentaci<97>n, igual a la Licenciada Sara Amelia Rosales, Gerente, General del Banco Central y al Se<96>or Antonio Brenes, Gerente de An<87>lisis Macroecon<97>mico.

Title: Wood and Leather Art Exhibition
text: EXHIBITION ART IN WOOD AND LEATHER PRESIDENT OF THE BCN, CRO. OVID REYES R. 27/05/2019 In his book El viaje a Nicaragua, published one hundred years ago, Ruben Dario describes the geography and history, society and culture of his homeland. Not only of the elites, but also of the common people, "who do not deal," he said, "with politics or literature." Craftsmanship, combining the useful and the beautiful, caught his attention. That is, the ceramic and goldsmith works, the hammocks woven to cabuya and dyed with colors, as well as their mats or mats and the shoes described by Ruben as "famous". Leatherderived from livestockand wood--from the richness of our forestsdeserved his praise. Our carpenters and cabinetmakers, he noted, "execute exhibition pieces that constitute wonderful mosaics." Today the Central Bank of Nicaragua recognizes this admirable work of the artisans of Masaya by bringing together representative pieces, both large and small, identical for their artistic finish. We hope that our initiative will serve as a stimulus to these efficient artisans, whose products give prestige to the country. Our sincere respects and wishes for success to you. Thanks a lot

Title: Opening act of the Art in Stone Exhibition
text: OPENING CEREMONY OF THE EXHIBITION "ART IN STONE" PRESIDENT OF THE BCN, CRO. OVID REYES R. 07/08/2019 The beauty of the universe is not only unity in diversity, but also diversity in unity. Umberto Eco (1932-2016) Stone is a characteristic material that appears in the artistic manifestations of every culture and that has survived the passage of time. Its hardness gives it an imperishable quality of permanence. The materials created by Nature serve as an expressive means to the human being to transfer to them their personal feelings and concerns. In the case at hand, stone sculpture is the oldest known artistic tradition. In prehistoric times man used as support his engravings (petroglyphs) and drawings (pictograph) the rocky walls of the caverns; The reliefs, cavities and projections of these walls served to create completing what they saw in them: an animal or another human being. In Nicaragua there is knowledge of the use of stone as a means of expression since pre-Hispanic times: the rock art developed on the slopes of rivers, lakes and lagoons are a good example of this the petroglyphs of Isla del Muerto, those of Montelimar, La Gallina, among many others. In addition, they used the stone to make hunting and fishing tools, body ornaments, statuettes and large statues of deities and warriors; mounds, where they celebrate cults or sacrifices; site demarcations. The sculptor in each culture and at different times selects stones of a certain typology according to his plastic and expressive interests, and the technical possibilities available, creating a very particular link with her in the development of his personal work. There are currently in Nicaragua a large number of sculptors, heirs of that artistic tradition who maintain a special interest in stone. They have made their way through that essential link with this privileged material, creating styles, trends, influences, analogies and differences, symbolic and social values that transcend their own materiality. The sculptor Edith Grpn used marble to perpetuate the image of our great Ruben Dario; Jorge Navas Cordonero, Genaro Amador Lira, Fernando Saravia, Orlando Sobalvarro, Roberto de la Selva, Miguel angel Abarca, Leonel Cerrato, Ricardo Gomez are some of the sculptors who at some point in their Artistic life they have resorted to this material to conceive their creations. The new generations of sculptors, like their predecessors, feel that impulse to give life to the inert stone, to draw from its interior forms and volumes. Some do it with traditional tools such as the chisel and hammer; others with saws, drill bits and grinders; There are also those who embellish the stones by coloring them. But there are also other artists who use colored and semi-precious stones to set threads of silk, silver or other metal, combining them with crystal beads thus creating beautiful pieces of jewelry highly appreciated within society. The artisans of San Juan de Limay have acquired an unparalleled skill in the handling of marble stone, maintaining an impeccable invoice, a constant search for their personal work that identifies them within the national plastic. Title: Central Bank of Nicaragua holds award ceremony of the Young Poetry Contest "Aura Rostand" 2019
text: BCN AWARDS THE YOUNG POETRY CONTEST "AURA ROSTAND" 2019 16/01/2020 Year after year, the Central Bank of Nicaragua carries out an important cultural work, with the purpose of promoting the arts of our society through activities such as literature and painting contests, book publishing, exhibitions of plastic arts and crafts. Title: Announcement of Activities in Celebration of the 60th Anniversary of the Central Bank of Nicaragua
text: PRESIDENT OVIDIO REYES R. ANNOUNCES ACTIVITIES IN CELEBRATION OF THE BCN'S 60TH ANNIVERSARY 22/01/2020 President of the NCB: Good morning friends, journalists and people who can see us on television and radio. We want to inform today that we will be initiating the Celebration of the 60th Anniversary of the Central Bank of Nicaragua, an institution that was created in order to implement the Monetary and Exchange Policy of the State, and in addition to that, guarantee the stability of the national currency. Particularly, with the issuance of the currency the Cordoba that has been in force for a long time in our country. In addition, the Central Bank regulates the operation of Payment Systems and contributes to promoting the stability of the National Financial System. The Bank and its Board of Directors decided to celebrate this 60th Anniversary with a set of activities that I am pleased to present below: The first activity will occur on February 28, we will participate with the issuance of a Postage Stamp in commemoration of the 60th Anniversary of the Bank. Given the importance of monetary and exchange rate policy, the Central Bank will also offer open courses in programs that will be aimed at all those interested in knowing the functioning of our institution, and the courses will be in the following topics: Monetary and Exchange Policy in March 2020; another Financial Stability course in May 2020; Payment Systems in June; National and International Financial Markets in August; and Macroeconomic Indicators in October. For these courses, students, journalists, professionals and economists will be able to register and, of those registered, a selection will be made and we will be training people in topics of the Central Bank of Nicaragua. On March 25 we will hold a meeting that we are already convening all those former Bank officials and founders of the Bank, to have a meeting here in our institution and highlight it. On April 29 we will hold a meeting with information providers of the Central Bank of Nicaragua, aimed at all those companies and people that provide economic and financial information, and that serve as a basis for the construction of statistical indicators, prices, and especially production and construction of the System of National Accounts. Likewise, we are pleased to inform that, from May 25 to 29 at the Casa de los Pueblos, we will be presenting all the works of art that exist in the Central Bank of Nicaragua. In that week, the House of the Peoples will be a kind of national art museum. The Bank has come in its 60 years, accumulating many works of art by renowned national artists, consisting of paintings, paintings, historical documents, and also art in stone, wood, leather and other figures that are here in our institution and are scattered throughout our buildings. However, we believe that it is also time to make it available to the public so that they can admire, contemplate and learn about this important asset that the Central Bank of Nicaragua has. Similarly, on June 5 we will be participating in the circulation of a National Lottery Ticket commemorating the 60th Anniversary of the Bank. On July 3 we will be holding an International Seminar entitled "Implementation of Monetary Policy in the Central American region", in which economists from Central America from Central Banks will be participating where they will explain how monetary policy works and how it operates in each of their countries. Likewise, on July 23, the meeting of central bank presidents will be held, which we are all grouped in the Central American Monetary Council. On September 18 we will be holding a Cultural Gala in commemoration of the 60th Anniversary of the Central Bank at the Ruben Dario National Theater and on September 25 we will be presenting commemorative banknotes and coins, also alluding to this 60th Anniversary. Likewise, it is known that for several years we have been compiling the poetic work of Ruben Dario and his total literary work and we would expect on November 6 to present the complementary book of Poetic Anthology of Ruben Dario. The Central Bank has already produced a book of Poetic Anthology of Ruben Dario and now this time we would be completing it with the rest of the poems that would be sealing a sequence of books by Ruben Dario that the Central Bank has promoted, such as Political Writings, his Poetry Poetry Collection, the book of Novels by Ruben Dario, the book of Short Stories by Ruben Dario and now the Complementary Poetic Anthology. Likewise, we would be launching the Economics Prize and the Journal of Economics and Finance on November 12, alluding to the 60th Anniversary and at the end of the year on December 3 we will be presenting a book that will contain all those works of art that we will be exhibiting at the Casa de los Pueblos in the month of May. With these activities we would hope to contribute to the knowledge of the operations of the Central Bank, to the dissemination of how the Central Bank works, but in addition to that to the culture and art in Nicaragua that we hope will be the delight of all those who participate and join these activities. That is what we wanted to inform you today, invite all people to participate in the public events that we will be holding and presenting and also inviting all those who want to join this celebration. Thanks a lot

Title: Award Ceremony of the Painting Contest "Nicaragua proud of its culture and traditions 2019"
text: PRESIDENT OF THE BCN AWARDS THE PAINTING CONTEST "NICARAGUA PROUD OF ITS CULTURE AND TRADITIONS 2019" 24/01/2020 The cultural work of the Central Bank of Nicaragua (BCN) is one of the most important traditions of our institution. To promote the arts, the BCN holds literature and painting competitions, book publishing, exhibitions of plastic arts and handicrafts. The Painting Contest "Nicaragua proud of its culture and traditions 2019" was convened with the purpose of promoting and publicizing contemporary painting in our country. The theme of the contest offered artists a large number of options to capture in their works: celebrations, landscapes, characters, architecture, emblematic sites, among others. Once the contest was over, the jury awarded first place to Noche de apante, by Engel Adolfo Urbina Martinez, "for its originality in addressing a folkloric and mystical theme", "with vestiges of the European tenebrist current", thus bringing it closer to the national culture. The second place went to La fritanga, by Juan David Hernandez Blandon, a work characterized by "a broad mastery of drawing and color" and its "timely approach to the hyperrealistic current" by capturing -and in this way aesthetically exalting- a common and widespread Nicaraguan custom. The third place was awarded to Childhood, by Franck Kevin Laguna Guevara, for its originality, excellent technical mastery and the particular validity of the theme in contemporary culture, "alluding to childhood through a popular object, a traditional toy" and thus generating a flow of associations and remembrances. With great satisfaction I emphasize that all the winners are young, who are just beginning their careers, which indicates that in the plastic arts of Nicaragua a new promotion is emerging that combines the autochthonous and the universal, the traditional and the contemporary. Title: Issuance of 5 cordobas note and commemorative coins
text: ISSUANCE OF 5 CoRDOBAS BANKNOTE AND COMMEMORATIVE COINS. REMARKS BY THE PRESIDENT OF THE BCN, CRO. OVID REYES R. 30/09/2020 Good morning, everyone. In the context of the Celebration Plan of the 60th Anniversary of the founding of the Central Bank of Nicaragua, I am pleased to announce the issuance of a new commemorative banknote of 5 cordobas and commemorative coins of gold, silver and nickel. The last issue of a 5 cordobas note made by the Central Bank of Nicaragua was 25 years ago, in 1995. Today a 5 cordobas banknote is reissued that commemorates our 60th anniversary of foundation and that will facilitate small denomination payments. The Central Bank of Nicaragua was created on September 16, 1960 by Legislative Decree No. 525 of July 28, 1960 and published in La Gaceta, Official Gazette, No. 211 of September 16 of the same year. The Central Bank was entrusted with the responsibility of formulating and executing monetary and exchange policy, as well as the issuance of the national currency, the Cordoba. The issuance of the commemorative note of 5 cordobas and coins Issuance of 5 cordobas banknote and commemorative coins. Word... ... Gold, silver and nickel commemorations were approved by the Board of Directors of the Central Bank within the framework of the celebrations that the institution has been executing during this year. The issuance of the new commemorative banknote and commemorative coins pursues the following objectives: 1. Commemorate the 60th anniversary of the founding of the Central Bank of Nicaragua, 2. Facilitate low-denomination payments, and 3. Supply quality numismatic products to collectors and the general public. . The new 5 cordobas banknote is grey. Like the banknotes in circulation today, it is printed on polymer substrate, a material that is characterized by its high durability, greater difficulty of counterfeiting and kindness to the environment. . Its dimensions are 126 millimeters long and 67 millimeters high, which makes it the shortest banknote compared to the banknotes in current circulation. . The banknote bears the signature of the President of the Central Bank of Nicaragua and the Minister of Finance and Public Credit. . This ticket will start circulating from tomorrow, Thursday, October 01, 2020 The obverse of the banknote presents the image of the buildings of the Central Bank of Nicaragua, where it has operated since 1976. Over time, the infrastructure has been expanded and modernized. The banknote contains the legend "Sixty Anniversary of the BCN, issuing confidence and stability" and the number of Resolution of the Board of Directors of the Central Bank of October 23, 2019. Issuance of 5 cordobas banknote and commemorative coins. Word... ... For its part, on the back of the ticket and projecting an image of modernity, the image of the Las Piedretitas Overpass, inaugurated in November 2018, connecting the Western roads to Managua and vice versa, is shown. Additionally, the ticket contains the following outstanding features: . The BCN logo on both sides of the banknote, in silver on the obverse, and in blue on the back. . A vertical line of three tactile points in relief, on the front and back of the note, in order to facilitate its identification to people with visual limitations. . An image shaded with the acronym of the BCN. . Special Intaglio ink on the image of the BCN buildings, as well as the name of the institution and denomination of the banknote. . Complex window with the denomination of 5 cordobas. . Transparent window with the denomination of 5 cordobas. . Iridescent band on the back of the note, which, when rotated, shows triangles with the denomination of 5 cordobas. On the other hand, the commemorative coins of gold, silver and nickel have the following outstanding characteristics: . Face value of 60 cordobas, alluding to the 60th anniversary of the institution. . The obverse shows the BCN building and on the reverse the logo of the institution. . The diameter of the coins is 35 millimeters. Issuance of 5 cordobas banknote and commemorative coins. Word... ... . The year of issuance is 2020. These commemorative coins will be available for sale at the BCN counters, from Thursday, October 1, 2020. I detail below, the outstanding features of each coin. The commemorative gold coin is minted in pure gold (Law 999.9), finished with Proof quality and weight of 31.1 grams. The coin and its certificate of authenticity are contained in a wooden case. For its part, the commemorative silver coin is minted in pure silver (Law 999.9), finished with Proof quality and weight of 31.1 grams. The coin and its certificate of authenticity are contained in a black leatherette case. Finally, the commemorative coin of Niguel is minted in steel coated with niguel, finished with Proof-like quality and weight of 20 grams. Like the silver coin, this nickel coin and its certificate of authenticity are contained in a black leatherette case. I conclude this speech by thanking everyone for their attention, hoping for the new commemorative banknote of 5 Cordobas and commemorative coins, are well received by users and collectors. Thanks a lot.
