Title: Presentation of the "State of the Nicaraguan Economy and Perspectives as of October 2020"
text: PRESENTATION OF THE "STATE OF THE NICARAGUAN ECONOMY AND PERSPECTIVES TO OCTOBER 2020" 15/10/2020 Good morning, everyone. This morning, I will be sharing with you the vision of the Central Bank of Nicaragua on the State of the Nicaraguan Economy to October 2020. During 2020, the evolution of Nicaragua's economy, like that of the entire Central American region and the world, has been affected by the global COVID-19 pandemic. It should be noted that the impact on the Nicaraguan economy in production and trade, although relevant, has been less than that observed in the rest of the countries of the Central American region and the Dominican Republic. During the first quarter, the economy maintained the path of stabilization and recovery that had been observed since mid-2019. However, in the second quarter, the impact of COVID-19 was directly manifested through the reduction of world trade and production, which affected Nicaragua mainly in economic activities related to the tourism sector: hotels and restaurants, and services in general. At the beginning of the third quarter, by contrast, economic signs of recovery have emerged. In this recovery, the positive evolution of merchandise exports, bank deposits and international reserves stands out, which has led to exchange rate stability and the financial system, which have favored a decline in interest rates. Production and employment are showing signs of recomposition after their reduction has been contained. For its part, inflation has been converging to a lower level. The international economic context in 2020 became adverse, with the country's main trading partners in deep recession caused by the confinement of families, the closure of borders and the consequent paralysis of travelers, as well as the reduction of world trade. Global demand also declined, resulting in mixed results with reductions in certain international prices of exportable goods, although some of them have picked up recently. In October 2020, the International Monetary Fund (IMF) upgraded its forecast for the global economy (from its June projections), based on second-quarter GDP results in large advanced economies being less negative than expected, growth restoring in China, and signs of a faster recovery in the third quarter. Thus, the IMF projects a reduction in world GDP of 4.4 percent in 2020 (-5.2% in the June projection) and a recovery of 5.2 percent in 2021 (5.4% in the June projection). In this environment, economic policy responses in both the monetary and fiscal spheres have been expansionary, thus mitigating the economic impact of the pandemic. According to recent developments, the world's two largest economies, the United States and China, could exhibit less negative growth rates than predicted in 2020. In the case of the United States, in the third week of September, the US Federal Reserve (Fed) improved its forecast for the contraction of US economic activity in 2020 to 3.7 percent (from 6.5% in June). On the other hand, China recovered its economic growth in the second quarter (3.2% compared to a contraction of 6.8% in the first quarter). According to the Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI), which is based on a survey on purchases in the manufacturing sector and offers an outlook regarding possible future growth, as of September 2020 the world economy shows a recovery trend, after the critical months of April and May. The Gross Domestic Product (GDP) corresponding to the first quarter of 2020 reflected a growth of 1.7 percent. At the same time, the open unemployment rate declined year-on-year to 4.8 percent. However, from March, the economic effects of the coronavirus pandemic began to manifest, mainly in some external flows, which affected the performance of the second quarter and the short-term economic outlook. As a result, GDP in the second quarter registered a year-on-year reduction of 7.9 percent, with mixed sectoral results: a primary sector that continued to grow and a services sector showing reduction. Thus, the activities that remained with growth were: livestock (2.1%) and agriculture (1.1%); Meanwhile, the activities that were reduced were: hotels and restaurants (-53%), mining and quarrying (-30.2%) and manufacturing industry (-18.8%). By expenditure components, external aggregate demand fell (-26.8%) mainly due to the decrease in exports of free zones, visitors and transport and insurance services, even though merchandise exports continued to grow. Consumption fell (-4.8%), while gross capital formation improved (5.2%), due to the execution of public investment and the variation in inventories. On the other hand, the signals observed from the monthly evolution of economic activity, collected by the IMAE, present the month of April as the one with the greatest impact of the pandemic (-9.9%), with increasingly less negative rates during May and July, suggesting that economic activity is in the process of recovery. When the year-on-year series of IMAE cycle trends is analyzed, the growth rate results in -0.6 percent, thus indicating the convergence rate of the monthly IMAE over the coming months. In line with quarterly GDP results, the activities with the greatest year-on-year reduction to July were those related to the provision of services, mainly hotels and restaurants (-51.2%). However, some activities have been less impacted and have managed to recover towards July, after having registered year-on-year reductions in April and May. In this regard, year-on-year growth was recovered in agriculture (9.7%), livestock (4.6%) and trade (5.5%). In addition, some activities, such as public administration, education and health, have continued to show positive growth rates. Within the countries of the Central American region and the Dominican Republic, Nicaragua's quarterly GDP shows the best performance in terms of year-on-year variation, both in the first and second quarters of 2020. In particular, in the first quarter Nicaragua was the country that grew the most and in the second quarter it was the economy with the lowest incidence in production. Comparing the IMAE of the countries of the Central American region and the Dominican Republic, all show the same pattern of reduction in economic activity and subsequent trend towards recovery, with Nicaragua being observed as the economy with the least impact on economic activity. Domestic production and exports, as well as the fact that general confinement measures have not been adopted, become the elements that explain this result. The open unemployment rate went from 4.8 percent in the first quarter to 5.4 percent in the second quarter, a moderate rate of increase from the reduction seen in economic activity. However, the overall labor participation rate fell by 4 percentage points, from 71.0 percent in the first quarter to 66.5 percent in the second quarter. This reduction could be associated with the decision of a part of the economically active population not to look for work, both for health precautionary reasons and for the less encouraging prospects of finding employment due to the reduction in economic activity. For its part, the underemployment rate went from 44.7 percent in the first quarter to 45.9 percent in the second quarter. In this environment, affiliation to the Nicaraguan Social Security Institute (INSS), which is another employment indicator, shows signs of stabilizing after June. Specifically, the number of INSS affiliates grew in August and September by 2,391 and 958 affiliates, respectively, after 4 consecutive months of net disaffiliation. The employment and labor participation rates are expected to increase significantly during the second half of the year, once the world economy reactivates and the national economy consolidates its recovery. Social security participant participation is also expected to improve. Until September 2020, inflation has shown a downward trend. This result has been mainly influenced by: lower food prices, lower oil prices and lower cost pressure due to the reduction of the shift from 5 to 3 percent that occurred in October 2019. This result shows that the policies implemented in the productive field and monetary and exchange policy have been appropriate, favoring low prices that benefited purchasing power and cost reduction. The accumulated variation of the CPI to September was 0.63 percent (3.89% to September 2019) and the year-on-year variation was 2.81 percent (5.62% in September 2019). In terms of contribution to cumulative inflation, the biggest impulses came from the education (0.26 p.p.), health divisions. (0.23 p.p.), goods and services (0.22 p.p.), furniture and household goods (0.16 p.p.), and alcoholic beverages and tobacco (0.10 p.p.), which together added 0.97 percentage points. The division with the highest year-on-year inflation was alcoholic beverages and tobacco, with 7.62 percent. Meanwhile, the transport division recorded negative year-on-year inflation for the sixth consecutive month (-2.65%). Core year-on-year inflation was 2.62 percent, lower than the 3 percent change slippage rate. Despite the adverse consequences on the real economy, monetary and financial variables perform well. Thus, as of September 2020, all monetary aggregates continued to reflect positive year-on-year growth rates, the foreign exchange market remained stable and through its monetary operations the BCN continued to promote active management of liquidity in the financial system. The performance of the variables of the monetary and fiscal sector have favored the strengthening of gross international reserves, reaching a balance of 2,907.6 million dollars in September, which represented an accumulation of 510.1 million dollars compared to the level of December 2019 and a coverage of 2.97 times the monetary base and 7.96 months of imports. In response to the adverse effect of the pandemic, a series of measures have been adopted in the monetary area to encourage the recovery of the economy, to promote liquidity, support the flow of credit and the transmission of monetary policy. Among the main measures approved are: i) expression in nominal cordobas of the instruments that make up the BCN's interest rate corridor, i) reduction of the monetary reference rate (TRM) and related rates, iii) adjustment in the period of the reserve rate in national currency and iv) release of the mandatory legal reserve in national currency up to an amount of four billion cordobas. The investments made by the financial system in NCB instruments have also been decisive, as a response to the greater credit risk and to take advantage of the better domestic returns in the face of lower interest rates abroad. The policy of reducing the TRM, as well as in the interest rates of its main instruments, aimed to lower the cost of monetary reports for banks, signal more lax policy conditions and maintain consistency with the evolution of international interest rates. Thus, as of September 2020, the BCN made 9 adjustments to its TRM, reaching a reduction of 350 basis points, from 7.75 percent (3% corresponding to the exchange rate slippage to the TRM in force on January 1, 2020, which was expressed in dollars at that time) to 4.25 percent in August 2020. Financial activity has continued its stabilisation process, reflected in an increase in deposits, although due to a risk issue, banks are being cautious in credit deliveries, maintaining high liquidity that will favour financial investment, mainly in deposits and NCB instruments. In this sense, as of August 2020, deposits have continued their growth started in December 2019, increasing 13.2 percent year-on-year. The year-on-year change in credit was the least negative since November 2018 (-6.4%). In terms of indicators, the availability of the banking sector represented 46.6 percent of obligations, capital adequacy amounted to 23.1 percent (higher than the 10% required), and the overdue and judicial collection portfolio stood at 4.4 percent of the gross portfolio. For its part, given in the context of COVID-19 and its impact on the payment capacity of households and companies, the Superintendency of Banks and Other Financial Institutions (SIBOIF), implemented a rule to facilitate special conditions for debtors affected by the pandemic. Consistent with the above, in the second quarter of 2020 the Financial Intermediation Conditions index (ICIF) reached a neutral point, with 0.03 standard deviations. In the behavior of the index, a reversal is observed from the third quarter of 2019, reflecting increasingly tight financial intermediation conditions. The reduction in economic activity consequently affected tax collection, although in recent months there has been a trend towards recovery. Spending in 2020 is executed as budgeted. The placement in Bonds of the Republic of Nicaragua (BRN) together with the entry of external resources have guaranteed the financing of said expenditure. As of July 2020, the Non-Financial Public Sector (NFPS) recorded an accumulated deficit of 4,457.7 million cordobas (surplus C2,708.4 million as of July 2019), consistent with an increase in revenues of 2.9 percent year-on-year (mainly due to the increase in social contributions and other revenues, although tax revenues were reduced) and an increase in total disbursement of 13.1 percent. Public debt remains at sustainable levels, although it has grown in terms of GDP due to the decline in GDP and partly due to the increase in disbursements of concessional loans from multilateral and bilateral creditors (US386.4 million as of September 2020 vs. US367.9 million as of September 2019). Government bond placements have also increased, compared to the accumulated as of September 2019. The financing obtained has largely allowed that, despite the health situation facing the country, the financial execution of the Public Investment Program remains at adequate levels (40% of the total programmed to June 2020). The merchandise trade deficit continued to decline in cumulative January-July (-22.8% year-on-year) driven by merchandise export growth of 9.5 percent year-on-year, supported by an improvement in the terms of trade of 16.1 percent. This result was also affected by the reduction in FOB imports of 1.9 percent, mainly explained by the lower oil bill. In the case of free zone exports, the positive trend of the first quarter of the year was reversed from April, so that in the accumulated to July they registered a reduction of 22.1 percent year-on-year, attributable to the economic impact of the pandemic. The largest reduction has been observed in textile exports, due to declining demand from the US economy. The cumulative flows of the balance of payments as of June 2020 show a current account surplus and a positive capital account. In the net, during the first half of the year, capital inflows were observed. In the accumulated to July, family remittances grew 8.5 percent in year-on-year terms, after slowing down in April when they were -9.1 percent. Meanwhile, as a result of border closures in other countries and travel restrictions, revenues from exports of services, including tourism, which in the first quarter had been 360.9 million dollars, reached 137.8 million dollars in the second quarter. For the remainder of 2020, the main variables of the real economy are expected to recover, which could accelerate once travel and trade restrictions are lifted and the international economy recovers. Monetary and financial variables are also expected to maintain their growth trend. Thus, a GDP growth rate projection of -4.5 percent is maintained, with a range of between 1 percent. Likewise, an inflation rate of 3.7 percent is projected, with a range of between 0.5 percent. The current account of the balance of payments is expected to end in surplus, driven by the improvement in the trade and services balance. Deposits are expected to grow, credit is expected to show increasingly less negative net placements and international reserves are expected to continue to consolidate. As for public finances, it is expected to keep them under control and a larger public sector deficit than in 2019, which includes higher health spending. Thanks a lot.
text_original: PRESENTACI<ee>N DEL "ESTADO DE LA ECONOM<ea>A NICARAG<86>ENSE Y PERSPECTIVAS A OCTUBRE 2020" PRESENTACI<ee>N DEL "ESTADO DE LA ECONOM<ea>A NICARAG<86>ENSE Y PERSPECTIVAS A OCTUBRE 2020" 15/10/2020 Buenos d<92>as a todos. En esta ma<96>ana, estar<8e> compartiendo con ustedes la visi<97>n del Banco Central de Nicaragua sobre el Estado de la Econom<92>a Nicarag<9f>ense a octubre de 2020. Durante el a<96>o 2020, la evoluci<97>n de la econom<92>a de Nicaragua, como la de toda la regi<97>n centroamericana y del mundo, se ha visto afectada por la pandemia mundial del COVID-19. Cabe destacar, que la afectaci<97>n en la econom<92>a nicarag<9f>ense en producci<97>n y en comercio, aunque relevante, ha sido menor que la observada en el resto de los pa<92>ses de la regi<97>n centroamericana y Rep<9c>blica Dominicana. Durante el primer trimestre, la econom<92>a mantuvo la trayectoria de estabilizaci<97>n y recuperaci<97>n que se ven<92>a observando desde mediados de 2019. Sin embargo, en el segundo trimestre, se manifest<97> directamente el impacto del COVID-19 a trav<8e>s de la reducci<97>n del comercio y de la producci<97>n mundial, la que afect<97> a Nicaragua principalmente en las actividades econ<97>micas relacionadas con el sector tur<92>stico: hoteles y restaurantes, y de servicios en general. A principios del tercer trimestre, por el contrario, han surgido se<96>ales econ<97>micas de recuperaci<97>n. En esta recuperaci<97>n, se destaca la evoluci<97>n positiva de las exportaciones de mercanc<92>as, dep<97>sitos bancarios y reservas internacionales, lo que ha dado lugar a una estabilidad cambiar<92>a y del sistema financiero, que han favorecido a la baja en las tasas de inter<8e>s. La producci<97>n y el empleo est<87>n dando se<96>ales de recomposici<97>n despu<8e>s de haberse contenido su reducci<97>n. Por su parte, la inflaci<97>n ha estado convergiendo a un nivel m<87>s bajo. El contexto econ<97>mico internacional en 2020 se torn<97> adverso, con los principales socios comerciales del pa<92>s en profunda recesi<97>n originada por el confinamiento de las familias, el cierre de fronteras y la consecuente par<87>lisis de viajeros, as<92> como la reducci<97>n del comercio mundial. Tambi<8e>n la demanda mundial se redujo, lo que origin<97> resultados mixtos con reducci<97>n en ciertos precios internacionales de los bienes exportables, aunque recientemente algunos de ellos han repuntado. En octubre de 2020, el Fondo Monetario Internacional (FMI) mejor<97> su pron<97>stico sobre la econom<92>a mundial (respecto sus proyecciones de junio), con base en que los resultados del PIB del segundo trimestre en las grandes econom<92>as avanzadas fueron menos negativos de lo esperado, el restablecimiento del crecimiento en China y signos de una recuperaci<97>n m<87>s r<87>pida en el tercer trimestre. As<92>, el FMI proyecta una reducci<97>n del PIB mundial de 4.4 por ciento en 2020 (-5.2% en la proyecci<97>n de junio) y una recuperaci<97>n del 5.2 por ciento en 2021 (5.4% en la proyecci<97>n de junio). En este entorno, las respuestas de pol<92>ticas econ<97>micas tanto en el <87>mbito monetario como en el fiscal han sido expansivas, mitigando de esta manera el impacto econ<97>mico de la pandemia. Seg<9c>n desarrollos recientes, las dos econom<92>as m<87>s grandes del mundo, Estados Unidos y China, podr<92>an presentar tasas de crecimiento menos negativas que las previstas en 2020. En el caso de Estados Unidos, en la tercera semana de septiembre, la Reserva Federal de Estados Unidos (Fed) mejor<97> su pron<97>stico de contracci<97>n de la actividad econ<97>mica estadounidense en 2020 a un 3.7 por ciento (desde un 6.5% de junio). Por otra parte, China recuper<97> su crecimiento econ<97>mico en el segundo trimestre (3.2% en comparaci<97>n con una contracci<97>n del 6.8% en el primer trimestre). Seg<9c>n el <92>ndice de Gestores de Compra (PMI, por sus siglas en ingl<8e>s), que se basa en una encuesta sobre compras en el sector manufacturero y que ofrece una perspectiva con respecto al posible crecimiento futuro, a septiembre de 2020 la econom<92>a mundial muestra una tendencia a la recuperaci<97>n, luego de los meses cr<92>ticos de abril y mayo El Producto Interno Bruto (PIB) correspondiente al primer trimestre de 2020 reflej<97> un crecimiento de 1.7 por ciento. Al mismo tiempo, la tasa de desempleo abierto disminuy<97> interanualmente para ubicarse en 4.8 por ciento. No obstante, a partir de marzo, se comenzaron a manifestar los efectos econ<97>micos de la pandemia del coronavirus, principalmente en algunos flujos externos, lo que afect<97> el desempe<96>o del segundo trimestre y las perspectivas econ<97>micas a corto plazo. Como resultado, el PIB del segundo trimestre registr<97> una reducci<97>n interanual de 7.9 por ciento, con resultados sectoriales mixtos: un sector primario que continu<97> creciendo y un sector servicios presentando reducci<97>n. As<92>, las actividades que se mantuvieron con crecimiento fueron: pecuario (2.1%) y agricultura (1.1%); mientras que, las actividades que se redujeron fueron: hoteles y restaurantes (-53%), explotaci<97>n de minas y canteras (-30.2%) e industria manufacturera (-18.8%). Por los componentes del gasto, la demanda agregada externa se redujo (-26.8%) principalmente por la disminuci<97>n en las exportaciones de zona franca, visitantes y servicios de transporte y seguros, aun cuando las exportaciones de mercanc<92>as continuaron creciendo. El consumo se redujo (-4.8%), mientras que la formaci<97>n bruta de capital mejor<97> (5.2%), por la ejecuci<97>n de la inversi<97>n p<9c>blica y la variaci<97>n de existencias. Por otra parte, las se<96>ales observadas a partir de la evoluci<97>n mensual de la actividad econ<97>mica, recogidas por el IMAE, presentan al mes de abril como el de mayor impacto de la pandemia (-9.9%), con tasas cada vez menos negativas durante mayo y julio, sugiriendo que la actividad econ<97>mica se encuentra en proceso de recuperaci<97>n. Cuando se analiza la serie interanual de tendencia ciclo del IMAE, la tasa de crecimiento resulta en -0.6 por ciento, indicando as<92> la tasa de convergencia del IMAE mensual durante los pr<97>ximos meses. En l<92>nea con los resultados del PIB trimestral, las actividades con una mayor reducci<97>n interanual a julio fueron aquellas relacionadas con la prestaci<97>n de servicios, principalmente hoteles y restaurantes (-51.2%). No obstante, algunas actividades han sido menos impactadas y han logrado recuperarse hacia julio, despu<8e>s de haber registrado reducciones interanuales en abril y mayo. En este sentido, se observ<97> recuperaci<97>n del crecimiento interanual en agricultura (9.7%), pecuario (4.6%) y comercio (5.5%). Asimismo, algunas actividades, como la administraci<97>n p<9c>blica, ense<96>anza y salud, no han dejado de presentar tasas positivas de crecimiento. Dentro de los pa<92>ses de la regi<97>n centroamericana y Rep<9c>blica Dominicana, el PIB trimestral de Nicaragua muestra el mejor desempe<96>o en t<8e>rminos de variaci<97>n interanual, tanto en el primero como en el segundo trimestre de 2020. En particular, en el primer trimestre Nicaragua fue el pa<92>s que m<87>s creci<97> y en el segundo trimestre fue la econom<92>a con la menor incidencia en producci<97>n. Comparando los IMAE de los pa<92>ses de la regi<97>n centroamericana y Rep<9c>blica Dominicana, todos muestran el mismo patr<97>n de reducci<97>n de la actividad econ<97>mica y posterior tendencia hacia la recuperaci<97>n, observ<87>ndose a Nicaragua como la econom<92>a con la menor afectaci<97>n en actividad econ<97>mica. La producci<97>n interna y exportaciones, as<92> como por el hecho de no haberse adoptado medidas generales de confinamiento, pasan ser los elementos que explican este resultado. La tasa de desempleo abierto pas<97> de 4.8 por ciento en el primer trimestre a 5.4 por ciento en el segundo trimestre, una tasa de incremento moderada con respecto a la reducci<97>n observada en la actividad econ<97>mica. Sin embargo, la tasa global de participaci<97>n laboral se redujo en 4 puntos porcentuales, al pasar de 71.0 por ciento en el primer trimestre a 66.5 por ciento en el segundo trimestre. Esta reducci<97>n podr<92>a estar asociada a la decisi<97>n de una parte de la poblaci<97>n econ<97>micamente activa de no buscar trabajo, tanto por motivos precautorios sanitarios, como por las perspectivas menos alentadoras de encontrar empleo por la reducci<97>n de la actividad econ<97>mica. Por su parte, la tasa de subempleo pas<97> de 44.7 por ciento en el primer trimestre a 45.9 por ciento en el segundo trimestre. En este entorno, la afiliaci<97>n al Instituto Nicarag<9f>ense de Seguridad Social (INSS), que constituye otro indicador de empleo, muestra se<96>ales de estabilizaci<97>n despu<8e>s de junio. Espec<92>ficamente, el n<9c>mero de afiliados al INSS creci<97> en agosto y septiembre en 2,391 y 958 afiliados, respectivamente, luego de 4 meses consecutivos de desafiliaci<97>n neta. Se espera que la tasa de ocupaci<97>n y de participaci<97>n laboral aumenten de manera importante durante la segunda mitad del a<96>o, una vez que la econom<92>a mundial se reactive y que la econom<92>a nacional consolide su recuperaci<97>n. Tambi<8e>n se espera que mejore la participaci<97>n de los afiliados de la seguridad social. Hasta septiembre de 2020, la inflaci<97>n ha presentado una tendencia hacia la baja. Este resultado ha estado principalmente influido por: baja en los precios de los alimentos, menores precios del petr<97>leo y menor presi<97>n de costos por la reducci<97>n del deslizamiento cambiado del 5 al 3 por ciento que ocurri<97> en octubre de 2019. Este resultado evidencia que las pol<92>ticas implementadas en el campo productivo y de pol<92>tica monetaria y cambiar<92>a han sido las apropiadas, favoreciendo precios bajos que beneficiaron el poder adquisitivo y la reducci<97>n de los costos. La variaci<97>n acumulada del IPC al mes de septiembre fue de 0.63 por ciento (3.89% a septiembre 2019) y la variaci<97>n interanual fue de 2.81 por ciento (5.62% en septiembre de 2019). En t<8e>rminos de contribuci<97>n a la inflaci<97>n acumulada, los mayores impulsos provinieron de las divisiones de educaci<97>n (0.26 p.p.), salud (0.23 p.p.), bienes y servicios (0.22 p.p.), muebles y art<92>culos para el hogar (0.16 p.p.), y bebidas alcoh<97>licas y tabaco (0.10 p.p.), las cuales sumaron en conjunto 0.97 puntos porcentuales. La divisi<97>n de mayor inflaci<97>n interanual fue bebidas alcoh<97>licas y tabaco, con 7.62 por ciento. Mientras que, la divisi<97>n de transporte registr<97> una inflaci<97>n interanual negativa por sexto mes consecutivo (-2.65%). La inflaci<97>n interanual subyacente fue de 2.62 por ciento, menor que la tasa de deslizamiento cambiado de 3 por ciento. A pesar de las consecuencias adversas en la econom<92>a real, las variables monetarias y financieras presentan un buen desempe<96>o. As<92>, al mes de septiembre de 2020, todos los agregados monetarios continuaron reflejando tasas de crecimiento interanual positivas, el mercado cambiario continu<97> estable y mediante sus operaciones monetarias el BCN continu<97> propiciando un manejo activo de la liquidez del sistema financiero. El desempe<96>o de las variables del sector monetario y fiscal han favorecido el fortalecimiento de las reservas internacionales brutas, alcanzando en septiembre un saldo de 2,907.6 millones de d<97>lares, lo que represent<97> una acumulaci<97>n de 510.1 millones de d<97>lares respecto al nivel de diciembre de 2019 y una cobertura de 2.97 veces la base monetaria y de 7.96 meses de importaciones. Como respuesta al efecto adverso de la pandemia, en el <87>mbito monetario se han adoptado una serie de medidas para incentivar la recuperaci<97>n de la econom<92>a, para favorecer la liquidez, apoyar el flujo de cr<8e>dito y la transmisi<97>n de la pol<92>tica monetaria. Dentro de las principales medidas aprobadas est<87>n: i) expresi<97>n en c<97>rdobas nominales de los instrumentos que conforman el corredor de tasas de inter<8e>s del BCN, <c1>i) reducci<97>n de la tasa de referencia monetaria (TRM) y tasas conexas, iii) ajuste en el periodo de la tasa de encaje en moneda nacional y iv) liberaci<97>n del encaje legal obligatorio en moneda nacional hasta por un monto de cuatro mil millones de c<97>rdobas. Tambi<8e>n ha sido determinante, las inversiones realizadas por el sistema financiero en instrumentos del BCN, como una repuesta frente al mayor riesgo crediticio y para aprovechar los mejores rendimientos internos frente a la baja de tasas de inter<8e>s en el exterior. La pol<92>tica de reducci<97>n de la TRM, as<92> como en las tasas de inter<8e>s de sus principales instrumentos, tuvo como objetivo de abaratar el costo de los reportos monetarios para la banca, se<96>alizar condiciones m<87>s laxas de pol<92>tica y guardar consistencia con la evoluci<97>n de las tasas de inter<8e>s internacionales. As<92>, a septiembre de 2020, el BCN realiz<97> 9 ajustes a su TRM, alcanzando una reducci<97>n de 350 puntos b<87>sicos, pasando de 7.75 por ciento (3% correspondiente al deslizamiento cambiario a la TRM vigente el 1 de enero de 2020, la cual estaba expresada en d<97>lares en ese momento) a 4.25 por ciento en agosto de 2020. La actividad financiera ha continuado su proceso de estabilizaci<97>n, reflej<87>ndose en aumento de los dep<97>sitos, aunque por un tema de riesgo la banca est<87> siendo cautelosa en las entregas de cr<8e>dito, manteniendo una elevada liquidez que favorecer<87> la inversi<97>n financiera, principalmente en dep<97>sitos e instrumentos del BCN. En este sentido, a agosto de 2020, los dep<97>sitos han continuado su crecimiento iniciado en diciembre de 2019, aumentando 13.2 por ciento interanual. La variaci<97>n interanual del cr<8e>dito fue la menos negativa desde noviembre de 2018 (-6.4%). En t<8e>rminos de indicadores, las disponibilidades del sector bancario representaron el 46.6 por ciento de las obligaciones, la adecuaci<97>n de capital ascendi<97> a 23.1 por ciento (superior al 10% requerido), y la cartera vencida y en cobro judicial se ubic<97> en 4.4 por ciento de la cartera bruta. Por su parte, dado en contexto del COVID-19 y su incidencia en la capacidad de pago de los hogares y de las empresas, la Superintendencia de Bancos y de Otras Instituciones Financieras (SIBOIF), implemento una norma para facilitar condiciones especiales a los deudores afectados por la pandemia. Consistente con lo anterior, en el segundo trimestre de 2020 el <92>ndice de Condiciones de Intermediaci<97>n Financiera (ICIF) alcanz<97> un punto neutro, con 0.03 desviaciones est<87>ndar. En el comportamiento del <92>ndice se observa una reversi<97>n a partir del tercer trimestre de 2019, que refleja condiciones de intermediaci<97>n financiera cada vez menos estrechas. La reducci<97>n de la actividad econ<97>mica afect<97> consecuentemente la recaudaci<97>n tributaria, aunque en los <9c>ltimos meses se observa una tendencia hacia la recuperaci<97>n. El gasto en 2020 se ejecuta conforme lo presupuestado. La colocaci<97>n en Bonos de la Rep<9c>blica de Nicaragua (BRN) conjuntamente con la entrada de recursos externos han garantizado el financiamiento de dicho gasto. A julio de 2020, el Sector P<9c>blico no Financiero (SPNF) registr<97> un d<8e>ficit acumulado de 4,457.7 millones de c<97>rdobas (super<87>vit C$2,708.4 millones a julio 2019), consistente con un incremento de los ingresos del 2.9 por ciento interanual (principalmente por el incremento de las contribuciones sociales y otros ingresos, aunque los ingresos tributarios se redujeron) y un aumento de la erogaci<97>n total de 13.1 por ciento. La deuda p<9c>blica se mantiene en niveles sostenibles, aunque ha crecido en t<8e>rminos del PIB debido a la baja de este <9c>ltimo y en parte por el aumento de desembolsos de pr<8e>stamos concesionales de acreedores multilaterales y bilaterales (US$386.4 millones a septiembre 2020 vs. US$367.9 millones a septiembre 2019). Tambi<8e>n han aumentado las colocaciones de bonos gubernamentales, respecto al acumulado al mes de septiembre de 2019. El financiamiento obtenido ha permitido en buena medida, que pese a la situaci<97>n sanitaria que enfrenta el pa<92>s, la ejecuci<97>n financiera del Programa de Inversi<97>n P<9c>blica se mantenga en niveles adecuados (40% del total programado a junio 2020). El d<8e>ficit comercial de mercanc<92>as continu<97> disminuyendo en el acumulado enero-julio (-22.8% interanual) impulsado por un crecimiento de las exportaciones de mercanc<92>as del 9.5 por ciento interanual, favorecido por una mejora de los t<8e>rminos de intercambio del 16.1 por ciento. Tambi<8e>n incidi<97> en este resultado la reducci<97>n de las importaciones FOB de 1.9 por ciento, explicada principalmente por la menor factura petrolera. En el caso de las exportaciones de zona franca, la tendencia positiva del primer trimestre del a<96>o se revirti<97> a partir de abril, de tal forma que en el acumulado a julio registraron una reducci<97>n del 22.1 por ciento interanual, atribuible al impacto econ<97>mico de la pandemia. La mayor reducci<97>n se ha observado en las exportaciones de textiles, debido a la disminuci<97>n de la demanda de la econom<92>a estadounidense. Los flujos acumulados de la balanza de pagos a junio de 2020 muestran un super<87>vit de la cuenta corriente y una cuenta de capital positiva. En el neto, durante el primer semestre, se observ<97> una entrada de capitales. En el acumulado a julio, las remesas familiares crecieron 8.5 por ciento en t<8e>rminos interanuales, despu<8e>s de desacelerarse en abril cuando fueron de -9.1 por ciento. En tanto, como resultado del cierre de fronteras en otros pa<92>ses y las restricciones de viajes, los ingresos por exportaciones de servicios, entre los que se encuentra el turismo, que al primer trimestre hab<92>an sido de 360.9 millones de d<97>lares, alcanzaron los 137.8 millones d<97>lares en el segundo trimestre. Para lo que resta del a<96>o 2020, se prev<8e> una recuperaci<97>n de las principales variables de la econom<92>a real, la que podr<92>a acelerarse una vez que se levanten las restricciones de viajes y al comercio y la econom<92>a internacional se recupere. Tambi<8e>n se espera que las variables monetarias y financieras mantengan su tendencia de crecimiento. As<92>, se mantiene una proyecci<97>n de tasa de crecimiento del PIB de -4.5 por ciento, con un rango de entre +1 por ciento. Asimismo, se proyecta una tasa de inflaci<97>n de 3.7 por ciento, con un rango de entre +0.5 por ciento. La cuenta corriente de la balanza de pagos se espera que finalice con super<87>vit, impulsado por la mejora de la balanza comercial y de servicios. Se espera que los dep<97>sitos crezcan, que el cr<8e>dito presente colocaciones netas cada vez menos negativas y que las reservas internacionales contin<9c>en consolid<87>ndose. En cuanto a las finanzas p<9c>blicas, se espera mantenerlas controladas y un d<8e>ficit del sector p<9c>blico mayor que en 2019, el que incluye un mayor gasto en salud. Muchas gracias.

Title: Award Ceremony of the "Economics, Finance and Development Award 2020" and Presentation of the "Journal of Economics and Finance Vol. 7"
text: AWARD OF THE CONTEST "ECONOMIC, FINANCE AND DEVELOPMENT AWARD 2020" AND PRESENTATION OF THE "REVISTA DE ECONOMiA Y FINANZAS VOL 7" 26/11/2020 Good morning everyone. In the framework of the commemoration of the 60th anniversary of the Central Bank of Nicaragua, I would like to warmly welcome you to the award ceremony of the Economy, Finance and Development Award 2020 contest and the presentation of Vol. 7 of the Journal of Economy and Finance sponsored by the Central Bank of Nicaragua. For our Bank it is very gratifying to have the presence of researchers, Central Bank officials, media and special guests. We are also accompanied virtually: teachers, students and interested public. In this event we will hold the award of the Economy, Finance and Development Award 2020 contest. For this occasion, 8 investigations were presented addressing topics as varied as the influence of income and savings on the growth of the Gross Domestic Product; approaches to productivity estimation; the interrelationship of public and private investment in growth; the determinants of labor share of national income; the gender pay gap; economic growth and external constraint; fiscal multipliers; and systemic risk in Nicaraguan banking. The studies were prepared by Nicaraguan students and researchers. This year, the jury decided to award three prizes: 1. The first place was awarded to the work "The wage gap by gender: Triple penalty, woman, mother and informal", which participated under the pseudonym Macho Raton, and corresponds to the author Jonathan Josue Garcia Fuentes 2. The second place was awarded to the work "Systemic risk in banking in Nicaragua: An approach through interbank networks", pseudonym rmg-5, corresponding to the author Jeffrey Wilber Serrano Hernandez. 3. The third place was awarded to the work "Economic Growth and External Restriction in a Multisectoral and Multilateral Context: The Case of Nicaragua", pseudonym Desargues, corresponding to the author Jafet Alejandro Baca Obando. The winners on this occasion belong to the university community. The first as a master's student and research assistant at the University of Gottingen, Germany. The second, graduated from the career of Engineering in Economics and Business of the National University of Engineering of Nicaragua and the third place as a fifth-year student of Applied Economics of the Central American University. Congratulations to the winners. From these, we will know through a brief presentation, the fundamental aspects of their research in terms of method, results and policy implications. Additionally, this morning the Central Bank will present the seventh edition of the Journal of Economy and Finance, an instrument through which the Central Bank also promotes research and dissemination of studies on issues relevant to the national economy, especially those that contribute to the design and analysis of economic policies that favor inclusive and sustainable economic and financial growth. In the present volume of this journal, there are five research papers on various topics. The first: Symmetry or asymmetry in the adjustment of passive interest rates?; His Evidence for Nicaragua: the second: Effects of fiscal policy shocks in Nicaragua, evidenced through an SVAR analysis; the third: Implications of strengthening the dollar for the region of Central America and the Dominican Republic; the fourth: Minimum wage and its impact on wages: the case of Nicaragua; and the fifth: Drivers and brakes of entrepreneurship in Nicaragua: an analysis from a Kirznerian and Schumpeterian perspective. Finally, I thank everyone for their face-to-face and virtual participation in this event. The Central Bank of Nicaragua will continue its commitment to promote research, especially those studies that contribute to the design and analysis of economic policies aimed at promoting long-term economic and sustainable growth. Thank you very much and congratulations again to the winners.

En el marco de la conmemoraci<97>n del 60 aniversario del Banco Central de Nicaragua, quisiera darles la m<87>s cordial bienvenida al acto de premiaci<97>n del certamen Premio de Econom<92>a, Finanzas y Desarrollo 2020 y a la presentaci<97>n del Vol. 7 de la Revista de Econom<92>a y Finanzas que patrocina el Banco Central de Nicaragua. Para esta ocasi<97>n, se presentaron 8 investigaciones abordando temas tan variados como la influencia de la renta y ahorro en el crecimiento del Producto Interno Bruto; enfoques para la estimaci<97>n de la productividad; la interrelaci<97>n de la inversi<97>n p<9c>blica y privada en el crecimiento; los determinantes de la participaci<97>n laboral en el ingreso nacional; la brecha salarial de g<8e>nero; el crecimiento econ<97>mico y la restricci<97>n externa; los multiplicadores fiscales; y el riesgo sist<8e>mico en la banca de Nicaragua. Los estudios fueron elaborados por estudiantes e investigadores nicarag<9f>enses. Este a<96>o, el jurado calificador decidi<97> otorgar tres premios: 1. El primer lugar se otorg<97> al trabajo "La brecha salarial por g<8e>nero: Penalidad triple, mujer, madre e informal<d3>, que particip<97> bajo el seud<97>nimo Macho Rat<97>n, y corresponde al autor Jonathan Josu<8e> Garc<92>a Fuentes 2. El segundo lugar se concedi<97> al trabajo "Riesgo sist<8e>mico en la banca de Nicaragua: Una aproximaci<97>n a trav<8e>s de redes interbancarias", de seud<97>nimo rmg-5, correspondiente al autor Jeffrey Wilber Serrano Hern<87>ndez. 3. El tercer lugar se otorg<97> al trabajo "Crecimiento Econ<97>mico y la Restricci<97>n Externa en un Contexto Multisectorial y Multilateral: El Caso de Nicaragua", de seud<97>nimo Desargues, correspondiente al autor Jafet Alejandro Baca Obando. Los ganadores en esta ocasi<97>n pertenecen a la comunidad universitaria. El primero como estudiante de maestr<92>a y asistente de investigaci<97>n en la universidad de G<97>ttingen, Alemania. El segundo, graduado de la carrera de Ingenier<92>a en Econom<92>a y Negocios de la Universidad Nacional de Ingenier<92>a de Nicaragua y el tercer lugar como estudiante de quinto a<96>o de Econom<92>a Aplicada de la Universidad Centroamericana. Muchas felicidades a los ganadores. De ellos, conoceremos mediante una breve presentaci<97>n, los aspectos fundamentales de sus investigaciones en t<8e>rminos de m<8e>todo, resultados e implicaciones de pol<92>ticas. Adicionalmente, durante esta ma<96>ana el Banco Central realizar<87> la presentaci<97>n de la s<8e>ptima edici<97>n de la Revista de Econom<92>a y Finanzas, instrumento mediante el cual el Banco Central tambi<8e>n fomenta la investigaci<97>n y divulgaci<97>n de estudios en temas relevantes para la econom<92>a nacional, especialmente aquellos que contribuyen al dise<96>o y an<87>lisis de pol<92>ticas econ<97>micas que favorezcan un crecimiento econ<97>mico y financiero inclusive y sostenible. En el presente volumen de esta revista, se tienen cinco trabajos de investigaci<97>n en diversos temas. El primero: <c0>Simetr<92>a o asimetr<92>a en el ajuste de las tasas de inter<8e>s pasivas?; Su Evidencia para Nicaragua: el segundo: Efectos de shocks de pol<92>tica fiscal en Nicaragua, evidencia mediante un an<87>lisis SVAR; el tercero: Implicancias del fortalecimiento del d<97>lar para la regi<97>n de Centroam<8e>rica y Rep<9c>blica Dominicana; el cuarto: Salario m<92>nimo y su impacto en las remuneraciones: el Caso de Nicaragua; y el quinto: Drivers y frenos del emprendimiento en Nicaragua: un an<87>lisis desde una perspectiva Kirzneriana y Schumpeteriana. Para finalizar, agradezco a todos y a todas su participaci<97>n presencial y virtual en este evento. El Banco Central de Nicaragua continuar<87> con su compromiso de promover la investigaci<97>n, especialmente, aquellos estudios que contribuyan al dise<96>o y an<87>lisis de pol<92>ticas econ<97>micas orientadas a fomentar el crecimiento econ<97>mico y sostenible de largo plazo. Muchas gracias y felicidades nuevamente a los ganadores.

Title: CABEI Forum on Economic Situation of the Region and Perspectives 2021
text: CABEI FORUM ON THE ECONOMIC SITUATION OF THE REGION AND OUTLOOK 2021 17/12/2020 I would like to thank Mr. Dante Mossi, CABEI Executive President, for his kind invitation to participate in this event held in the framework of CABEI's 60th anniversary. This year the Central Bank of Nicaragua is also celebrating its 60th anniversary, so we share that spirit of institutional celebration. I would like to greet my fellow Central Bank Presidents in the region and the general public, who join us through digital media. In my case, I will do the tour they asked us and I will be deepening on the issues of projections and challenges in the next one. Measures implemented Without a doubt, 2020 has been a challenging year. The world has faced an unprecedented global crisis, both from the point of view of public health and the world economy. The reduction of productive activities and international trade, as well as the fall in consumption and the postponement of investment decisions, have harmed the economic and financial dynamics of the world and the region. In Central America and the Dominican Republic, we have seen significant external flows, such as tourism, exports of services and foreign investment, affected. Public finances were also pressured by reductions in tax collection and social security revenues. Central banks have taken action to mitigate the initial economic risks of this shock, and all institutions in the region set out to use the monetary instruments we already had and create new ones. We have agreed on some actions, such as the decisive reduction of policy or monetary benchmark interest rates, as well as keeping our liquidity lines open to commercial banks and implementing policies to make reserve requirements more flexible, it was also another area in common. In some cases, central banks have implemented innovative policies, as our legal frameworks have allowed, to encourage the delivery of credit in order to safeguard financial intermediation and avoid a negative spiral between credit and economic activity. In the case of the Central Bank of Nicaragua, the main policy measures that have been implemented are: Reductions in the Reference Rate of Monetary Reports, until accumulating a reduction of 375 basis points during 2020. The breadth of the interest rate corridor implemented by our institution was also reduced. Likewise, through the legal reserve policy, funds in cordobas were released to banks, for the equivalent of one percentage point of GDP. There are several elements that make this measure unconventional: the fact that it allows differentiated reserve requirements by bank and that it is conditioned to credit deliveries. Banks that use it will be able to reduce their reserve requirements in national currency by up to 10 points and this will happen over a period of three years. In addition, recognizing the high liquidity of the financial system and the environment of low international interest rates, the policy of rates of dollar instruments has remained relatively stable, which has led to the stability and accumulation of international reserves. Then in other results, in the banking financial system, a growth in deposits has been observed, as a response of companies and households to generate greater savings in the face of uncertainty, as well as by the lower mobilization of people. However, credit has been reduced by the increase in risk and a reduction in demand for it. Public finances, despite the increase in the deficit and a moderation in spending, have managed to achieve adequate financing. The external sector continues with a mixed performance, with indicators with good performance in merchandise exports and in the flow of family remittances, but with indicators with a lower level of tourism earnings and foreign direct investment. The combination of these elements has improved the external position producing a surplus in the current account of the balance of payments. On the other hand, the real sector has begun to show signs of recovery from the third quarter of the year, with growth rates in economic activity becoming less negative and a recovery in the participation of employment in the labor force. Main economic challenges With regard to economic challenges, the world in general, and our region in particular, continues to face uncertainty. In this environment, the main immediate public policy challenge will be to protect the population with COVID-19 vaccines, which are already in distribution. Economic recovery will also depend on the speed with which vaccination is implemented. That is why this is a priority of the first order. Therefore, it will also be a challenge to ensure that all countries can recover quickly from the pandemic, aspiring not to a "V" shaped recovery, as rapid recoveries are often described among economists, but to one that I would call a "check mark: /" ensuring an accelerated recovery with a growth rate higher than at the beginning of the crisis, until the economy returns to its long-term potential growth. I believe that the countries of Central America and the Dominican Republic should once again propose to be a leading region in economic growth in America, as happened a few years ago, for the benefit of our societies. On the other hand, monetary and financial policy must remain active, adjusting existing instruments in this context and creating new ones to strengthen economic recovery and continue to ensure macroeconomic stability, which must continue to be one of the main challenges, since vulnerabilities emerged with the pandemic, and it will be essential to redirect macroeconomic balance sheets by carrying out reforms and financial management processes that ensure the sustainability of debt and public finances. Macroeconomic projections With respect to the main economic projections, uncertainty reduced the projectability of economic models by widening the variance of estimates. The Central Bank of Nicaragua, since the beginning of the pandemic, has maintained an estimate of the GDP growth rate in 2020 of -4.5%. However, in light of the results observed in the GDP of the third quarter and the evolution of certain indicators of productive and commercial activity of the fourth quarter, the BCN now projects a less negative growth rate that could end between -1.5% and -2.5%, for the year 2020. In the case of 2021, the BCN has estimated a growth of 0.5%. But with the new observations, this rate will be higher, which we will be reviewing and releasing during the first months of 2021 once we obtain more information and that it is robust. Likewise, inflation in 2020 was estimated at 3.7% and with the results obtained in November we believe that it will be lower, expecting it to end between 2.0% and 3.0%. We also expect that in 2021 there will be an improvement in the participation of the employed population as part of the labor force, that the export sector will continue its positive dynamics and that public finances will remain stable and financed. Opportunities for economic integration and CABEI's role This new environment of great challenges reinforces the need for greater integration of the region, which is effectively taking place in trade and the financial system. The pandemic and the effects of hurricanes Eta and Iota impacted the region equally, reinforcing the argument of seeking joint financing solutions and coordinating monetary and financial policies. The role of the authorities in this reality should be to facilitate integration, factor mobility and promote efficiency, among others. The Central American Bank for Economic Integration can continue to play a fundamental role in this integration effort, supporting investment in its different programs, and strengthening the liquidity management program for central banks by increasing the line of financial assistance it has designed for this purpose, so that central banks can count on immediate unconditional solutions to future imbalances and financial stress. mobilizing resources within the region. For the Central Bank of Nicaragua, this program was a timely source of financing that helped confront the financial imbalances that occurred in 2018 and 2019. I reiterate my thanks to Mr Dante Mossi for the opportunity he gives us to share these views and my sincere greetings to my fellow central bank presidents in the region and to the other participants. Thanks a lot.
text_original: FORO DEL BCIE SOBRE SITUACI<ee>N ECON<ee>MICA DE LA REGI<ee>N Y PERSPECTIVAS 2021 17/12/2020 Quiero agradecer al Se<96>or Dante Mossi, Presidente Ejecutivo del BCIE, por su amable invitaci<97>n a participar en este evento que se celebra en el marco del 60 aniversario del BCIE. Este a<96>o el Banco Central de Nicaragua tambi<8e>n est<87> celebrando su 60 aniversario, as<92> que compartimos ese esp<92>ritu de celebraci<97>n institucional. Quisiera saludar a mis colegas presidentes de Bancos Centrales de la regi<97>n y al p<9c>blico en general, que nos acompa<96>a por los medios digitales. En mi caso, voy a hacer el recorrido que nos pidieron y estar<8e> profundizando sobre los temas de proyecciones y desaf<92>os en el siguiente. Medidas implementadas Sin duda alguna el a<96>o 2020 ha sido un a<96>o desafiante. El mundo ha enfrentado una crisis global sin precedentes, tanto desde el punto de vista de salud p<9c>blica, como de la econom<92>a mundial. La reducci<97>n de las actividades productivas y del comercio internacional, as<92> como la ca<92>da del consumo y la postergaci<97>n de las decisiones de inversi<97>n, han perjudicado la din<87>mica econ<97>mica y financiera del mundo y la regi<97>n. En Centro Am<8e>rica y Rep<9c>blica Dominicana hemos visto c<97>mo se han afectado flujos externos importantes, como el turismo, las exportaciones de servicios y la inversi<97>n extranjera. Tambi<8e>n las finanzas p<9c>blicas se vieron presionadas por las reducciones en la recaudaci<97>n tributaria y de los ingresos de la seguridad social. Los bancos centrales hemos emprendido acciones para mitigar los riesgos econ<97>micos iniciales de este choque y todas las instituciones de la regi<97>n nos dispusimos a utilizar los instrumentos monetarios con que ya cont<87>bamos y a crear nuevos. En algunas acciones hemos coincidido, como en la decidida reducci<97>n de las tasas de inter<8e>s de pol<92>tica o de referencia monetaria, as<92> como en mantener abiertas nuestras l<92>neas de liquidez hacia la banca comercial y en implementar pol<92>ticas de flexibilizaci<97>n del encaje legal, tambi<8e>n fue otra <87>rea en com<9c>n. En algunos casos, los bancos centrales hemos implementado pol<92>ticas novedosas, seg<9c>n lo han permitido nuestros marcos legales, para propiciar la entrega de cr<8e>dito con el objetivo de salvaguardar la intermediaci<97>n financiera y evitar se presente una espiral negativa entre el cr<8e>dito y la actividad econ<97>mica. En el caso del Banco Central de Nicaragua, las principales medidas de pol<92>tica que se han implementado son: Reducciones en la Tasa de Referencia de Reportos Monetarios, hasta acumular una rebaja de 375 puntos base durante 2020. Tambi<8e>n se redujo la amplitud del corredor de tasas de inter<8e>s que implementa nuestra instituci<97>n. Asimismo, a trav<8e>s de la pol<92>tica de encaje legal se liberaron fondos en c<97>rdobas a la banca, por el equivalente a un punto porcentual del PIB. Hay varios elementos que hacen que esta medida sea no convencional: el hecho que permite encajes diferenciados por banco y el que sea condicionada a las entregas de cr<8e>dito. Los bancos que la usen podr<87>n reducir sus encajes en moneda nacional hasta en 10 puntos y esto ocurrir<87> durante un periodo de tres a<96>os. Adicionalmente, reconociendo la alta liquidez del sistema financiero y el entorno de bajas tasas de inter<8e>s internacionales, se ha mantenido relativamente estable la pol<92>tica de tasas de los instrumentos en d<97>lares, lo que ha propiciado la estabilidad y acumulaci<97>n de las reservas internacionales. Luego en otros resultados, en el sistema financiero bancario, se ha observado un crecimiento de los dep<97>sitos, como respuesta de las empresas y las familias para generar mayores ahorros frente a la incertidumbre, as<92> como por la menor movilizaci<97>n de personas. Sin embargo, el cr<8e>dito se ha visto disminuido por el incremento del riesgo y por una reducci<97>n de la demanda de <8e>ste. Las finanzas p<9c>blicas, a pesar del aumento del d<8e>ficit y una moderaci<97>n del gasto, han conseguido alcanzar un financiamiento apropiado. El sector externo continua con un comportamiento mixto, con indicadores con buen desempe<96>o en las exportaciones de mercanc<92>as y en el flujo de remesas familiares, pero con indicadores con menor nivel en los ingresos por turismo y en la inversi<97>n extranjera directa. La combinaci<97>n de estos elementos ha mejorado la posici<97>n externa produciendo un super<87>vit en la cuenta corriente de la balanza de pagos. Por otra parte, el sector real ha comenzado a dar muestras de recuperaci<97>n a partir del tercer trimestre del a<96>o, present<87>ndose tasas de crecimiento de la actividad econ<97>mica cada vez menos negativas y una recuperaci<97>n en la participaci<97>n de la ocupaci<97>n en la fuerza laboral. Principales desaf<92>os econ<97>micos Respecto de los desaf<92>os econ<97>micos, el mundo en general y nuestra regi<97>n en particular, contin<9c>a confrontando incertidumbre. En ese entorno, el principal reto inmediato de pol<92>ticas p<9c>blicas ser<87> el proteger a la poblaci<97>n con las vacunas contra el COVID-19, las que ya se encuentran en distribuci<97>n. De la velocidad con que se aplique la vacunaci<97>n, depender<87> tambi<8e>n la recuperaci<97>n econ<97>mica. De ah<92> que sea esta, una prioridad de primer orden. Por ello, ser<87> tambi<8e>n un reto lograr que todos los pa<92>ses nos podamos recuperar r<87>pido de la pandemia, aspirando no a una recuperaci<97>n en forma de "V", como se suele describir a las recuperaciones r<87>pidas entre economistas, sino a una que yo llamar<92>a de "check mark: /" asegurando una recuperaci<97>n acelerada con una tasa de crecimiento superior a la del inicio de la crisis, hasta que la econom<92>a retorne a su crecimiento potencial de largo plazo. Considero que los pa<92>ses de Centro Am<8e>rica y Rep<9c>blica Dominicana deber<92>amos proponernos nuevamente ser una regi<97>n puntera en crecimiento econ<97>mico en Am<8e>rica, como ocurri<97> hace unos a<96>os, para beneficio de nuestras sociedades. Por otro lado, la pol<92>tica monetaria y financiera deber<87>n continuar activas, ajustando en este contexto los instrumentos existentes y creando nuevos para fortalecer la recuperaci<97>n econ<97>mica y continuar asegurando la estabilidad macroecon<97>mica que debe de continuar siendo uno de los principales desaf<92>os, ya que con la pandemia afloraron vulnerabilidades, y ser<87> fundamental reencauzar los balances macroecon<97>micos realizando reformas y procesos de ordenamiento financiero que aseguren la sostenibilidad de la deuda y de las finanzas p<9c>blicas. Proyecciones macro econ<97>micas Con respecto a las principales proyecciones econ<97>micas, la incertidumbre redujo la capacidad de proyecci<97>n de los modelos econ<97>micos al ampliar la varianza de las estimaciones. El Banco Central de Nicaragua, desde el inicio de la pandemia, ha mantenido una estimaci<97>n de la tasa de crecimiento del PIB en 2020 de -4.5%. Sin embargo, a la luz de los resultados observados en el PIB del tercer trimestre y de la evoluci<97>n de ciertos indicadores de actividad productiva y comercial del cuatro trimestre, el BCN ahora proyecta una tasa de crecimiento menos negativa que podr<92>a finalizar entre -1.5% y -2.5%, para el a<96>o 2020. En el caso del a<96>o 2021, el BCN ha estimado un crecimiento de 0.5%. Pero con las nuevas observaciones, esta tasa resultar<87> mayor, la que estaremos revisando y dando a conocer durante los primeros meses de 2021 una vez que obtengamos m<87>s informaci<97>n y que <8e>sta sea robusta. Asimismo, la inflaci<97>n en 2020 la estim<87>bamos en 3.7% y con los resultados obtenidos a noviembre creemos que <8e>sta ser<87> menor, esperando que finalice entre 2.0% y 3.0%. Tambi<8e>n esperamos que en 2021 se produzca una mejora en la participaci<97>n de la poblaci<97>n ocupada como parte de la fuerza laboral, que el sector exportador contin<9c>e su din<87>mica positiva y que las finanzas p<9c>blicas se mantengan estables y financiadas. Oportunidades para la integraci<97>n econ<97>mica y rol del BCIE Este nuevo entorno de grandes desaf<92>os refuerza la necesidad de una mayor integraci<97>n de la regi<97>n, la que efectivamente se est<87> produciendo en el comercio y en el sistema financiero. La pandemia y las afectaciones de los huracanes Eta e Iota impactaron a la regi<97>n por igual, lo que refuerza el argumento de buscar soluciones de financiamiento conjuntas y de coordinar pol<92>ticas monetarias y financieras. El papel de las autoridades en esta realidad debe ser facilitar la integraci<97>n, la movilidad de factores y propiciar la eficiencia, entre otros. El Banco Centroamericano de Integraci<97>n Econ<97>mica puede continuar jugando un papel fundamental en este esfuerzo de integraci<97>n, apoyando la inversi<97>n en sus diferentes programas, y reforzando el programa de gesti<97>n de liquidez a los bancos centrales aumentado la l<92>nea de asistencia financiera que tiene dise<96>ada para tal fin, para que los bancos centrales podamos contar con soluciones inmediatas no condicionadas frente a futuros desequilibrios y estr<8e>s financieros, movilizando recursos dentro de la regi<97>n. Para el Banco Central de Nicaragua, este programa fue una fuente oportuna de financiamiento que apoy<97> confrontar los desequilibrios financieros que ocurrieron en los a<96>os 2018 y 2019. Reitero mi agradecimiento al se<96>or Dante Mossi por la oportunidad que nos brinda para compartir estos puntos de vistas y mis saludos sinceros a mis colegas presidentes de bancos centrales de la regi<97>n y al resto de participantes. Muchas gracias.

Title: Award Ceremony of the "Painting Contest Nicaragua, Proud of its Culture and Traditions 2020"
text: AWARD CEREMONY OF THE "NICARAGUA PAINTING CONTEST, PROUD OF ITS CULTURE AND TRADITIONS 2020" - WORDS OF THE PRESIDENT OF THE BCN, OVIDIO REYES R. 16/02/2021 Good morning. I would like to warmly welcome you to the awards ceremony of the Painting Contest "Nicaragua, Proud of its Culture and Traditions 2020". For the Central Bank of Nicaragua it is very gratifying to have the presence of plastic artists, officials of our institution and the media. As is known, it is a contest that our institution holds year after year with the aim of promoting and encouraging artistic creativity among young Nicaraguan painters. This time the participants numbered 27, presenting works in various styles: figurative, realistic, primitivist, semi-abstract, among others. And we must highlight his fidelity to the proposed theme that was an exaltation of the cultural roots of our country. Thus, maritime landscapes of the Caribbean Coast and lacustrine and volcanic landscapes of the Pacific region were executed, scenes of typical dishes, portraits of popular characters, protagonists of our traditional festivals and the dances developed in them (such as La Gigantona in Leon and Los Mantudos in Chinandega); In short, conceptions of our myths and legends of Mesoamerican origin. I am pleased to congratulate the winners of the painting contest: "Nicaragua Proud of its Cultures and Traditions 2020" which are the following: First place: CHAVALO CHONTALEnO DREAMS AND PLAYS; THE FESTIVITIES OF JUIGALPA. It is an oil on canvas by Ricardo Augusto Gomez Miranda, to which I ask him to stand up, please, and give him his well-deserved applause. The work presents all aspects of the call, neatness and aesthetics, very well executed, visually pleasing, there is an interposition of forms, between abstract, figurative and cubism, quality in the management of space and cleanliness and harmony in color. Second place: RETURN. Acryllco on compressed cardboard and resin protection executed by Denis Xavier Granizo Ramirez, who is here with us and we give him his well-deserved applause, highlights a high chromatic content, original composition of muralist cut, made with four panels, simulating a colorful mosaic of shapes and figures that mark the national identity with good use of the resin technique. Folklore is present in the characters and dances, evidencing the customs, beliefs, myths and legends of Nicaragua. Good management of the landscape that allows to visit and identify places and the different artistic and cultural expressions of each of the departments of the country. The third place corresponds to the work. MY MOTHER PREPARING THE SYRUP. It is an oil on canvas executed by Ismael Antonio Tercero Ruiz, who is here also with us, the work stands out for its harmonious composition, color cleanliness, good use of drawing and correct handling of the contrast of light and shadow, in addition to the simplicity that the theme has, the content of the work is not saturated. Costumbrista theme, reflects the unity of the Nicaraguan family. Finally, I thank everyone for their participation in this event. The Central Bank of Nicaragua reiterates with this initiative its commitment to continue supporting the development of the plastic arts and the promotion of talent in Nicaraguan painting. I also inform you that as there were many works that were presented, we are going to promote them through the website of the Central Bank so that artists can make themselves known, even if they have not been among the first three places, and those who want to acquire them can also do so. Thanks a lot

Title: Presentation of the "State of the Economy and Perspectives as of March 2021"
text: PRESIDENT OF THE BCN PRESENTED THE "STATE OF THE ECONOMY AND PROSPECTS TO MARCH 2021" 24/03/2021 Good morning everyone, I am pleased to be before you this morning, presenting the State of the Economy Report and its Outlook to March 2021. This report summarizes the country's economic performance during 2020 and the beginning of 2021. During 2020, the evolution of the Nicaraguan economy, as well as the world economy and the region of Central America and the Dominican Republic, was affected by the COVID-19 pandemic. Additionally, Nicaragua was negatively affected by the effects of hurricanes Eta and Iota. However, until October 2020, Nicaragua registered one of the lowest impacts of the pandemic in the region, in terms of affecting production and trade. In this context, the economic authorities implemented a series of coordinated actions in order to preserve the macroeconomic and financial stability of the country and meet the immediate needs of the health crisis and climatic events. On the fiscal policy side, resources were allocated to meet increased spending on health and response to natural disasters. Social and public investment programs were maintained, while the job stability of public jobs was safeguarded. This was done through an active management of external and internal financing. For its part, the BCN adopted measures to support the recovery of the economy, favouring liquidity and the flow of credit by reducing interest rates, making the legal reserve policy conditionally more flexible, and reducing the exchange rate slippage rate of the cordoba against the dollar from 3 to 2 per cent. among other measures. The Gross Domestic Product (GDP) of 2020 registered a contraction of 2 percent (-3.7% in 2019), with a heterogeneous and unequal behavior between sectors. During the first quarter of 2020, the stabilization and recovery trajectory that had been observed since mid-2019 was maintained, showing positive growth. However, as of the second quarter, the impact of COVID-19 reversed the trend, mainly in activities related to the services and tourism sector. In line with a better performance of global economic activity, the second half of 2020 began to see a stabilization in most macroeconomic variables. Towards the months of November and December, hurricanes Eta and Iota affected exports and agricultural and fishing activities and caused severe damage and losses among the affected population. The recovery in economic activity from the second half of the year was also reflected in the labour market. According to the Continuous Household Survey (ECH), the global labor participation rate fell to 66.5 percent in the second quarter, resulting in an estimated reduction of 211,222 employed compared to the fourth quarter of 2019, and then recover in the third and fourth quarters (to 70.5%), resulting in an estimated increase of 218,456 employed compared to the second quarter of 2020, reaching levels similar to those observed at the beginning of the year. The same behavior registered the open unemployment rate, which went from 4.8 percent in the first quarter to 5.4 percent in the second quarter, however, it ended the fourth quarter at 4.8 percent, registering a reduction of 0.1 percentage points compared to the fourth quarter of 2019. On the other hand, affiliation to the INSS increased between August 2020 and February 2021 by 51,921 insured, after 5 consecutive months of net disaffiliation. In January-February 2021, affiliation grew by 22,191 new policyholders. Reduced global and domestic demand led to downward pressure on domestic food prices. Lower oil prices and international inflation, as well as lower cost pressure due to the lagged effect of the reduction of the shift slippage from 5 to 3 percent in October 2019, led to a reduction in inflation, standing at 2.93 percent at the end of 2020 (6.13% in 2019). In February 2021, year-on-year inflation was 3.77 percent (6.41% in February 2020) and, in terms of contribution, the greatest impulses came from the food and non-alcoholic beverages, miscellaneous goods and services, alcoholic beverages and tobacco, education and health divisions (which totaled 3.11 p.p.). The highest levels of year-on-year inflation were observed in alcoholic beverages and tobacco, food and non-alcoholic beverages, and health. Core inflation was 3.24 percent year-on-year (6.52% in February 2020). For its part, public finances showed prudent management, in a context of lower collection and greater spending pressures, mainly health to face the pandemic and emergency spending to attend to the victims of hurricanes Eta and Iota. Thus, in 2020, the Non-Financial Public Sector (NFPS) registered a deficit of 10,774.6 million cordobas (2.5% of GDP), which was financed with higher disbursements of external loans and placements of Bonds of the Republic of Nicaragua (BRN). Public debt remained at sustainable levels, standing at 64.8 percent of GDP at the end of 2020, although it has grown in terms of GDP, both due to the lower level of GDP, as well as the increase in disbursements of concessional loans from multilateral and bilateral creditors. In the external sector, a mixed performance has been observed. The improvement in the terms of trade (16% in 2020), the stability in the demand for merchandise exports and the growth of remittances (10% in 2020 and 12.1% in January 2021) favored a greater surplus of the current account of the balance of payments (US957.8 million in 2020, equivalent to 7.6% of GDP). Merchandise exports grew 5.8 percent year-on-year in 2020, while FOB merchandise imports had moderate growth (1.4%), mainly reflecting lower prices in the oil bill. For its part, the impact of the pandemic was directly reflected in variables such as tourism (-61.5%), FDI flows (-63.8%) and free zone exports (-14.7%). Monetary variables continue to perform positively, creating space to support the recovery. As of February 2021, all monetary aggregates reflect positive year-on-year growth rates, the foreign exchange market remains stable and the NCB continues to favour active management of liquidity in the financial system. In addition, in order to promote more lax conditions for financial intermediation, the NCB has continued with its policy of reducing interest rates. As of February, the BCN's Gross International Reserves (RIB) reached a balance of 3,276.7 million dollars (US64.8 million more than in December 2020), which represents a coverage of 2.93 times the monetary base and 8.25 months of imports. In 2020, RIBs increased 814.5 million. In terms of consolidated international reserves (which include the BCN's RIBs and those of the financial system), at the end of February they stood at 3,893.8 million dollars, which represented an increase of 119.9 million with respect to the end of 2020 (US3,773.9 million) and 767.6 million with respect to the end of 2019 (US3,126.2 million). For its part, financial intermediation has continued its stabilisation process in line with the actions of the economic authorities to safeguard financial stability. Thus, financial activity as of February reflected a double-digit increase in deposits (14.4%) and lower rates of reduction in bank credit (-3.5% year-on-year, the least negative since November 2018), maintaining high liquidity. Deposits grew as a result of uncertainty that led to lower aggregate spending, leading to an increase in precautionary household and business savings. The availability of the banking sector represented 40.4 percent of the obligations, the overdue portfolio and in judicial collection represented 3.8 percent of the gross portfolio and in January the capital adequacy stood at 21.8 percent (higher than the 10% required). The credit granted by microfinance institutions showed a recovery from the third quarter of the year, reflecting a positive variation rate of 2.4 percent in 2020 compared to 2019, as well as a reduction in arrears. For 2021, positive results are estimated in the main macroeconomic variables, considering the recovery trajectory observed at the end of 2020 and a favorable external outset, characterized by the global economic reactivation, although there is still uncertainty and risks that a resurgence of COVID-19, and its variants, will once again motivate the adoption of new confinements that slow down the recovery, or at least limit it. Thus, the Nicaraguan economy, after three years of negative growth rates, is projected to return to the path of positive growth with a growth rate of between 2.5 and 3.5 percent. This favorable performance would also be reflected in a recovery in the labor market. Likewise, the process of economic reactivation would be boosted by the significant increase in the Public Investment Program, product of the reconstruction of infrastructure damaged by hurricanes Eta and Iota, which nevertheless will affect the increase in the deficit of the non-financial public sector. On the other hand, an inflation rate is projected in a range of between 3.5 and 4.5 percent, which would reflect an increase compared to 2020, mainly due to the growth in international fuel prices and the increase in prices of the main economies, which are being adjusted by the greater demand and by the increase in costs caused by the reallocation of production and trade that happened afterwards. of the pandemic. Higher fuel prices could have a significant negative income effect, constituting a risk that could slow down the economic recovery. The deficit of the non-financial public sector will be moderate, although increasing compared to 2020, which is mainly associated with the higher expenditure on health and reconstruction financed with external resources received at the end of 2020. Thus, the deficit of the Non-Financial Public Sector is projected to end 2021 at 6.2 percent of GDP (2.5% in 2020). With regard to public debt, moderate growth is expected in terms of the debt-to-GDP indicator, as a result of higher external disbursements to finance the public investment programme. The variables of the external sector will continue with their dynamism, encouraged by the higher growth of the economies of the country's main trading partners. Thus, it is estimated that the surplus of the current account of the balance of payments will be reduced by higher merchandise imports associated with the recovery of the economy and the higher oil bill. Finally, the positive performance of monetary and financial variables is expected to continue, highlighting the reactivation of credit to the productive sectors. Gross international reserve levels of more than 3.2 billion are projected for 2021, roughly equivalent to 2.5 times the monetary base. The NCB's monetary policy will emphasize financial intermediation and the recovery of bank credit. However, no further cuts are expected in the TRM, which would rather react in correspondence to movements in international interest rates and domestic monetary conditions. Thank you for your attention.

Por su parte, la intermediaci<97>n financiera ha continuado su proceso de estabilizaci<97>n en l<92>nea con las acciones de las autoridades econ<97>micas para salvaguardar la estabilidad financiera. As<92>, la actividad financiera a febrero reflej<97> un aumento de dos d<92>gitos en los dep<97>sitos (14.4%) y menores tasas de reducci<97>n del cr<8e>dito bancario (-3.5% interanual, la menos negativa desde noviembre de 2018), manteni<8e>ndose una elevada liquidez. Los dep<97>sitos crecieron como resultado de la incertidumbre que condujo a un menor gasto agregado, lo que conllev<97> a un aumento del ahorro precautorio de los hogares y las empresas. Las disponibilidades del sector bancario representaron el 40.4 por ciento de las obligaciones, la cartera vencida y en cobro judicial represent<97> el 3.8 por ciento de la cartera bruta y a enero la adecuaci<97>n de capital se ubic<97> en 21.8 por ciento (superior al 10% requerido).
