Para 2021 se estiman resultados positivos en las principales variables macroecon<97>micas, considerando la trayectoria de recuperaci<97>n observada al cierre de 2020 y un extorno externo favorable, caracterizado por la reactivaci<97>n econ<97>mica mundial, aunque persiste a<9c>n la incertidumbre y riesgos de que un rebrote del COVID-19, y sus variantes, vuelva a motivar la adopci<97>n de nuevos confinamientos que frenen la recuperaci<97>n, o al menos la limiten. As<92>, se proyecta que la econom<92>a nicarag<9f>ense, despu<8e>s de tres a<96>os de tasas negativas de crecimiento, retorne a la senda de crecimiento positivo con una tasa de crecimiento de entre 2.5 y 3.5 por ciento. Este desempe<96>o favorable tambi<8e>n se ver<92>a reflejado en una recuperaci<97>n en el mercado laboral. As<92> mismo, el proceso de reactivaci<97>n econ<97>mica se ver<92>a impulsado por el importante incremento en el Programa de Inversi<97>n P<9c>blica, producto de la reconstrucci<97>n de infraestructura da<96>ada por los huracanes Eta e Iota, lo que no obstante incidir<87> en el aumento del d<8e>ficit del sector p<9c>blico no financiero. Por otra parte, se proyecta una tasa de inflaci<97>n en un rango de entre 3.5 a 4.5 por ciento, lo que reflejar<92>a un incremento respecto a 2020, debido principalmente al crecimiento en los precios internacionales de los combustibles y el aumento de precios de las principales econom<92>as, los que se est<87>n ajustando por la mayor demanda y por el aumento de costos originado por la reasignaci<97>n de la producci<97>n y el comercio que sucedi<97> despu<8e>s de la pandemia. El alza de los precios del combustible podr<92>a ocasionar un efecto ingreso negativo importante, constituy<8e>ndose en un riesgo que podr<92>a ralentizar la recuperaci<97>n econ<97>mica. El d<8e>ficit del sector p<9c>blico no financiero ser<87> moderado, aunque increment<87>ndose con respecto a 2020, lo que est<87> principalmente asociado al mayor gasto en salud y reconstrucci<97>n financiado con recursos externos recibidos a finales de 2020. As<92> el d<8e>ficit del Sector P<9c>blico No Financiero se proyecta finalice 2021 en 6.2 por ciento del PIB (2.5% en 2020). Con relaci<97>n a la deuda p<9c>blica se espera un crecimiento moderado en t<8e>rminos del indicador de deuda a PIB, producto de los mayores desembolsos externos para financiar el programa de inversi<97>n p<9c>blica. Las variables del sector externo continuar<87>n con su dinamismo, incentivadas por el mayor crecimiento de las econom<92>as de los principales socios comerciales del pa<92>s. As<92>, se estima que el super<87>vit de la cuenta corriente de la balanza de pagos se reduzca por mayores importaciones de mercanc<92>as asociadas con la recuperaci<97>n de la econom<92>a y la mayor factura petrolera. Finalmente, se espera que contin<9c>e el desempe<96>o positivo de las variables monetarias y financieras, destacando la reactivaci<97>n del cr<8e>dito a los sectores productivos. Para 2021 se proyectan niveles de reservas internacionales brutas superiores a los 3,200 millones de d<97>lares, equivalente aproximadamente a 2.5 veces la base monetaria. La pol<92>tica monetaria del BCN har<87> <8e>nfasis en la intermediaci<97>n financiera y la recuperaci<97>n del cr<8e>dito bancario. Aunque, no se esperan rebajas adicionales en la TRM, la que m<87>s bien reaccionar<92>a en correspondencia a los movimientos de las tasas de inter<8e>s internacionales y de las condiciones monetarias internas. Les agradezco su atenci<97>n.

Title: Presentation of the Financial Stability Report as of December 2020
text: PRESIDENT OF THE BCN PRESENTS FINANCIAL STABILITY REPORT TO DECEMBER 2020-REMARKS BY THE PRESIDENT OF THE BCN, OVIDIO REYES R 09/04/2021 Good morning everyone. It is a pleasure for me to address you on this occasion to present the Financial Stability Report, corresponding to the year 2020, prepared by the Central Bank of Nicaragua, and which will be available on the website of our institution from today. Since the 2009 international financial crisis, the world's central banks and financial regulators have paid more attention to monitoring major financial markets to try to identify problems that could lead to a financial crisis. This is because financial markets are volatile in nature and react abruptly to any news or indication that reduces the returns or value of their investments. In this way, today most central banks carry out an analysis of financial stability, as part of their activity of crisis prevention and promotion of financial stability. The objective of the 2020 Financial Stability Report, prepared by the Central Bank of Nicaragua, is to monitor the main vulnerabilities and identify potential systemic risks that could affect financial stability. The Report also incorporates considerations to mitigate these risks and reduce their impact, should they materialize. The promotion of the stability of the National Financial System is a function assigned to the BCN in its Organic Law. This function is also established in the Law establishing the Financial Stability Committee (CEF), which is the inter-institutional coordination body to safeguard national financial stability and is composed of the Central Bank of Nicaragua (BCN), which chairs it, the Ministry of Finance and Public Credit (MHCP), the Superintendency of Banks and Other Financial Institutions (SIBOIF). the National Microfinance Commission (CONAMI) and the Deposit Guarantee Fund (FOGADE). The IEF includes a description of the international environment and the national financial environment. It also presents an analysis of the financial indicators for monitoring financial stability, that is, those that could be reflecting the accumulation of vulnerabilities, such as: asset valuation, liquidity of the financial system, leverage of the financial system, indebtedness of companies and households and public indebtedness. The Report identifies risks that could affect financial stability, conducting stress tests, or stress tests to assess the ability (strength) of the financial system to address these risks. The Financial Stability Report highlights that, during 2020, Nicaragua faced the global COVID-19 pandemic in difficult conditions, having been subjected to financial stress for three years that reduced its margins of action. However, the country was able to confront the pandemic and continue to strengthen financial stability. The economic authorities implemented actions to energize the financial markets with the aim of ensuring the provision of mechanisms for the financial system to function properly. As a result, major financial markets remain stable. The exchange market reduced its volatility. The money market remains active and dynamic. The stock market has increased its transactions as a result of the largest monetary operations and the greater placements of Bonds of the Republic. The credit market, although it has declined, it has done so at less and less negative rates. The mortgage market has limitations due to the lack of long-term funds. The insurance market continues to increase its risk hedging operations. Meanwhile, the remaining asset market shows signs of stabilisation due to the perception of a temporary disruption from the pandemic. The pandemic generated uncertainty with volatility in financial markets. However, the main financial indicators reflect stability and in several cases reduced vulnerabilities, as follows: 1. The valuation of asset prices does not present major imbalances. In most cases these remain stable and their evolution corresponds to the risk perceptions of each market. 2. The pandemic did not cause an increase in demand for aggregate liquidity, which is at adequate levels. Economic agents responded to the shock by reducing aggregate private spending and increasing deposits 3. The leverage of the financial system has been reduced, mainly from external financiers, although obligations to the public have increased. While the financial burden has fallen due to lower debt and lower interest rates in its main sources of funding. 4. The indebtedness of households and firms continued to fall faster than economic activity, although this diminishes the capacity to generate higher spending. However, compliance with both internal and external obligations has continued. 5. Public debt continued to rise, but under concessional conditions of low interest rates and long repayment terms. The sustainability analysis of public debt shows a sustainability condition. Despite the fact that the main financial indicators contain vulnerabilities, risks remain, such as the risk of greater effects on production and trade that could occur due to the uncertainty still prevailing due to the pandemic. Additionally, the risk of a loss of credit dynamism is identified, which is necessary to reverse to ensure financial stability in the medium and long term. As well as the risk of increases in international fuel prices that would increase costs and drain part of the national disposable income abroad. In the analysis of stress scenarios simulated in this Report, Nicaragua is able to withstand each of the three risks identified when evaluated separately, thus presenting the economy and the financial system with great resilience. However, other global events and risks, such as climate change and natural disasters, will need to be monitored in order to assess financial conditions and stability on an ongoing basis. The financial authorities, depending on the evolution of credit and the pandemic, will promote greater financial intermediation to finance economic activities, adopting a proactive monetary policy. The monetary authority will also promote financial stability by maintaining a loose monetary policy with the low monetary reference rate, at its current levels. Finally, it will be necessary in the medium term to strengthen the current financial legal framework that allows it to adapt to the new environment, such as the implementation of a macroprudential policy, the promotion of financial inclusion, new regulations on financial technologies and payment systems and means, as well as everything that benefits intermediation and financial services. Thanks a lot
text_original: PRESIDENTE DEL BCN PRESENTA INFORME DE ESTABILIDAD FINANCIERA A DICIEMBRE 2020-PALABRAS DEL PRESIDENTE DEL BCN, OVIDIO REYES R PRESIDENTE DEL BCN PRESENTA INFORME DE ESTABILIDAD FINANCIERA A DICIEMBRE 2020-PALABRAS DEL PRESIDENTE DEL BCN, OVIDIO REYES R 09/04/2021 Muy buenos d<92>as a todos. Es un placer para m<92> dirigirme a ustedes en esta ocasi<97>n para presentar el Informe de Estabilidad Financiera, correspondiente al a<96>o 2020, elaborado por el Banco Central de Nicaragua, y que estar<87> disponible en la p<87>gina web de nuestra instituci<97>n desde hoy. A partir de la crisis financiera internacional de 2009, los bancos centrales del mundo y las entidades reguladoras financieras han prestado m<87>s atenci<97>n al monitoreo de los principales mercados financieros para tratar de identificar problemas que pudiesen devenir en una crisis financiera. Esto se debe a que los mercados financieros son de naturaleza vol<87>til y reaccionan abruptamente frente a cualquier noticia o indicio que reduzca los rendimientos o el valor de sus inversiones. De esta manera, hoy la mayor<92>a de los bancos centrales realizan un an<87>lisis de la estabilidad financiera, como parte de su actividad de prevenci<97>n de crisis y promoci<97>n de la estabilidad financiera. El objetivo del Informe de Estabilidad Financiera 2020, elaborado por el Banco Central de Nicaragua es monitorear las principales vulnerabilidades e identificar los riesgos potenciales de alcance sist<8e>mico que pudieran afectar a la estabilidad financiera. El Informe tambi<8e>n incorpora consideraciones para mitigar estos riesgos y reducir su impacto, en caso de que llegasen a materializarse. La promoci<97>n de la estabilidad del Sistema Financiero Nacional es una funci<97>n consignada al BCN en su Ley Org<87>nica. Tambi<8e>n esta funci<97>n se encuentra establecida en la Ley constitutiva del Comit<8e> de Estabilidad Financiera (CEF), que es la instancia de coordinaci<97>n interinstitucional para resguardar la estabilidad financiera nacional y que est<87> compuesto por el Banco Central de Nicaragua (BCN) que lo preside, el Ministerio de Hacienda y Cr<8e>dito P<9c>blico (MHCP), la Superintendencia de Bancos y Otras Instituciones Financieras (SIBOIF), la Comisi<97>n Nacional de Microfinanzas (CONAMI) y el Fondo de Garant<92>a de Dep<97>sitos (FOGADE). El IEF incluye una descripci<97>n del entorno internacional y del entorno financiero nacional. Tambi<8e>n presenta un an<87>lisis de los indicadores financieros de seguimiento a la estabilidad financiera, es decir, aquellos que pudieran estar reflejando la acumulaci<97>n de vulnerabilidades, tales como: valoraci<97>n de activos, liquidez del sistema financiero, apalancamiento del sistema financiero, endeudamiento de empresas y hogares y endeudamiento p<9c>blico. El Informe identifica los riesgos que podr<92>an afectar la estabilidad financiera, realizando pruebas de resistencia, o pruebas de estr<8e>s para evaluar la capacidad (fortaleza) del sistema financiero para confrontar estos riesgos. El Informe de Estabilidad Financiera destaca que, durante 2020, Nicaragua confront<97> la pandemia mundial del COVID-19 en condiciones dif<92>ciles, al haber estado sometida a estr<8e>s financiero durante tres a<96>os que redujo sus m<87>rgenes de acci<97>n. No obstante, el pa<92>s pudo confrontar la pandemia y continuar afianzando la estabilidad financiera. Las autoridades econ<97>micas implementaron acciones para dinamizar los mercados financieros con el objetivo de asegurar la provisi<97>n de mecanismos para que el sistema financiero funcionara de manera apropiada. Como resultado, los principales mercados financieros se mantienen estables. El mercado cambiarlo redujo su volatilidad. El mercado monetario se mantiene activo y din<87>mico. El mercado de valores ha aumentado sus transacciones por efecto de las mayores operaciones monetarias y por las mayores colocaciones de Bonos de la Rep<9c>blica. El mercado de cr<8e>dito si bien ha disminuido, lo ha hecho a tasas cada vez menos negativas. El mercado hipotecario presenta limitaciones debido a la falta de fondos de largo plazo. El mercado de seguros contin<9c>a aumentando sus operaciones de cobertura frente a riesgos. Mientras que, el restante mercado de activos presenta indicios de estabilizaci<97>n por la percepci<97>n de perturbaci<97>n transitoria de la pandemia. La pandemia gener<97> incertidumbre con volatilidad en los mercados financieros. Sin embargo, los principales indicadores financieros reflejan estabilidad y en varios casos reducci<97>n de vulnerabilidades, como sigue: 1. La valoraci<97>n de los precios de los activos no presenta mayores desequilibrios. En la mayor<92>a de los casos estos se mantienen estables y su evoluci<97>n se corresponde con las percepciones de riesgos de cada mercado. 2. La pandemia no ocasion<97> un aumento de la demanda de liquidez agregada, la que se encuentra en niveles adecuados. Los agentes econ<97>micos respondieron a la perturbaci<97>n reduciendo el gasto agregado privado y aumentando los dep<97>sitos 3. El apalancamiento del sistema financiero se ha venido reduciendo, principalmente el proveniente de financiadores externos, aunque se han aumentado las obligaciones con el p<9c>blico. Mientras que la carga financiera ha bajado por la menor deuda y por la baja en las tasas de inter<8e>s en sus principales fuentes de fondeo. 4. El endeudamiento de los hogares y empresas continu<97> reduci<8e>ndose a mayor velocidad que la actividad econ<97>mica, aunque esto disminuye la capacidad para generar un mayor gasto. Sin embargo, ha continuado el cumplimiento de las obligaciones tanto internas como externas. 5. La deuda p<9c>blica continu<97> aumentando, pero en condiciones concesionales de bajas tasas de inter<8e>s y largos plazos de repago. El an<87>lisis de sostenibilidad de la deuda p<9c>blica muestra una condici<97>n de sostenibilidad. A pesar de que los principales indicadores financieros presentan una contenci<97>n de las vulnerabilidades, a<9c>n persisten riesgos, como el riesgo de mayores afectaciones a la producci<97>n y el comercio que podr<92>an ocurrir por la incertidumbre a<9c>n prevaleciente por la pandemia. Adicionalmente, se identifica el riesgo de una p<8e>rdida de dinamismo del cr<8e>dito que es necesario revertir para asegurar la estabilidad financiera de mediano y largo plazo. As<92> como el riesgo de aumentos en los precios internacionales de los combustibles que aumentar<92>an los costos y drenar<92>an parte del ingreso nacional disponible hacia el exterior. En el an<87>lisis de escenarios de estr<8e>s simulados en este Informe, Nicaragua est<87> en la capacidad de resistir cada uno de los tres riesgos identificados cuando se eval<9c>an por separado, presentando as<92> la econom<92>a y el sistema financiero una gran resiliencia. Sin embargo, se deber<87>n monitorear otros acontecimientos y riesgos globales, como el del cambio clim<87>tico y desastres naturales, para poder ir realizando una evaluaci<97>n de las condiciones y estabilidad financiera sobre una base continua. Las autoridades financieras, dependiendo de la evoluci<97>n del cr<8e>dito y de la pandemia, promover<87>n una mayor intermediaci<97>n financiera para el financiamiento de las actividades econ<97>micas, adoptando una pol<92>tica monetaria proactiva. Tambi<8e>n la autoridad monetaria promover<87> la estabilidad financiera manteniendo una pol<92>tica monetaria laxa con la tasa de referencia monetaria baja, en sus actuales niveles. Finalmente, se requerir<87> en el mediano plazo fortalecer el marco legal financiero vigente que permita adaptarlo al nuevo entorno, como la implementaci<97>n de una pol<92>tica macroprudencial, la promoci<97>n de la inclusi<97>n financiera, nuevas regulaciones sobre tecnolog<92>as financieras y de los sistemas y medios de pagos, as<92> como todo aquello que redunde en beneficio de la intermediaci<97>n y de los servicios financieros. Muchas Gracias

Title: Scheme and formulation of the Monetary and Exchange Policy of the Central Bank of Nicaragua, on the occasion of the completion of the Monetary and Exchange Policy Course 2021
text: OUTLINE AND FORMULATION OF THE MONETARY AND EXCHANGE POLICY OF THE CENTRAL BANK OF NICARAGUA, ON THE OCCASION OF THE CULMINATION OF THE MONETARY AND EXCHANGE POLICY COURSE 2021 WORDS OF THE PRESIDENT OF THE BCN, OVIDIO REYES R. 21/05/2021 Introduction Good morning, everyone. It is a pleasure for me to present the closing remarks of the 2021 monetary and exchange policy course carried out by the Central Bank of Nicaragua and in which 19 people and virtually 64 people have participated in person. Since last year the Central Bank of Nicaragua decided to promote these open and free courses in Economics and Finance, so that a wide public could know about the functions performed by the Central Bank of Nicaragua, which allows them a better understanding of the publications and statistics provided by our institution. Thus, the courses have been organized into five thematic areas: monetary and exchange rate policy, financial stability, financial operations, payment systems and economic statistics. Due to its high demand, we have been limiting the participation of one course per person, which does not prevent these same people from continuing to take the remaining courses in the future. I believe that these courses have been well used by you and we hope that in the future you will continue to show your interest in our trainings, as well as disseminate them among your family and friends. Monetary and exchange rate policy scheme During these two weeks of the course on monetary and exchange policy, you have been able to learn from our officials the conceptual and practical elements from which the Central Bank formulates and executes monetary and exchange policy for the fulfillment of its central objective, which consists of the stability of the national currency. For this, a conceptual scheme is designed that we have been identifying with the passage of time and that we believe is the one that corresponds to the practice of economic agents. The Nicaraguan reality indicates that the economy benefits greatly from free trade, both internal and external, from the free movement of goods and services and from a free financial market, so monetary and exchange rate policy favors predictability on the nominal exchange rate. The exchange arrangement is such that the Central Bank does not control the money supply, but rather is determined by the demand for money, so that it is endogenous. Thus, a greater monetary demand for cordobas is satisfied through the sale of foreign currency to the Central Bank and a reduction in the monetary demand for cordobas is compensated through the purchase of foreign currency from the Central Bank. Thus, monetary and aggregate expenditure imbalances manifest themselves through international reserves, given the exchange rate set by the Central Bank, and are ultimately reflected in the current account of the balance of payments. The Central Bank announces the official exchange rate month by month, while active and passive financial operations at the national level are adjusted according to their evolution. Other transactions in the goods and services markets, as well as contracts, are also indexed to the evolution of the official exchange rate. As a key component, the Central Bank guarantees the free convertibility of Cordoba against the Dollar, thus operating an unrestricted free market for all types of operations in all markets in which foreign currency is traded, without there being any obligation for agents and collecting institutions to inform the Central Bank. In this way, the monetary and exchange rate policy scheme of the Central Bank establishes an intermediate objective for exchange rate policy and two intermediate objectives for monetary policy. In the case of exchange rate policy, the intermediate objective is to anchor price adjustments and expectations based on the fixing of the nominal exchange rate, using as an instrument the pre-announced daily devaluations, known as a change slippage, and establishing a follow-up of the exchange rate gap and the exchange table of the BCN to evaluate the behavior of the foreign exchange market. On the other hand, in the case of monetary policy, the first intermediate objective is to maintain adequate levels of international reserves, using as instruments open market operations and legal reserve requirements, evaluating the evolution of the coverage of gross international reserves with respect to the monetary base as the variable for monitoring monetary balance. The second intermediate objective is related to favoring the liquidity of the financial system, using as an instrument short-term open market operations, monetary deposits and liquidity advances, monitoring the liquidity ratios of the financial system and interbank interest rates to evaluate this market. This scheme is subject to the use of the slippage of the exchange rate as a nominal anchor of prices and expectations, so monetary policy must use its instruments to ensure adequate levels of international reserves that support it, as well as favor the liquidity of the financial system that is consistent with the above objectives. Thus, through exchange rate policy, the Central Bank directly affects domestic prices, which are additionally determined by variations in international prices and by other factors that affect the supply and demand of domestic goods and services that are not under the control of the monetary authority. This scheme introduces rigidities, the main one being the limited capacity to issue money and absorb the exchange rate in the face of internal and external shocks. However, it has worked reasonably well for the Nicaraguan economy since 1993, favoring price stability, and is considered to remain adequate under current conditions. The advantage of this scheme is its flexibility, because it allows alternating between price objectives, competitiveness and financial stability, and which have been highlighted at different times of past Nicaraguan economic practice. However, in recent experience, stability would change to anchor expectations and thus obtain low and stable inflation is the intention of monetary and exchange rate policy that prevails. Monetary policy instruments The main monetary and exchange rate policy instruments of the Central Bank are: the daily fixing of the official exchange rate, open market operations, legal reserve requirements, monetary deposits and loans and liquidity advances. All these instruments are activated at different times to either inject or absorb liquidity, which allows to satisfy the objectives and goals contemplated in the monetary program of the Central Bank. The way in which these instruments are transmitted in the economy is widely studied and contained in the different economic research documents published by the Central Bank and available on its website. These studies are relevant for decision-making since they parameterize sensitivity analyses, help detect the interrelationships between sectors and establish the lags with which monetary policy operates. For example, through research we have found that it takes about three quarters for changes in the exchange rate to be passed on to domestic prices. We have also detected an important correlation between external conditions and variations in national real economic activity, with the economy benefiting from openness and competition. Finally, important transmission channels have been identified between market and external interest rates to the real economy. From these studies, we were able to infer that there was room to influence interest rates and the different liquidity markets, despite the fact that the Central Bank has adopted a fixed exchange scheme with pre-announced slippage. The reason for this incidence is that in the short run the real economy reacts to movements in monetary instruments, even though it is established that in the long run these are neutral. In this way, the Central Bank introduced since 2019 the Monetary Reference Rate as the main instrument for signaling the monetary policy position of the Central Bank. This rate rises when financial conditions require moderation and falls when monetary conditions need to be accommodative. The monetary reference rate is accompanied by a rate for the monetary deposit window and another rate for the monetary reporting window. Both rates constitute the lower and upper bound, respectively, of what the Central Bank has termed the interest rate corridor. The lower limit refers to the possibility of making deposits in the Central Bank for those operations that were not placed through competitive auction, while the upper limit refers to the possibility of being able to receive liquidity through reports for those operations that were also not placed through competitive auction mechanisms. This scheme is transparent based on public operations with reference rates and windows to which all financial agents have access. The magnitude of the Central Bank's monetary operations has become increasingly relevant. For example, in 2020 the monetary absorption operations were the following: open market operations 519,181 million cordobas, monetary deposits 112,099 million cordobas and the legal reserve 2,360 million cordobas, to total absorption operations for 633,640 million cordobas and expansion for 628,669 million cordobas. On the other hand, operations in foreign currency of absorption were: open market operations for 1,574 million dollars, monetary deposits 20,665 million dollars and reserve requirements 114 million dollars, for a total amount of 22,354 million dollars in absorption and 21,944 million dollars of expansion. Conclusion Finally, allow me to conclude by congratulating yourself on having successfully completed this training, motivating you to continue investigating, analyzing and listening to monetary and financial issues in Nicaragua. It helps a lot that more and more Nicaraguans have access to this information in order to have a greater understanding of our economic reality. I also invite you to follow up on the rest of the courses, even if you do not take them in person or virtually as is happening in this case, since we will give access to all the material through our website, so that those interested can also study on their own. I thank you this morning for your participation and for my wishes for a good weekend. Thanks a lot
text_original: ESQUEMA Y FORMULACI<ee>N DE LA POL<ea>TICA MONETARIA Y CAMBIARIA DEL BANCO CENTRAL DE NICARAGUA, CON MOTIVO DE LA CULMINACI<ee>N DEL CURSO DE POL<ea>TICA MONETARIA Y CAMBIARIA 2021 PALABRAS DEL PRESIDENTE DEL BCN, OVIDIO REYES R. ESQUEMA Y FORMULACI<ee>N DE LA POL<ea>TICA MONETARIA Y CAMBIARIA DEL BANCO CENTRAL DE NICARAGUA, CON MOTIVO DE LA CULMINACI<ee>N DEL CURSO DE POL<ea>TICA MONETARIA Y CAMBIARIA 2021 PALABRAS DEL PRESIDENTE DEL BCN, OVIDIO REYES R. 21/05/2021 Introducci<97>n Buenos d<92>as a todos. Es un placer para m<92> presentar las palabras de clausura del curso de pol<92>tica monetaria y cambiar<92>a 2021 que realiza el Banco Central de Nicaragua y en el que han participado presencialmente 19 personas y virtualmente 64 personas. Desde el a<96>o pasado el Banco Central de Nicaragua decidi<97> impulsar estos cursos abiertos y gratuitos en Econom<92>a y Finanzas, para que un p<9c>blico amplio pudiese conocer sobre las funciones que realiza el Banco Central de Nicaragua, que les permita una mejor comprensi<97>n de las publicaciones y estad<92>sticas que provee nuestra instituci<97>n. Es as<92> como, los cursos se han organizado en cinco <87>reas tem<87>ticas: pol<92>tica monetaria y cambiar<92>a, estabilidad financiera, operaciones financieras, sistemas de pagos y estad<92>sticas econ<97>micas. Debido a su alta demanda, hemos estado limitando la participaci<97>n de un curso por persona, lo que no impide que en un futuro estas mismas personas puedan continuar tomando los restantes cursos. Creo que estos cursos han sido bien aprovechados por ustedes y esperamos que en el futuro contin<9c>en mostrando su inter<8e>s por nuestras capacitaciones, as<92> como tambi<8e>n divulg<87>ndolos entre sus familiares y amigos. Esquema de pol<92>tica monetaria y cambiar<92>a Durante estas dos semanas del curso de pol<92>tica monetaria y cambiar<92>a, ustedes han podido conocer de parte de nuestros funcionarios los elementos conceptuales y pr<87>cticos a partir de los cuales el Banco Central formula y ejecuta la pol<92>tica monetaria y cambiar<92>a para el cumplimiento de su objetivo central, que consiste en la estabilidad de la moneda nacional. Para ello se dise<96>a un esquema conceptual que hemos venido identificando con el paso del tiempo y que creemos que es el que se corresponde con la pr<87>ctica de los agentes econ<97>micos. La realidad nicarag<9f>ense indica que la econom<92>a se beneficia mucho del libre comercio, tanto interno como externo, de la libre circulaci<97>n de bienes y servicios y de un mercado financiero libre, por lo que la pol<92>tica monetaria y cambiar<92>a favorece la previsibilidad sobre el tipo de cambio nominal. El arreglo cambiarlo es tal que el Banco Central no controla la oferta monetaria, sino que, m<87>s bien, est<87> determinada por la demanda de dinero, por lo que aquella resulta end<97>gena. As<92>, una mayor demanda monetaria de c<97>rdobas se satisface a trav<8e>s de la venta de divisas al Banco Central y una reducci<97>n de la demanda monetaria de c<97>rdobas se compensa a trav<8e>s de la compra de divisas al Banco Central. Por lo tanto, los desequilibrios monetarios y de gasto agregado se manifiestan a trav<8e>s de las reservas internacionales, dado el tipo de cambio prefijado por el Banco Central y, en <9c>ltima instancia, se reflejan en la cuenta corriente de la balanza de pagos. El Banco Central anuncia mes a mes el tipo de cambio oficial, mientras que las operaciones financieras activas y pasivas a nivel nacional se ajustan conforme su evoluci<97>n. Tambi<8e>n otras operaciones en los mercados de bienes y servicios, as<92> como de los contratos, se indexan a la evoluci<97>n del tipo de cambio oficial. Como componente clave, el Banco Central garantiza la libre convertibilidad del C<97>rdoba frente al D<97>lar, funcionando as<92> un mercado libre irrestricto para todo tipo de operaciones en todos los mercados en que se tranzan divisas, sin que exista ninguna obligatoriedad para los agentes y las instituciones captadoras de enterarlas al Banco Central. De esta manera, el esquema de pol<92>tica monetaria y cambiar<92>a del Banco Central establece un objetivo intermedio para la pol<92>tica cambiar<92>a y dos objetivos intermedios para la pol<92>tica monetaria. En el caso de la pol<92>tica cambiar<92>a, el objetivo intermedio consiste en anclar los ajustes de precios y las expectativas a partir de la fijaci<97>n del tipo de cambio nominal, utilizando como instrumento las devaluaciones diarias preanunciadas, conocida como deslizamiento cambiado, y estableciendo un seguimiento de la brecha cambiar<92>a y de la mesa de cambios del BCN para ir evaluando el comportamiento del mercado de divisas. Por otro lado, en el caso de la pol<92>tica monetaria, se establece como primer objetivo intermedio mantener niveles adecuados de reservas internacionales, utilizando como instrumentos las operaciones de mercado abierto y el encaje legal, evaluando la evoluci<97>n de la cobertura de reservas internacionales brutas con respecto a la base monetaria como la variable de seguimiento del equilibrio monetario. El segundo objetivo intermedio se relaciona con favorecer la liquidez del sistema financiero, utilizando como instrumento las operaciones de mercado abierto de corto plazo, los dep<97>sitos monetarios y los anticipos de liquidez, d<87>ndole seguimiento a los coeficientes de liquidez del sistema financiero y las tasas de inter<8e>s interbancarias para evaluar dicho mercado. Este esquema est<87> supeditado a la utilizaci<97>n del deslizamiento del tipo de cambio como ancla nominal de los precios y de las expectativas, por lo que la pol<92>tica monetaria debe utilizar sus instrumentos para asegurar los niveles adecuados de reservas internacionales que lo soporten, as<92> como favorecer la liquidez del sistema financiero que sea consistente con los anteriores objetivos. As<92>, mediante la pol<92>tica cambiar<92>a el Banco Central incide directamente sobre los precios internos, los que adicionalmente se determinan por las variaciones de los precios internacionales y por otros factores que afectan la oferta y demanda de bienes y servicios nacionales que no est<87>n bajo el control de la autoridad monetaria. Este esquema introduces rigideces, siendo la principal la capacidad limitada de emisi<97>n monetaria y de absorci<97>n del tipo de cambio ante perturbaciones internas y externas. Sin embargo, ha funcionado razonablemente bien para la econom<92>a nicarag<9f>ense desde 1993, favoreciendo la estabilidad de precios, y se considera que contin<9c>a siendo el adecuado en las actuales condiciones. La ventaja de este esquema es su flexibilidad, porque permite alternar entre objetivos de precios, competitividad y estabilidad financiera, y que se han visto destacados en diferentes momentos de la pr<87>ctica econ<97>mica nicarag<9f>ense pasada. Sin embargo, en la experiencia reciente la estabilidad cambiar<92>a para anclar expectativas y as<92> obtener una inflaci<97>n baja y estable es la intenci<97>n de pol<92>tica monetaria y cambiar<92>a que prevalece. Instrumentos de pol<92>tica monetaria Los principales instrumentos de pol<92>tica monetaria y cambiar<92>a del Banco Central son: la fijaci<97>n diaria del tipo de cambio oficial, las operaciones de mercado abierto, el encaje legal, los dep<97>sitos monetarios y los pr<8e>stamos y anticipos de liquidez. Todos estos instrumentos se activan en diferentes momentos para bien inyectar o bien absorber liquidez, que permita satisfacer los objetivos y las metas contempladas en el programa monetario del Banco Central. La forma en que se transmiten estos instrumentos en la econom<92>a se encuentra ampliamente estudiada y contenida en los diferentes documentos de investigaci<97>n econ<97>mica que publica el Banco Central y que est<87>n disponibles en su p<87>gina web. Estos estudios son relevantes para la toma de decisiones ya que parametrizan los an<87>lisis de sensibilidad, ayudan a detectar las interrelaciones entre sectores y a establecer los rezagos con los que opera la pol<92>tica monetaria. Por ejemplo, a trav<8e>s de la investigaci<97>n hemos detectado que toma alrededor de tres trimestres para que las variaciones en el tipo de cambio se trasladen a los precios internos. Tambi<8e>n, hemos detectado una importante correlaci<97>n entre las condiciones externas y las variaciones de la actividad econ<97>mica real nacional, benefici<87>ndose la econom<92>a de la apertura y de la competencia. Por <9c>ltimo, se han identificado importantes canales de transmisi<97>n entre las tasas de inter<8e>s de mercado y externas hacia la econom<92>a real. A partir de estos estudios, pudimos inferir que hab<92>a espacio para incidir sobre las tasas de inter<8e>s y sobre los diferentes mercados de liquidez, ello a pesar de que el Banco Central ha adoptado un esquema cambiarlo fijo con deslizamiento preanunciado. La raz<97>n de esta incidencia es que en el corto plazo la econom<92>a real reacciona a los movimientos en los instrumentos monetarios, aun cuando est<87> establecido que en el largo plazo estos resulten neutrales. De esta manera el Banco Central introdujo desde 2019 la Tasa Referencia Monetaria como principal instrumento de se<96>alizaci<97>n de la posici<97>n de pol<92>tica monetaria del Banco Central. Dicha tasa sube cuando las condiciones financieras requieren moderarse y bajan cuando las condiciones monetarias requieren ser laxas. La tasa de referencia monetaria se hace acompa<96>ar por una tasa para la ventanilla de dep<97>sitos monetarios y otra tasa para la ventanilla de reportos monetarios. Ambas tasas constituyen el l<92>mite inferior y superior, respectivamente, de lo que el Banco Central ha denominado el corredor de tasas de inter<8e>s. El l<92>mite inferior est<87> referido a la posibilidad de realizar dep<97>sitos en el Banco Central para aquellas operaciones que no fueron colocadas mediante subasta competitiva, mientras que el l<92>mite superior est<87> referido a la posibilidad de poder recibir liquidez mediante reportos para aquellas operaciones que tambi<8e>n que no fueran colocadas mediante los mecanismos de subasta competitiva. Este esquema es transparente a partir de operaciones p<9c>blicas con tasas de referencia y ventanillas a las que tienen acceso todos los agentes financieros. La magnitud de las operaciones monetarias del Banco Central ha llegado a ser cada vez m<87>s relevante. Por ejemplo, en el a<96>o 2020 las operaciones monetarias de absorci<97>n fueron las siguientes: operaciones de mercado abierto 519,181 millones de c<97>rdobas, los dep<97>sitos monetarios 112,099 millones de c<97>rdobas y el encaje legal 2,360 millones de c<97>rdobas, para totalizar operaciones de absorci<97>n por 633,640 millones de c<97>rdobas y de expansi<97>n por 628,669 millones de c<97>rdobas. Por su parte, las operaciones en moneda extranjera de absorci<97>n fueron: operaciones de mercado abierto por 1,574 millones de d<97>lares, los dep<97>sitos monetarios 20,665 millones de d<97>lares y el encaje 114 millones de d<97>lares, para totalizar un monto de 22,354 millones de d<97>lares en absorci<97>n y 21,944 millones de d<97>lares de expansi<97>n. Conclusi<97>n Perm<92>tame finalmente concluir felicit<87>ndose por haber concluido satisfactoriamente esta capacitaci<97>n, motiv<87>ndolos para continuar indagando, analizando y auscultando sobre temas monetarios y financieros de Nicaragua. En mucho contribuye que cada vez m<87>s nicarag<9f>enses tengamos acceso a esta informaci<97>n para poder tener una mayor comprensi<97>n de nuestra realidad econ<97>mica. Los invito tambi<8e>n a dar seguimiento al resto de cursos, aun cuando no los tomen de manera presencial o virtual como est<87> ocurriendo en este caso, ya que daremos acceso a todo el material a trav<8e>s de nuestra p<87>gina web, para que aquellos interesados tambi<8e>n puedan estudiar por cuenta propia. Les agradezco en esta ma<96>ana su participaci<97>n y mis deseos de que pasen un buen fin de semana. Muchas Gracias

Title: Central Bank of Nicaragua and Financial Stability, on the occasion of the completion of the Financial Stability Course 2021
text: CENTRAL BANK OF NICARAGUA AND FINANCIAL STABILITY, ON THE OCCASION OF THE CULMINATION OF THE FINANCIAL STABILITY COURSE 2021, WORDS OF THE PRESIDENT OF THE CENTRAL BANK OF NICARAGUA, OVIDIO REYES R. 11/06/2021 Good morning. I am pleased to present the closing remarks of the 2021 financial stability course carried out by the Central Bank of Nicaragua and in which 17 people and virtually 115 people participated during these two weeks in person. This is already the second year that the Central Bank conducts open and free courses in economics and finance in the areas of: monetary and exchange rate policy, financial stability, financial operations, payment systems and economic statistics. These courses have been well accepted among the population and we are sure that many more people will show interest in these trainings. In this presentation I will briefly explain how the Central Bank of Nicaragua promotes the stability of the financial system, in coordination with other entities responsible for its regulation and supervision, by identifying risks and vulnerabilities in the financial system, monitoring and tracking financial variables, analyzing financial conditions and observing financial infrastructure. Introduction The financial system is a group of institutions composed of: financial intermediaries, in this case, (banks, financial institutions, microfinance institutions, savings and credit cooperatives, insurance companies and general deposit warehouses, mainly), in addition, markets, especially (money and capital markets) and financial infrastructure, is referred to the (legal framework, regulatory framework and payment and settlement systems, among others). The main objective of the financial system is to channel resources from surplus sectors to sectors demanding funds, which is known as financial intermediation. In addition, the financial system provides financial services to different agents. There is a positive correlation between aggregate developments in financial intermediation and services financial with economic activity. When intermediation and financial services grow, so does economic activity, as increased financing contributes to the acquisition of capital, employment, and inputs required for the production of goods and services. From this relationship, financial stability is a condition in which the financial system is able to maintain this intermediation and to provide financial services, resist shocks and correct its imbalances. Conversely, financial instability occurs when intermediation and financial services slow or decline. If the financial system is subjected to stress, and acute imbalances occur in the markets that lead to exchange rate devaluations, capital outflows and/or bankruptcies of financial institutions, then a financial crisis occurs. It is interesting to note that the processes of financial imbalances are incubated during periods of expansion and, therefore, of financial stability. The generalized growth of economic indicators under certain conditions generates excessive enthusiasm among participants in the financial system. Credit expansion occurs in tandem with debt accumulation, increasing risk exposure. Asset prices increase, as well as again the guarantees offered and credit. On some occasions, but not all, this growth distances itself from its economic fundamentals, thus emerging vulnerabilities that manifest themselves abruptly in events of materialized risks. Once a shock occurs, there is a loss of confidence that is expressed in a fall in asset prices and the weakening of collateral, thus reducing credit and increasing the demand for liquidity. In the worst case, this process is accompanied by "panic", bank runs and bankruptcies of financial institutions and companies. All this process is fed back through various transmission channels, generating a cycle of contraction of intermediation and financial services that drags and amplifies the contraction of economic activity. These scenarios are harmful, because in the financial system very large institutions are constituted that when they fail drag others, as well as the entire system, these institutions are called systemic institutions, or systemic risk. The financial rescue of these institutions is carried out by the State, thus imposing high burdens on taxpayers. For this reason, regulatory and supervisory entities have the function of promoting financial stability to mitigate systemic risks and protect the interests of savers and investors. 1. Inter-institutional coordination to promote the stability of the financial system. To exercise institutional coordination among the regulatory and supervisory bodies of the financial system that promote financial stability, the Financial Stability Committee (FSB) was established in Nicaragua on August 15, 2018. This committee is made up of the following institutions: Ministry of Finance and Public Credit (MHCP), Central Bank of Nicaragua (BCN), Superintendency of Banks and Other Financial Institutions (SIBOIF), the National Microfinance Commission (CONAMI) and the Deposit Guarantee Fund (FOGADE). The Committee acts as a technical, consultative and coordinating body among its members on financial stability, so it analyzes, monitors and issues recommendations for actions, measures and policies that contribute to the financial stability of the country, among other functions. Each member institution, in accordance with its laws and regulations, attends to the recommendations arising from the Committee, mainly those that are macroprudential in scope. As for the Central Bank, it coordinates the Financial Stability Committee, which is also reinforced by the mandate of its Organic Law to promote the stability of the financial system, without prejudice to the powers of the rest of the institutions supervising and regulating it. 2. Monitoring Financial Stability. Among the functions and attributions of the Central Bank is the promotion of the proper functioning and stability of the financial system, which is a responsibility shared with the other entities that make up the Financial Stability Committee. In this case, the Central Bank monitors the main vulnerabilities and identifies potential systemic risks that could affect financial stability. This monitoring of financial stability carried out by the Central Bank of Nicaragua is communicated through the Financial Stability Report (IEF). This report includes a description of the international environment and the national financial environment. Next, it presents an analysis of the financial indicators for monitoring financial stability, that is, those that could be reflecting the accumulation of vulnerabilities, such as: asset valuation, liquidity of the financial system, leverage of the financial system, indebtedness of companies and households and public debt. Subsequently, the identified risks that could affect financial stability are presented. This analysis also includes conducting stress tests or stress tests that assess the ability (strength) of the financial system to confront these risks. Finally, the conclusions are presented. The Central Bank analyzes a group of selected indicators to monitor the accumulation of potential vulnerabilities, which includes the following: asset valuation, liquidity of the financial system, leverage, the indebtedness that I had already mentioned. In the case of risk identification, the Bank carries out an analysis of the external environment and the domestic economic and financial situation, to identify risks that may disturb financial stability. This risk analysis focuses on assessing potential shocks and their effects on performance. or the infrastructure of the financial system, in this case (liquidity, solvency, profitability, payment system, etc.). While risks are difficult to predict, if not impossible, it is very difficult to say when an event will occur, in fact it could ensure that nobody knows, you can simply assign a probability of occurrence, for the identification of risks to financial stability, it takes into account the main potential risks of systemic scope that could affect the relevant financial indicators, and exacerbate vulnerabilities. These risks differ from other risks that are part of the standard methodology of monitoring and supervision based on risks, this is the name of this monitoring, which is applied to the different financial institutions in their different lines of business, for which a map is built to measure the following types of risks: credit, market, liquidity, operations and strategic. The assessment of risks to financial stability allows the Central Bank and the Committee to recommend actions to promote the resilience of the financial system. To this end, we had already mentioned that these stress tests are carried out to quantify the sensitivity and resilience of the financial system to the identification of these risks and systemic threat that could put pressure on financial stability. This exercise incorporates the modeling of these risks using econometric techniques used for forecasting macroeconomic and financial variables and for the analysis of transmission mechanisms. In the analysis it is usual to incorporate three risk scenarios (low, moderate and high). Through these scenarios, the shocks and the expected evolution of the main macroeconomic variables and financial indicators are replicated, and in this way the resilience and capacity of the financial system to withstand these adverse contexts is evaluated. The results of the exercises are compared with the historical performance of the variables and the established normative parameters. 3. Monitoring of financial markets. The monitoring of the financial system covers the joint dynamics of financial markets in Nicaragua to monitor the evolution of key financial variables. This analysis is carried out by monitoring relevant indicators and prices, consolidating markets from different sources of information such as regulatory entities and balance of payments statistics. The above is communicated through the Financial Markets Report (IMF), which is published quarterly. In this sense, the monitoring of the financial system includes the following markets: exchange, monetary, securities, credit, real estate and insurance. 4. Other tools for monitoring financial conditions. Additionally, as part of the analytical framework for the analysis of financial conditions, the Central Bank prepares a series of tools or reports for monitoring the financial system that contain short-term information on banking and financial financial statements, financial indicators and the behavior of financial conditions, among others. a. Report on the Banking and Financial System. It presents information on the main sources and uses of funds of banks and financial institutions operating in Nicaragua. This report presents information on the management of bank and financial facilities, the dynamics of investments, with emphasis on the credit portfolio, the performance of deposits and the situation of the financial statements. In addition, the main indicators, such as liquidity, profitability, solvency and risk, are analyzed. This report is published monthly on the NCB's website. b. Financial Intermediation Conditions Index (ICIF). This is a tool that describes how favorable the conditions for intermediation relative in the analysis period, when conditions are more accommodative, the index rises and when conditions are more restrictive, the index goes down. This index contains elements on the state of liquidity, profitability and macroeconomic environment in which financial intermediation takes place and is published quarterly on the NCB's website. c. Risk map. It is an analysis scheme divided into different components that allows to simultaneously visualize the dynamics over time of several indicators, so that it offers an overview of the situation of the financial system in different periods. This risk map is used as input to the Regional Financial Stability Report prepared by the Secretariat of the Central American Monetary Council, of which the Central Bank is a member. Conclusion I would like to conclude by congratulating you all on having successfully completed this course and I urge you to continue studying the different topics on monetary and financial issues in Nicaragua on your own. On our website, which we have recently updated, you can have access to all the material of this course and the remaining courses that the Central Bank is offering, both those of this year and the past, so that you can continue training from your homes. I thank you this morning for your participation and my best wishes for a good weekend. Thank you very much and congratulations for completing the course.
