BANCO CENTRAL DE NICARAGUA Y ESTABILIDAD FINANCIERA, CON MOTIVO DE LA CULMINACI<ee>N DEL CURSO DE ESTABILIDAD FINANCIERA 2021, PALABRAS DEL PRESIDENTE DEL BANCO CENTRAL DE NICARAGUA, OVIDIO REYES R. 11/06/2021 Buenos d<92>as. Me complace presentar las palabras de clausura del curso de estabilidad financiera 2021 que realiza el Banco Central de Nicaragua y en el que han participado durante estas dos semanas presencialmente 17 personas y virtualmente 115 personas. Ya este es el segundo a<96>o que el Banco Central realiza cursos abiertos y gratuitos en econom<92>a y finanzas en las <87>reas de: pol<92>tica monetaria y cambiar<92>a, estabilidad financiera, operaciones financieras, sistemas de pagos y estad<92>sticas econ<97>micas. Estos cursos han tenido buena aceptaci<97>n entre la poblaci<97>n y estamos seguros que mucho m<87>s personas mostraran inter<8e>s por estas capacitaciones. En esta presentaci<97>n explicar<8e> brevemente c<97>mo el Banco Central de Nicaragua promueve la estabilidad del sistema financiero, en coordinaci<97>n con otras entidades encargadas de la regulaci<97>n y supervisi<97>n de <8e>ste, mediante la identificaci<97>n de riesgos y vulnerabilidades en el sistema financiero, el monitoreo y seguimiento de variables financieras, el an<87>lisis de las condiciones financieras y la observancia de la infraestructura financiera. Introducci<97>n El sistema financiero es un grupo de instituciones compuesto por: intermediarios financieros, en este caso, (bancos, financieras, microfinancieras, cooperativas de ahorro y cr<8e>dito, compa<96><92>as de seguros y almacenes generales de dep<97>sitos, principalmente), adem<87>s, mercados, sobretodo (de dinero y mercados de capital) e infraestructura financiera, est<87> referida al (marco legal, el marco regulatorio y los sistemas de pagos y liquidaci<97>n, entre otros). El sistema financiero tiene como objetivo principal canalizar recursos de sectores superavitarios a sectores demandantes de fondos, lo que se conoce como intermediaci<97>n financiera. Adem<87>s, el sistema financiero brinda servicios financieros a los diferentes agentes. Existe una correlaci<97>n positiva entre la evoluci<97>n agregada de la intermediaci<97>n financiera y de los servicios financieros con la actividad econ<97>mica. Cuando la intermediaci<97>n y servicios financieros crecen, tambi<8e>n lo hace la actividad econ<97>mica, ya que un mayor financiamiento contribuye a la adquisici<97>n de capital, empleo e insumos requeridos para la producci<97>n de bienes y servicios. A partir de esta relaci<97>n, la estabilidad financiera es una condici<97>n en la que el sistema financiero est<87> en la capacidad de mantener esta intermediaci<97>n y de brindar servicios financieros, resistir perturbaciones y corregir sus desequilibrios. Por el contrario, ocurre inestabilidad financiera cuando se desacelera o disminuye la intermediaci<97>n y los servicios financieros. Si el sistema financiero es sometido a estr<8e>s, y se producen desequilibrios agudos en los mercados que conducen a devaluaciones cambiar<92>as, salidas de capitales y/o quiebras de instituciones financieras, entonces, sucede una crisis financiera. Es interesante destacar que los procesos de desequilibrios financieros se incuban durante los per<92>odos de expansi<97>n y, por tanto, de estabilidad financiera. El crecimiento generalizado de los indicadores econ<97>micos bajo determinadas condiciones genera un entusiasmo desmedido entre los participantes del sistema financiero. La expansi<97>n del cr<8e>dito ocurre a la par de acumulaci<97>n de deudas, aument<87>ndose la exposici<97>n al riesgo. Los precios de los activos se incrementan, as<92> como nuevamente las garant<92>as ofertadas y el cr<8e>dito. En algunas ocasiones, no en todas, este crecimiento se distancia de sus fundamentos econ<97>micos, surgiendo as<92> vulnerabilidades que se manifiestan abruptamente en eventos de riesgos materializados. Una vez que ocurre una perturbaci<97>n, se produce una p<8e>rdida de confianza que se expresa en una baja de los precios de los activos y el debilitamiento de las garant<92>as, reduci<8e>ndose as<92> el cr<8e>dito y aument<87>ndose la demanda por liquidez. En el peor de los casos, este proceso es acompa<96>ado por "p<87>nico", corridas bancadas y quiebras de instituciones financieras y de empresas. Todo este proceso se retroalimenta por diversos canales de transmisi<97>n, generando un ciclo de contracci<97>n de la intermediaci<97>n y servicios financieros que arrastra y amplifica la contracci<97>n de la actividad econ<97>mica. Estos escenarios resultan perjudiciales, porque en el sistema financiero llegan a constituirse instituciones muy grandes que al fracasar arrastran a otras, as<92> como a todo el sistema, estas instituciones se denominan instituciones sist<8e>micas, o de riesgo sist<8e>mico. El rescate financiero de estas instituciones lo realiza el Estado, imponi<8e>ndose as<92> elevadas cargas para los contribuyentes. Por esta raz<97>n, las entidades reguladoras y supervisoras tenemos como funci<97>n promover la estabilidad financiera para mitigar los riesgos sist<8e>micos y proteger los intereses de los ahorrantes y de los inversionistas. 1. Coordinaci<97>n interinstitucional para promover la estabilidad del sistema financiero. Para ejercer la coordinaci<97>n institucional entre los <97>rganos de regulaci<97>n y supervisi<97>n del sistema financiero que promuevan la estabilidad financiera, se constituy<97> el 15 de agosto de 2018 en Nicaragua el Comit<8e> de Estabilidad Financiera (CEF). Dicho comit<8e> est<87> conformado por las siguientes instituciones: Ministerio de Hacienda y Cr<8e>dito P<9c>blico (MHCP), Banco Central de Nicaragua (BCN), Superintendencia de Bancos y de Otras Instituciones Financieras (SIBOIF), la Comisi<97>n Nacional de Microfinanzas (CONAMI) y el Fondo de Garant<92>a de Dep<97>sitos (FOGADE). El Comit<8e> act<9c>a como <97>rgano t<8e>cnico, de consulta y coordinaci<97>n entre sus miembros en materia de estabilidad financiera, por lo que analiza, monitorea y emite recomendaciones de acciones, medidas y pol<92>ticas que contribuyan a la estabilidad financiera del pa<92>s, entre otras funciones. Cada instituci<97>n miembro, conforme sus leyes y reglamentos, atiende las recomendaciones surgidas del seno del Comit<8e>, principalmente aquellas que revisten alcance macro prudencial. En cuanto al Banco Central, <8e>ste ejerce la coordinaci<97>n del Comit<8e> de Estabilidad Financiera, lo que adem<87>s se refuerza con el mandato de su Ley Org<87>nica de promover la estabilidad del sistema financiero, sin perjuicio de las atribuciones que tienen el resto de las instituciones de supervisi<97>n y regulaci<97>n de <8e>ste. 2. Seguimiento a la Estabilidad Financiera. Entre las funciones y atribuciones del Banco Central est<87> la promoci<97>n del buen funcionamiento y la estabilidad del sistema financiero, lo cual es una responsabilidad compartida con las otras entidades que conforman el Comit<8e> de Estabilidad Financiera. En este caso, el Banco Central monitorea las principales vulnerabilidades e identifica los riesgos potenciales de alcance sist<8e>mico que pudieran afectar a la estabilidad financiera. Dicho seguimiento a la estabilidad financiera que realiza el Banco Central de Nicaragua se comunica mediante el Informe de Estabilidad Financiera (IEF). Este informe incluye una descripci<97>n del entorno internacional y del entorno financiero nacional. Seguidamente, presenta un an<87>lisis de los indicadores financieros de seguimiento a la estabilidad financiera, es decir, aquellos que pudieran estar reflejando la acumulaci<97>n de vulnerabilidades, tales como: valoraci<97>n de activos, liquidez del sistema financiero, apalancamiento del sistema financiero, endeudamiento de empresas y hogares y endeudamiento p<9c>blico. Posteriormente, se presentan los riesgos identificados que podr<92>an afectar la estabilidad financiera. Este an<87>lisis tambi<8e>n incluye la realizaci<97>n de pruebas de resistencia o pruebas de estr<8e>s que eval<9c>an la capacidad (fortaleza) del sistema financiero para confrontar estos riesgos. Finalmente se presentan las conclusiones. El Banco Central analiza un grupo de indicadores seleccionados para monitorear la acumulaci<97>n de vulnerabilidades potenciales, que incluye los siguientes: valuaci<97>n de activos, liquidez del sistema financiero, el apalancamiento, el endeudamiento que ya les hab<92>a mencionado. En el caso de la identificaci<97>n de riesgos, el Banco realiza un an<87>lisis del entorno externo y de la coyuntura econ<97>mica y financiera dom<8e>stica, para identificar riesgos que pueden perturbar la estabilidad financiera. Este an<87>lisis de riesgos se concentra en evaluar los choques potenciales y sus efectos sobre el desempe<96>o o la infraestructura del sistema financiero, en este caso (liquidez, solvencia, rentabilidad, sistema de pagos, etc.). Si bien los riesgos son dif<92>ciles de predecir, por no decir imposible, es muy dif<92>cil decir cu<87>ndo va a ocurrir un evento, de hecho podr<92>a asegurar que nadie lo sabe, simplemente se le puede asignar una probabilidad de ocurrencia, para la identificaci<97>n de los riesgos a la estabilidad financiera, se toma en cuenta los principales riesgos potenciales de alcance sist<8e>mico que podr<92>an afectar los indicadores financieros relevantes, y que exacerben las vulnerabilidades. Estos riesgos difieren de otros riesgos que forman parte de la metodolog<92>a est<87>ndar de monitoreo y supervisi<97>n basada en riesgos, as<92> se llama este monitoreo, que se aplica a las diferentes instituciones financieras en sus diferentes l<92>neas de negocios, para lo que se construye un mapa para medir los siguientes tipos de riesgos: cr<8e>dito, mercado, liquidez, operaciones y estrat<8e>gico. La evaluaci<97>n de los riesgos a la estabilidad financiera permite al Banco Central y al Comit<8e> recomendar acciones para promover la resiliencia del sistema financiero. Para ello, ya hab<92>amos mencionado que, se realizan estas pruebas de estr<8e>s que permiten cuantificar la sensibilidad y resistencia del sistema financiero a la identificaci<97>n de estos riesgos y amenaza sist<8e>mica que podr<92>an poner presi<97>n sobre la estabilidad financiera. Este ejercicio incorpora la modelaci<97>n de estos riesgos mediante t<8e>cnicas econom<8e>tricas utilizadas para pron<97>sticos de variables macroecon<97>micas y financieras y para el an<87>lisis de mecanismos de transmisi<97>n. En el an<87>lisis es usual incorporar tres escenarios de riesgos (bajo, moderado y alto). A trav<8e>s de estos escenarios se replican los choques y la evoluci<97>n esperada de las principales variables macroecon<97>micas e indicadores financieros, y de esta forma se eval<9c>a la resistencia y la capacidad del sistema financiero de soportar estos contextos adversos. Los resultados de los ejercicios se comparan con el desempe<96>o hist<97>rico de las variables y los par<87>metros normativos establecidos. 3. Monitoreo de mercados financieros. El seguimiento del sistema financiero abarca la din<87>mica conjunta de los mercados financieros en Nicaragua para monitorear la evoluci<97>n de variables financieras claves. Dicho an<87>lisis se realiza mediante el seguimiento a indicadores y precios relevantes, consolidando los mercados a partir de diferentes fuentes de informaci<97>n como las entidades regulatorias y las estad<92>sticas de la balanza de pagos. Lo anterior, es comunicado mediante el Informe de Mercados Financieros (IMF), el cual se publica trimestralmente. En este sentido, el monitoreo del sistema financiero incluye los siguientes mercados: cambiario, monetario, valores, cr<8e>dito, inmobiliario y de seguros. 4. Otras herramientas para el seguimiento de las condiciones financieras. Adicionalmente, como parte del marco anal<92>tico para el an<87>lisis de las condiciones financieras, el Banco Central elabora una serie de herramientas o informes para el seguimiento del sistema financiero que contienen informaci<97>n coyuntural sobre estados financieros de la banca y financieras, indicadores financieros y el comportamiento de las condiciones financieras, entre otros. a. Informe del Sistema Bancario y Financieras. Presenta informaci<97>n de los principales fuentes y usos de fondos de los bancos y financieras que operan en Nicaragua. En dicho informe se presenta informaci<97>n del manejo de las disponibilidades de bancos y financieras, la din<87>mica de las inversiones, con <8e>nfasis en la cartera de cr<8e>dito, el desempe<96>o de los dep<97>sitos y la situaci<97>n de los estados financieros. Adem<87>s, se analizan los principales indicadores, como liquidez, rentabilidad, solvencia y riesgo. Este informe se publica mensualmente en la p<87>gina web del BCN. b. <92>ndice de Condiciones de la Intermediaci<97>n Financiera (ICIF).Esta es una herramienta que describe que tan favorable las condiciones para la intermediaci<97>n relativas en el periodo de an<87>lisis, cuando las condiciones son m<87>s laxas, el <92>ndice sube y cuando las condiciones son m<87>s restrictivas, el <92>ndice baja. Este <92>ndice contiene elementos sobre el estado de liquidez, rentabilidad y entorno macroecon<97>mico en el cual se desarrolla la intermediaci<97>n financiera y se publica trimestralmente en la p<87>gina web del BCN. c. Mapa de riesgos.Es un esquema de an<87>lisis dividido en diferentes componentes que permite visualizar simult<87>neamente la din<87>mica a lo largo del tiempo de varios indicadores, de manera que ofrece un panorama general de la situaci<97>n del sistema financiero en distintos per<92>odos. Este mapa de riesgo se utiliza como insumo del Informe de Estabilidad Financiera Regional que elabora la Secretar<92>a del Consejo Monetario Centroamericano, de la cual el Banco Central forma parte. Conclusi<97>n Quiero concluir felicit<87>ndolos a todos por haber finalizado satisfactoriamente este curso y los insto para que por su propia cuenta contin<9c>en estudiando los diferentes t<97>picos en temas monetarios y financieros de Nicaragua. En nuestra p<87>gina web, que hemos recientemente actualizado, ustedes podr<87>n tener acceso a todo el material de este curso y los restantes cursos que est<87> brindando el Banco Central, tanto los del corriente a<96>o como los pasados, para que puedan continuarse capacitando desde sus hogares. Les agradezco en esta ma<96>ana su participaci<97>n y mis mejores deseos para que pasen un buen fin de semana. Muchas gracias y felicidades por haber culminado el curso.

Title: Central Bank of Nicaragua, Payment Systems and Financial Services, on the occasion of the completion of the Payment Systems and Financial Services Course of the Central Bank of Nicaragua
text: CENTRAL BANK OF NICARAGUA, PAYMENT SYSTEMS AND FINANCIAL SERVICES, ON THE OCCASION OF THE COMPLETION OF THE BCN'S PAYMENT SYSTEMS AND FINANCIAL SERVICES COURSE REMARKS BY THE PRESIDENT OF THE BCN, OVIDIO REYES R 02/07/2021 Good morning. It is a pleasure for me to present the closing remarks of the course on Payment Systems and Financial Services offered by the Central Bank of Nicaragua. In this course that lasted two weeks, 24 people have participated in person and virtually 97 people. To all of you, I offer my sincere congratulations. The Central Bank conducts these courses open and free to all audiences with the aim that those interested can know and study the key functions carried out by our institution in the following areas: monetary and exchange policy, financial stability, financial operations, payment systems and economic statistics. These courses have been well received by the population and we are sure that they will continue to apply to these more people interested in knowing about economics and finance banking. In this presentation I will explain in a synthetic way the role of the Central Bank of Nicaragua (BCN) to ensure the normal development of internal and external payments, including regulatory and supervisory aspects of payment systems, the provision of financial services to the Government, banks and financial entities; and the issuance of money. 1. Introduction Payments play a fundamental role in any financial system, and the way in which they occur reflects, to a large extent, the level of development, strength and stability of this. Hence, central banks pay close attention to the normal development of payments so that they happen in a timely, efficient and safe manner. Payments in the economy are made through different means, the main one being "cash" money, composed of bills and coins. Likewise, there are means of payment that operate as substitutes for money, through instruments, channels and systems. Fridays, July 2, 2021 payment instruments refer to checks, credit cards, debit cards, bank deposits, electronic funds transfers and mobile wallets, among others. While payment channels refer to ATMs and counters, internet banking (virtual banking, online banking, e-banking), mobile banking, ATMs and points of sale, among others. Finally, payment systems are made up of interbank networks, transfer networks between customers and clearing and settlement houses, among others. Likewise, as a result of technological advances, new financial technologies for payment services have been developed, included within FINTECH, such as: digital wallets, mobile points of sale, electronic money, virtual currencies, purchase and exchange of electronic divides and / or funds transfers. The BCN has exclusivity in the issuance of national money or currency, the Cordoba, which is the means of payment and unit of account for all transactions. The remaining means of payment are mainly provided by banks and other private payment service providers. The NCB has the function of regulating and supervising payment systems and also participates as a user, supplier, administrator and liquidator of these; And where the complexity and security of transactions requires it, it organizes the payment system. On the other hand, it is responsible for the regulation of payment service providers of remittances, purchase and sale of currencies and financial technology payment services. The NCB also provides banking services to the Government, banks and other financial institutions in order to operationalize monetary and financial policy, as well as to ensure that liquidity flows into the economy. 2. Regulate and Supervise Payment Systems In order to fulfil its fundamental objective, the NCB has among its main functions, inter alia, regulating and supervising payment systems. A payment system is a set of tools, procedures and rules for the transfer of funds (physical, electronic or virtual) between the participants of the system. Through payment systems, it is guaranteed that payment orders between economic agents are made in a timely, efficient and secure manner, contributing to the proper functioning of the economy and contributing to financial stability. Payment systems make it possible to mobilize money to materialize transactions of financial and productive activities. In addition, they promote banking and financial inclusion, enabling the population to access financial products and services, with positive effects on economic well-being. Payment systems also function as a channel of monetary policy, so much so that an interruption in their operation affects the effectiveness of it. With regard to the regulation of payment systems, the NCB is responsible for approving the rules so that they operate in accordance with the laws in force and the standards in this area. With regard to the supervision of payment systems, the NCB is responsible for monitoring their functioning. In the exercise of this task, it collects information and documentation to assess the efficiency and security of payment systems, both from the entities that administer a specific payment system, as well as from any other payment service provider. The NCB also contributes to the development of payment systems. to. Payment systems in Nicaragua The payment systems in Nicaragua are: i. Nicaraguan Interbank System of Electronic Payments (SINPE) SINPE is a high-value payment system administered by the NCB through which banks settle transactions between themselves and between their customers. This system connects the Government, banks, financial institutions and administrators of private payment systems, through a telecommunications network that allows them to carry out the electronic mobilization of funds. SINPE has different settlement modalities depending on the service (real-time gross settlement or net multilateral settlement in deferred time). Its operating hours, tariffs, operating rules, among other operational aspects, are established by the BCN. The SINPE is a systemically important national payment system, recognizing that, in the event of a failure in its operation, negative effects can be generated or transmitted on a larger scale among its participants or create systemic alterations in all economic agents. The services covered by SINPE are: Electronic Funds Transfers (TEF), Interbank Chamber of Electronic Check Clearing (CCE), Settlement of Operations of the Automated Clearing House (ACH), Foreign Exchange Table Module (MMC), Cash Management Module (MAE). ii. UNIRED BUT UNIRED ACH is a low-value Automated Clearing House managed by the company "ACH de Nicaragua S.A.", authorized by the BCN in December 2015. Through the UNIRED ACH platform, from a bank account, users, who can be natural or legal persons, can send real-time transfers to accounts constituted in any other bank of the National Financial System, as well as make payments of credit cards and loans (own and third parties), transfers to prepaid cards, multiple payments, among others. Transfers are made online and the service is available 24 hours a day, 365 days a year. Currently, the direct participants of UNIRED ACH are commercial banks. iii. Payment Interconnection System (SIPA) of Central America and the Dominican Republic The SIPA is a payment system that arises as an initiative of the Central American Monetary Council (CMCA) with the purpose of modernizing, harmonizing, strengthening and interconnecting the national payment systems of its member states, as well as to promote the development and integration of regional financial systems, having as its main goal the creation of a single financial space in the region. SIPA is a primarily low-value regional electronic payment system through which customers of participating financial institutions can make electronic funds transfers in United States dollars to Central America and the Dominican Republic. Transfers through SIPA are credited the same business day to the final beneficiary of the same, from its entry into the local payment system of the indirect recipient participant (destination bank), once the origin and origin of the funds has been verified. The direct participants of SIPA are the central banks of the member countries, while the financial intermediation entities of each country act as indirect participants. The operations carried out through SIPA are: remittances, payment of imports and payment of invoices, mainly. 3. Provide financial services to banks, financial institutions and the Government The NCB offers banks, financial institutions and the Government various financial services and acts on their behalf vis-a-vis correspondent banks. In this sense, the Central Bank of Nicaragua has the function of being the banker of banks, financial institutions and the Government. The provision of these services is vital to ensure the stability of the financial system and the execution of monetary and exchange rate policy. to. Financial services offered by the NCB using payment systems Through payment systems, the Central Bank provides the following financial services: Electronic funds transfers, Electronic check clearing and settlement, ACH Operations Settlement, SIPA electronic transfers, International transfers, Purchase and sale of foreign currency and Deposit and withdrawal of cash. b. Other banking services The NCB also provides the following financial and banking services specific to its central banking operations: Open Market Operations (WCO), Monetary Deposits, Current Accounts, Government Deposits, Liquidity Loans and Advances, Placement of MHCP Securities, Custody of Securities and Administration of the Registry of State Issues and Public Institutions. 4. Issue the National Currency One of the functions and attributions of the BCN is to be exclusively responsible for the issuance of national currency, the Cordoba, as well as for the circulation and withdrawal of banknotes and coins of legal tender. In order to fulfil this mandate, and in order to facilitate the fluidity of cash transactions carried out by economic agents, the NCB ensures the provision of cash at the place, time and denominations and quality required by the public, through the acquisition and supply of banknotes and coins and through cash management operations. to. Banknote printing and coinage The NCB contracts the purchase of banknotes and coins through an international bidding process involving various banknote printing firms, based on specific rules and regulations issued by the NCB. The amount and denominations of the cash purchased must be sufficient to cover the operating demand for cash, which is determined by the following factors: Demand for money from economic agents to carry out transactions, Replacement of damaged banknotes and Adjustments in inventories for precautionary reasons. Once the quantities of banknotes and coins to be printed and minted are determined, according to the elements mentioned above, the design, specifications and denominations of the same are decided. At this stage, aspects such as banknote security, durability, cleanliness, ease of identification, manufacturing costs, among others, are considered. To define the design and theme, each issue considers the relevance or opportunity to highlight events or historical figures, geographical areas of the country, monuments, customs and traditions, among others. For the color and dimensions are considered aspects such as security, ease of identification, difficulty for counterfeiting. An important decision to consider is the type of material with which the banknotes are printed, which can be cotton or polymer paper. The BCN has been using polymer banknotes since 2009, when 10, 20 and 200 cordobas banknotes began to circulate, and currently all its banknotes are printed in this material, which increases durability, substantially reduces counterfeiting and makes them environmentally friendly, as they can be recycled. Also, the durability cost ratio is superior to paper banknotes. Equally relevant are the security features that banknotes must possess to prevent counterfeiting and generate confidence in them; thus, the BCN uses security measures such as transparent windows, complex windows, ink stamps with dynamic effect, iridescent bands and prints in intaglio, among others. Once the NCB receives the new banknotes and coins, the time for their distribution and circulation is determined, which is done through the banks. These are responsible for distributing them through their branches throughout the national territory. b. Cash Management In order to ensure that banknotes in circulation are available in a timely and quality manner, the NCB implements various cash management processes: i. Handling of deposits and cash withdrawals with commercial banks: Banks withdraw notes and coins from the NCB to meet the public's demand for cash, which withdraws cash at bank and ATM counters. ii. Sorting and destroying cash: the NCB performs a filter function on the cash cycle by keeping banknotes and coins in circulation in good condition and withdrawing counterfeit banknotes and coins. In no case are unfit banknotes that have torn, broken, dirty, deteriorated, painted or that have lost any of their initial characteristics put back into circulation. Destroyed cash is incinerated in the case of paper banknotes, while polymer banknotes are destroyed and recycled. iii. Response to requests for opinions on allegedly inauthentic national and foreign banknotes and coins: the NCB responds to requests for opinions from the public, banks and competent authorities when they detect forms of banknotes or pieces of coins that are allegedly not authentic in national or foreign currency. Conclusion To conclude, I would like to reiterate my congratulations to all for having completed this course and I would like to motivate you to continue training in the other courses offered by our institution and auscultate on the abundant information and economic studies that we have available to the public on our website. I thank you for listening to me this morning and wish you all a good weekend. Thanks a lot
text_original: BANCO CENTRAL DE NICARAGUA, SISTEMAS DE PAGOS Y SERVICIOS FINANCIEROS, CON MOTIVO DE LA CULMINACI<ee>N DEL CURSO DE SISTEMAS DE PAGOS Y SERVICIOS FINANCIEROS DEL BCN PALABRAS DEL PRESIDENTE DEL BCN, OVIDIO REYES R BANCO CENTRAL DE NICARAGUA, SISTEMAS DE PAGOS Y SERVICIOS FINANCIEROS, CON MOTIVO DE LA CULMINACI<ee>N DEL CURSO DE SISTEMAS DE PAGOS Y SERVICIOS FINANCIEROS DEL BCN PALABRAS DEL PRESIDENTE DEL BCN, OVIDIO REYES R 02/07/2021 Buenos d<92>as. Es un placer para m<92> presentar las palabras de clausura del curso de Sistemas de Pagos y Servicios Financieros que brinda el Banco Central de Nicaragua. En el presente curso que dur<97> dos semanas, han participado presencialmente 24 personas y virtualmente97 personas. Para todos ustedes, les brindo mis sinceras felicitaciones. El Banco Central realiza estos cursos abiertos y gratuitos para todo p<9c>blico con el objetivo que los interesados puedan conocer y estudiar las funciones clave que realiza nuestra instituci<97>n en las siguientes <87>reas: pol<92>tica monetaria y cambiar<92>a, estabilidad financiera, operaciones financieras, sistemas de pagos y estad<92>sticas econ<97>micas. Estos cursos han sido bien recibidos por la poblaci<97>n y estamos seguros que continuar<87>n postulando a <8e>stos m<87>s personas interesadas en conocer de econom<92>a y finanzas bancacentralina. En esta presentaci<97>n explicar<8e> de manera sint<8e>tica el papel del Banco Central de Nicaragua (BCN) para asegurar el normal desenvolvimiento de los pagos internos y externos, incluyendo los aspectos normativos y de supervisi<97>n de los sistemas de pagos, la prestaci<97>n de servicios financieros al Gobierno, los bancos y entidades financieras; y la emisi<97>n de dinero. 1. Introducci<97>n Los pagos juegan un rol fundamental en todo sistema financiero, y la forma en c<97>mo estos ocurren refleja, en buena medida, el nivel de desarrollo, fortaleza y estabilidad de este. De ah<92> que los bancos centrales presten mucha atenci<97>n al normal desenvolvimiento de los pagos para que los mismos sucedan en forma oportuna, eficiente y segura. Los pagos en la econom<92>a se realizan a trav<8e>s de diferentes medios, siendo el principal el dinero "efectivo", compuesto por billetes y monedas. Asimismo, existen medios de pagos que operan como sustitutos del dinero, a trav<8e>s de instrumentos, canales y sistemas. Los Viernes, 2 de julio de 2021 instrumentos de pagos est<87>n referidos a cheques, tarjetas de cr<8e>dito, tarjetas de d<8e>bito, dep<97>sitos bancarios, transferencias electr<97>nicas de fondos y billeteras m<97>viles, entre otros. Mientras que los canales de pagos se refieren a cajeros y ventanillas, banca por internet (banca virtual, banca en l<92>nea, e-banking), banca m<97>vil, cajeros autom<87>ticos y puntos de venta, entre otros. Por <9c>ltimo, los sistemas de pagos est<87>n constituidos por redes interbancarias, redes de transferencias entre clientes y c<87>maras de compensaci<97>n y liquidaci<97>n, entre otros. Asimismo, producto de los avances tecnol<97>gicos se han desarrollado nuevas tecnolog<92>as financieras de servicios de pagos, comprendidas dentro de las FINTECH, tales como: carteras digitales, puntos de ventas m<97>viles, dinero electr<97>nico, monedas virtuales, compraventa e intercambio de dividas de forma electr<97>nica y/o transferencias de fondos. El BCN tiene la exclusividad en la emisi<97>n del dinero o moneda nacional, el C<97>rdoba, que es el medio de pago y unidad de cuenta para todas las transacciones. Los restantes medios de pagos son provistos principalmente por la banca y otros proveedores privados de servicios de pagos. El BCN tiene la funci<97>n de normar y supervisar los sistemas de pagos y adem<87>s participa como usuario, proveedor, administrador y liquidador de <8e>stos; y ah<92> donde la complejidad y seguridad de las transacciones lo requiere, organiza el sistema de pagos. Por otro lado, se encarga de la regulaci<97>n de los proveedores de servicios de pagos de remesas, compra y venta de monedas y tecnolog<92>a financiera de servicios de pagos. Tambi<8e>n el BCN presta servicios bancarios al Gobierno, bancos y otras entidades financieras con el fin de operativizar la pol<92>tica monetaria y financiera, as<92> como garantizar que fluya la liquidez en la econom<92>a. 2. Normar y Supervisar los Sistemas de Pagos Para cumplir con su objetivo fundamental, el BCN tiene dentro de sus funciones principales, entre otras, normar y supervisar los sistemas de pagos. Un sistema de pagos es un conjunto de instrumentos, procedimientos y normas para la transferencia de fondos (f<92>sico, electr<97>nico o virtual) entre los participantes del sistema. A trav<8e>s de los sistemas de pagos se garantiza que las <97>rdenes de pago entre los agentes econ<97>micos se realicen de forma oportuna, eficiente y segura, contribuyendo con el buen funcionamiento de la econom<92>a y coadyuvando a la estabilidad financiera. Los sistemas de pagos permiten movilizar dinero para materializar transacciones de actividades financieras y productivas. Adem<87>s, fomentan la bancarizaci<97>n y la inclusi<97>n financiera, posibilitando el acceso de la poblaci<97>n a los productos y servicios financieros, con efectos positivos sobre el bienestar econ<97>mico. Los sistemas de pagos tambi<8e>n funcionan como un canal de la pol<92>tica monetaria, de tal mantera que una interrupci<97>n en su funcionamiento afecta la efectividad de <8e>sta. Respecto a la regulaci<97>n de los sistemas de pagos, el BCN se encarga de la aprobaci<97>n de las normas para que operen conforme a las leyes vigentes y los est<87>ndares en la materia. Respecto a la supervisi<97>n de los sistemas de pagos, le corresponde al BCN la vigilancia de su funcionamiento. En el ejercicio de esta tarea, recaba la informaci<97>n y documentaci<97>n para valorar la eficiencia y seguridad de los sistemas de pagos, tanto de las entidades que administran un sistema de pagos en espec<92>fico, as<92> como tambi<8e>n de cualquier otro proveedor de servicios de pago. Tambi<8e>n el BCN contribuye en el desarrollo de los sistemas de pagos. a. Sistemas de pagos en Nicaragua Los sistemas de pagos en Nicaragua son: i. Sistema Interbancario Nicarag<9f>ense de Pagos Electr<97>nicos (SINPE) El SINPE es un sistema de pagos de alto valor administrado por el BCN a trav<8e>s del cual los bancos liquidan transacciones entre ellos y entre sus clientes. Este sistema conecta al Gobierno, los bancos, entidades financieras y administradores de sistemas de pagos privados, a trav<8e>s de una red de telecomunicaciones que les permite realizar la movilizaci<97>n electr<97>nica de fondos. El SINPE cuenta con diferentes modalidades de liquidaci<97>n en dependencia del servicio (liquidaci<97>n bruta en tiempo real o multilateral neta en tiempo diferido). Sus horarios de operaci<97>n, tarifas, reglas de funcionamiento, entre otros aspectos operativos, son establecidos por el BCN. El SINPE es un sistema de pago nacional de importancia sist<8e>mica, reconociendo que, ante una falla en su operaci<97>n, se pueden generar o transmitir efectos negativos a mayor escala entre sus participantes o crear alteraciones sist<8e>micas en el conjunto de agentes econ<97>micos. Los servicios cubiertos por el SINPE son: Transferencias Electr<97>nicas de Fondos (TEF), C<87>mara Interbancaria de Compensaci<97>n Electr<97>nica de Cheques (CCE), Liquidaci<97>n de Operaciones de la C<87>mara de Compensaci<97>n Automatizada (ACH), M<97>dulo de Mesa de Cambio de Divisas (MMC), M<97>dulo de Administraci<97>n de Efectivo (MAE). ii. UNIRED ACH UNIRED ACH es una C<87>mara de Compensaci<97>n Automatizada de bajo valor administrada por la empresa "ACH de Nicaragua S.A.<d3>, autorizada por el BCN en diciembre de 2015. A trav<8e>s de la plataforma de UNIRED ACH, desde una cuenta bancaria los usuarios, que pueden ser personas naturales o jur<92>dicas, pueden enviar en tiempo real transferencias a cuentas constituidas en cualquier otro banco del Sistema Financiero Nacional, as<92> como realizar pagos de tarjetas de cr<8e>dito y pr<8e>stamos (propios y de terceros), transferencias a tarjetas prepagadas, pagos m<9c>ltiples, entre otros. Las transferencias son realizadas en l<92>nea y el servicio est<87> disponible las 24 horas del d<92>a los 365 d<92>as del a<96>o. Actualmente, los participantes directos de UNIRED ACH son los bancos comerciales. iii. Sistema de Interconexi<97>n de Pagos (SIPA) de Centroam<8e>rica y Rep<9c>blica Dominicana El SIPA es un sistema de pago que surge como iniciativa del Consejo Monetario Centroamericano (CMCA) con el prop<97>sito de modernizar, armonizar, fortalecer e interconectar los sistemas de pago nacionales de sus estados miembros, as<92> como para promover el desarrollo e integraci<97>n de los sistemas financieros regionales, teniendo como meta principal la creaci<97>n de un espacio financiero <9c>nico en la regi<97>n. El SIPA es un sistema electr<97>nico de pagos regional principalmente de bajo valor, por medio del cual los clientes de las entidades financieras participantes pueden realizar transferencias electr<97>nicas de fondos, en d<97>lares de los Estados Unidos de Am<8e>rica, a Centroam<8e>rica y Rep<9c>blica Dominicana. Las transferencias a trav<8e>s del SIPA son acreditadas el mismo d<92>a h<87>bil al beneficiario final de la misma, desde su ingreso al sistema de pagos local del participante indirecto receptor (banco destino), una vez compruebe la procedencia y origen de los fondos. Los participantes directos del SIPA son los bancos centrales de los pa<92>ses miembros, mientras que las entidades de intermediaci<97>n financiera de cada pa<92>s fungen como participantes indirectos. Las operaciones que se realizan a trav<8e>s del SIPA son: remesas, pago de importaciones y pago de facturas, principalmente. 3. Prestar servicios financieros a los bancos, entidades financieras y al Gobierno El BCN ofrece a los bancos, instituciones financieras y al Gobierno, diferentes servicios financieros y act<9c>a en representaci<97>n de estos frente a bancos corresponsales. En este sentido, el Banco Central de Nicaragua tiene la funci<97>n de ser el banquero de los bancos, de las instituciones financieras y del Gobierno. La prestaci<97>n de estos servicios es vital para que asegurar la estabilidad del sistema financiero y la ejecuci<97>n de la pol<92>tica monetaria y cambiar<92>a. a. Servicios financieros que el BCN ofrece utilizando los sistemas de pagos A trav<8e>s de los sistemas de pagos el Banco Central brinda los siguientes servicios financieros: Transferencias electr<97>nicas de fondos, Compensaci<97>n y liquidaci<97>n electr<97>nica de cheques, Liquidaci<97>n de Operaciones ACH, Transferencias electr<97>nicas SIPA, Transferencias internacionales, Compra y venta de divisas y Dep<97>sito y retiro de efectivo. b. Otros servicios bancarios El BCN tambi<8e>n brinda los siguientes servicios financieros y bancarios propios de sus operaciones de banca central: Operaciones de Mercado Abierto (OMA), Dep<97>sitos Monetarios, Cuentas corrientes, Dep<97>sitos del Gobierno, Pr<8e>stamos y Anticipos de Liquidez, Colocaci<97>n de valores del MHCP, Custodia de valores y Administraci<97>n del registro de las emisiones del Estado y las instituciones p<9c>blicas. 4. Emitir la Moneda Nacional Una de las funciones y atribuciones del BCN es la de ser responsable exclusivo de la emisi<97>n de moneda nacional, el C<97>rdoba, as<92> como de la puesta en circulaci<97>n y retiro de billetes y monedas de curso legal. Para cumplir con este mandato, y con el prop<97>sito de facilitar la fluidez de las transacciones en efectivo que realizan los agentes econ<97>micos, el BCN garantiza la provisi<97>n de efectivo en el lugar, momento y denominaciones y calidad requeridas por el p<9c>blico, a trav<8e>s de la adquisici<97>n y suministro de billetes y monedas y mediante operaciones de administraci<97>n de efectivo. a. Impresi<97>n de billetes y acu<96>aci<97>n de monedas El BCN contrata la adquisici<97>n de billetes y monedas mediante un proceso de licitaci<97>n internacional en el que participan diversas firmas impresoras de billetes, con base en normativas y reglamentos espec<92>ficos dictados por el BCN. El monto y denominaciones del efectivo adquirido tienen que ser suficiente para cubrir la demanda operativa de efectivo, la cual est<87> determinada por los siguientes factores: Demanda de dinero de los agentes econ<97>micos para realizar transacciones, Reposici<97>n de billetes deteriorados y Ajustes en los inventarios por motivos precautorios. Una vez que se determinan las cantidades de billetes y monedas a imprimir y acu<96>ar, de acuerdo con los elementos mencionados anteriormente, se deciden el dise<96>o, especificaciones y denominaciones de los mismos. En esta etapa se consideran aspectos como seguridad de los billetes, durabilidad, limpieza, facilidad de identificaci<97>n, costos de fabricaci<97>n, entre otros. Para definir el dise<96>o y tem<87>tica, se considera en cada emisi<97>n la relevancia u oportunidad de destacar eventos o personajes hist<97>ricos, zonas geogr<87>ficas del pa<92>s, monumentos, costumbres y tradiciones, entre otros. Para el color y dimensiones se consideran aspectos tales como seguridad, facilidad de identificaci<97>n, dificultad para falsificaci<97>n. Una decisi<97>n importante para tomar en consideraci<97>n es el tipo de material con el que se imprimen los billetes, el cual puede ser papel de algod<97>n o pol<92>mero. El BCN utiliza billetes de pol<92>mero desde el a<96>o 2009, cuando comenzaron a circular billetes de 10, 20 y 200 c<97>rdobas, y actualmente todos sus billetes est<87>n impresos en este material, el cual aumenta la durabilidad, disminuye sustancialmente la falsificaci<97>n y los hace amigables con el medio ambiente, al poder ser reciclados. Asimismo, la relaci<97>n durabilidad costo es superior a los billetes de papel. Igualmente relevante son las caracter<92>sticas de seguridad que deben poseer los billetes para evitar su falsificaci<97>n y generar confianza en los mismos; as<92> el BCN utiliza medidas de seguridad como ventanas transparentes, ventanas complejas, sellos de tinta con efecto din<87>mico, bandas iridiscentes e impresiones en intaglio, entre otras. Una vez que el BCN recibe los nuevos billetes y monedas, se determina el momento para su distribuci<97>n y puesta en circulaci<97>n, la cual se realiza a trav<8e>s de los bancos. Estos se encargan de distribuirlos a trav<8e>s de sus sucursales en todo el territorio nacional. b. Administraci<97>n del efectivo A fin de garantizar que los billetes en circulaci<97>n est<8e>n disponibles de forma oportuna y con calidad, el BCN ejecuta diversos procesos de administraci<97>n del efectivo: i. Atenci<97>n de dep<97>sitos y retiro de efectivo con los bancos comerciales: Los bancos retiran billetes y monedas del BCN para atender la demanda de efectivo del p<9c>blico, el cual retira efectivo en las ventanillas de los bancos y de los cajeros autom<87>ticos. ii. Clasificaci<97>n y destrucci<97>n del efectivo: el BCN realiza una funci<97>n de filtro sobre el ciclo del efectivo, al mantener en buen estado los billetes y monedas en circulaci<97>n y retirar los billetes y monedas falsos. En ning<9c>n caso se vuelven a poner en circulaci<97>n billetes no aptos que presentan rasgaduras, rotos, sucios, deteriorados, pintados o que hayan perdido alguna de sus caracter<92>sticas iniciales. El efectivo destruido es incinerado en el caso de los billetes de papel, mientras que los billetes de pol<92>mero son destruidos y reciclados. iii. Atenci<97>n de solicitudes de dictamen de billetes y monedas nacional y extranjeras presuntamente no aut<8e>nticas: el BCN atiende solicitudes de dictamen que el p<9c>blico, los bancos y las autoridades competentes soliciten al BCN cuando detecten formas de billetes o piezas de monedas presuntamente no aut<8e>nticas en moneda nacional o extranjera. Conclusi<97>n Para concluir, quisiera reiterar mis felicitaciones a todos por haber finalizado este curso y quisiera motivarlos para que contin<9c>en capacit<87>ndose en los otros cursos que brinda nuestra instituci<97>n y se ausculten sobre la abundante informaci<97>n y estudios econ<97>micos que tenemos disponible al p<9c>blico en nuestra p<87>gina web. Les agradezco haberme escuchado en esta ma<96>ana y les deseo a todos que pasen un buen fin de semana. Muchas Gracias

Title: Speech at the Presentation Exhibition National School of Plastic Arts "Rodrigo Pealba"
text: WORDS OF THE PRESENTATION EXHIBITION NATIONAL SCHOOL OF PLASTIC ARTS "RODRIGO PEnALBA", PRESIDENT OF THE BCN OVIDIO REYES R. 15/07/2021 Buenastardes. I wish to greet and thank the presence of the Architect Luis Morales, Co-Director of the Nicaraguan Institute of Culture, Mrs. Celeste Gonzalez, director of the National School of Plastic Arts "Rodrigo Penalba" and the 30 students and 8 teachers of said school, who accompany us to the inauguration of this exhibition. The Central Bank of Nicaragua, through its Cultural Program, disseminates and promotes Nicaraguan art in all its manifestations. Among other cultural activities, the Bank organizes exhibitions to promote new values and enrich the artistic knowledge of our population. Fulfilling this function, we have organized this exhibition of the artistic creations of students of the National School of Plastic Arts "Rodrigo Penalba". These young people, students of regular and Saturday courses, show off their skills with chisel and dry point; the brush and the different techniques used: oil, acrylic, mixed and collage; pencil drawings of graphite, pastel chalk and charcoal. Academic or free, they always express their vision of the world, without putting limits on the imagination and enhancing their creativity. In this exhibition we can appreciate figurative and abstract works; of neo-expressionist, surrealist, impressionist or neoclassical tendency. The plastic arts, both painting and sculpture, are the representation of concepts, emotions and events through material or virtual elements that can be perceived by the senses, especially that of sight. We invite all those interested in these works to visit our Pinacoteca to admire them and, if it is of their interest, acquire them from their authors. Our most sincere greetings, recognition and congratulations to all the young people and teachers who are part of the National School of Plastic Arts "Rodrigo Penalba" and, particularly, to those who present their artistic manifestations in this exhibition. Thanks a lot.

Title: Transcript of Interview on "Economy in recovery towards growth"
text: TRANSCRIPT OF INTERVIEW OF THE PRESIDENT OF THE BCN IN TN8 STUDY ON THE TOPIC "ECONOMY IN RECOVERY TOWARDS GROWTH" 27/08/2021 Journalist Erving Vega Good morning, thank you for joining us. Central Topic of Study TN8 for today Thursday, August 26, we are going to talk about Economy, "Closing of the First Semester 2021". The most recent Report of the Monthly Index of Economic Activity of the Central Bank refers that the IMAE accumulated in the First Semester, January-June, grew by 9.3%. We are also going to talk about the recent Report on Foreign Trade and the Monetary aspect. Our guest, Ovidio Reyes, President of the Central Bank. Good morning, thank you for joining us, Ovid. Words of Ovidio Reyes Good morning, Erving. Journalist Erving Vega In the last opportunity we had to interview you in this Program we were left with an estimated projection between 4 and 6% growth. Are we on track to stay in that range? Words of Ovidio Reyes Indeed, Erving, in the figures that we have been compiling recently, shows how economic activity not only maintained the dynamism that it had already been presenting of recovery, but consolidated it and exceeded what we were expecting. For example, the IMAE of the month of May grew 15.8% and already in June it is growing 16.7%. Journalist Erving Vega Is that the highest month? 0 is it that we are going to more? Words of Ovidio Reyes That's the highest month. Come on, I would think, with a kind of strong reaction, but then it will moderate, because remember that last year the pandemic affected the Second Quarter more harshly; then we are comparing a Quarter with an economic activity quite depressed by the initial impact of the pandemic, and now a Second Semester in 2021 already recovering. However, the interesting thing is that now the economy is beginning to move already looking for its path of growth. It will be a little different because the productive structure of the Country has changed, as a result of 2 years of decrease, 2018 and 2019, but above all of the pandemic, which changed World Trade, changed the Productive Structures. And we believe that it could, already towards the Third and Fourth Quarters, especially already towards the First Quarter of next year, land in a growth between 3% and 4%. Journalist Erving Vega I would like to leave the following: We started 2021 with an estimate or projection of growth of 3.5, but that projection now, if that was the ceiling, now is not even the floor, because it is 4% the floor. That is, the most conservative projection at the moment is 4, it is no longer 3.5 the most optimistic, it is 4 the most conservative. That's right? Words of Ovidio Reyes Indeed, because when we made the estimates between 4 and 6 we thought that the range could be around 5% growth, but what we are observing is that already 9% accumulated, and 4% is even very conservative and could be closer to 6 than 4. But we will see how the economy evolves, because in these things, the pandemic and international shocks, caused the forecasting capacity to be lost a lot, but now it is recovering again, given that there are already well-marked trends. Journalist Erving Vega Let's look at the scenarios, both internal and external, to raise the hypothesis, estimate, on how the behavior of the Economy is expected to continue in the Second Semester, and we expand the data for the First Semester. We are talking about the Central Bank Reports, the most recent, the Monthly Index of Economic Activity that already makes an evaluation of the First Semester, January-June, and there is an accumulated growth of 9.3%; there is also a recent Report on Foreign Trade which is positive. We talked about growth and growth estimates in the initial part of the Program; An estimate is maintained between 4% and 6% growth, with 4% being a projection, in this scenario, quite conservative. Words of Ovidio Reyes That's right, and that can even be estimated in a fairly simple way: For example, if growth today accumulates around 9%, then towards the Second Semester, if the Economy converges to that 3%, 4% that I mentioned at the beginning of the Program, then we would have 6%; In other words, the estimate is already a little more skewed towards 6%. But, as in all this there are imponderables, there are situations that may arise, so it is best to maintain an estimate by range, which is what we are preserving, between 4 and 6%; However, for the purpose of our monetary programming we are working with 3% initially, which we had since the beginning of the year. Journalist Erving Vega What happened between January and June? Words of Ovidio Reyes I think there has been a fairly firm change in the economy in the sense that at the beginning we estimated that the economy was going to recover and some activities were going to be a little slower than others, but already at this moment all activities are in recovery; therefore, we believe that the recovery is now fully consolidated and that the economy is now on track to seek a new path of growth. All sectors are in recovery, some more than others; Even if I can no longer speak of a reduction in economic activity in any sector, even if some are negative, simply because the rate they are reflecting is less negative, therefore they are also in recovery. In fact, there are only two sectors that are still pending: The Hotel Sector, as a result of the pandemic itself, and the Financial Intermediation Sector, but it is becoming less negative, and credit is already reactivating. Journalist Erving Vega That is, if we talk about the Tourism Sector as such, we cannot even say the Tourism Sector, it is a part of the Tourism Sector: The hotel part nothing more. Words of Ovidio Reyes Exactly. But interestingly in the hotel part has also been showing some activity, and if it refers to the Restaurant component, these are already growing, Then, in our indexes both are collected and that is why they appear with negative, but the truth is that the Restaurant Sector is already dynamic. The Commerce Sector, for example, is growing at 16%, which is a fairly strong rate. Last time I had mentioned a growth of 8%, but that is no longer the case. And except for these two sectors, all economic activity is already positive. We had already highlighted on the previous occasion the Mining and Quarrying Sector, but today we can highlight the Manufacturing Industry Sector that is growing strongly, that is observed, both in the production of AgroExport products, as well as in the Industry as such, which is a supplier of chemical articles, pharmaceutical products, including all the activity of Free Zones and the industrial activity that is coupled with the primary production sector. So, that's what we have. For example, Agriculture is growing 1.5% in the accumulated. A bit of weakness in Agriculture as a result of last year's effects that occurred with hurricanes Eta and Iota, and that has its impact on Agriculture. But we observe that Fisheries and Aquaculture is growing 14.5%; Mines and Quarries 55%; the Manufacturing Industry Sector that I mentioned, is growing 19.6% in the accumulated. Construction, a very important sector that generates a lot of employment, has recovered by 20%, and here goes all the constructive activity that is promoted from the Public Programs, such as the Private, the Private has had an important rebound. Energy and Water 6.1%; Trade 16.5%; Transport and Communications that were also affected, are already growing by 3.3%. So, as you can see, the recovery is already dynamic; In other words, it is recovering, but we are already entering into dynamics. What will happen towards the Second Semester, was one of your questions. Journalist Erving Vega I would like to ask a question, Ovid. I was struck by the data on Agriculture, growing but little compared to the rest of the sectors, product of hurricanes Eta and Iota. Is there a better scenario, however, now that we are already facing the 2021-2022 Cycle? Why is it going to start dating or is it already starting to leave...? Words of Ovidio Reyes Towards the Second Semester, yes, because Agriculture also moves by incentives, and in the International Market there are excellent prices for the Goods we produce. There is an excellent price for Coffee, there is an excellent price for Livestock, and almost for all Agricultural Goods; So this sector is also stating that there is a good harvest expectation, and in addition to that, it depends on the rainfall regime that preliminarily has been showing a good behavior, therefore, it is most likely that it will recover. Journalist Erving Vega I interviewed the Deputy Minister of Agriculture on Tuesday and he was precisely talking about the behavior of the Cycle, how it has been showing, and in all areas considerable growth is experienced or projected, so there is optimism. Words of Ovidio Reyes Yes, it is most certain that there will be a recovery also in the case of Agriculture and that there will be improve your rate. Returning again to what is the estimate of the Second Semester; well, suppose that the Economy lands at the 4% that we had mentioned, then 9% accumulated and 4% in the Second Semester would be around the 6% we have been talking about; then, that's where the economy could evolve. And if the rate is lower, it converges more towards 4, but we already believe that this is a pessimistic scenario, as I mentioned, 4%. Journalist Erving Vega And 6% is not too much optimism either...? Words of Ovidio Reyes It is almost real, but we will make sure as it evolves and advances. Journalist Erving Vega What would have to converge, converge, for us to achieve that 6%? Words of Ovidio Reyes Well, I think that already at this moment the conditions are in place for it to occur; the world is recovering, global growth rates are very strong; the demand for products worldwide has grown a lot, and this is also observed in International Trade. We have just produced this Trade Report, and it is clear from the report that all export products are positive, except very few, but after that the growth is significant. For example, coffee is growing 3.3%, the total amount of export amounted to 354 million dollars, higher than the 342 million dollars of the First Half of last year. The case of peanuts, the same, 54.6 million dollars of peanut exports versus 48.3 last year. The Bean, which as I mentioned was affected by the intense rains of last year, is at 49 million dollars. But then you find Fishing growing by 18.9% in export; 55.1 million dollars exported versus 46.3 in the semester of the previous year. Mining, 441 million dollars, this amount is spectacular because it is predicting that they can reach, without problems, more than 800 million dollars in mining exports if it continues at this pace, which would be fantastic, and last year it was 270 million dollars. If it is Manufacturing, which is the sector that strengthened the dynamism towards the end of the semester, it is exporting 778 million dollars; this is apart from Zona Franca, then I mention Zona Franca. This is in First Semester. So, who are the ones here who are having very important results? Well, meat exports are 315 million versus 266 million last year; Dairy Products, 99 million versus 92 million a year earlier. These are those related to the Agricultural Sector, Agro-exporter. But if we go to the other components that I mentioned of the Manufacturing Industry, they are all in positive rate, and very strong. For example, Beverages and Rones, 35.3 million dollars exported, versus 24 million the previous year; tobacco production, 15 million versus 10 million last year; Chemicals, 30 million versus 14 million last year, and so on; wood products, footwear manufacturing, leather products and footwear, and the rest of the products are dynamic. In total, 1,824 million versus 1,519. If you observe it is a strong rate of 20%, and if we consider that the dynamics of external prices have already jumped, but there is no more dynamic, it remained at an important and attractive level, these amounts are already a reflection of higher export volumes; It's not so much price, it's already volume. Journalist Erving Vega And isn't there a tendency for prices to fall in the international market? Words of Ovidio Reyes There is no trend because global demand is robust, apart from the fact that policies have been promoted worldwide to stimulate consumption and production. And when we go later to the Free Trade Zones there the growth is quite strong as well. Free Trade Zone already towards the Second Quarter had such a strong dynamic that already today exports from Free Zone have grown by 48%. For example, you have Arneses, 314 million dollars exported versus 150 million the previous year. Then all the other components: Palm Oil, Footwear, Cardboard Matches, Linings for upholstering furniture, Fruits and Vegetables, Bee Honey, Fish Products, Tobacco, Textile and others, all growing. Tobacco in particular is another that is having a strong rebound, 155 million dollars versus 100 the previous year. Well, the Tobacco Sector could reach the 300 million aspiration that it has set as a goal a long time ago, and it has a lot of potential to achieve it. The same goes for the rest of the activities, the Textile and other Free Trade Zone activities. That is, a total of 1,587 million dollars exported from the Zone Frankish versus 1,070 the previous year. So the Statistics in the Export Sector also indicate and corroborate what we are observing in the Production Statistics, that there is already a consolidation and a search for a path of growth. And finally, if we go to the side of imports, it is the same dynamic. This year imports have reflected a rebound. Journalist Erving Vega What do imports reflect on us? Words of Ovidio Reyes It reflects consumer spending and investment spending, it reflects both. For example, Consumer Goods growth is 19%, there were 1,078 million dollars of imports in Consumer Goods versus 900 million the previous year. But Capital Goods also grew, and by 72% imports of Capital Goods, and this is investment for business. We are talking about 623 million dollars of Imports of Goods and Capital against 360. And another that is also related to Production are the Intermediate Goods that are the inputs for Production... 889 million versus 687 million, for a growth of 29%. If you look closely, the rates we are talking about are very important rates. So, behind what is observed is that growth is demanding; the Economy is not only supplying the World through its exports and at considerable rates, a rate of 20%, but it is also demanding from the World at equivalent rates. In total, for example, global imports grew by 35.9%, of course, a part is Oil that rose in price and the oil bill also increased by 55%, but the dynamics are generalized, both on the side of Foreign Trade and on the side of domestic production. Journalist Erving Vega We have an international scenario with solid demand and favorable prices. And we are producing. Words of Ovidio Reyes That's right, and we're producing. Journalist Erving Vega Imponderable risks? I mean, could one say that everything is in favor of us continuing to grow? Words of Ovidio Reyes Yes, but it has always been said, at the international level, that the pandemic continues to be, let's call it that, the main risk for the World Economy, because the new variants can affect this rate of growth. In some economies there were also certain lockdowns, etc., it is not our case, but if the World Economy suddenly came to suffer it it could be a problem. Journalist Erving Vega But isn't it the scenario being considered? Words of Ovidio Reyes The truth is that, in all analyses, the pandemic reappears as the main element of risk, but the truth is that Countries have increased Spending Policies; So, even when this phenomenon occurs, the truth is that spending will continue and therefore our products will continue to be sold. The other risk has been that the pandemic has led to confinement; first the withdrawal of labor from production and then the return of labor force was not equal; that is, there was a labor force that could recover, another labor force made other decisions and then the World Economy was decoupled. That is why you see many costs rising, and that is another element of risk, because then prices also begin to reflect that reality. So some are worried, there are some economies that are having strong inflation rates, strong in the sense that they are rates that they had not seen for many years, although everyone claims that it is transitory. That movement of inflations could lead to a rise in interest rates, and that could also have some effect. But the truth is that we, even if these phenomena occur in the case of the Nicaraguan economy, because others could be affected differently, but in the case of the Nicaraguan economy we do not see that these actions will have a result that will reverse this trend. Journalist Erving Vega And the pandemic already at its worst did not paralyze us; But we keep working. Words of Ovidio Reyes Well, it affected us, but the economy continued to advance; the activities that we observed in a later analysis that were most affected are those related to mobilization and Goods and Services, but the central Productive Activities were always present. A particularity that we have and that we have had in the different shocks that we have faced in the last 3 years, is that the Agricultural Sector and the Primary Sector, Mining, Fishing, Agriculture, are backbones of this Country; So, regardless of what happens they always continue to move forward and continue to export. Journalist Erving Vega The climate issue would probably also be another risk. Words of Ovidio Reyes The last one would be the Climate. It is indeed an element of risk; for example, last year we received two impacts: the pandemic, and at the end of the year the hurricanes. There are always these meteorological problems that have now been aggravated by the issues of Climate Change. But let's not see it that way... It is also interesting to see how some economic sectors are even better than pre-pandemic levels, even some are returning to the point of the First Quarter 2018, that is, they are already even better than in 2017. For example, when we look at the levels of economic activity, the Livestock Sector is already above April 2018 and is above pre-pandemic levels. Another sector that has been advancing very strongly and that is in all the statistics is the Mining and Quarrying Sector; we also observe that the Manufacturing Industry is already above even the First Quarter of 2018, it is already with quite considerable production levels. The Construction Sector is above pre-pandemic levels, it still needs to return to 2017. The Energy and Water Sector is already at the Pre-Pandemic level, it is a little short of 2017; but in a very spectacular way, I would say, because it was during the last 4 months of the last Semester, the Trade Sector is already approaching the levels of 2017, it has already exceeded the First Quarter of 2018, it exceeded not only the levels prior to the Pandemic but it is also already entering 2017. Transportation and Communications do not; He needs it. And if we look at the Financial Sector, Deposits are approaching, it lacks; pre-pandemic levels are already exceeded, but the Deposit Sector for example, which in the First Quarter of 2018 was 171,000 million, are already at 159,000 million, are getting closer. Journalist Erving Vega Reflection there... Is that capacity for savings, growth of the economy, but confidence too? Words of Ovidio Reyes In fact, it is the combination of the 3 things, effectively that is what it is, because they do not stop growing; that is, after they reached a minimum back in April 2019, they continue to grow, the Deposits. Then the savings balance of the economy is being reconstituted. And if it is exports, let it not be said, they are above the Pandemic, but above 2017. For example, in the First Quarter of 2018 283 million dollars were exported monthly, now it is 316 million dollars, we are already above. The same happens with the monthly exports of Free Zones, 228 million dollars were being exported in the First Quarter of 2018 and now 293 million dollars are being exported; So exports are already in that situation. And if we were to observe product by product, it is also observed that many activities are already above. Journalist Erving Vega More lagging behind the Tourism Sector and especially Hospitality? Words of Ovidio Reyes Yes, in the Tourism Sector revenues have really fallen; for example, the first quarter saw little revenue, such as 30 million; We are quite long. What factors could collaborate, we would think, so that this dynamic is strengthened, because at this moment the Agricultural Sector, the Export Sector, Manufacturing and now Trade are the ones that are pushing? So now, what might next year push as well? Well, a return of tourism, that would be an important factor. And, if conditions align as well, we would say a rebound in Foreign Investment as well. In fact, already this year we believe that we will observe levels of Foreign Investment higher than those observed last year due to the important investments that are being made, but a return of these factors would also give it a new impetus. Journalist Erving Vega And in the First Semester, what is the data we have? Words of Ovidio Reyes We do not have it yet because we are closing information, but the preliminary thing we are observing is that there will be an increase and especially because of the effect that existing Foreign Investment already has, because one thing is the Company that is already installed, and another is the new one that arrives. The Company that is already installed, and with these production levels, can only occur if you reinvest; that is, every company produces, a foreign company produces and what it reinvests is also foreign investment, because it increases the installed capacity and that causes its volumes to increase. So, that reinvestment component is going to increase, it's definitely going to be higher than last year, but also, another one that we've been detecting, is going to help this overcome. Journalist Erving Vega What factors have been decisive for such behavior of our economy? Words of Ovidio Reyes I think it is important to emphasize that the Economy has a very firm basis of knowledge of Markets, of Production; I think there has been a lot of accumulated experience that was waiting for a good moment, found the moment, and there had a way out. On the other hand, there was a lot of mobilization of Entrepreneurial Activity, Small and Medium Activity that could absorb a lot of employment. That component was vital even if Nicaragua's unemployment rate did not skyrocket; that is, the Non-Formal Sector I would call it, I do not like to call them Informal, because they are really productive sectors that generate a lot of production and wealth to the country. But the Sector that is not in Formality absorbed a lot of unemployment from the Formal Sector, to the point that even the dynamics of employment have been recovering. The employment that is being registered, from the Social Security Institute, is already above pre-pandemic levels: 758,000 jobs. It still does not reach the levels of the First Quarter of 2018, but it is already in recovery. That element was fundamental. The other element that was key, I think, is that a massive policy of confinement was not implemented in Nicaragua. That was fundamental, because it allowed the entire production force, both business owners and jobs to mobilize and engage. And on the other hand, the facilities that exist here to produce and export, that helped a lot. Journalist Erving Vega To close, I would like the approach from the impact of all this growth, of all this behavior of the Economy, how is it reflected? How can we see it reflected in the real economy of the worker, the taxi driver, the pulpero, the neighborhood, the street, the Community? The Popular Economy, how can we measure the reflection of this behavior there on the street? Words of Ovidio Reyes I think there is already a perception and there is a reality that there are more sales, there is more activity; There are businesses that are in activity a little more continuous, it is clearly observed. For example, with this barbaric growth that Commerce is having, there is more mobilization, there are more sales of products, and there is also more mobilization of the vehicle fleet that is felt in the Capital and in the Departments. So, there are more opportunities, and all this collaborates and contributes to the emergence of new businesses and for people to find a path of personal and family growth and development. Journalist Erving Vega Growth is already happening, recovery; Many of the sectors, you shared the data, already surpassed the pre-pandemic scenarios, and even 2017, before the coup attempt.
