Y si observamos el Sector Financiero, los Dep<97>sitos est<87>n acerc<87>ndose, le falta; ya los niveles de pre-pandemia est<87>n superados, pero el Sector de Dep<97>sitos por ejemplo, que en el Primer Trimestre del 2018 eran de 171,000 millones, ya est<87>n en 159,000 millones, se van acercando. Periodista Erving Vega Reflejo ah<92>... <c0>Esa es capacidad de ahorro, crecimiento de la Econom<92>a, pero confianza tambi<8e>n? Palabras de Ovidio Reyes De hecho, es la combinaci<97>n de las 3 cosas, efectivamente eso es lo que es, porque no paran de crecer; es decir, despu<8e>s que alcanzaron un m<92>nimo all<87> por Abril de 2019, ellos contin<9c>an en crecimiento, los Dep<97>sitos. Entonces se est<87> reconstituyendo el saldo de ahorro de la Econom<92>a. Y si son las exportaciones, ya no se diga, est<87>n por encima de la Pandemia, pero por encima del 2017. Por ejemplo, en el Primer Trimestre de 2018 mensualmente se exportaban 283 millones de d<97>lares, ahora es 316 millones de d<97>lares, ya estamos por encima. Igual ocurre con las exportaciones mensuales de Zonas Francas, se estaban exportando 228 millones de d<97>lares en el Primer Trimestre de 2018 y ahora se est<87>n exportando 293 millones de d<97>lares; entonces las exportaciones ya est<87>n en esa situaci<97>n. Y si fu<8e>ramos observando producto por producto, tambi<8e>n se observa que muchas actividades ya est<87>n por encima. Periodista Erving Vega <c0>M<87>s rezagadito el Sector Turismo y especialmente Hoteler<92>a? Palabras de Ovidio Reyes S<92>, en el Sector Turismo realmente los ingresos han bajado; por ejemplo, en el Primer Trimestre se observaron pocos ingresos, como 30 millones de d<97>lares; estamos bastante largo. <c0>Qu<8e> factores podr<92>an colaborar, pensar<92>amos nosotros, para que esta din<87>mica se fortalezca, porque en este momento el Sector Agropecuario, el Sector Exportador, Manufactura y ahora Comercio despuntando, son los que est<87>n empujando? Entonces ahora, <c0>qu<8e> es lo que podr<92>a el pr<97>ximo a<96>o empujar tambi<8e>n? Bueno, una vuelta del Turismo, eso ser<92>a un importante factor. Y, si las condiciones se alinean tambi<8e>n, dir<92>amos que igualmente un repunte de la Inversi<97>n Extranjera. De hecho ya este a<96>o creemos que vamos a observar niveles de Inversi<97>n Extranjera superiores a los observados el a<96>o pasado por las inversiones importantes que se est<87>n realizando, pero una vuelta tambi<8e>n de estos factores le dar<92>a un nuevo impulso. Periodista Erving Vega <c0>Y en el Primer Semestre, cu<87>l es el dato que tenemos? Palabras de Ovidio Reyes No lo tenemos a<9c>n porque estamos cerrando informaci<97>n, pero lo preliminar que estamos observando es que se va a producir un aumento y sobre todo por el efecto que tiene ya la Inversi<97>n Extranjera existente, porque una cosa es la Empresa que ya est<87> instalada, y otra es la nueva que llega. La Empresa que ya est<87> instalada, y con estos niveles de producci<97>n, solo pueden ocurrir si reinvierte; es decir, toda Empresa produce, una Empresa extranjera produce y lo que reinvierte es tambi<8e>n inversi<97>n extranjera, porque aumenta la capacidad instalada y eso hace que aumenten sus vol<9c>menes. Entonces, ese componente de reinversi<97>n va a aumentar, va a ser definitivamente superior a la del a<96>o pasado, pero tambi<8e>n, otra que hemos estado detectando, va a colaborar en que esto supere. Periodista Erving Vega <c0>Qu<8e> factores han sido decisivos para semejante comportamiento de nuestra Econom<92>a? Palabras de Ovidio Reyes Creo que es importante destacar que la Econom<92>a tiene unas bases muy firmes de conocimientos de Mercados, de Producci<97>n; creo que ha habido mucha experiencia acumulada que estuvo a la espera de un buen momento, encontr<97> el momento, y por ah<92> tuvo una salida. Por el otro lado, hubo mucha movilizaci<97>n de Actividad Emprendedora, de Actividad Peque<96>a y Mediana que pudo absorber mucho empleo. Ese componente fue vital incluso para que la tasa de desempleo de Nicaragua no se disparara tanto; es decir, el Sector No Formal le llamar<92>a, no me gusta llamarles Informales, porque realmente son sectores productivos que generan mucha producci<97>n y riqueza al Pa<92>s. Pero el Sector que no est<87> en la Formalidad absorbi<97> mucho desempleo del Sector Formal, al punto tal, que incluso la din<87>mica del empleo viene recuper<87>ndose. El empleo que se est<87> registrando, del Instituto de la Seguridad Social, ya est<87> por encima de los niveles pre-pandemia: 758,000 empleos. Todav<92>a no alcanza los niveles del Primer Trimestre de 2018, pero ya viene en recuperaci<97>n. Ese elemento fue fundamental. El otro elemento que fue clave, creo yo, es que en Nicaragua no se implemento una pol<92>tica masiva de confinamiento. Eso fue fundamental, porque permiti<97> que toda la fuerza de producci<97>n, tanto las due<96>as de negocios como los empleos pudieran movilizarse y acoplarse. Y por otro lado, las facilidades que aqu<92> existen para producir y para exportar, eso ayud<97> much<92>simo. Periodista Erving Vega Para cerrar, me gustar<92>a el enfoque desde el impacto de todo este crecimiento, de todo este comportamiento de la Econom<92>a, <c0>c<97>mo se refleja? <c0>C<97>mo lo podemos ver reflejado en la Econom<92>a real del trabajador, del taxista, del pulpero, del Barrio, de la Calle, de la Comunidad? La Econom<92>a Popular, <c0>c<97>mo podemos dimensionar el reflejo de este comportamiento all<92> en la calle? Palabras de Ovidio Reyes Creo que ya hay una percepci<97>n y hay una realidad de que hay m<87>s ventas, hay m<87>s actividad; hay negocios que est<87>n en actividad un poco m<87>s continua, se observa claramente. Por ejemplo, con este crecimiento b<87>rbaro que est<87> teniendo el Comercio, hay m<87>s movilizaci<97>n, hay m<87>s ventas de productos, y hay tambi<8e>n m<87>s movilizaci<97>n del parque vehicular que se siente en la Capital y en los Departamentos. Entonces, hay m<87>s oportunidades, y todo esto colabora y contribuye para que surjan nuevos negocios y para que las personas encuentren una ruta de crecimiento y desarrollo personal y familiar. Periodista Erving Vega El crecimiento ya se est<87> dando, la recuperaci<97>n; muchos de los sectores, nos compart<92>as el dato, ya superaron los escenarios prepandemia, e incluso 2017, antes de la intentona golpista. <c0>Cu<87>ndo podr<92>amos, de acuerdo a este comportamiento de la Econom<92>a, ya estar diciendo, la Econom<92>a en su conjunto, ya regresamos al punto en que se destruy<97> todo a partir de la intentona golpista? Es decir, <c0>cu<87>ndo podr<92>amos decir, ya estamos de vuelta en el escenario 2017? Palabras de Ovidio Reyes Esta Informaci<97>n son avances productivos, el IMAE es solo un <92>ndice que va recogiendo la evoluci<97>n productiva de diferentes sectores. Esa respuesta la tenemos que ver ya cuando produzcamos el Producto Interno Bruto del Segundo Trimestre; va a ser pronto, unos 15 d<92>as a lo sumo. Ah<92> vamos a ver c<97>mo se est<87> ubicando la Econom<92>a respecto a la tendencia, pero con lo que ya estamos observando, pensar<92>a que quiz<87>s, ya hacia el Segundo Semestre del pr<97>ximo a<96>o, si esta din<87>mica se mantiene, podr<92>amos estar convergiendo, aunque podr<92>a tomar el pr<97>ximo o el mediado del siguiente a<96>o a m<87>s tardar. En la ocasi<97>n anterior te hab<92>a dicho una referencia, que podr<92>a tomar un par de a<96>os recuperar el paso perdido, pero como la din<87>mica es muy fuerte podr<92>a producirse, m<87>s pronto que tarde, el pr<97>ximo a<96>o. Periodista Erving Vega Much<92>simas gracias, Ovidio, por tu participaci<97>n en TN8, vamos a continuar pendientes, ojal<87> nos mantengamos en esa ruta de crecimiento. Todo hace indicar que el Segundo Semestre, igual, seguiremos creciendo. Palabras de Ovidio Reyes Va a ser un buen Semestre, as<92> es. Periodista Erving Vega Y que estamos m<87>s cerca del 6 que del 4? Palabras de Ovidio Reyes As<92>es. Periodista Erving Vega Esto es altamente positivo. Much<92>simas gracias por habernos acompa<96>ado.

Title: Evolution of Economic Thought and Future Challenges of the Central American Region Presentation at the Central Bank of Honduras Roundtable in the framework of the Bicentennial of Central American Independence
text: 'EVOLUTION OF ECONOMIC THOUGHT AND FUTURE CHALLENGES IN THE CENTRAL AMERICAN REGION' PRESENTATION OF THE PRESIDENT OF THE BCN, OVIDIO REYES R" IN CONVERSATION OF THE CENTRAL BANK OF HONDURAS IN THE FRAMEWORK OF THE BICENTENNIAL OF THE INDEPENDENCE OF CENTRAL AMERICA 08/09/2021 Good morning everyone. I thank the Central Bank of Honduras for the invitation to participate in this conversation that takes place within the framework of the commemoration of the bicentennial of the independence of Central America and I congratulate its President, Wilfredo Cerrato for promoting this activity. The economic history of our countries, since their independence 200 years ago, has been full of challenges associated with different critical junctures. But we have also learned to adapt and innovate in order to respond effectively to changing challenges. In some cases eventualities They have affected each country in the region in a particular way, in others, they have affected us all and we have Faced these challenges together. In this context, the Central Bank of the region has played an essential role, positioning itself in each country as relevant institutions; pursuing as a fundamental objective to contribute to monetary stability and the well-being of our societies. The role of Central Banks in our countries arises largely from the need for institutional strengthening derived from the creation of our currencies. In Nicaragua, the modern history of our monetary system dates back to 1912 with the birth of Cordoba, almost 100 years after the independence of Central America. In this period the National Bank of Nicaragua emerges, which was responsible for issuing notes and coins, developing the first functions of a Central Bank. Although the National Bank initially had private participation, it was nationalized in 1940, thus achieving a greater concentration in the monetary function. The issuance of the national currency remained in the National Bank of Nicaragua until the foundation of the Central Bank of Nicaragua in 1960 whose main objective was: "to create, promote and maintain the most favorable monetary, exchange and credit conditions for the orderly development of the national economy." At that time, the main functions attributed to the Central Bank were the following: Ensure the maintenance of the internal and external value of the currency; Control the circulating environment in order to avoid disturbances in the general domestic level of prices, wages and other activities; Regulate bank credit in general and channel the credit policy of State financial institutions; Promote the liquidity and solvency of banking institutions; Seek the most effective coordination between monetary and fiscal policy, including the investment programs of those public entities capable of affecting money and capital markets; To be the only institution that will enjoy the privilege of issuing money; Monitor and manage the country's international monetary reserves; And act as an economic policy advisor and financial agent of the State. The first (Annual) Report of the Central Bank of Nicaragua in 1961 explains the general mandate to carry out a "supervigilance" of monetary stability, to keep the country with high levels of employment, also seeking to channel economic forces to achieve a rapid and orderly level of growth. Thus, the role of the Central Bank of Nicaragua as a credit regulator is highlighted to guarantee the achievement of its objective of monetary and price stability, thus promoting the "orderly development of the economy". Throughout the history of the Central Bank of Nicaragua, which this year 2021 celebrates 61 years of foundation, although there have been different contexts and policy frameworks, the institution today has focused on what we identify as its 5 main functions, which are the following: 1. Formulate and execute monetary and exchange rate policy. 2. Regulate and supervise the payment system. 3. Promote the proper functioning and stability of the financial system. 4. Provide financial services to the Government, banks and other financial institutions; and 5. Issue the national currency. Thus, we can see that, although most of the functions established in 1960 still prevail, significant changes have been incorporated, such as: First, abandoning the function of regulating trade credit. And the second is now to incorporate the stability function of the financial system. And it is that throughout our institutional history there have been difficulties that led to seek various objectives such as: growth, inflation and exchange rate, as the most important. This has not been easy to prioritize, having to face various challenges derived from historical events, which have resulted in the need to move through different schemes for conducting our monetary, exchange, financial and credit policy. Thus, in December 1972 Nicaragua faced one of the most important shocks of that decade, derived from the earthquake that occurred in the capital, Managua. With that episode, 12 years after the founding of the Central Bank of Nicaragua, the fundamental objective of the monetary authority was put under pressure, which was to maintain the stability of the currency. Despite this adversity, the objective was achieved by preserving the exchange rate parity in the country, and by being able to contain the inflationary pressures that were observed in 1973 and 1974. It also led to the significant challenge of ensuring the continuity of payment systems. The eighties was a complex period for the Central American region, and in particular for Nicaragua. The occurrence of various internal conflicts in most of the countries of the isthmus implied a major challenge to maintain not only price stability, but also economic and financial stability. In Nicaragua, the eighties led to relevant structural changes, the establishment of a mixed economy, the nationalization of banks, financing the public sector and confronting a greater demand for resources that affected the balance of payments, but it was also the scene of economic blockades and a war that led to a monetization of public deficits and hyperinflation. causing high macroeconomic stress. Already in the 1990s the challenge of economic consolidation was presented. During this period, institutional changes and structural reforms were implemented to ensure policy predictability. This translated into containing inflation through greater monetary and exchange rate stability and reinforcing the role of commercial banks in their key role in channeling financial intermediation. Although Nicaragua suffered climatic shocks such as the devastation of Hurricane Mitch at the end of that decade, financial stability was preserved, given the strength of the institutional scheme previously prevailed by the monetary authority. This demonstrated the strength and leadership of the Central Bank in properly managing its policies. The beginning of the new millennium was not without its challenges. The role of the Central Bank in promoting the stability of the national currency and financial stability was threatened by the domestic banking crisis of 2000. The immediate actions of the monetary authority, in conjunction with the banking supervisor, made it possible to mitigate the effect of the banks' financial imbalances on the real economy. The crisis was the basis for adopting greater regulations of capital requirements, liquidity and bank governance, as well as deposit guarantee schemes, which helped regain agents' confidence in the banking system, where the Central Bank played an active role. Then the financial crisis of 2008 was one of the events that most affected our countries economically in their recent history. The effect of the crisis was direct given the high relationship of our economies with the world economy, mainly through the commercial and financial channel. The crisis implied a cooling of economic growth and subsequently reflected inflationary pressures. Thus, the monetary authorities of our region had less room to act and mitigate the effects of the shock. Even with these limitations, the Central Banks were able to facilitate the financing of productive activities in our countries. Subsequently, the shock derived from socio-political events in Nicaragua in 2018 produced significant financial imbalances and effects on the real economy. This episode was, however, the scenario where the Central Bank strengthened its monetary and exchange rate policy, in order to strengthen the fulfillment of its fundamental objective and tested its powers in terms of financial stability, which was guaranteed through the incorporation of new liquidity provision mechanisms, credit facilities and issuance of flexible regulatory frameworks. Similarly, 2020 was a challenging year for our region. On the one hand, the Covid-19 pandemic was an unprecedented shock in health, economic and social terms. On the other hand, hurricanes Eta and Iota generated significant economic damage in most of our countries, exacerbating those caused by the pandemic. That year was characterized by a global economic and trade contraction directly affecting our countries in key activities such as trade, investment and tourism. Given the restrictions imposed by the pandemic, the Central Banks of the region have once again adapted and implemented innovative measures, implementing conventional and unconventional actions to mitigate their effects. During the pandemic, synchrony was observed in the decisions taken by the Central Banks of the region, regarding the reduction of monetary policy rates and the provision of liquidity; in order to guarantee bank liquidity that is usually demanded in a precautionary manner in periods of crisis. During the pandemic, efforts have also been made to ensure the fluidity of credit to the productive sectors. In Nicaragua, in particular, in the last three years measures have been implemented to provide conditional liquidity in the granting of productive credit, in order to avoid generating a feedback effect between the economic and credit contractions. This has sought to mitigate the sudden reduction in credit derived from the adverse events that have impacted the country recently. A fact that I would like to highlight is that the development of response instruments by the monetary authorities has been implemented thanks to the continuous formation of human capital at their disposal. This has allowed policy decisions to be based on technical aspects, which contributes to maximizing the probability of success and the effectiveness of those policies, according to the objectives for which they are designed. In this development process, I would also like to emphasize that the participation of integrating bodies, such as the Central American Monetary Council, which with its powers has facilitated communication, coordination and policy adoption on the part of the Central Banks of the region, has been central. Despite the progress and maturity that Central Banks have acquired, or have acquired, there are still future challenges, some of which we can foresee now, and others, which will surely take us by surprise, as happened with the current pandemic. Among these challenges we can identify two: economic integration and technological advances in the financial field. In this regard, it is important to continue making efforts to ensure that economic integration is further strengthened among the countries of the isthmus. This in order to facilitate financial and commercial exchange between countries. We must act so that the integration process is strengthened by its own dynamics, without that in the long term there is a need for additional efforts on the part of the authorities to Keep. Integration in the financial sphere must be strengthened through the modernization of financial operations, and in particular payment systems, in order to make the movements of financial resources between our countries more cost-efficient. With this, payments and capital flows can be dynamized, seeking to maximize, above all, the well-being of agents who need this type of financial facilities. In the context of this financial integration, it is important to continue strengthening regulatory and surveillance schemes, to avoid actions related to money laundering and other illicit activities that may jeopardize the credibility of our financial systems. It is also important to make joint efforts to facilitate the detection and monitoring of financial activities that violate laws. We must also continue to work on facilitating adaptation to continuing technological advances. In this sense, it is important to promote the adoption of technologies that facilitate intermediary activities to sectors traditionally excluded through the FinTech industry. It is also important to adapt to new trends in terms of payment schemes through BlockChain platforms, looking for efficiency, agility and timeliness of financial operations. Surely the next few decades will have their own economic dynamics that will require further adjustments in the policies and actions of central banks. I am confident that in this uncertain future we will know how to face the new challenges, supporting each other, as Central American nations. Finally, I reiterate my sincere thanks to the Central Bank of Honduras for the invitation to this event, and for allowing me to share with my colleagues from Central Banks of the region and other participants, some reflections on relevant facts of recent economic evolution, focused on the work of the Central Bank of Nicaragua, and the future challenges of our monetary authorities. Thanks a lot.
text_original: 'EVOLUCI<ee>N DEL PENSAMIENTO ECON<ee>MICO Y LOS RETOS FUTUROS DE LA REGI<ee>N CENTROAMERICANA' PRESENTACI<ee>N DEL PRESIDENTE DEL BCN, OVIDIO REYES R<e3> EN CONVERSATORIO DEL BANCO CENTRAL DE HONDURAS EN EL MARCO DEL BICENTENARIO DE LA INDEPENDENCIA DE CENTROAM<83>RICA <d2>EVOLUCI<ee>N DEL PENSAMIENTO ECON<ee>MICO Y LOS RETOS FUTUROS DE LA REGI<ee>N CENTROAMERICANA" PRESENTACI<ee>N DEL PRESIDENTE DEL BCN, OVIDIO REYES R<e3> EN CONVERSATORIO DEL BANCO CENTRAL DE HONDURAS EN EL MARCO DEL BICENTENARIO DE LA INDEPENDENCIA DE CENTROAM<83>RICA 08/09/2021 Muy buenos d<92>as a todos. Agradezco al Banco Central de Honduras por la invitaci<97>n a participar en este conversatorio que se realiza en el marco de la conmemoraci<97>n del bicentenario de la independencia de Centroam<8e>rica y felicito a su Presidente, Wilfredo Cerrato por impulsar esta actividad. La historia econ<97>mica de nuestros pa<92>ses, desde su independencia hace 200 a<96>os, ha estado llena de retos asociados con distintas coyunturas cr<92>ticas. Pero tambi<8e>n hemos aprendido a adaptarnos y a innovar con el objetivo de responder de forma efectiva a los cambiantes desaf<92>os. En algunos casos las eventualidades han afectado de manera particular a cada pa<92>s de la regi<97>n, en otros, nos han afectado a todos y hemos transitado juntos estos retos. En este contexto, la Banca Central de la regi<97>n ha jugado un rol esencial, posicion<87>ndose en cada pa<92>s como instituciones relevantes; persiguiendo como objetivo fundamental de contribuir con la estabilidad monetaria y al bienestar de nuestras sociedades. El papel de los Bancos Centrales en nuestros pa<92>ses surge en buena medida por la necesidad del fortalecimiento institucional derivado de la creaci<97>n de nuestras monedas. En Nicaragua, la historia moderna de nuestro sistema monetario se remonta a 1912 con el nacimiento del C<97>rdoba, casi 100 a<96>os despu<8e>s de la independencia de Centroam<8e>rica. En este per<92>odo surge el Banco Nacional de Nicaragua, el cual se encargaba de emitir billetes y monedas, desarrollando las primeras funciones de un Banco Central. Si bien, el Banco Nacional en sus inicios pose<92>a participaci<97>n privada, fue estatizado en 1940, logrando as<92> una mayor concentraci<97>n en la funci<97>n monetaria. La emisi<97>n de la moneda nacional se mantuvo en el Banco Nacional de Nicaragua hasta la fundaci<97>n del Banco Central de Nicaragua en 1960 que tuvo como objetivo principal: "crear, promover y mantener las condiciones de orden monetario, cambiarlo y crediticio m<87>s favorables para el desarrollo ordenado de la econom<92>a nacional". En ese entonces, las funciones principales que se atribuyeron al Banco Central fueron las siguientes: Velar por el mantenimiento del valor interno y externo de la moneda; Controlar el medio circulante a efecto de evitar perturbaciones en el nivel general interno de los precios, salarios y otras actividades; Regular el cr<8e>dito bancario en general y encauzar la pol<92>tica de cr<8e>dito de las instituciones financieras del Estado; Promover la liquidez y solvencia de las instituciones bancarias; Procurar la m<87>s efectiva coordinaci<97>n entre la pol<92>tica monetaria y la pol<92>tica fiscal, inclusive los programas de inversi<97>n de aquellas entidades p<9c>blicas capaces de afectar a los mercados de dinero y de capital; Ser la <9c>nica instituci<97>n que gozar<87> del privilegio de emisi<97>n monetaria; Vigilar y administrar las reservas monetarias internacionales del pa<92>s; Y actuar como consejero de pol<92>tica econ<97>mica y agente financiero del Estado. El primer Informe (Anual) del Banco Central de Nicaragua en 1961 se explica el mandato general de realizar una "supervigilancia" de la estabilidad monetaria, para mantener el pa<92>s con altos niveles de ocupaci<97>n, buscando tambi<8e>n encausar las fuerzas econ<97>micas para lograr un nivel de crecimiento r<87>pido y ordenado. Es as<92> que se resalta el papel del Banco Central de Nicaragua como regulador del cr<8e>dito para garantizar el logro de su objetivo de estabilidad monetaria y de precios, promoviendo as<92> el "desarrollo ordenado de la econom<92>a". A lo largo de la historia del Banco Central de Nicaragua, que este a<96>o 2021 cumple 61 a<96>os de fundaci<97>n, si bien ha habido contextos y marcos de pol<92>tica diferentes, la instituci<97>n hoy se ha centrado en lo que identificamos como sus 5 funciones principales, que son las siguientes: 1. Formular y ejecutar la pol<92>tica monetaria y cambiar<92>a. 2. Normar y supervisar el sistema de pagos. 3. Promover el buen funcionamiento y la estabilidad del sistema financiero. 4. Prestar servicios financieros al Gobierno, los bancos y las dem<87>s instituciones financieras; y 5. Emitir la moneda nacional. As<92>, podemos ver que, aunque la mayor<92>a de las funciones establecidas en 1960 a<9c>n prevalecen, se han incorporado cambios significativos, como: Primero, abandonar la funci<97>n de regulaci<97>n del cr<8e>dito comercial. Y el segundo es incorporar ahora la funci<97>n de estabilidad del sistema financiero. Y es que a lo largo de nuestra historia institucional se han presentado dificultades que conllevaron a procurar diversos objetivos como: crecimiento, inflaci<97>n y tipo de cambio, como los m<87>s importantes. Lo anterior no ha sido f<87>cil de priorizar, al tener que confrontar diversos desaf<92>os derivados de acontecimientos hist<97>ricos, que han resultado en la necesidad de transitar por diferentes esquemas de conducci<97>n de nuestra pol<92>tica monetaria, cambiar<92>a, financiera y crediticia. As<92>, en diciembre de 1972 Nicaragua se enfrent<97> a uno de los choques m<87>s importantes de esa d<8e>cada, derivado del terremoto ocurrido en la capital, Managua. Con ese episodio, 12 a<96>os despu<8e>s de la fundaci<97>n del Banco Central de Nicaragua, se pon<92>a a presi<97>n el objetivo fundamental de la autoridad monetaria que era mantener la estabilidad de la moneda. A pesar de esta adversidad, el objetivo se logr<97> al preservar la paridad cambiar<92>a en el pa<92>s, y al poder contener las presiones inflacionarias que se observaron en el a<96>o 1973 y 1974. Tambi<8e>n conllev<97> al reto importante de asegurar la continuidad de los sistemas de pagos. La d<8e>cada de los ochenta fue un periodo complejo para la regi<97>n centroamericana, y en particular para Nicaragua. La ocurrencia de diversos conflictos internos en la mayor<92>a de los pa<92>ses del istmo implic<97> un reto may<9c>sculo para mantener no s<97>lo la estabilidad de precios, sino tambi<8e>n la estabilidad econ<97>mica y financiera. En Nicaragua, la d<8e>cada de los ochenta conllev<97> a cambios estructurales relevantes, al establecerse una econom<92>a mixta, la nacionalizaci<97>n de la banca, el financiamiento al sector p<9c>blico y confrontar una mayor demanda de recursos que afectaron la balanza de pagos, pero tambi<8e>n fue el escenario de bloqueos econ<97>micos y una guerra que condujo a una monetizaci<97>n de los d<8e>ficits p<9c>blicos y a una hiperinflaci<97>n, causando un elevado estr<8e>s macroecon<97>mico. Ya en la d<8e>cada de 1990 se present<97> el desaf<92>o de la consolidaci<97>n econ<97>mica. En este periodo se implementaron cambios institucionales y reformas estructurales para asegurar la previsibilidad de las pol<92>ticas. Eso se tradujo en la contenci<97>n de la inflaci<97>n a trav<8e>s de una mayor estabilidad monetaria y cambiar<92>a y reforzar el rol de la banca comercial en su papel clave para canalizar la intermediaci<97>n financiera. A pesar de que Nicaragua sufri<97> los embates clim<87>ticos como la devastaci<97>n del hurac<87>n Mitch a finales de esa d<8e>cada, se preserv<97> la estabilidad financiera, dada la fortaleza del esquema institucional prevalecido por la autoridad monetaria previamente. Esto puso de manifiesto la solidez y el liderazgo del Banco Central de manejar de forma adecuada sus pol<92>ticas. El inicio del nuevo milenio no estuvo exento de desaf<92>os. La funci<97>n del Banco Central de propiciar la estabilidad de la moneda nacional y la estabilidad financiera se vio amenazada tras la crisis bancaria interna ocurrida en el a<96>o 2000, que ocurri<97> a nivel dom<8e>stico. Las acciones inmediatas de la autoridad monetaria, en conjunto con el supervisor bancario, permitieron mitigar el efecto de los desequilibrios financieros de los bancos en la econom<92>a real. La crisis fue la base para adoptar mayores regulaciones de exigencias de capital, liquidez y gobernanza bancaria, as<92> como esquemas de garant<92>a de dep<97>sitos, que ayudaron a recuperar la confianza de los agentes en el sistema bancario, donde el Banco Central jug<97> un rol activo. Luego la crisis financiera del a<96>o 2008 fue uno de los eventos que m<87>s afect<97> econ<97>micamente a nuestros pa<92>ses en su historia reciente. El efecto de la crisis fue directo dada la alta relaci<97>n de nuestras econom<92>as con la econom<92>a mundial, principalmente mediante el canal comercial y financiero. La crisis implic<97> un enfriamiento del crecimiento econ<97>mico y posteriormente reflej<97> presiones inflacionarias. As<92>, las autoridades monetarias de nuestra regi<97>n tuvieron un menor espacio para actuar y atenuar los efectos del choque. Aun con esas limitantes, los Bancos Centrales fuimos capaces de facilitar la financiaci<97>n de actividades productivas en nuestros pa<92>ses. Posteriormente, el choque derivado de eventos sociopol<92>ticos en Nicaragua en 2018 produjo importantes desequilibrios financieros y afectaciones a la econom<92>a real. Este episodio fue, sin embargo, el escenario donde el Banco Central fortaleci<97> su pol<92>tica monetaria y cambiar<92>a, con el fin de robustecer el cumplimiento de su objetivo fundamental y puso a prueba sus atribuciones en t<8e>rminos de estabilidad financiera, la que fue garantizada a trav<8e>s de la incorporaci<97>n de nuevos mecanismos de provisi<97>n de liquidez, facilidades crediticias y emisi<97>n de marcos normativos flexibles. Del mismo modo, el a<96>o 2020 fue un a<96>o de retos para nuestra regi<97>n. Por un lado, la pandemia del Covid- 19 supuso un choque sin precedentes en t<8e>rminos sanitarios, econ<97>micos y sociales. Por el otro lado, los huracanes Eta e Iota generaron da<96>os econ<97>micos significativos en la mayor<92>a de nuestros pa<92>ses, exacerbando los ocasionados por la pandemia. Ese a<96>o se caracteriz<97> por una contracci<97>n econ<97>mica y del comercio a nivel global afectando directamente a nuestros pa<92>ses en actividades claves como la comercial, la inversi<97>n y el turismo. Ante las restricciones impuestas por la pandemia, los Bancos Centrales de la regi<97>n nuevamente nos adaptamos y ha implementado medidas innovadoras, implementando acciones convencionales y no convencionales para atenuar sus efectos. Durante la pandemia se observ<97> sincron<92>a en las decisiones tomadas por los Bancos Centrales de la regi<97>n, en lo referente a la reducci<97>n de las tasas de pol<92>tica monetaria y la provisi<97>n de liquidez; con el fin de garantizar la liquidez bancaria que suele ser demandada de forma precautoria en per<92>odos de crisis. Durante la pandemia, tambi<8e>n se han realizado esfuerzos por garantizar la fluidez del cr<8e>dito hacia los sectores productivos. En Nicaragua, particularmente, en los <9c>ltimos tres a<96>os se han implementado medidas de provisi<97>n de liquidez condicionada en otorgamiento de cr<8e>dito productivo, a fin de evitar que se genere un efecto de retroalimentaci<97>n entre la contracci<97>n econ<97>mica y la crediticia. Con ello se ha buscado atenuar la reducci<97>n repentina del cr<8e>dito derivada de los eventos adversos que han impactado al pa<92>s recientemente. Un hecho que quisiera resaltar es que el desarrollo de instrumentos de respuesta de parte de las autoridades monetarias se ha logrado implementar gracias a la continua formaci<97>n de capital humano del que disponen. Esto ha permitido que las decisiones de pol<92>tica est<8e>n fundamentadas en aspectos t<8e>cnicos, lo que contribuye a maximizar la probabilidad de <8e>xito y la efectividad de esas pol<92>ticas, de acuerdo con los objetivos para los que son dise<96>adas. En este proceso de desarrollo tambi<8e>n quisiera destacar que ha sido central la participaci<97>n de <97>rganos integradores, como el Consejo Monetario Centroamericano, que con sus atribuciones ha facilitado la comunicaci<97>n, coordinaci<97>n y adopci<97>n de pol<92>ticas de parte de los Bancos Centrales de la regi<97>n. A pesar de los avances y la madurez que han adquirido, o que hemos adquirido los Bancos Centrales, a<9c>n existen retos futuros, algunos de los cuales los podemos prever desde ahora, y otros, que seguramente nos tomar<87>n por sorpresa, como ocurri<97> con la actual pandemia. Entre estos retos podemos identificar dos: la integraci<97>n econ<97>mica y los avances tecnol<97>gicos en el campo financiero. En este sentido, es importante seguir realizando esfuerzos para que entre los pa<92>ses del istmo se siga fortaleciendo la integraci<97>n econ<97>mica. Esto con el fin de facilitar el intercambio financiero y comercial entre pa<92>ses. Debemos actuar para que el proceso de integraci<97>n se fortalezca por su propia din<87>mica, sin que en el largo plazo haya necesidad de realizar esfuerzos adicionales de parte de las autoridades para mantenerla. Es preciso que la integraci<97>n en el <87>mbito financiero se fortalezca a trav<8e>s de la modernizaci<97>n de las operaciones financieras, y en particular de los sistemas de pagos, con el fin de hacer m<87>s costo-eficientes los movimientos de recursos financieros entre nuestros pa<92>ses. Con esto se pueden dinamizar los pagos y flujos de capitales, buscando maximizar, sobre todo, el bienestar de los agentes que precisan de este tipo de facilidades financieras. En el contexto de esta integraci<97>n financiera es importante continuar fortaleciendo los esquemas regulatorios y de vigilancia, para evitar acciones relacionadas con el blanqueo de capitales y dem<87>s actividades il<92>citas que pueden poner en riesgo la credibilidad de nuestros sistemas financieros. Tambi<8e>n es importante realizar esfuerzos conjuntos para facilitar la detecci<97>n y seguimiento de actividades financieras que transgredan las leyes. Asimismo, debemos seguir trabajando en la facilitaci<97>n de la adaptaci<97>n a los continuos adelantos tecnol<97>gicos. En este sentido, es relevante promover la adopci<97>n de tecnolog<92>as que faciliten las actividades intermediadoras a los sectores tradicionalmente excluidos a trav<8e>s de la industria FinTech. Tambi<8e>n es importante adecuarnos a las nuevas tendencias en cuanto a esquemas de pago mediante plataformas BlockChain, buscando la eficiencia, agilidad y oportunidad de las operaciones financieras. Seguramente las pr<97>ximas d<8e>cadas tendr<87>n sus propias din<87>micas econ<97>micas que requerir<87>n de nuevos ajustes en las pol<92>ticas y acciones de los bancos centrales. Conf<92>o que en ese incierto futuro transitar sabremos enfrentar los nuevos retos, apoy<87>ndonos entre s<92>, como naciones centroamericanas. Para finalizar, reitero mi m<87>s sincero agradecimiento al Banco Central de Honduras por la invitaci<97>n a este evento, y por permitirme compartir con mis colegas de Bancos Centrales de la regi<97>n y dem<87>s participantes, algunas reflexiones sobre hechos relevantes de la evoluci<97>n econ<97>mica reciente, enfocadas en el quehacer del Banco Central de Nicaragua, y los retos futuros de nuestras autoridades monetarias. Muchas Gracias.

Title: Transcript of Interview on "Economic performance projects extraordinary growth 2021"
text: TRANSCRIPT OF INTERVIEW OF THE PRESIDENT OF THE BCN IN TN8 STUDY ON THE TOPIC "ECONOMIC PERFORMANCE PROJECTS EXTRAORDINARY GROWTH 2021" 09/09/2021 Erving Vega: How is it going. Good morning, welcome and welcome, thank you for joining us, a pleasure to be with you, remember every morning from Monday to Friday live from 7 to 8 in the morning and in repetition at one in the afternoon. Study TN8 for today, Thursday, September 9. Central theme: We are going to talk about the economy, we are going to talk, we are going to talk, our interviewee, our guest is the president of the Central Bank, Ovidio Reyes, whom we welcome. Thank you Ovid for joining us, welcome. President of the NCB: Thank you. Erving Vega: Welcome. The last time we spoke was to share with our viewers the behavior of our economy, evaluated from the Monthly Index of Economic Activity, which really marked a very, very positive trend. But we already have the end of the first half in terms of the behavior of the economy and everything indicates that the behavior is much better than expected, much better than estimated. And I would like you to introduce and later expand the interview. What can we say about what the economy has shown in its performance in this first half of the year? We are already talking about figures for the end of the second quarter, that is, the end of the first half of 2021. President of the NCB: That's right. Good morning, Erving. Thank you for the opportunity you give me to explain to the population economic issues. In this case, what we are publishing from the Central Bank of Nicaragua is the calculation of the Gross Domestic Product. On the previous occasion we talked about the monthly index of economic activity, which measures how the production of a set of goods and services of the economy evolves to monitor activity. But now what we have is the Gross Domestic Product, which already measures global economic evolution, includes not only the production side, but also the consumption and investment side. And that's the part we're going to add to the analysis we had done previously. In addition, the Gross Domestic Product is the standard international measure with which we can compare the economic evolution of different countries. That said, the calculation of the Gross Domestic Product in the second quarter turned out to be a growth and dynamics, as you mentioned, a little higher than what we were expecting. GDP in the second quarter was a growth of 16.7 percent. The first quarter had grown 3.8 percent. We are therefore talking about a significant increase. Here's a baseline element that is last year, GDP decreased by six and a half percent, but there's also an element of recovery because it's growing much more than there was last year. Erving Vega: When the balance sheet is made, the first semester: the first quarter, second quarter, which we have as the first semester. President of the NCB: That's right, then, when we see the accumulated, the accumulated GDP is growing 9.9 percent, rounding up 10 percent and that is a very good rate, it is a very good rate, because then it allows us now to redo and recalibrate the estimates again. But the important and relevant thing is that the economy is showing, just as we talked before that there was a generalized growth in all sectors of production, there is also a generalized growth in all sectors of expenditure, household consumption expenditure, government consumption expenditure, individual collective consumption expenditure, as well as investment. It sees growth in both public investment spending, private investment and gross fixed capital formation in general. Erving Vega: We expand the interview later and well, the question would be how do we expect to close 2021? Taking into account that we already have a first semester that GDP rounds up 10 percent. What would be the projection? How do we expect to close in 2021 and see what the sectors are?, because there are differentiated growths depending on one or another sector. President of the NCB: That's right. Erving Vega: We expand on it later. Thank you for continuing with us. As I indicated at the beginning of the program, our guest in an interview Central de Estudios TN8 today is the president of the Central Bank, Ovidio Reyes, and the topic is the performance of our economy that makes us project a closing 2021 with extraordinary growth, again Ovid, thank you for joining us and welcome. We start from the behavior of the economy at the end of the first half of the year. There we already have an accumulated 9.9 percent GDP growth, that is, rounding up 10 percent. If Nicaragua grew 0 percent in the rest of the year, what would the GDP growth rate look like? President of the NCB: If on the previous occasion we had talked about that with the estimation of the preliminary information of the Monthly Index of Economic Activity, we could be expecting a growth that could be between 4 and 6 percent. Already observing these growth figures and the trend behind them, we could make a fairly rough estimate of how the year could end and recalibrate what we had already said before. This tells us that if the economy did not grow in a second in the second half, to be conservative, then we would already have 5 percent growth. Erving Vega: Even if the economy grew zero? President of the NCB: Even if it grows to zero, which will not be the case, the safest thing will not happen because they have already passed, we are going through the third month of the second semester, and the economy continues to show dynamics as we will see in the statistics. And if we go to the trend that we believe the economy could take in the following quarters of 4 percent, then it would end the economy this year growing with 7 percent. In other words, the estimate we had previously talked about was moved by one percentage point. That is, we could end the year growing instead of the 4 or 6 percent we had predicted, between 5 and 7 percent of growth. Erving Vega: The 5 already guaranteed? President of the NCB: The 5 is the floor, right? Now, this is also corroborated by other statistical indicators that we obtain from the original GDP series. For example, in the Gross Domestic Product report there is a series that we calculate from the observed data that is called the trend-cycle series of GDP. That is, we obtain, the high peaks and the low peaks are extracted and an intermediate point is obtained. Well, at that midpoint, quarterly GDP is growing 5.7 percent year-over-year which is roughly the range we're mentioning between 5 and 7. And when you take that same trend and remove those irregular elements, you see that only from one month to the next, from the quarter to the next, for example from this second quarter against the first quarter, the growth was 2.1 percent, that is, an important rate is added every quarter, but the trend also, Then place us in this estimate that I have mentioned. Erving Vega: Once again we are talking here about Nicaragua, on the road to recovery. We've talked every time we talk about growing a little bit. Well, we talked about how fast, at what pace we walk or march on that road to recovery, because well, we had already had growth rates of the order of 5 percent here for many years and back before the unfortunate events, the 2018 coup attempt. What pace are we setting to redirect this scenario? President of the NCB: We think that the Nicaraguan economy in the global context of recovery may well have a 2021 growing at that rate between 5 and 7, but also the momentum can last in 2022, it can be maintained, perhaps a little less, but with a boost higher than the trend we are observing. Then we think that the economy could be between 4 and 5 percent already by the end of or the beginning of 2022 the rate could start to land at 4 percent or 5 percent average growth, that is more or less our global estimate. But in our monetary projections and those we incorporate into global analyses, we are a bit more conservative and take the lowest scenarios, but it is important to see what factors may be behind. Erving Vega: But hey, there's an estimate, a projection of at least a couple of years with strong growth rates. President of the NCB: We could say that the average of 4 percent, which is what we estimate in the long term, three Or four years, if we estimate a minimum 4 percent, these two years are going to be well above that. Erving Vega: Now we are not here sinning of too much optimism, because more or less it is also a scenario that is also presenting at the global level. President of the NCB: That's right. All the economies of the world are showing a fairly strong, important recovery. In fact, all economies, in the estimates of the main organizations, are showing growth rates higher than their trend, with the consequence that it also has a higher expenditure of higher inflation and that Nicaragua is not exempt. We are also getting rates a little slightly above the rates we have been observing regularly. But, yes, we are indeed going to be in two good years above the averages. Erving Vega: Which sectors are showing better performance? President of the NCB: Yes, in the case of value added, what measures the Gross Domestic Product, it is observed, for example, that agriculture in the semester, true, is growing by 3.4 percent, although in the second quarter it grew 0.8 percent due to the factors we talked about last time, especially climatic elements that have been affecting agriculture a little. But the livestock sector grew already in the second quarter 12.1 percent and grows in the semester 6.2 percent. Fisheries and aquaculture grew 27.07 percent in the second quarter and is now growing 14.6 percent. The exploitation of mines and quarries we have been mentioning, has had an important rebound due to two factors due to the export of gold, silver and minerals, but also because there has been a recovery of construction, as we will see, and therefore increases the production of quarry, select material, crushed stone, carbonate, plaster, and all of it grew in the second quarter 91 percent forgiveness and now grows in the accumulated of the semester 55 percent. The manufacturing industry has also had an important rebound, since a part of the industrial sector is measured by the agro-export production that is growing. Livestock, for example, that I mentioned, but also for the Free Trade Zone, production of textile harnesses and tobacco production. In this case, the second quarter grew by 35 percent and has already accumulated 19.2 percent. The construction activity, this activity we measure by the areas effectively built through a survey carried out by the INIDE in this case, and is growing 31.7 percent in the second quarter and so far in the first semester grows 30.4 percent. It is also important to highlight the recovery observed in electricity generation, which had been a little low, is growing in the second quarter by 13.5 percent and 6.3 percent in the accumulated. On the other hand, another important sector that has to do with the dynamics of consumption is the trade sector, the second quarter saw a growth of 28 percent trade and now accumulates 16.8 percent. And the hotels and restaurants that we have always said was seen as one of the sectors most affected by the pandemic and the lack of influx of tourists, already in the second quarter grew by 52 percent compared to the second quarter of the previous year and, however, still shows a reduction so far this year of 1.7 percent, But the remarkable thing is the significant growth that was observed in the second quarter after it came in negative, and the hotels and restaurants sector is already showing an improvement. The other sector is transportation and communications, which is growing and showed a significant recovery in the second quarter, which was 10.5 percent, although it accumulates 4.2 percent in the semester. These two sectors had really been with quite timid growth rates and now they already show a recovery and that of financial intermediation that continues in negative, decreasing by 5 percent that nevertheless, credit activity is already showing rates of 2.4 percent and this sure in the following quarters will reverse this trend. Erving Vega: Financial intermediation, which is nothing more than loans. President of the NCB: The loans, on the lending sector that was quite timid, but as I mentioned in the previous interview, the negative rate is becoming less negative and already in the last two months it is presenting positive rates, then, the safest thing is that already in this quarter and in the subsequent one it will reflect positive rates. Erving Vega: Is there liquidity? President of the NCB: There is plenty of liquidity. Erving Vega: Has savings grown? President of the NCB: Savings have grown. But there, on the financial issue, we should expect that already in this second semester savings will decrease a little. Because consumption and investment are returning, and therefore, it is going to make use of that surplus of liquidity that was in the financial system, including the surplus reserves that we have in the Central Bank of Nicaragua. Back to the subject... Erving Vega: But is the projection around the behavior of financial intermediation that it is increasingly mobilized? President of the NCB: Of course, the growth rate, for example, of savings is 20 percent of aggregate savings in the economy, and credit that was negative in the first half of the year already in the last two months is growing at 2 percent. Therefore, we should expect that this economic dynamic, which is very strong, will also generate greater demand for intermediation. Erving Vega: That in turn, has an impact, right?, in the dynamics, since economic growth are projects, they are... President of the NCB: That's right, it should reflect economic growth, but here there are paradigms that are going to have to be reviewed, because what the economy has shown is that it is quite resilient, even the financing of banking activity and even when the activity banked in three years was negative, the economy recovered first than the banked activity, So it's a pretty strange phenomenon, but we're going to have to study it. Erving Vega: That's it, it's already studied enough to explain how this happens? President of the NCB: In fact, it is a rather strange phenomenon that productive activity has gone ahead of banking activity. Well, to a large extent the export sector is financed with sources not necessarily banked or unconventional, and the production sector also has investments that finance it directly. So it's something we're going to have to go deeper into later. Erving Vega: Well, there is a set of programs too that don't necessarily depend on right? bank financing and yes more government policies that mobilize, let's say, small producers, entrepreneurship and all that. President of the NCB: That's right, and they also looked for their own resources, that is a fact in the economy, that there was a lot of effort of the country, of the nation to push, and of entrepreneurs, and that is the result. On the other hand, I would now like to refer to another element and component that is measured with the Gross Domestic Product, which is the expenditure component. That is, if "x" amount of production is produced, well, you also have to spend that amount in some way, and the way we see it is that you measure consumption, investment and also incorporate the levels of spending on exports and what is spent on imports, and What resulted in the second quarter? Well, that consumption grew 10.6 percent and already accumulates a growth of 7 percent, than investment; Gross capital formation grew by 58.3 percent and now accumulates 31 percent. Exports in the second quarter grew 43.6 percent and accumulates 21.3 percent, which is quite similar to the data we have been talking about exports that are growing around 20 percent. Erving Vega: Is there a direct relationship there between imports and consumption? President of the NCB: Yes, because imports feed consumption, for example, imports are required for the acquisition of vehicles, for the acquisition of durable goods such as appliances, computers, even clothing and a wide variety of other goods that are brought from abroad. And as for imports, this important dynamic is also noticeable. For example, in the second quarter they are growing 36.5 percent, versus just 0.1 percent in the first quarter. So, that's where you see that spending is effectively being recomposed and that all activity is increasing. Erving Vega: Is this good or bad? President of the NCB: Imports are already growing by 18 percent during the first half of the year. Now, this is good, this is not bad. Imports are used for three purposes, right?, imports for consumption, but also imports of capital goods and imports of intermediate goods. Even there are the oil companies for mobilization. So, if imports are growing, it is a sign that aggregate spending in the economy is also growing and therefore, that inputs and capital goods are being supplied to production, then it is a good sign. As you can see then the generalized dynamics. For example, in the case of individual consumption, family consumption, these are growing 1 percent, the collective is growing 11 percent and individual household consumption is growing 12.5 percent. This is also coupled with the dynamics observed in imports, but also with the dynamics observed on the production side, and already in the accumulated 7.8 percent this type of consumption grows. And if we do not go into more detail, for example, in the second quarter, perhaps the most outstanding on the side of gross capital formation was the growth of private investment, the fixed, this grew 80 percent in the second quarter compared to the second quarter of the previous year, and already accumulates a growth of 45.2 percent. For its part, public investment is growing by 25 percent. Overall, gross fixed capital formation is growing by 37.9 percent. Just as we mentioned that the recovery is widespread on the production side, it is now also widespread on the expenditure side. And as I also mentioned in the previous presentation, I already believe that we are in this quarter, not only in a moment of recovery, but in the search for that path of growth that we have been talking about. Erving Vega: Employment? President of the NCB: Employment is stable. It has been recovering in the figures that will be presented today by the National Institute of Information and Development, the INIDE, it is shown that the net employment rate at the national level stands at 94.9 percent, that indicates an unemployment rate of 5.1 percent. Most importantly, rates remain in stable ranges, she is always between a range between 4.8 and 5.3 percent. In recent quarters it has remained at 4.8, 4.9, 5.1, that is, we are in a fairly positive situation and the information that we will also be publishing the latest information from the Social Security Institute also show a stability of occupation in the case of formal employment. Erving Vega: We talked or you shared data on imports, well, there we are talking about foreign trade, but we do not talk about the other component, which are exports. President of the NCB: Well, also the Central Bank is recently publishing Foreign Trade information for the month of July. The previous time we had talked about the month of June and there is even some advance information from the Export Processing Center that indicates that the dynamics are continuous, it has not stopped. For example, already speaking in millions of exportable dollars, that is the reading of the export sector, as of July we have an accumulated of 2,137.3 million dollars, in the last interview we talked about 1,824, well, we are already 2,137 million dollars against 1,764 million of the accumulated to July of the previous year. And if we look at imports on the side, we are already at 3,398 million dollars imported in July against 2,492 million dollars the previous year. That is going to lead to an increase in the trade deficit, which again is not a bad sign, of course, if the reduction of the trade deficit occurs due to an unusual increase in exports, it is a good sign, in this case it is happening with an increase in exports and an increase in imports, then, it is a good sign, and what does it mean in the case of the deficit? Well, this has reached the month of July 1,260 million dollars and has increased because last year it was barely 728 million dollars, but because spending had fallen and because the economy was really negative the previous year. Then, when we go to export goods, we observe the same phenomenon, generalized everything. Users can review the statistics that we are going to locate on the website of the Central Bank to evaluate each of the items. For example, in the case of coffee, 402.2 million dollars were already accumulated in January-July against 382 million dollars the previous year. Then, the peanut accumulates a growth of 63.9 million dollars against 55.5 million dollars the previous year and fishing 67.7 million dollars, 61.4 million dollars the previous year. Mining is already at 512.6 million dollars against 338 million dollars the previous year and all manufacturing is exporting 934 million dollars against 761 million dollars the previous year and there is again widespread growth in all export items. That adds up to the 2.137 billion we mentioned. And if it is the side of imports, already in January-July we also observed generalized dynamics, for example, consumer goods 1,277 million dollars against 1,051 million dollars the previous year, oil and fuels 618 million dollars and 389 million dollars the previous year, in intermediate goods, 1,060 million dollars against 816 million dollars the previous year and capital goods 725.8 million versus 333 million the previous year. As you can see Erving intermediate goods, capital goods, that go straight to production also grow at the same rate of consumption. Erving Vega: Is this investment, whether new or an expanding operation? President of the NCB: This is investment. They are capital goods for agriculture and industry. They are products that are used to generate more production, this tool and industrial machinery, equipment for telecommunications, machinery and apparatus of trades, services and scientific, that is, it is direct support to production. Por ejemplo, en el segundo trimestre ellas est<87>n creciendo un 36.5 por ciento, versus apenas un 0.1 por ciento en el primer trimestre. Entonces, ah<92> es donde se ve que efectivamente se est<87> recomponiendo el gasto y que est<87> aumentando toda la actividad. Erving Vega: <c0>Esto es bueno o malo? Presidente del BCN: Un 18 por ciento ya crecen las importaciones durante el primer semestre. Ahora, esto es bueno, esto no es malo. Las importaciones se utilizan para tres prop<97>sitos, <c0>verdad?, importaciones para consumo, pero tambi<8e>n importaciones de bienes de capital e importaciones de bienes intermedios. Incluso ah<92> est<87>n las petroleras para la movilizaci<97>n. Entonces, si las importaciones crecen, es una se<96>al de que el gasto agregado en econom<92>a tambi<8e>n est<87> creciendo y por lo tanto, que se est<87> abasteciendo de insumos y de bienes de capital a la producci<97>n, entonces, es una buena se<96>al. Como podr<87>s observar entonces la din<87>mica generalizada. Por ejemplo, en el caso del consumo individual, del consumo de la familia, estos est<87>n creciendo 1 por ciento, el colectivo est<87> creciendo 11 por ciento y el consumo individual de los hogares est<87> creciendo 12.5 por ciento. Esto est<87> aparejado tambi<8e>n con la din<87>mica observada en las importaciones, pero tambi<8e>n con la din<87>mica observada por el lado de la producci<97>n, y ya en el acumulado crecen 7.8 por ciento este tipo de consumo. Y si no vamos m<87>s al detalle, por ejemplo, en el segundo trimestre, quiz<87> lo m<87>s destacado por el lado de la formaci<97>n bruta de capital fue el crecimiento de la inversi<97>n privada, la fija, esta creci<97> 80 por ciento en el segundo trimestre comparado con el segundo trimestre del a<96>o anterior, y ya acumula un crecimiento del 45.2 por ciento. Por su parte, la inversi<97>n p<9c>blica est<87> creciendo un 25 por ciento. En general, la formaci<97>n bruta de capital fijo est<87> creciendo un 37.9 por ciento. As<92> como hab<92>amos mencionado de que la recuperaci<97>n est<87> generalizada en el lado de la producci<97>n, tambi<8e>n ahora ya se encuentra generalizada por el lado del gasto. Y como mencion<8e> tambi<8e>n en la presentaci<97>n anterior, ya creo que estamos en este trimestre, ya no solo en un momento de recuperaci<97>n, sino en la b<9c>squeda de esa senda de crecimiento que hemos venido platicando. Erving Vega: <c0>El empleo? Presidente del BCN: El empleo est<87> estable. Ha venido recuper<87>ndose en las cifras que va a estar presentando hoy el Instituto Nacional de Informaci<97>n y Desarrollo, el INIDE, se muestra que la tasa neta de ocupaci<97>n a nivel nacional se ubica en 94.9 por ciento, eso indica una tasa de desempleo de 5.1 por ciento. Lo m<87>s importante es que las tasas se mantienen en rangos estables, ella se encuentra siempre entre un rango entre 4.8 y 5.3 por ciento. En los <9c>ltimos trimestres se ha mantenido en 4.8, 4.9, 5.1, es decir, nos encontramos en una situaci<97>n bastante positiva y la informaci<97>n que estaremos publicando tambi<8e>n la <9c>ltima informaci<97>n del Instituto de Seguridad Social tambi<8e>n muestran una estabilidad de ocupaci<97>n en el caso del empleo formal. Erving Vega: Hablamos o nos compartiste datos sobre las importaciones, bueno, ah<92> estamos hablando de comercio exterior, pero no hablamos del otro componente, que son exportaciones. Presidente del BCN: Bueno, tambi<8e>n el Banco Central est<87> recientemente publicando la informaci<97>n de Comercio Exterior al mes de julio. La vez anterior hab<92>amos hablado del mes de junio e incluso ya hay alguna informaci<97>n adelantada del Centro de Tr<87>mite de Exportaci<97>n que indican que la din<87>mica viene continua, no ha parado. Por ejemplo, ya hablando en millones de d<97>lares exportables, eso es la lectura del sector exportador, al mes de julio tenemos un acumulado de 2,137.3 millones de d<97>lares, en la <9c>ltima entrevista habl<87>bamos de 1,824, bueno, ya estamos de 2,137 millones de d<97>lares contra 1,764 millones del acumulado a julio del a<96>o anterior. Y si vemos por el lado las importaciones, pues ya estamos en 3,398 millones de d<97>lares importados al mes de julio contra 2,492 millones de d<97>lares el a<96>o anterior. Eso va a conllevar a un aumento del d<8e>ficit comercial, que nuevamente no es una mala se<96>al, claro, si la reducci<97>n del d<8e>ficit comercial ocurre por un aumento inusitado de exportaciones, es una buena se<96>al, en este caso est<87> ocurriendo con aumento de exportaciones y aumento de importaciones, entonces, es una buena se<96>al, <c0>Y qu<8e> significa en el caso del d<8e>ficit? Bueno, que este ha alcanzado al mes de julio 1,260 millones de d<97>lares y se ha aumentado porque el a<96>o pasado apenas era de 728 millones de d<97>lares, pero porque el gasto hab<92>a bajado y porque la econom<92>a estaba realmente en negativo el a<96>o anterior. Luego, cuando vamos a los bienes de exportaci<97>n, observamos el mismo fen<97>meno, generalizado todo. Los usuarios pueden revisar las estad<92>sticas que vamos a ubicar en la p<87>gina web del Banco Central para evaluar cada uno de los rubros. Por ejemplo, en el caso del caf<8e> ya se acumulan 402.2 millones de d<97>lares en enero-julio contra 382 millones de d<97>lares el a<96>o anterior. Luego, el man<92> acumula un crecimiento de 63.9 millones de d<97>lares contra 55.5 millones de d<97>lares del a<96>o anterior y la pesca 67.7 millones de d<97>lares, 61.4 millones de d<97>lares el a<96>o anterior. La miner<92>a ya est<87> en 512.6 millones de d<97>lares contra 338 millones de d<97>lares el a<96>o anterior y toda manufactura est<87> exportando 934 millones de d<97>lares contra 761 millones de d<97>lares del a<96>o anterior y se observa nuevamente crecimiento generalizado en todos los rubros de exportaci<97>n. Eso nos suma los 2,137 millones de d<97>lares que hab<92>amos mencionado. Y si es el lado de las importaciones, ya en enero-julio observamos tambi<8e>n din<87>micas generalizadas, por ejemplo, bienes de consumo 1,277 millones de d<97>lares contra 1,051 millones de d<97>lares el a<96>o anterior, el petr<97>leo y combustibles 618 millones de d<97>lares y 389 millones de d<97>lares el a<96>o anterior, en bienes intermedios, 1,060 millones de d<97>lares contra 816 millones de d<97>lares el a<96>o anterior y bienes de capital 725.8 millones de d<97>lares contra 333 millones de d<97>lares del a<96>o anterior. C<97>mo podr<87>s observar Erving los bienes intermedios, bienes de capital, que van directo a la producci<97>n tambi<8e>n crecen a la misma velocidad del consumo. Erving Vega: <c0>Esto es inversi<97>n, ya sea nueva o una operaci<97>n que se ampl<92>a? Presidente del BCN: Esto es inversi<97>n. Son bienes de capital para la agricultura y la industria. Son productos que se utilizan para generar m<87>s producci<97>n, est<87> herramienta y maquinaria industrial, equipos para telecomunicaciones, maquinaria y aparatos de oficios, servicios y cient<92>fico, es decir, es directo apoyo a la producci<97>n. Erving Vega: Ahora, los bienes de consumo, uno entender<92>a, la gente est<87> comprando m<87>s, y tiene un impacto en el estado de bienestar de la familia, de las personas en t<8e>rminos de que compran para satisfacer alguna necesidad, etc. <c0>Pero tiene su impacto tambi<8e>n en la inflaci<97>n? Presidente del BCN: S<92>, pero me gustar<92>a mencionar algunos bienes de consumo que los mencionaste, por ejemplo, los bienes no duraderos. Los clasificamos en dos: bienes duraderos, por ejemplo, cuando uno consume, uno puede consumir un televisor que va a tardar varios a<96>os el televisor de vida <9c>til, pero tambi<8e>n puede consumir bienes de consumo inmediato, por ejemplo, una lata de sardinas. Entonces, los no duradero crecen 1,074 millones contra 913 millones del a<96>o anterior y los bienes duraderos crecen 202.7 millones de d<97>lares contra 137 del a<96>o anterior, en otras palabras, estamos hablando de un crecimiento de un 80%. Ahora, los bienes duraderos como aparatos el<8e>ctricos y electrodom<8e>sticos, son bienes muy <9c>tiles porque aumentan la productividad del hogar. No son bienes de consumo de distracci<97>n, sino que son bienes que vienen a mejorar el bienestar de los hogares. <c0>C<97>mo afecta esto la inflaci<97>n? Bueno, s<92> lo afecta, porque primero el mundo est<87> teniendo una inflaci<97>n y una demanda generalizada de bienes de consumo. Ha aumentado la demanda por autom<97>viles, ha aumentado la demanda por computadora, la demanda por celulares, ha aumentado la demanda de todos los electrodom<8e>sticos de los televisores, porque la pandemia llev<97> a muchas familias, a muchos pa<92>ses al confinamiento y entonces la gente aument<97> la demanda de Medios de Comunicaci<97>n y de producci<97>n incluso comestibles dentro del hogar, entonces, los precios se han aumentado a nivel mundial. Hay algunas econom<92>as industriales que est<87>n creciendo con una inflaci<97>n del 6 por ciento, cuando sus inflaciones hab<92>an sido del 2 <97> 3 por ciento. Entonces, al aumentar el consumo y al aumentar las importaciones, se aumenta tambi<8e>n el componente importado de inflaci<97>n. El INIDE hoy tambi<8e>n va a estar publicando el <92>ndice de Precios al Consumidor y se observa, pues, que la inflaci<97>n del mes de agosto fue de 0.24 por ciento. Ya la inflaci<97>n acumula 2.84 por ciento en lo que va del a<96>o. Esto es un poco mayor que lo que acumul<97> el a<96>o pasado, y la interanual, que es la de tendencia, se ubica en 4.98 por ciento. Nosotros pensamos que va a andarse ubicando alrededor de un 4.5 por ciento, es un poco superior a la del a<96>o pasado, que finaliz<97> en 2.9 por ciento, entonces s<92> hay un componente de inflaci<97>n que, no obstante, para nuestro pa<92>s esto es una inflaci<97>n realmente moderada, la econom<92>a la absorbe sin mayor problema. Erving Vega: <c0>Y 4.5 por ciento, eso es lo estimado? Presidente del BCN: 4.5 por ciento (de inflaci<97>n) es lo que estar<92>amos estimando. Nosotros en nuestra estimaci<97>n por rango, la tenemos entre 3.5 y 4.5 por ciento, pero a como est<87> resultando ya la inflaci<97>n al mes de agosto podr<92>amos finalizar en un 4.5 por ciento. Me gustar<92>a tambi<8e>n destacar la evoluci<97>n de la Zona Franca en sus exportaciones que se presentan en el reporte de exportaci<97>n enero-julio. Las exportaciones de Zona Franca est<87>n creciendo en este acumulado ya en 1,897 millones de d<97>lares, el a<96>o pasado est<87>s eran de 1,305 millones de d<97>lares, hay un importante crecimiento tambi<8e>n ac<87> de que 592 millones de d<97>lares de aumento de las exportaciones de Zonas Francas y nuevamente observamos un crecimiento generalizado en todos los sectores: aceite de palma 33.2 millones de d<97>lares contra 13.4 millones de d<97>lares el a<96>o anterior, arneses 374.9 millones de d<97>lares contra 186.5 millones de d<97>lares el a<96>o anterior, textil 1,008 millones de d<97>lares contra 755 millones de d<97>lares el a<96>o anterior y el tabaco 184.3 millones de d<97>lares contra 126.2 millones de d<97>lares del a<96>o anterior. Y luego los otros productos: productos pesqueros, frutas y hortalizas, el cart<97>n, tambi<8e>n est<87>n mostrando din<87>micas positivas. Entonces, como podr<87>s observar ya el informe enero-julio tambi<8e>n reafirma de que la econom<92>a contin<9c>a esta tendencia, y la informaci<97>n adelantada de la CETREX, igual. Erving Vega: Sobre el tema de las Zonas Francas, bueno, convers<8e> con Alfredo Coronel, Vicepresidente de la Comisi<97>n Nacional de Zona Franca el martes, y me gustar<92>a destacar y agregar en ese punto dos datos que nos comparti<97>, es la inversi<97>n al menos siete proyectos en ejecuci<97>n en este momento, 7 entre zonas francas o complejos que se ampl<92>an y otros nuevos, y en ese sentido, una proyecci<97>n de crecimiento del empleo hasta cerrar 2021 en 130,000 empleos. Presidente del BCN: As<92> es. Erving Vega: Y caminando a 135 mil para el 2022, dice Alfredo Coronel. Y ya estamos en 125,500, que era el dato que ten<92>amos o la cantidad de empleo en Zonas Francas que ten<92>amos antes de la intentona golpista de 2018. Presidente del BCN: S<92>, el empleo est<87> tambi<8e>n mostrando una recuperaci<97>n y est<87> mostrando una sostenibilidad que es m<87>s importante, es decir, los empleos que se han recuperado se han mantenido, en algunos casos estos han incrementado, pero lo que est<87> ocurriendo no solo en Nicaragua, en el mundo entero, es que hab<92>a mucho empleo antes de la pandemia, porque la din<87>mica mundial era positiva, vino la pandemia y se redujo mucho el empleo, luego el empleo creci<97>, pero se qued<97> ah<92>, en el mundo entero. Erving Vega: <c0>Se estanc<97>? Presidente BCN: Se qued<97> all<92> sin crecer m<87>s r<87>pido. Y pueden haber muchos factores que expliquen esto, pero pareciera ser que un factor importante es que las personas que salieron y buscaron otros empleos se quedaron en esa condici<97>n de emprendedurismo, trabajos desde casa, es decir, ha habido un cambio importante en la forma incluso como la gente est<87> ahora trabajando despu<8e>s de la pandemia, entonces nosotros deber<92>amos esperar de que la recuperaci<97>n econ<97>mica contin<9c>e estas din<87>micas y que el empleo tambi<8e>n crezca, aunque crezca a menor velocidad que la producci<97>n. Eso es un fen<97>meno mundial que est<87> ocurriendo y nosotros no vamos a estar exento del mismo, pero lo importante es de que se mantienen las tasas. Por ejemplo, te mencion<8e> de que en el caso del informe de empleo, de la Encuesta Continua de los Hogares se mantiene la participaci<97>n neta de la poblaci<97>n en 94.9 por ciento, que es una tasa importante, y el empleo de la Seguridad Social se est<87> manteniendo alrededor de los 758 mil empleos en lo que va de este mes. Erving Vega: Tengo una segunda pausa. Voy a venir con las conclusiones del Presidente del Banco Central despu<8e>s de este corto. Gracias por continuar con nosotros conversando esta ma<96>ana con Ovidio Reyes, Presidente del Banco Central. A manera de conclusiones Ovidio, me gustar<92>a m<87>s que agregar, recapitular un poco los datos m<87>s relevantes. Estamos hablando, el dato m<87>s importante es el PIB, <c0>verdad? Producto Interno Bruto, primer semestre con un comportamiento de 9.9, redondeando 10 y con una proyecci<97>n de cerrar entre 5 y 7 por ciento el a<96>o 2021. Presidente BCN: As<92> es. Erving Vega: <c0>Qu<8e> significa? <c0>Qu<8e> tan bueno es esto para la econom<92>a y qu<8e> podemos esperar en t<8e>rminos del impacto a toda la escala de la econom<92>a nacional? Presidente BCN: Si, <8e>stos resultados del segundo trimestre significan que la econom<92>a ya est<87> entrando a una din<87>mica fuerte de crecimiento y de recuperaci<97>n, en sinton<92>a con lo que est<87> ocurriendo en Centroam<8e>rica y las principales econom<92>as industriales, es decir, nuestro pa<92>s se encuentra bien en t<8e>rminos econ<97>micos, se encuentra sano financieramente y adem<87>s de eso se encuentra con generaci<97>n de empleo y con inflaci<97>n baja y moderada. Eso es bueno, porque entonces las expectativas de las empresas, de los empresarios, de los due<96>os de negocios son positivas, en ese escenario, y significa tambi<8e>n que podemos tener entonces esta misma din<87>mica hacia este y el pr<97>ximo a<96>o, manteni<8e>ndose constante, y recuperando el terreno que se hab<92>a perdido en estos tres a<96>os precedentes de crecimiento negativo. Erving Vega: Much<92>simas gracias por habernos acompa<96>ado

Title: Speech at the Opening of the Exhibition "Masters of Nicaraguan Plastic Art"
text: WORDS OF THE PRESIDENT OF THE BCN, OVIDIO REYES R. AT THE INAUGURATION OF THE EXHIBITION "MASTERS OF PLASTIC ARTS NICARAGUAN" 20/10/2021 Since 1964, when it began its collection of plastic arts, the Central Bank of Nicaragua has been characterized by encouraging the creativity of our artists and recognizing their values. Among many other activities, we must highlight the edition of two wonderful books, very well illustrated and translated into English, in which the history of painting and sculpture in Nicaragua is developed. The promotion of young artists has also been a permanent object of the Bank, through annual competitions that have borne the name of great masters such as Alejandro Alonso Rochi, Rodrigo Penalba, Armando Morales, Fernando Saravia, Alejandro Arostegui and Amoldo Guillen, recently deceased. All were projected abroad where they thoroughly carried out their work and obtained excellent critical reception. On this occasion, the Bank sponsors an exhibition-sale of the following masters of Nicaraguan plastic arts, currently alive, who have continued the example of the previous teachers cited. I am referring to Roger Perez de la Rocha, Alfonso Ximenez, Leonel Cerrato, Aparicio Artola, Sergio Velazquez, Porfirio Garcia Romano, Itziar Garralda, Jair Sanchez, Reinaldo Bosquez, Socrates Martinez, Raul Valverde, Rebeca Carolina Flores, Ricardo Gomez and Sara Lynn. In total, FOURTEEN plastic artists, whose varied styles and technical resources can be seen from today October 20 until the 29th of the current month. Welcome, therefore, to this call for solidarity with our creators of visual beauty, all of them industrious and aware that life is short and art perennial. My greetings to all, hoping that those visitors interested in art, not only enjoy, but also acquire their works for personal enjoyment and family. Thank you very much and have a good afternoon.

La promoci<97>n de artistas j<97>venes tambi<8e>n ha sido objeto permanente del Banco, a trav<8e>s de cert<87>menes anuales que han llevado el nombre de grandes maestros como Alejandro Alonso Rochi, Rodrigo Pe<96>alba, Armando Morales, Fernando Saravia, Alejandro Ar<97>stegui y Amoldo Guill<8e>n, recientemente fallecido. En esta oportunidad, el Banco auspicia una exposici<97>n-venta de los siguientes maestros de la pl<87>stica nicarag<9f>ense, actualmente vivos, que han continuado el ejemplo de los anteriores maestros citados. Me refiero a R<97>ger P<8e>rez de la Rocha, Alfonso Xim<8e>nez, Leonel Cerrato, Aparicio Artola, Sergio Vel<87>zquez, Porfirio Garc<92>a Romano, Itziar Garralda, Jair S<87>nchez, Reinaldo B<97>squez, S<97>crates Mart<92>nez, Ra<9c>l Valverde, Rebeca Carolina Flores, Ricardo G<97>mez y Sara Lynn.
