Title: Report on the State of the Economy and Perspectives
text: REPORT ON THE STATE OF THE ECONOMY AND PROSPECTS, WORDS OF THE PRESIDENT OF THE BCN, OVIDIO REYES R. 28/10/2021 Good morning. Thank you to everyone who sees and hears us through the media, as well as those present for joining us in this presentation of the State of the Economy and Outlook Report 2021, which will also be published today on the BCN website. This report aims to present an assessment of the main macroeconomic aggregates, describes the economic policy actions implemented and presents a projection of the main macroeconomic variables, with emphasis on the strengths and risks that could arise both in the national and international context. Next, I will summarize the content of this Report, as well as a reference to the Financial Stability Report recently published by our institution and which is part of this evaluation. Economic Developments The State of the Economy and Outlook report highlights that, in 2021, the Gross Domestic Product (GDP) showed a significant economic recovery, consolidating the positive trajectory that had been observed since the end of 2020, after the economy was affected by COVID-19. Most economic sectors are already reactivated and growing. The main impulse came from higher exports, caused by a resurgence of international demand and better external prices, as well as the advance of vaccination that improved expectations, increasing aggregate spending, both consumption and investment, consequently also increased imports. Employment stabilized with a moderate unemployment rate. After having observed a global rate of labor participation rising at the end of the second half of last year, during 2021 it returned to the average, indicating that the labor market has not yet completed its adjustment and that the pandemic could be affecting both labor supply and demand. The recovery of economic activity and higher demand have put pressure on prices, which have grown during 2021. The main factors driving higher inflation have been international, such as: higher fuel prices, rising international freight transport costs, supply chain shortages and fiscal stimulus packages that increased spending. Monetary variables continue to perform well, reinforcing the space for economic recovery. In this regard, all monetary aggregates continued to reflect positive double-digit interannual rates of change. The exchange market remained stable and the BCN, through its monetary operations, continued to promote an adequate management of the liquidity of the financial system that supported the accumulation of international reserves. Financial intermediation has continued its stabilization process in line with the actions of the economic authorities to safeguard financial stability, particularly in the face of the stress scenario caused by COVID-19. Thus, the growth of deposits, bank credit and the stability of liquidity and solvency indicators stand out. For its part, credit has begun to grow in year-on-year terms since May 2021 as demand returns and financial conditions have improved, which have entered the upward part of the financial cycle. Public finances have seen a significant improvement in tax collection, but maintained a prudent policy in terms of spending, prioritizing social spending on health and investment in productive infrastructure. Likewise, the management of internal and external financing has allowed the healthy financing of the public deficit, which has been under and controlled, with growth in indebtedness below what has happened in other countries. The recovery of the world economy has boosted stronger external demand and boosted the price of export products, reflected in greater dynamism. The international environment has also facilitated greater flows of family remittances, mainly from growing economies, as well as an increase in foreign investment flows. Financial Stability For its part, the Financial Stability Report indicates that during 2021, Nicaragua consolidated financial stability in the midst of a significant economic recovery that has improved the expectations and payment capacity of households and companies. Banking and financial institutions also show stability. In particular, there is a return in banking financial intermediation activity, with credit beginning to flow to the productive sectors, which will enhance the current economic recovery and the stability of the national financial system. For their part, the main financial markets have strengthened their stability. The exchange market develops without demand pressures, which was reflected in a smaller exchange rate gap in sales. The money market continued to provide liquidity to the financial system and the Central Bank of Nicaragua (BCN) maintained an accommodative policy with the reference rate of monetary reports (TRM) stable, at a low level. The stock market continued to facilitate transactions in securities, particularly public securities, which show a reduction in their rates. The credit market began to reflect positive growth, which will reinforce the process of economic recovery. The mortgage market shows signs of stabilization. Meanwhile, the insurance market continues to increase its hedging operations against risks. At the local level, the main financial indicators reflected stabilization and increases and, in several cases, reduction of vulnerabilities, such as: The valuation of asset prices does not present imbalances, behaving in line with the economic recovery. Aggregate liquidity has remained stable at high levels. The leverage of the financial system shows a reduction, although decreasing, mainly from external financiers, as obligations to the public continue to grow. Consistent with the economic recovery, household and corporate indebtedness began to grow, having declined through the first quarter of 2021, which would increase the capacity to generate higher spending. Public debt continued to rise, but under concessional conditions of low interest rates and long repayment terms. Perspectives Taking into account the favorable external environment and the positive evolution of domestic economic activity in the first part of the year, as well as the solid condition of financial stability, the BCN estimates that the Nicaraguan economy will grow in 2021 in a range of between 6.0 and 8.0 percent. This growth projection is based on: the recovery of the world economy that will have a positive effect on export demand, remittances and the private flow of financing, the recovery of credit, the advance of vaccination and the better expectations that have activated consumer and investment spending. As for inflation, it is projected that by 2021 it will be in a range of between 4.5 -5.5 percent, as a result, above all, of the pass-through of international prices to domestic prices. This higher inflation, compared to that observed in 2020, is mainly due to: the rise in international fuel prices, the increase in transport costs due to logistical problems in supply chains and the increase in global demand for goods and services as a result of the economic recovery. In this environment, the NCB will continue to maintain an accommodative monetary policy for the remainder of 2021, with emphasis on financial intermediation and the mobilization of credit to the productive sectors. No changes are expected in the BCN's TRM for the remainder of the year, although vigilance will be maintained to react in correspondence with movements in international interest rates and domestic monetary conditions. Exchange rate policy will also remain unchanged, with a changed slide of 2 percent annually. Despite the favorable outlook, there is still some uncertainty and risks that a resurgence of COVID-19 and its variants will slow down the global recovery, or at least limit it. An additional external risk factor could be a persistent increase in the level of international prices that affects inflation expectations and makes central banks react with a reversal of monetary stimulus programs and interest rate hikes that would tighten global financial conditions. In our stress analyses that we published in the Financial Stability Report, it is shown how the economy presents a great residence against these shocks, so we expect full compliance with the projections and estimates that we are presenting on this occasion. So far the presentation of the State of the Economy Report. Thanks a lot

La recuperaci<97>n de la actividad econ<97>mica y la mayor demanda han presionado los precios, los que han crecido durante 2021. Los principales factores que impulsaron la mayor inflaci<97>n han sido de orden internacional, como lo son: el alza de los precios de los combustibles, el aumento de los costos de transporte de carga internacional, el desabastecimiento de la cadena de suministros y los paquetes de est<92>mulos fiscales que aumentaron el gasto. La intermediaci<97>n financiera ha continuado su proceso de estabilizaci<97>n en l<92>nea con las acciones de las autoridades econ<97>micas para salvaguardar la estabilidad financiera, particularmente, frente al escenario de estr<8e>s provocado por el COVID-19. As<92>, se destaca el crecimiento de los dep<97>sitos, del cr<8e>dito bancario y la estabilidad de los indicadores de liquidez y de solvencia. Por su parte, el cr<8e>dito ha comenzado a crecer en t<8e>rminos interanuales desde mayo de 2021 al retornar su demanda y al mejorarse las condiciones financieras que han entrado en la parte ascendente del ciclo financiero. Las finanzas p<9c>blicas han observado una mejora significativa de la recaudaci<97>n tributaria, pero mantenido una pol<92>tica prudente en t<8e>rminos de gasto, priorizando el gasto social en salud y de inversi<97>n en infraestructura productiva. Asimismo, la gesti<97>n del financiamiento interno y externo, han permitido el financiamiento sano del d<8e>ficit p<9c>blico el que ha estado bajo y controlado, con crecimiento del endeudamiento por debajo de lo ocurrido en otros pa<92>ses. La recuperaci<97>n de la econom<92>a mundial ha impulsado una mayor demanda externa y ha favorecido el precio de los productos de exportaci<97>n, lo que se ha reflejado en un mayor dinamismo. Asimismo, el entorno internacional ha facilitado mayores flujos de remesas familiares, principalmente las provenientes de econom<92>as en crecimiento, as<92> como un aumento en los flujos de inversi<97>n extranjera. Estabilidad Financiera Por su parte, el Informe de Estabilidad Financiera indica que durante 2021, Nicaragua consolid<97> la estabilidad financiera en medio de una significativa recuperaci<97>n econ<97>mica que ha mejorado las expectativas y la capacidad de pago de los hogares y las empresas. Particularmente, se observa un retorno de la actividad de intermediaci<97>n financiera bancaria, con el cr<8e>dito comenzando a fluir hacia los sectores productivos, lo que vendr<87> a potenciar la recuperaci<97>n econ<97>mica actual y la estabilidad del sistema financiero nacional. Por su parte, los principales mercados financieros han afianzado su estabilidad. El mercado cambiarlo se desarrolla sin presiones de demanda, lo que se reflej<97> en una menor brecha cambiar<92>a de venta. El mercado monetario continu<97> proveyendo de liquidez al sistema financiero y el Banco Central de Nicaragua (BCN) mantuvo una pol<92>tica acomodaticia con la tasa de referencia de reportos monetarios (TRM) estable, a un bajo nivel. El mercado de valores continu<97> facilitando las transacciones de t<92>tulos, particularmente p<9c>blicos, los que presentan una reducci<97>n en sus tasas. El mercado de cr<8e>dito comenz<97> a reflejar un crecimiento positivo, que reforzar<87> el proceso de recuperaci<97>n econ<97>mica. El mercado hipotecario presenta se<96>ales de estabilizaci<97>n. Mientras que, el mercado de seguros contin<9c>a aumentando sus operaciones de cobertura frente a riesgos. A nivel local, los principales indicadores financieros reflejaron estabilizaci<97>n e incrementos y, en varios casos, reducci<97>n de vulnerabilidades, como las siguientes: La valoraci<97>n de los precios de los activos no presenta desequilibrios, comport<87>ndose en l<92>nea con la recuperaci<97>n econ<97>mica. La liquidez agregada se ha mantenido estable, ubic<87>ndose en niveles elevados. El apalancamiento del sistema financiero muestra una reducci<97>n, aunque cada vez menor, principalmente el proveniente de financiadores externos, ya que contin<9c>an creciendo las obligaciones con el p<9c>blico. Consistente con la recuperaci<97>n econ<97>mica, el endeudamiento de los hogares y las empresas comenz<97> a crecer, despu<8e>s de haber disminuido hasta el primer trimestre de 2021, lo que aumentar<92>a la capacidad para generar un mayor gasto. La deuda p<9c>blica continu<97> aumentando, pero en condiciones concesionales de bajas tasas de inter<8e>s y largos plazos de repago. Perspectivas Tomando en cuenta el entorno externo favorable y la evoluci<97>n positiva de la actividad econ<97>mica dom<8e>stica en la primera parte del a<96>o, as<92> como la condici<97>n s<97>lida de la estabilidad financiera, el BCN estima que la econom<92>a nicarag<9f>ense crecer<87> en 2021 en un rango de entre 6.0 -8.0 por ciento. Esta proyecci<97>n de crecimiento est<87> sustentada en: la recuperaci<97>n de la econom<92>a mundial que tendr<87> un efecto positivo sobre la demanda de exportaciones, las remesas y el flujo privado de financiamiento, la recuperaci<97>n del cr<8e>dito, el avance de la vacunaci<97>n y las mejores expectativas que han activado el gasto de consumo y de inversi<97>n. En cuanto a la inflaci<97>n, se proyecta que para 2021 esta se ubicar<87> en un rango de entre 4.5 -5.5 por ciento, como resultado, sobre todo, del traspaso de los precios internacionales a los precios dom<8e>sticos. Esta mayor inflaci<97>n, respecto de la observada en 2020, se debe principalmente a: el alza en los precios internacionales de los combustibles, el aumento de los costos de transporte debido a problemas log<92>sticos en las cadenas de suministros y al aumento de la demanda global de bienes y servicios como secuencia de la recuperaci<97>n econ<97>mica. En este entorno, el BCN continuar<87> manteniendo una pol<92>tica monetaria acomodaticia en lo que resta de 2021, haciendo <8e>nfasis en la intermediaci<97>n financiera y la movilizaci<97>n del cr<8e>dito hacia los sectores productivos. No se esperan cambios en la TRM del BCN para lo que resta del a<96>o, aunque se mantendr<87> la vigilancia para reaccionar en correspondencia con los movimientos de las tasas de inter<8e>s internacionales y de las condiciones monetarias internas. La pol<92>tica cambiar<92>a tambi<8e>n se mantendr<87> inalterada, con un deslizamiento cambiado del 2 por ciento anual. Pese a las perspectivas favorables, persiste a<9c>n cierta incertidumbre y riesgos de que un rebrote del COVID-19 y sus variantes, frene la recuperaci<97>n mundial, o al menos la limite. Un factor de riesgo externo adicional podr<92>a ser un incremento persistente en el nivel de precios internacionales que afecte las expectativas de inflaci<97>n y haga reaccionar a los bancos centrales con una reversi<97>n de los programas de est<92>mulo monetario y aumento de las tasas de inter<8e>s que endurecer<92>a las condiciones financieras globales. En nuestros an<87>lisis de estr<8e>s que publicamos en el Informe de Estabilidad Financiera se muestra como la econom<92>a presenta una gran residencia frente a estos choques, por lo que esperamos el cumplimiento pleno de las proyecciones y estimaciones que estamos presentando en esta ocasi<97>n. Hasta aqu<92> la presentaci<97>n del Informe de Estado de la Econom<92>a. Muchas gracias

Title: Remarks to the Media on the presentation of the State of the Economy and Perspectives 2021
text: STATEMENTS BY BCN PRESIDENT OVIDIO REYES R. TO THE MEDIA IN THE PRESENTATION OF THE STATE OF THE ECONOMY AND OUTLOOK 2021 29/10/2021 Journalist Kenia Dona, Channel 4: How is the Nicaraguan economy and the prospects? President of the NCB: On this occasion we have presented the State of the Economy and Outlook 2021 report. In March we had submitted our first report and this time we are reviewing our estimates. And everything indicates that the revision that we have been carrying out, now comes upwards, given that the economy, as a whole, has been reacting very well throughout the year: trade has grown, exports have grown, investment is growing, even imports, as a result of the reactivation of demand that has been driven by many factors. The first thing is that in the current context vaccination is already advancing and that has made expectations improve. But also economies, such as industrial and emerging economies, are growing at significant rates of 6 percent. Nicaragua, then, is part of that environment, our exports have increased and that has driven greater production and greater demand. So, we believe that for this year, which at the beginning we had expected growth within, 2 and a half and 3 and a half percent, then we revised it towards a growth of between 5 and 7 percent, this time, we are talking about a growth of between 6 and 8 percent. We are also making a slight adjustment in inflation expectations, as fuel prices are impacting the entire world and input costs are rising. There are many problems in supply chains that have increased transportation costs, although in the world, and also in Nicaragua, it is perceived as a transitory phenomenon. So, that's in great summary what we are projecting. We see that public finances are also quite stable. Investment programs are giving another boost to the economy, especially those that have to do with investment and infrastructure, investment in health, spending that is being made, as well as that investment that is also made from municipalities in social housing. So, that, coupled with the fact that banks have already recovered their ability to grant credit and the demand for credit has returned, makes us now in a more optimistic scenario. And that's why it's our expectation that the economy will end up growing between 6 and 8 percent. Journalist Marcos Medina, Channel 12: Was a policy recently announced of not transferring the rise in the international price of fuels to prices in Nicaragua? How might this affect these growth projections? President of the NCB: In the case of inflation, we already have them incorporated. In fact, cumulative inflation is 5.86 percent and that's why our limit is now five and a half percent, we have incorporated that new reality. This will undoubtedly contribute to a stability of inflation variability and will support economic recovery. *Explanatory note: Refers to year-on-year inflation Journalist Kenia Dona, Channel 4: In the case of this economic figure that Nicaragua obtains of growth of 6 to 8 percent, taking into account scenarios of other countries that are well below. President of the NCB: Yes, we believe we are in a good position. Last year, if there was a decrease of 2 percent, so it is logical that in the face of that scenario we will now have positive growth. But the important thing is that we are growing much more than expected, than average. And we are, I think, at the average level, above the rest of the country estimates. And that's very good for Nicaragua. Journalist Kenia Dona, Channel 4: In the case of stable employment and growth conditions. According to the perspective? President of the NCB: Indeed, financial stability, macroeconomic stability, monetary, for example, the exchange market, as we mentioned in our report, is totally stable. There is a significant flow of foreign exchange of more than 4,000 million dollars in purchases and sales of foreign currency. There is financial flow, increased remittances, increased foreign investment, also, we are receiving reports that existing companies are leading... Existing foreigners are leading this investment. So I think this year is going to end in a very good perspective and lays the groundwork for next year to continue. Journalist Marcos Medina, Channel 12: In the case of employment, you mentioned that it has not yet recovered so quickly due to the pandemic situation and other social situations, what do you foresee then for this next one? President of the NCB: Yes. The unemployment rate we are seeing moderate around 5 percent on average during the first half of the year. The economy has been able to have an unemployment rate of 3 percent. In that sense we see that, as has been happening around the world, both companies are being prudent in hiring and have increased their efficiency, and people who also have fears because vaccination levels have not yet been reached. We believe that when that market stabilizes, then the unemployment rate is going to fall faster.

Title: Evolution of Direct Foreign Investment
text: EVOLUTION OF FOREIGN DIRECT INVESTMENT WORDS OF BCN PRESIDENT OVIDIO REYES R. 04/11/2021 Good morning, everyone. Thanks to those who are watching and listening to us through the different media. Today we are presenting a report on the update and evolution of Foreign Direct Investment in Nicaragua for the first half of 2021. The Central Bank has been publishing reports on improvements in Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) indicators, which is carried out according to comparable international standards. This work is carried out with the recommendations and accompaniment of international organizations that register these flows, such as the CAPTAC-DR center of the International Monetary Fund. In the last three years, FDI flows in Nicaragua have been affected by socio-political events and recently, in 2020, by the COVID-19 pandemic. In our records published in the Annual Report of the Central Bank for 2020 and the last Balance of Payments report for the first half of 2021, this impact is observed. But with recent information, this one seems to have been better and the result of the first half of 2021 is very encouraging. For this reason, we are proceeding with this publication and updating of data on our website that we want to make known to the population and investors. This update of Foreign Direct Investment is made with data from the Quarterly Foreign Investment Survey that consults 225 companies with foreign capital participation, and which is described below. In 2020, the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on the net income and flows of Foreign Direct Investment was observed. However, as happened in the rest of the countries of the Central American region, Panama and the Dominican Republic, in the first half of 2021, they showed a recovery trend, aligned with the recovery of economic activity and the world economy. Thus, in the first half of 2021, gross income from Foreign Direct Investment in Nicaragua amounted to 632.1 million dollars, which represented 1.9 times the amount registered in the same period of 2020, when it was 334.9 million dollars. This increase came mainly from new investments that were financed through its parent company, as well as from the recovery of income from Foreign Direct Investment. The amount of foreign investment income represented 9.3 percent of GDP, (5.5% in the first half of 2020). In relation to net flows, these were 577.8 million, resulting in an increase of 371.6 million compared to The same period of 2020, when it was 206.2 million dollars, an increase that came mainly from new investments in the energy and mining sector, and from greater reinvestments of profits in companies in the manufacturing, telecommunications, commerce and services sectors, among others. The economic sector with the highest net flow of Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) was Energy and Mines with 261.5 million dollars (US61.1 million in the first half of 2020), for comparison purposes; followed by the Telecommunications sector with 95.8 million dollars (US40.1 million in the first half of 2020); Industry by registering 80.9 million dollars (US23.2 million in the first half of 2020); Financial Sector with 44.6 million dollars (US27.2 million in the first half of 2020); and Trade and Services with 40.3 million dollars (US32.2 million in the first half of 2020); among others. In terms of the source of net FDI flows, 214.4 million dollars were recorded from the United States, representing 37.1 percent of total net income received. Canada and Mexico recorded net flows of 101.1 million (17.5% of the total) and 76.3 million (13.2% of the total), respectively. From Central America, there was net flow from Panama for 80.3 million dollars (13.9% of the total), followed by Costa Rica with 18.5 million dollars (3.2% of the total). From other regions, the net flow from Spain stands out with 49.1 million dollars, which represented 8.5 percent of the total income in the period. In the first half of 2021, net FDI flows registered in the Central American region, Panama and the Dominican Republic totaled 6,317.7 million dollars, being 36.0 percent higher than that observed in 2020, when it was 4,645.3 million dollars. Title: Press Conference Seasonal Liquidity Projections for the end of 2021
text: PRESS CONFERENCE SEASONAL LIQUIDITY PROJECTIONS FOR THE END OF 2021 PRESIDENT OF THE BCN, OVIDIO REYES R. 11/11/2021 Good morning, we have convened you on this occasion to explain about the liquidity projections that the Central Bank is making towards the end of 2021 and that we recently published in a press release yesterday. The importance of being able to evaluate and be able to make a reference of how the year will end is that, during the end of the year, the months of November and December, we all know that there are relevant parties and extraordinary income of resources for families, for people, as it is in the first place the Christmas bonus and also sources of financing from remittances, as well as the credit that occurs as a result of this event. On top of that, two key holidays occur that are important to the family. One is the activity of celebration of the Immaculate Conceptions, which occurs in the first weeks of December, and the other is the celebration of Christmas on December 24. And I would add a third, which would be the New Year's Eve celebrations on December 31. These events generate positive expectations in all economic agents and a lot of joy, and people look forward to the dates. Specifically, last year we estimated, for example, a bonus of 10, 966 million cordobas, for this year we would be waiting for a bonus of 12 thousand 246 million cordobas. In other words, we are talking about a significant increase of 12 percent of the Christmas bonus. One of the important factors is the recovery in employment that has been taking place. The latest figure we have received from the Social Security Institute in terms of formal employment indicates that employment would be reaching, already towards the last month that we have recorded, which is the month of October and that we will publish soon, the 760,000 formal employees. These will receive their bonus and also the rest of the employees of the economy, not necessarily the formal ones, also the informal sector are given bonuses. As a result, it will generate a monetary flow that we expect to go from 5,982 million to 6,523 million cordobas this year, that is, an increase of 541 million cordobas in the money supply, that is, 9 percent more than that observed last year. The maximum of this emission reaches around the first 10 days of December and we would expect it to go from 6,383 million cordobas that was last year, to 7,444.9 million cordobas during this year, that is, an increase of 1,061 million cordobas. In growth rate, the expansion of liquidity in the economy represents a 17 percent growth. On the other hand, commercial activity comes at a very good pace that is reflected in the volume of sales collected by the General Directorate of Revenue and also in the amounts of collection reported, which are reported to the Ministry of Finance and Public Credit. Last year, the amount of commercial activity, sales, registered, reached the sum of 41, 178.4 million cordobas. This year we are projecting 52,730.4 million cordobas. With the trend we have been observing, we believe that this growth will be the equivalent of 28 percent, that is, a greater increase in sales of commercial activity by 11,552 million cordobas. On the other hand, the credit, as we have been mentioning in our reports, has been recovering and we would expect that of 1,092 million cordobas of credit that was delivered last year, remember that last year we were quite affected by the pandemic itself and by other factors, this year it reaches the sum of 2,331.9 million cordobas, that is, 1,238 million cordobas more, an increase of a little more than 100 percent. On the other hand, the indicator of external income flow, which is closely linked to the commercial activity and the purchasing activity of the family, has to do with family remittances, which will basically support the family sustenance of many families in the country. Last year 343 million cordobas entered this period, that is, from here until the end of the year, November-December, and this year we would be expecting an increase of 382 million cordobas, 38.8 million dollars of increase, that is, a growth of 11 percent. In summary, what we are observing is that the dynamics that the recovery economy has been showing will also be reflected in the expansion of commercial activity and credit activity, due to the increase in remittances and the significant increase that the delivery of the Christmas bonus is obtaining. So we join this celebration, let's call it that, because it really is, of delivery of this benefit that all workers receive, and we call on merchants, workers themselves, sellers and companies to take advantage of this moment to make sales. Remember that part of the expectation of many companies and businesses is to be able to take advantage of the Christmas bonus to make products. For example, we have been observing an increase in imports of products in consumer goods that are undoubtedly going to be and are destined for this time of year. So it is a time when all businesses, small businesses and also transportation activity businesses, such as collective transport activity and taxi activity, and private transport activity, take advantage, truth, to be able to make sales and obtain extraordinary profits at this time of year. So this is the explanation of what we published yesterday and we hope that it will be of benefit and very useful for all of you and our population. Thanks a lot.

text: WORDS OF THE PRESIDENT OF THE BCN, OVIDIO REYES R. AT THE AWARD CEREMONY OF THE PAINTING CONTEST: NICARAGUA: PROUD OF ITS CULTURE AND TRADITIONS. 18/11/2021 Good morning, everyone. Title: Remarks to the Media Award Ceremony of the Economics, Finance and Development Award 2021 and Journal Presentation of Economics, Finance and Development, Vol. 8 2021
text: STATEMENTS TO THE MEDIA AWARD OF THE ECONOMIC, FINANCE AND DEVELOPMENT AWARD CONTEST 2021 AND PRESENTATION OF THE MAGAZINE OF ECONOMY, FINANCE AND DEVELOPMENT, VOL. 8 2021 STATEMENTS TO THE MEDIA AWARD OF THE ECONOMIC, FINANCE AND DEVELOPMENT AWARD CONTEST 2021 AND PRESENTATION OF THE MAGAZINE OF ECONOMY, FINANCE AND DEVELOPMENT, VOL 8 2021 25/11/2021 President of the NCB: The Central Bank of Nicaragua has been promoting economic research among young people and independent professionals every year; They participate in these contests, send their works. This year 13 works arrived in different topics, monetary topics, finance topics, public sector topics and also productive sector topics, as was the expression of third place in cocoa research. The others are macroeconomic issues, which are about seeking and finding economic relationships that we did not know existed. And that is the meaning of this research to know a little more about Nicaragua, how it works, what are the parameters that are moving the main factors of development so that they contribute, through these studies, to decision-making and knowledge of our reality. Journalist, Winston Lopez, Radio La Primerisima: And do they coincide with reality, with the panorama we have right now? President of the NCB: All the studies that we have promoted are applied studies and try to extract from the data the best experiences found in them, to disseminate that information and make it public knowledge. These reports are already published on our website, everything can be found there, download and know in detail, right?, what each of them is about. Journalist Tania Sirias, Channel 2: President, have we seen investigations how the pandemic and the crisis have affected our economy, but, nevertheless, do they announce that there is growth of the Gross Domestic Product of our country? President of the NCB: Indeed, because the pandemic became a disruption that had to be treated with various mechanisms, but the fundamental one was health. And today that the health authorities have already announced that more than 60 percent of the population is vaccinated, that has allowed the economy to revive its production again and now we find ourselves an important moment of economic expansion. The Monthly Index of Economic Activity accumulated to September already reflects a significant growth of the 6.9 percent, almost 7 percent growth so far this year, and in the accumulated reflects 9.2 percent. The Central Bank has had an estimate of between 6 and 8 percent and what the IMAE is reflecting is that a growth of 6.9 percent is already guaranteed, with the information of the accumulated of 9 percent so far this year. So, yes, these studies are linked to what is happening in our reality and to the important recovery that our entire economy is showing. Journalist Winston Lopez, Radio La Primerisima: What is the reason for this significant growth? President of the NCB: Well, the world economy is expanding, the main economies of the world are promoting economic reactivation plans and that has greatly increased the prices of our export product, but also the demand, so we are placing more export products. We are also observing a very important dynamic in the trade sector that is growing between 8 and 9 percent, after the pandemic, it has been reactivated. And also the return of private investment is a determining factor, we are observing growth in the areas effectively built, and finally, we have also recently seen positive information of foreign direct investment that has been reactivated. All these factors are encompassed and that is the economic result we are observing. Well, thank you very much.

Title: Award Ceremony of the "Economics, Finance and Development Award 2021" and Presentation of Volume 8 of the "Journal of Economics and Finance 2021"
text: AWARD OF THE CONTEST "ECONOMIC, FINANCE AND DEVELOPMENT AWARD 2021" AND PRESENTATION OF VOLUME 8 OF THE "REVISTA DE ECONOMiA Y FINANZAS 2021" PRESIDENT OF THE BCN, OVIDIO REYES R. 25/11/2021 Good morning, everyone. I would like to warmly welcome you to the award ceremony of the contest "Economy, Finance and Development Award 2021" and the presentation of Volume 8 of the "Journal of Economy and Finance" promoted and promoted by the Central Bank of Nicaragua. For the Central Bank, it is very gratifying to have the presence of researchers, special guests, Central Bank officials and the media today. The Central Bank carries out various activities every year to promote economic research, recognizing the importance of having technical studies that support effective decision-making, both on the part of those responsible for monetary and exchange rate policy and on the part of the different economic agents. This is an ongoing process, not only because of the diversity of issues that affect the economic well-being of society, but also because of the changing environment facing our economy. Regarding the Economy, Finance and Development Award, one of the most outstanding activities in this effort to contribute to knowledge is the Economy, Finance and Development Award, since through this contest the Central Bank invites all members of society, whether independent researchers, think tanks, students, teachers, members of the private or public sector, that is, everyone, to contribute to economic research for the development of our country. This year, in response to the call of the Central Bank, 13 investigations were presented in the contest, which were carried out by students and independent researchers. The topics addressed in the studies were very varied, including the real sector, prices, public policies, and issues in the monetary, exchange rate and financial spheres. In the real sector, the research addressed issues related to shocks to productivity, economic cycles, disturbances in aggregate supply and demand, a sectoral analysis on cocoa cultivation and a study focused on the territorial development of the Ometepe biosphere reserve. Fiscal policy addressed the issue of the progressivity of labor income in Central America. And in the monetary, financial and changing spheres, the topics included the monetary compensation and sterilization coefficient, the determinants of the exchange rate gap, financial conditions and the competition of the Nicaraguan banking system. We thank all participants for their contributions. For the 2021 Economy, Finance and Development Prize, the qualifying jury decided to award three prizes and a special mention to the following works: First, the prize for first place was awarded to the study "Financial conditions and their contribution to macroeconomic fluctuations: Evidence for Nicaragua during the years 2003 to 2018", by authors Norvin Antonio Duarte, Klaus Aristides Fletes Espino and Norman Benigno Rios Matute, who are independent researchers and one is a master's student. I am going to ask you to stand up so that we can give the respective applause to the winners of the first place of the prize. Thanks a lot. The second place was awarded to the work "Shocks to productivity and real economic cycles in Nicaragua", by author David Ernesto Miranda Largaespada, university student. You are with us, please, thank you very much, congratulations. The third place was awarded to the work "Geospatial analysis of the stochastic frontier model in the cultivation of slime cocoa in Nicaragua", by the author Luisa Amanda Lopez Merlo, independent researcher. He is with us too, congratulations. The special mention went to the study "Chronology of economic cycles in Nicaragua: An analysis of turning points for the period 2006-2021", by researcher Israel Munguia Martinez. You are here with us too. We congratulate the winners for the recognition of their effort and dedication and for their contribution to research. On the other hand, as we mentioned, we are also presenting the Journal of Economics and Finance. The Bank promotes research through dissemination in this journal. Thus, today we are also pleased to report its publication, volume number 8 and new research papers in the series of Working Papers and a new series of Technical Papers. The research included in the journal and in the series is nourished by the winning works of the Economy, Finance and Development Prize of previous years, as well as the research agenda of the Central Bank of Nicaragua. This volume of the Journal of Economics and Finance contains five investigations, which are: The first, The Gender Pay Gap: Triple Penalty? woman, mother, and informal, by author Jonathan Josue Garcia Fuentes. The third research is A Credit Value at Risk model to manage the credit risk of the investments of International Reserves of the Central Bank of Nicaragua, by the author Jeancarlo Lopez Olivas. The fourth research is Stylized facts of the Nicaraguan economy, by author William Alberto Mendleta Alvarado; and the fifth research is called Economic Cost of Conflicts in Nicaragua: A Synthetic Control Approach, by author Nestor Adolfo Torres Betanco. I congratulate all of them and I also thank the officials of the Central Bank of Nicaragua for their contributions. Finally, I thank everyone present for their participation in this event. The Central Bank of Nicaragua will continue its commitment to promote research, especially those studies that contribute to the design and analysis of economic policies aimed at promoting inclusive and sustainable economic and financial growth. Thanks a lot.

Title: GDP Results for the Third Quarter of 2021 and Perspectives
text: GDP RESULTS FOR THE THIRD QUARTER 2021 AND OUTLOOK BCN PRESIDENT OVIDIO REYES R. GDP RESULTS FOR THE THIRD QUARTER 2021 AND OUTLOOK BCN PRESIDENT OVIDIO REYES R. 13/12/2021 Good morning to all those present at this event, journalists and the population that listens to us on the radio and sees us on television, or by any other means of communication. This morning, the Central Bank of Nicaragua presents the results of the evolution of economic activity, measured by the Gross Domestic Product to the third quarter of the year, which also allows us to make a more precise estimate of the expected result for 2021 and make a first approximation of what could be the result of economic activity in 2022. Economic developments in the third quarter of 2021 The year 2021 has been the year of Nicaragua's economic recovery. The pandemic generated great tension on our economy and public health, exerting a negative effect in 2020, both on production and employment. However, the effective response of public policies and the constant promotion of production have had a positive result in 2021, highlighting the recovery of the primary sector and exports, which facilitated the aggregate recovery of Consumption and Investment. The result of the Gross Domestic Product for the third quarter of 2021 published today by the Central Bank of Nicaragua on its website, indicates that economic activity during the third quarter presented a year-on-year growth of 9.7 percent. It should be noted that the year-on-year economic growth of the first quarter was 3.7 percent and that of the second quarter was 17.0 percent. With this, the accumulated economic growth during 2021 amounts to 9.9 percent. By the focus of production, the sectors with the highest accumulated growth during the year have been: mining and quarrying (43.2%), construction (40.7%), commerce (17.3%), manufacturing industry (14.7%), electricity (8.1%), livestock (6.8%), hotels and restaurants (6.5%), transport and communications (6.4%), agriculture (3.1%) and water (2.8%). By the expenditure approach, the different components showed accumulated growth in the following order of relevance: gross capital formation grew by 37.8 percent, of which private fixed investment grew by 39.8 percent and public fixed investment grew by 39.5 percent, then imports grew by 19.5 percent, exports grew by 17.4 percent, while consumption grew by 7.6 percent, of which, individual household consumption grew by 8.2 percent and government consumption grew by 4.9 percent. As can be seen, the main economic sectors are no longer only recovering, but expanding. We can infer from this behavior that the economy is returning to a new path of medium-term economic growth that we expect to strengthen in the coming year. The consequence of this improved economic performance is that employment has also been recovering, with a reduction in the unemployment rate that stood in the third quarter in 4.3 percent, even though the overall labor participation rate stands at 65.6 percent. For its part, formal employment measured by affiliation to the Nicaraguan Social Security Institute improved through the month of November, when 774,404 affiliates were registered, presenting a year-on-year growth of 8.4 percent. The recovery of the global economy and fiscal and monetary stimulus policies have boosted global spending and pushed up the expectations of the main players. As a result, there has been a significant rise in energy and fuel prices and a widespread adjustment in commodity prices, exacerbated by difficulties in supply chains and the emergence of new variants of COVID-19. In this way, inflation has resurfaced in the main industrial economies, transferring this effect also to our economy. Thus, the national inflation accumulated to November stood at 5.7 percent, while year-on-year inflation was 7.1 percent. Core inflation, which isolates the most volatile goods from the basket of goods with which the CPI is calculated, has also increased, standing at 5.0 percent. The Central Bank of Nicaragua expects this increase in inflation to be transitory, as it is mainly caused by external elements and especially by the impact of the rise in fuel prices, which seem to have reached an international maximum with a tendency to stabilize in the following year. Outlook 2021 and 2022 The good results of economic activity observed in September motivate the Central Bank of Nicaragua to make an upward adjustment to our estimate of economic growth for 2021, which now goes from an expected economic growth of between 6.0 and 8.0 percent to an economic growth of between 7.5 and 9.5 percent. For our part, we are also revising upwards the estimate of inflation for 2021, which goes from an expected inflation of between 5.0 and 6.0 percent to inflation of between 6.0 and 7.0 percent. For 2022, the Central Bank of Nicaragua estimates economic growth of between 3.5 and 4.5 percent and inflation estimated at a range of between 2.5 and 3.5 percent. We attach to this report a table with the main aggregate macroeconomic indicators that we hope will serve as a working guide for economic agents and the population in general, to formulate their production and business forecasts in the coming year. Finally, it remains for me to thank the help of all those Nicaraguans who pledged all their resources so that Nicaragua achieved higher levels of activity and positive economic prospects, which allow us to put our country back on the path of development and progress. Thank you very much and have a nice day.

RESULTADOS DEL PIB AL TERCER TRIMESTRE 2021 Y PERSPECTIVAS PRESIDENTE DEL BCN, OVIDIO REYES R. 13/12/2021 Buenos d<92>as a todos los presentes en este evento, periodistas y poblaci<97>n que nos escucha por la radio y nos ve por la televisi<97>n, o por cualquier otro medio de comunicaci<97>n. En esta ma<96>ana, el Banco Central de Nicaragua presenta los resultados de la evoluci<97>n de la actividad econ<97>mica, medida por el Producto Interno Bruto al tercer trimestre del a<96>o, que nos permite, as<92> mismo, realizar una estimaci<97>n m<87>s precisa del resultado esperado para 2021 y efectuar una primera aproximaci<97>n de lo que podr<92>a ser el resultado de actividad econ<97>mica de 2022. Evoluci<97>n econ<97>mica al tercer trimestre de 2021 El a<96>o 2021 ha sido el a<96>o de la recuperaci<97>n econ<97>mica de Nicaragua. La pandemia gener<97> gran tensi<97>n sobre nuestra econom<92>a y la sanidad p<9c>blica, ejerciendo un efecto negativo en 2020, tanto en la producci<97>n como en el empleo. Sin embargo, la efectiva respuesta de pol<92>ticas p<9c>blicas y la constante promoci<97>n de la producci<97>n han ejercido un resultado positivo en 2021, destac<87>ndose la recuperaci<97>n del sector primario y de las exportaciones, que facilitaron la recuperaci<97>n agregada del Consumo y de la Inversi<97>n. El resultado del Producto Interno Bruto al tercer trimestre de 2021 que ha publicado hoy el Banco Central de Nicaragua en su p<87>gina web, indica que la actividad econ<97>mica durante el tercer trimestre present<97> un crecimiento interanual de 9.7 por ciento. Hay que destacar que el crecimiento econ<97>mico interanual del primer trimestre fue de 3.7 por ciento y el del segundo trimestre fue de 17.0 por ciento. Con ello, el crecimiento econ<97>mico acumulado durante 2021 asciende a 9.9 por ciento. Por el enfoque de la producci<97>n, los sectores de mayor crecimiento acumulado durante el a<96>o han sido: explotaci<97>n de minas y canteras (43.2%), construcci<97>n (40.7%), comercio (17.3%), industria manufacturera (14.7%), electricidad (8.1%), pecuario (6.8%), hoteles y restaurantes (6.5%), transporte y comunicaciones (6.4%), agricultura (3.1%) y agua (2.8%). Por el enfoque del gasto, los diferentes componentes mostraron crecimiento acumulado en el siguiente orden de relevancia: la formaci<97>n bruta de capital creci<97> en 37.8 por ciento, de la cual, la inversi<97>n fija privada creci<97> en 39.8 por ciento y la inversi<97>n fija p<9c>blica creci<97> en 39.5 por ciento, luego, las importaciones crecieron en 19.5 por ciento, las exportaciones crecieron en 17.4 por ciento, mientras que el consumo creci<97> en 7.6 por ciento, del cual, el consumo individual de los hogares creci<97> en 8.2 por ciento y el consumo del Gobierno creci<97> en 4.9 por ciento. C<97>mo puede observarse, los principales sectores econ<97>micos se encuentran ya no s<97>lo en recuperaci<97>n, sino que en expansi<97>n. Podemos inferir a la luz de este comportamiento que la econom<92>a est<87> retornando a una nueva senda de crecimiento econ<97>mico de mediano plazo que esperamos se afiance en el siguiente a<96>o. La consecuencia de este mejor desempe<96>o econ<97>mico es que el empleo tambi<8e>n se ha venido recuperando, observ<87>ndose una reducci<97>n en la tasa de desempleo que se ubic<97> en el tercer trimestre en 4.3 por ciento, aun cuando la tasa global de participaci<97>n laboral se ubica en 65.6 por ciento. Por su parte, el empleo formal medido por la afiliaci<97>n al Instituto Nicarag<9f>ense de Seguridad Social mejor<97> hasta el mes de noviembre, cuando se registraron 774,404 afiliados, presentando un crecimiento interanual de 8.4 por ciento. La recuperaci<97>n de la econom<92>a mundial y las pol<92>ticas de est<92>mulo fiscal y monetario han impulsado el gasto mundial e influenciado hacia el alza las expectativas de los principales agentes. Debido a esto, se ha observado un alza importante en los precios de la energ<92>a y los combustibles y un ajuste generalizado de los precios de las materias primas, exacerbados por dificultades en las cadenas de suministros y por la aparici<97>n de nuevas variantes del COVID-19. De esta manera, la inflaci<97>n ha resurgido en las principales econom<92>as industriales traslad<87>ndose este efecto tambi<8e>n a nuestra econom<92>a. As<92>, la inflaci<97>n nacional acumulada a noviembre se ubic<97> en 5.7 por ciento, mientras que la inflaci<97>n interanual fue de 7.1 por ciento. Tambi<8e>n la inflaci<97>n subyacente, que a<92>sla los bienes m<87>s vol<87>tiles de la canasta de bienes con que se calcula el IPC, se ha visto incrementada, ubic<87>ndose en 5.0 por ciento. El Banco Central de Nicaragua espera que este incremento en la inflaci<97>n resulte transitorio, al estar originado principalmente por elementos externos y sobre todo por el impacto que ha tenido el alza de los precios de los combustibles, los que parecen haber alcanzado un m<87>ximo internacional con tendencia a estabilizarse en el siguiente a<96>o. Perspectivas 2021 y 2022 Los buenos resultados de la actividad econ<97>mica observados a septiembre motivan al Banco Central de Nicaragua a realizar un ajuste hacia el alza a nuestra estimaci<97>n de crecimiento econ<97>mico para 2021, que ahora pasa de un crecimiento econ<97>mico esperado de entre 6.0 y 8.0 por ciento a un crecimiento econ<97>mico de entre 7.5 y 9.5 por ciento. Por su parte, tambi<8e>n estamos revisando hacia el alza la estimaci<97>n de la inflaci<97>n para 2021, la que pasa de una inflaci<97>n esperada de entre 5.0 y 6.0 por ciento a una inflaci<97>n de entre 6.0 y 7.0 por ciento. Para el 2022, el Banco Central de Nicaragua estima un crecimiento econ<97>mico de entre 3.5 y 4.5 por ciento y una inflaci<97>n estimada en un rango de entre 2.5 y 3.5 por ciento. Adjuntamos a este informe una tabla con los principales indicadores macroecon<97>micos agregados que esperamos sirva de gu<92>a de trabajo para los agentes econ<97>micos y la poblaci<97>n en general, para formular sus previsiones de producci<97>n y negocios en el nuevo a<96>o que se avecina. Por <9c>ltimo, me resta agradecer el concurso de todos aquellos nicarag<9f>enses que empe<96>aron todos sus recursos para que Nicaragua alcanzase mayores niveles de actividad y perspectivas econ<97>micas positivas, lo que nos permiten reencauzar a nuestro pa<92>s en la ruta del desarrollo y del progreso. Muchas gracias y que tenga un buen d<92>a.

Title: Interview with Comrade Ovidio Reyes, President of the Central Bank of Nicaragua, with Journalist Alberto Mora, Live Magazine, Channel 4, May 17, 2023
text: INTERVIEW WITH COMRADE OVIDIO REYESPRESIDENT OF THE CENTRAL BANK OF NICARAGUA WITH JOURNALIST ALBERTOMORA LIVE MAGAZINE, CHANNEL 4 MAY 17, 2023 22/05/2023 Journalist Alberto Mora We welcome Comrade Ovidio Reyes, President of the Central Bank of Nicaragua. Good morning, it's always a pleasure to have you with us, Ovid. Thank you for being here this morning on the Programme, and what better occasion to talk a little about the National Plan for Production, Consumption and Trade, which was presented yesterday to the National Assembly and which is part of the work carried out by the Production, Consumption and Trade System. Thank you very much again, and I would like you to tell us about the aspects, to begin with, the most relevant and most important aspects contained in this 2023-2024 Plan and the importance for Nicaraguans. Welcome. Words by Ovidio Reyes Good morning. Thank you very much, Alberto, for the opportunity to present this relevant information for all Nicaraguans. Yes, yesterday the Minister of Finance presented the Production, Consumption and Trade Plan to the National Assembly, a work that has already been carried out for several years by the different Instances and set of Institutions that work to ensure that food is produced in the country, that export products are produced, products for mining and forestry production. We have been working on this Plan, the way in which it is prepared has been evolving, and today it contains a set of Policies, Strategies, Projections and Goals on the main economic activities of the Primary Sector of our economy, which is the sector that is served. It should be noted that, as this Plan has been implemented for several years, a comparison was made of its results that in some way in the introduction of this Program summarized them, and that indicate that this instrument has served to increase yields in the Agricultural Sector and in the Livestock Sector, in the meat production sector, sugars, etc. And production volumes and exports will also increase. It is a fact that today we have a consolidated export base and it is growing every time, approaching quite important export figures in the case of agricultural products in the order of, we would already be expecting almost 3,000 million dollars, just agricultural products. Exports could really already be reaching... Journalist Alberto Mora Without introducing the Free Trade Zone regime, right? Is that what you mean? Words by Ovidio Reyes No; everyone, everyone, everything that is Agribusiness and Food. Journalist Alberto Mora Without including the Free Trade Zone; That's what I mean. Words by Ovidio Reyes That's right. And when you incorporate all exports, we are already in important numbers of around 4,000 million dollars; In other words, these are numbers that a few years ago we did not think we would reach so soon, and this generates a lot of dynamism in employment, in foreign trade, and has laid the foundations for this to continue. When we add the Free Trade Zone, exports reach a more important amount, more than 7,000 million dollars. So, as you will see, this is a sector that all the Institutions attend to and that is relevant. What do you mean about those 1,000 million, I was talking about 3,000 million... Words by Ovidio Reyes Exactly 2,965 million dollars are expected in exports of Agricultural Goods for the year 2023. That is the amount. And total exports, already with the Free Trade Zone and everything, reach a little more than 7,000 million. Journalist Alberto Mora Yes, but he spoke of 1,000 million more that added up to 4,000 million. Words by Ovidio Reyes Ah, for the exports of Primary Goods. Journalist Alberto Mora Please explain, that people don't know. Words of Ovidio Reyes Free Trade Zone is a Special Regime, that is separate, and then there are exports that are not in the Free Trade Zone, that is around 4,000 million, and of those 4,000 million that are not Free Trade Zone, 2,965 million dollars are exports of Agricultural Goods; that is, it is a relevant moment. Journalist Alberto Mora You have also mentioned the word Primary and I would like you to explain it because the economy is divided into Primary Sector, Secondary Sector, Tertiary Sector, so when you say Primary which is what we are responsible for, but so that people understand it... Words by Ovidio Reyes Primary is the first product that is created, as a country, for example, grain, beans; for example, the cane to produce sugar, is planted there, that is why it is he calls it Primary, a somewhat technical separation that is made from production. Journalist Alberto Mora Correct, it is our strength, let's say, in the Primary Sector is our strength. Words of Ovidio Reyes That's right. Cattle, for example, comes from there; Gold, from there, comes out, and then goes to Industry, and Industry is known as the Secondary Sector. Then it reaches Commerce, it is already the Tertiary Sector. Journalist Alberto Mora That it should not be Tertiary, Commerce moves a lot. But this is how it has been learned technically, I am clear; it is so that the viewer friends who do not have any idea, some do not have any idea of the Primary Sector and everything else. Words by Ovidio Reyes And these products of the Primary Sector are important for the country, because the exports of that Sector are the ones that dominate our economy. In other words, we are exporters of raw materials, we produce... Journalist Alberto Mora Other countries have Industry as their Primary Sector. Words by Ovidio Reyes Others have more processing components. What's more, when we place coffee, coffee is an input to produce other varieties and to provide services in commerce. Some called comparative advantages what one country has, what the other has. Words by Ovidio Reyes That's right. But we export coffee beans, that is, they roast it there. Journalist Alberto Mora Are we still there? Words by Ovidio Reyes If what we are is a producer of primary commodities. Gold is going rough. Journalist Alberto Mora But some are already doing a process. Words by Ovidio Reyes Sure, sure. But the main demand is grain; the same as sugar, we produce sugar but we do not produce candy, but we produce sugar, the primary product. The same goes for meat, meat goes as a primary product. It has been a very important job because this is not only about setting a goal, this is about working on productivity issues, health issues. The Plan incorporates the Policies that will be followed in terms of Agricultural Health, Animal Health, so that pigs, meat and products are healthy. Journalist Alberto Mora Yes, as required, safety and everything else, the requirements that are necessary. Words by Ovidio Reyes The issue of productivity to increase yields is very important. Journalist Alberto Mora What Ivan mentioned seems interesting to me. It's still not optimal, Ovid, but we can move forward, I'm clear. Words by Ovidio Reyes But we have made progress, it is clearly seen. For example, in rice production there is a great advance, it is one of the most advanced, but other products have also been increasing. Journalist Alberto Mora And the deficit has decreased, because much more has also been produced than in 2006. Words by Ovidio Reyes Nicaragua's agro-export surplus has increased; that is, we produce food and import food, and that is a surplus. In other words, that is one of the great actions of this Plan, Food Security, a Policy and in fact it is the first Policy, to guarantee Food Security. We can say, with firm information, that we have Food Security guaranteed because we are net exporters of food; there are other countries that are the opposite, they are net importers of food. Now, in this there are products that go and other products that come, so to speak. In this net export we still import food, but the important thing is that globally we are net exporters, and the idea is, little by little, to reach the totality. For example, livestock does not say, we produce more meat than what the country consumes, but in the case of rice we are 20% short, we have advanced by 80%, we were at much less than 80%. Today we are at 80%, the idea is to reach 100%, and if we can start exporting, all the better! And with this spectacular improvement in performance it is possible, it is possible to achieve it. So what the Plan does is that, how do we improve productivity to be able to first guarantee Food Security, and secondly export more, because exports have turned out to be a pillar of our economy, strong; that is, the Export Sector has been able to overcome all the difficulties and has not succumbed as other sectors have; rather, what has been done is dynamized and has allowed and facilitated producers to focus on national production and consumption, but also on international markets, and that incorporates dynamics, incorporates competitiveness into the country, even forces everyone to improve quality and technologies. That is the new dynamic that our country is having now. So, it is also incorporated into the Plan, the Training, the Field Schools, the assistance provided by the different Institutions; the technological activity that is developed from INTA with the production of new varieties of seeds, production of plants that improve yields, and thousands of trainings that are provided to Producers, not only through INTA but also through INATEC and even the Universities that participate in this great effort to provide capacities in the Field, which is the main producer of all these goods that we are talking about. So it is a comprehensive Plan and it even incorporates Trade, the trade policy that we are going to follow, the opening of the markets and also broad lines of how to seek financing, because leverage is required to be able to do all this, huge resources are moved and, well, as you can see it is a comprehensive, and that is why all the Institutions participate, even those of us who define Macroeconomic Policies such as the Central Bank and who compile all these statistics so that we can assess its progress. And in the concrete, let's say, that it has to do with the numbers of the Plan; For this year we would be expecting to increase several production items to more than they have already been doing. For example, in Coffee we are expecting 3 million 804,000 quintals of production, we have been steadily increasing coffee production over time, and for this year we have this goal. Coffee at the international level is at good prices, it had bad moments about 3, 4 years ago, it was almost at 95 dollars for coffee, (then) it reached 250 dollars, now it has stabilized at 170, 180 dollars, which is not bad, it continues to be a good price. But since the price is oscillating and it is now located at that level, then we believe that it can still be taken advantage of by exporters to increase their areas and compensate for the fact that the price fell after it reached 250 and to be able to have more volumes of exports. Then we have a goal of 179,000 quintals of Tobacco. It is interesting how the country has positioned itself as one of the countries with the best quality tobaccos and has achieved very important goals. I remember that years ago when we talked about these goals, we dreamed of 300 million dollars, reaching those goals, when 160, 180 million dollars were exported. Well, that was more than surpassed now, it reached 300, we are already at 400 million dollars, and the Plan incorporates the Policies so that this continues and materializes. In Peanuts, 4 million 900,000 quintals is the goal, and in Cocoa, 220,000 quintals, that in that agro-export component. They are the main agricultural products that are exported, there are many more, but we also focus on those that generate more profitability for the countryside. Then, in Basic Grains, for example, the goal is to reach 8 million 853,000 quintals for this Cycle. I'll give you a number, in 2021, I'm leaving even 2 years ago, 8 million 263,000 quintals, and today we would be producing 8 million 853,000 quintals, that is, it is a great advance. Journalist Alberto Mora That's where consumption goes and exports, right? Words of Ovidio Reyes That's where all the production goes and, well, in the field a lot of corn is planted, and we don't produce massively with these high-yield technologies because they also generate dependence on the grain, but the progress that has been observed is important. In Red Beans, 4 million 968,000 quintals, that is, we are already going to reach 5 million quintals of beans. It is interesting that beans have now become a commodity that is traded internationally, that is, we are already producing more beans than we consume domestically and now we export them. Journalist Alberto Mora What was the first one you mentioned? Coffee, then Tobacco, Peanuts, Cocoa, Corn, and let's go with the Beans, then the Rice; in the case of Irrigated Rice, 5 million 553,000 quintals, the goal is to reach 6.7 million in the future so that we achieve 100% consumption. I believe that the sector is going to achieve it, There is a lot of talk that free trade, by eliminating tariffs, loses the country's competitiveness, but the truth is that we have been inserted for several years in the Free Trade Agreements and rather production has increased, there are even some goods that have a Rate of 0 already tariff; the case, for example, of pig production has increased more, it was not closed, quite the opposite. Journalist Alberto Mora They had an expiration date and were decreasing. Words by Ovidio Reyes On the contrary, they have become more technified, they have improved the breed, the genetics, they have improved the methods of fattening and cleaning treatment of the animals, and now we have a Pig Sector that is growing. Then I will mention the amounts of meat production. We have in Irrigated Rice reaching 5 million 553,000 quintals, and then in White Sorghum, here we call it Wheat, we call it wheat but it is really Sorghum, Wheat is not produced in Nicaragua, it is produced in other latitudes. White Sorghum 694,000 quintals of production, and Gold Rice, because the one I mentioned first is Irrigated Rice, Gold Rice 6 million 350,000 quintals. That is in the issue of grains, if one sees the amounts and scales are really important; that is, we are grain producers in this country, grain is one of the most precious activities of consumption, Rice and Beans. Journalist Alberto Mora Many are in the hands of Small Producers, in the case of Corn, Beans. Words by Ovidio Reyes Of course, the Nicaraguan economy is characterized by 85% of small trade, it is enormous, the participation is great, it is large, great. Journalist Alberto Mora That is not to the detriment of the big ones, but the Little Ones are there making an extraordinary effort. Words by Ovidio Reyes  it is the sector that the Production System prioritizes, because 85% of these are guaranteed by them; that is why thousands of Trainings in Field Schools, thousands of Trainings in INATEC, and also Seminars, Workshops, Fairs. All of this is incorporated in this Plan, the Fairs that are going to be promoted in the different productive areas of the country, and also in the localities that promote productive activity. Then we go to another important sector, the musaceae, the case of bananas, we are thinking of reaching one billion units of bananas; in 2021 there were 940,000 and now we already have a relevant goal, one billion units. Bananas have become a very popular product. Journalist Alberto Mora  ok? Words by Ovidio Reyes Yes, it is beginning to be traded and it was discovered recently, I say recently, 4, 5 years ago as a product also for packaging, and consumption is quite demanded for all kinds of activity. Journalist Alberto Mora And in fact they return it to us in fact chimi, I don't know how much. Words by Ovidio Reyes Yes, of course, just as you have to give it. It is how we produce and we also buy products such as Corn Flour. Journalist Alberto Mora Well, one day we are going to take that leap, the production of the raw material. Words by Ovidio Reyes Sure, there is not the slightest doubt because that is a natural process of development, one begins little by little and then ends with a lot, that's right, but we are not little by little, Alberto. Journalist Alberto Mora No, I'm not negative. Words by Ovidio Reyes I mean that we should not minimize ourselves, we have a large production in Nicaragua. Let's remember that when the Coronavirus came, all the countries came here to look for food, all the countries looking for food because they knew that Nicaragua is an arm in agricultural production of grains, export products, now of Musaceae that are also being exported. Then, we have the field of vegetables, vegetables are very delicate to produce, it is a fairly perishable product but it requires a lot of care, and here in the plan elements are incorporated to also be able to increase production in this sector. In Cebolla, the goal is to reach 600,000 quintals of Cebolla. Journalist Alberto Mora Do we still matter a little there? Words by Ovidio Reyes But it is because of a problem of seasonality, there are times when onion cannot be produced here, so production has to stop and then at that time it is imported. Journalist Alberto Mora But it is becoming less and less. That's right, because production has been increasing, if here we had an irrigation system everywhere and good control so that excess rain does not kill your vegetables, we are able to produce all year round, but there we are making progress in this Plan to achieve that totality. In potatoes we have a goal of 1 million 440,000 quintals; in Carrot, 520,000 quintals; Chiltoma, 490,000 quintals; Tomatoes 1,720,000 quintals and cabbage, 1,618,000. As you can see, we have each of these activities tabulated so that the actions carried out by the Institutions support and accompany the Producers to achieve this goal. They are achievable goals, as we have the history also in production that are present there in the Plan, one can compare and see how the evolution is coming, and they are realistic, we are not putting things here that we cannot (achieve). Journalist Alberto Mora Well, I understood that one has to be prudent with the projections, and then we continue with the goals and what the Cabinet and the Production System expect. What other numbers can be highlighted, from what you have projected? Words of Ovidio Reyes I had already mentioned the agro-export products, the products of Basic Grains, the Musaceae, the Vegetables; we also have the other block, Roots and Tubers; there is a production goal of 7 million 240,000 quintals of cassava; 975,000 quintals of Malanga, and 652,000 quintals of Quequisque. These are the goals in the case of the products that come from these groups; then we have goals for the Livestock sector, in the case of the Livestock Sector, which is a fairly widespread sector at the national level, and which has had relevant increases in meat production, what we have is an expected slaughter of 720,000 head by 2023. Here, when you look at the statistics, in 2021, 910,781 head were slaughtered; that is, you can think we were in less. Ah, there was a reason, meat prices rose significantly and producers took advantage of that moment. Now it has stabilized, so we already have a more realistic number of production, 820,000 and it does not mean that we are bad, because when we see the cattle herd it continues to grow. Journalist Alberto Mora How much is it now? Words by Ovidio Reyes About 5 million 700,000, 800,000 (heads) is the cattle herd, and growing. So the extraction is what we see because we have the stock of cattle there and we bring a part, and then, with breeding and reproduction, it is replenished and then the stock continues to grow. We are expecting 820,000. In pig slaughter 309,000 heads; this is the sector that I tell you has been growing more and more; for example, in 2021, 282,000 head extracted; in 2022, 300,000 head extracted and in 2023 we are expecting 309,000 heads, and all already with free trade, and they are incorporating technologies and expanding farms with higher quality. In fact, we have to advertise it in the supermarkets and today you find the packages of the national pig farms and the imported product is also sold, but you don't have to get tangled, you have to buy the one from the national farms, because it is a product that has a more balanced food, even the meat is a little darker, even to make nacatamales it is a better meat in relation to the imported one that is totally white and has no color. Journalist Alberto Mora But are you referring to the larger, deeper-cutting pork industry? Words by Ovidio Reyes No, I mean all the farms, the farms are producing very good meat, and also the people who are dedicated. Journalist Alberto Mora There is a whole effort of small, small farms. I am referring to all farms, if it comes from a farm it is better to buy that farm pig; Of course, there are also people who produce not necessarily on the farm. Journalist Alberto Mora But there are problems with the presentation, with the cost of feeding, there are still problems to be solved. Words by Ovidio Reyes Well, but we are still advancing, and with the rest of the sectors, with that production we also supply the Municipal Slaughterhouses, with the production of pork in all the neighborhoods of our country. So, what we have to favor here is national production, that is the Message I want to give, plus our own consumption, ours, first because it is increasing, it has better quality and is incorporating more and more technology; That's important. Today, the demanders of these products want good cattle, in this case pigs, so that they grow faster, fatten up quickly and produce more meat. Journalist Alberto Mora Then, there is an insemination effort that INTA does, genetic improvement and the breeds are giving better yields, there is less fat. Words by Ovidio Reyes There is a lot of training. Then in the poultry slaughter we are expecting 69 million 971,000. In the trade figures you can clearly see the businesses, poultry producers are growing; this sector has also come fast, for example, in 2021 it produced 62 million 553,000; 2022, 67 million 280,000 and now we are expecting 69 million 971,000, (well) we should have rounded it up to the 70 million practically estimated for the goal of the cycle. Then, derived from livestock, milk, in the collection of milk, dairy 185 million gallons; 401 million gallons of raw milk production; there we have the film of the Livestock Sector. As I have been explaining to you, how is this Plan organized? Well, INTA in the field of Technology; IPSA, in this case working to guarantee health and for marketing and to extend export permits for these assets; MIFIC for trade issues for facilitation; the MAG to work on information gathering, policies, advocacy; the same MEFCCA; that is, we all get together and push the cart so that this is successful. Then, as you know, in meat production there is the Meat Industry, because internally meat or cattle are also the raw material for the Meat Industry, here we are projecting 343 million pounds of beef; 34 million pounds of pork and 353 million pounds of poultry meat.
