La inflacin fue el factor internacional que ms impacto tuvo durante este ao y nosotros igual, la inflacin podra finalizar entre un 10% y un 11% este ao, pero esperaramos que el prximo ao ya se ubique entre un 5% y 6%. Y el fundamento de esto es que ya los precios de los bienes internacionales pararon de crecer y el precio del petrleo mismo ms bien baj un poco despus del alza significativa que tuvo a inicios del ao. Entonces, como los precios ya han parado de crecer, los precios internacionales, creemos que eso se va a traducir tambin en una menor inflacin durante el 2023 y se ubicara entre un 5% y un 6%. Y el empleo, nosotros creemos que se va a mantener una tasa de empleo entre 3 y 3.5%, * tanto en este ao como en el prximo, y vemos un fortalecimiento del crecimiento del sector formal, de empleo, de la economa y una ligera reduccin en la informalidad, eso nos estn diciendo las estadsticas a cierre 2022 y esperamos que as contine durante el 2023. Y as finalizamos, le agradecemos una vez ms por atender esta invitacin y compartir estas proyecciones de lo que se espera para el ao entrante, y a ustedes familias, les agradecemos por el privilegio de su tiempo. Title: Interview with Ovidio Reyes, President of the Central Bank, with Journalist Erving Vega TN8 Studio, Channel 8 - May 2, 2023
text: Interview with Ovidio Reyes, President of the Central Bank, with Journalist Erving Vega, Estudio TN8, Channel 8 May 2, 2023 Journalist Erving Vega We are going to have as a Central Theme today, to talk about the economy "State of the Economy, financial stability and prospects", there is already a report presented by the Central Bank, today we are going to share these data, and we are going to expand them with the President of the Central Bank Ovidio Reyes, he is our guest today this morning in Estudio TN 8 and we welcome him, thank you Ovidio for joining us. Words by Ovidio Reyes Thank you very much, thank you very much Erving. Journalist Erving Vega When we talk about the state of the economy, we are talking about the behavior of the first quarter of 2023. That's right, right? Words of Ovidio Reyes This is how our economy in the first quarter of this year has managed to stabilize and consolidate economic growth and how what is glimpsed is a growth trend perspective that could place the economy around 4 percent and the rest of the variables growing at that trend. Journalist Erving Vega When you talk about it since it has stabilized, it no longer depends on a, we no longer have a behavior of up and down let's say, it has its peaks, it goes down, then it goes up, it is already something sustained, constant. Words by Ovidio Reyes Indeed, the economy came out of a negative economic cycle. After going through a downturn, the economy rebounded in 2021 with growth of more than 10 percent and then stabilized in 2022 with growth of 3.8 percent. In 2023 it is growing in perspective by 3...3.5 percent and that is because the world slowed down and that has placed us in a trend in 2023 of that nature, but towards 2024 onwards we believe that the economy is positioned at a 4 percent trend. Journalist Erving Vega We can locate a milestone here, that is, by 2023 the economy reflects a trend of sustained growth. Words by Ovidio Reyes That's right, stabilization was consolidated, it is consolidating and now it is only growing, that is what we are observing in the behavior of economic evolution. Journalist Erving Vega: It depends on some circumstances or isn't the projection so fragile? Words by Ovidio Reyes The projection is quite solid because it is based on the fact that all economic sectors have been growing, they have all reached a level of production that is emerging as a trend and in that sense there is no doubt that there will be economic growth again, a third consecutive year of economic growth will be repeated, but the most important thing is that it is consolidated and that is what we are observing. Journalist Erving Vega Let's expand on the subject. I think we start with the conclusions, true, but well the news is this, to share the good news, to share with our viewers, with Nicaraguans: It is consolidated from the behavior of 2021, 2022 and what was observed in the first quarter of 2023, the Nicaraguan economy is consolidated. Words by Ovidio Reyes Effectively Journalist Erving Vega A sustained growth trend. Words by Ovidio Reyes It is consolidating and that is positive for business, for companies, for entrepreneurs and it is also positive for employment that is also being consolidated, as we are going to explain. Journalist Erving Vega We are going to expand on the topic later, state of the economy, financial stability and prospects, also perspectives, how we expect to close this year 2023. Later with Ovidio Reyes, President of the Central Bank. Journalist Erving Vega By way of introduction, I think we will start with the conclusions: The Nicaraguan economy is consolidated based on what has been observed. 2021 growing above 10%, 10.3%, right? Words of Ovidio Reyes That's right. Journalist Erving Vega In 2022? Words by Ovidio Reyes 3.8% Journalist Erving Vega, and First Quarter of 2023? Words by Ovidio Reyes In the First Quarter, as measured by the Federal Economic Activity Index, we are growing 3.5%. So, that also shows that the economy has already consolidated. I mentioned that the economic sectors have been advancing, in fact, in the bfensual index of Chronic Activity that is what we observe, that all sectors are in recovery, in positive; fishing a little less, but it is a cyclical tana, it is a tana of closures and things, it is not a trend tana. And if it is the ccns- truccicn, it is already recovering. Construction had a negative cash last year and was the result of the prices of construction materials becoming very expensive, which led to the halt of several Projects or the postponement of several Projects. So, construction had its bad moment in 2022, but already in 2023 we are observing that new Housing Projects, new Construction Projects and also the promotion of Public Investment Programs are joining a recovery. Etero then we observe, for example, that Hotels and Restaurants grow by 27%, in fact, they were the ones that were in the doldrums for a long time, but now they are in a momentum. Mines and Quarries 13%, Transport and Communications 12%, the Trade Sector 6.5%, Other Services 3%, and the Manufacturing Industry 2.5%. In other words, if I continue with the rest of the sectors, they are all growing, that is the positive thing and what gives us indications that it has already been consolidated and that this trend will continue now in the future. Journalist Erving Vega When we talk about sustainability, what does it mean technically, that there is no risk of ups and downs, of ups and downs, that from then on the outlook is only one of growth? In the words of Ovidio Reyes, solidarity means that the shocks suffered by the economy in the past will disturb investment, investment, capital, but that disturbance is no longer seen in the figures, therefore the explosion has stabilized, investment has stabilized, capital has stabilized, as a result production is stabilized and it is growing. Trade and demand, supply and supply and supply also stabilized; So, since they are all in balance, the economy is only on a growth trend. Journalist Erving Vega And the factors that have an impact on this are faworsible, both internal and external? Words of Ovidio Reyes the external factors am when the Mido seems to be under a lot of stress and the industrial economies are going to have a slowdown by 2023, our particularity of being a small economy and very open to international trade has made it easier for us to continue with the growth of our exports and actively participate in trade. That has left us with a better growth outlook than the rest of the world, 1.3% growth is outlined in the world and around 3.3.5% in Central America and the Dominican Republic. We, in estimates, in technical calculations, align and coordinate technically with the Financial Organizations and now we agree on estimates. That's why our target range is between 2.5 and 3.5. We believe that 3.5% is the most feasible, but we also have a downward range because the world in terms of growth is not so good; in fact, some industrial nations are reflecting financial problems, which is why it is important to talk about financial stability now as well. There are some industrial companies that have had quidstras benches, which is not happening in our country, but we are also putting that range of 2.5% as a possibility; so, in that range, between 2.5 and 3.5%, believe us that our economy is going to grow with more tendency to the positive, towards the positive side of the estimate. Journalist Erving Vega: That's the factor, those are the external variables. Internally, how does the situation look like? Words by Ovidio Reyes  The external variable of exports has also not been so bad, because prices continue to be attractive. This is something that we pointed out earlier, that despite the fact that prices were falling internationally but continue to be much better than they were before, therefore our exports have an outlet. Internally, the policies that have been implemented have been very important, that is, all the work that has been carried out by the different State Institutions to support and facilitate production has had the expected result.  the Fiscal Policy has been really outstanding, there has been a balance and an important fiscal consolidation, the Public Sector last year had a fiscal surplus. While many countries had deficits and imbalances in their accounts and increased their public debt, Nicaragua was able to consolidate, reduce public debt as a percentage of GDP and end the year with a fiscal surplus. So far in the First Quarter the same is observed, collection growing by 14% and expenditures contained. This is one of the fundamental pillars of macroeconomic stability. The other is that on the side of the Central Bank there has been a consistent Monetary Policy so that financial stability and financial flows continue, and that has allowed us a significant accumulation of international reserves of more than 4,800 million dollars. In fact, in these days that we will be publishing the data, we are already getting closer to 4,900 million dollars. We thought that if these policies continue, we would end the year with around 5,000 million dollars in accumulation of international reserves. And the exchange rate stability also reflects all this behavior, since the exchange rate is very stable; In the First Quarter, in February we have reduced the exchange rate slippage to 1% and we believe that little by little we are going to take steps and advance towards the definitive stabilization of the cordoba. So, we have that combination of Policies, Monetary, Fiscal, Institutional, to promote production and this is the result we have had. Journalist Erving Vega: And in the ordinary economy, in the street economy, how is this reflected? Let's talk about the IMAE precisely. Words of Ovidio Reyes Well, we have always mentioned that the most important thing is to look at employment when we talk about the economy. Employment is stabilized, at a rate around 3.2%, one month 3.4, another month 3.1, but the employment rate is at 3.2%. Today, when we have Monthly Employment Statistics, it allows us to see and evaluate the evolution of this important variable, which is perhaps the most important for all Nicaraguans, and we observe that there is an increase in formal employment and a reduction in what is known as informal employment. For example, the growth of Social Security Insured Persons allowed the total number of Insured Persons to reach 800,000 Insured Persons. That's a huge recovery after dropping to just under 700,000 Policyholders. And on the other hand, we see that affiliation is also improving. And on the side of informality, this has dropped to 36%, the rate of suberpletion, after which it was more than 40%. So we are seeing a recovery in employment that is also a manifestation of the speed at which the economy is moving. Journalist Erving Vega Inversiones, how is it shaping up for this year? Is the China variable still not estimated in the considerations to make the evaluation and projection of the behavior of our economy, for example, with the Early Harvest Agreement and the negotiation of an FTA that will probably be ready in 2024? Words of Ovidio Reyes Investment has had a component of pressure due to the issue of increases in the prices of construction materials, so investment for construction has been a little depressed for that reason. But we are already observing new Housing Projects, we are observing new pushes in Investment Projects now that the economy has stabilized, and also the push of Infrastructure Projects. On the Foreign Direct Investment side, it was really outstanding last year; we expected 1,200 million dollars of Foreign Direct Investment, but it ended at 1,800 million dollars; that is, there was a greater enthusiasm to reinvest profits and to start new projects. All those things that were on hold are coming out of the pipeline, and then we would think that during 2023 the 2022 phenomenon would be repeated, since it was the start and now this is consolidated. That is to say, Foreign Direct Investment has that particularity, which once it stabilizes is maintained, because you have to scan plants, you have to reinvest to maintain the equipment, and in addition to that to bid new sales projects, products. So, on the investment side, we say that there is enthusiasm, especially in Foreign Direct Investment, and we would hope that in the new conditions the national investment will return to positive terrain. Then, on Trade Agreements, it is an undoubted success that a set of goods have been achieved to reach zero tariff with China, that is a great incentive for all exporters to participate in these markets. It is also a fact that an entry of Nicaragua into business with China will generate economic growth, but we do not have those parameters in the estimates yet, we would wait for the businesses to be well profiled, to see those trade routes that are going to be opened, to see products that are already being placed, so that we can then draw perspectives and be able to incorporate them into this estimate. In other words, a boost from the economy on that side is going to be positive and would generate better results than those we are expecting. Journalist Erving Vega You spoke of Nicaraguan exports, which are also favored by good prices in the international market; At the same time, however, is there a prospect of inflation being unbalanced for this year? Words by Ovidio Reyes External prices have fallen, costs rose a lot during 2022 and that was reflected in domestic inflation: transportation costs, costs of goods and services that were imported, including oil, which then fell. Already for 2023 what we are observing is that the prices of the goods we export are falling, the prices of the main industrial economies are falling, inflation has already begun to fall in the world and that will also have a consequence in our economy that we are importing inflation, that is why we expect inflation to fall, that it is in a range between 6 and 7% after last year ended at more than 11%; by March it has already dropped by 10% and in April we are sure that it will continue to fall, perhaps to 9%. So, what does that mean for the prices of our export products? Well, they have also gone down but not much and not as much as the other products have done, so it continues to be a positive factor for exporters who are taking advantage of it and it can be seen in the figures that exports are growing by 9%; In other words, we are also doing well on the export side. And on the side of domestic prices, inflation is already easing and we believe that we are going to end up in that range, between 6 and 7% inflation for this year. Journalist Erving Vega Which last year exceeded 10%. Words of Ovidio Reyes Eue more than 10%. the positive thing is that the economy was recovering and consolidating, and as the external flows for the Nation did not stop, all the flows continued, the export activity continued. There was no reduction in consumption, that was something striking; that is, consumption at the aggregate level grew between 6 and 7%, real consumption. With an increase in prices, one should expect consumption to fall, but it was not like that, rather consumption grew and to a large extent this is due to the fact that the Financial System stood out, that is, in 2022 the Financial System once again presented positive growth rates. It came a bit like the Financial Sistara saga, in terms of economic reactivation, but it has already been consolidated and is consolidating strongly. What we have observed is a growth in credit, which even in the first quarter grows by 20% in credit. So, when one observes this inflationary phenomenon but sees that there is credit and that there is enough for consumer credit, one can then explain why consumption does not depress but continues to grow, and that is good, because consumption is the flip side of production and, therefore, a greater demand for consumption. of consumer goods, is also a greater demand for producer goods. So, to have that result of inflation that was high, is stabilizing and that we believe is going to go down. In fact, from the Central Bank, the reduction of the carbiary slide that we generate to 1%, which in fact we have come from 5% and we already have it at 1%, contributes to lowering pressures on prices and with the existing carrbiary stability this component should not be feeding inflation at all. Journalist Erving Vega: The result of changing the exchange rate, which has been on the cordoba, has it been consolidated, has it depreciated? Words by Ovidio Beyes Cordoba has consolidated. 2 and a half years ago the Central Bank sold dollars to the Financial System, to Economic Agents in general. Why? Because there was still a lag of instability, so the Central Bank intervened by selling dollars, selling its foreign currency, but this would be the third year in which the Central Bank does not intervene at all in the exchange market. That is to say, we no longer inject dollars into the economy, it is quite the opposite, rather they demand cordobas from us and in exchange they offer us dollars; is cfecar, the Central Bank is acquiring many dollars as a result of the consolidation of the cordoba, and that goes hand in hand with the reduction of the slippage of the exchange rate, because the less a currency depreciates it is, the more stable it is. This reduction is due to slippage, but above all the policies behind it, of fiscal consolidation and monetary stability, have allowed the cordoba to consolidate and there is a greater demand for it. Last year, for example, we bought about 380 million dollars; that is, they sold us the equivalent of 380 million dollars to the Central Bank and we gave cordobas in exchange. Already this year we are going for more than 200 million dollars the sale of dollars that private agents make to the Central Bank, and we hope that this will continue. Journalist Erving Vega It is interesting to wonder how this is reflected, for example, in the preference of Nicaraguans to have their savings in cordobas or in dollars, but what one appreciates on the street is that if the Nicaraguan is owed, am I going to pay them to you in cordoba? Make them for me in conha! They are no longer so desperate to have dollars. Words of Ovidio Beyes Because the currency is more stable, the depreciation of the currency is much lower and we hope, soon, to be able to fully stabilize the currency, and that will be a great benefit for all Nicaraguans, and that they will demand more cordobas. Indeed, before with a devaluation of 5% it could be convenient to take from cordobas to dollars and then from dollars to cordobas and have a profit, but with 1% you can end up losing in the exchanges, of carrying and bringing. And once fully stabilized, it would really be for other reasons, not to obtain an exchange income, because it would not make sense. Journalist Erving Vega You mentioned that the economy is consolidated, I would like to ask you why I don't know if we have sinned of insisting on this, but when journalists, when Nicaraguans evaluate the behavior of the economy, how are we going, we always have as a starting point whether we have already overcome the factors that severely disrupted the economy, as was the case with the pandemic and as was the failed coup attempt. We are always comparing ourselves with before 2018, how we came in 2017. Is that already a story totally overcome? From here on it is a new milestone? Words by Ovidio Reyes Indeed, the economy has already been consolidated, the economy first stabilized and then consolidated and now it is in trend, that is, there are three moments. The economy was stabilized, during the crisis actions were taken to stabilize it; Then, last year the economy was consolidated, since we were coming from bad time to good moment, extreme, more than 10%, now we consolidate at 3%, and now we have ridden a trend. So, the economy is no longer responding to what happened, now it has made a cut, the Economic Agents are rather, today for the future, preparing for the good that is observed in the movements of the factors, what is observed in the movements of products and merchandise. In other words, we now have to adopt a position forward, and I think that is what can be seen in the economic results of this First Quarter, that the Economic Agents are already consolidated, have ridden a new trend and are moving forward. Journalist Erving Vega What are, by way of summary that you could mention, the pillars that sustain this already consolidated strength of an economy in a sustained growth trend? Words by Ovidio Reyes I believe that there is a very dynamic economic sector in our country, one sector What now is observing the World. Our country has left behind the history of only seeing itself, now our markets are integrated into the region and the rest of the world; that is, we are facing an attitude towards different things. All our goods are being demanded, they are demanding everything that Nicaragua produces; the country has become a net producer of food, strong, as that is already recognized, to be food producers; the issue of Food Security, which was attacked, a priority in the Government's policies, has had its impact in terms of food production and that has made the country today have a reputation in that regard. That is a fundamental factor, that we can produce all our food, and not only produce for ourselves, to be able to sell it to the rest of the Lindo, it is the asset that has been behind it. The other thing is the great contest of all the Small and Medium Producers. It is a fact that this economy, which for me is wrongly called informal, I have already said it several times in this Program, is simply an economy of entrepreneurs, of people who trade, of people who work, it represents a large percentage of National Production, it moves around 85% of economic activity and services in that sector. and that sector is responding and moving forward.  Policies, Policies are key to generating this result, because bad Policies lead to a bad economy, and good Policies lead to a good economy. That's right. This has also been recognized by the International Organizations, the good Policies, the evaluations made by the Monetary Fund indicate that there are good Policies here, and the evaluations of the rest of the Organizations as well.  as for the financial component, this country has outstanding financial stability, we went through all these crises and the Financial System is stable, it was able to overcome all the problems, the stresses it experienced, and it is consolidating and advancing; that is, we have a real economy and a stable financial economy, which are the result of the participation of all Nicaraguans and the policies that the Government has implemented. Journalist Erving Vega: Thank you very much for joining us. Just as a closing comment, I will recapitulate some data. So the perspective is to grow in a range of 2.5 to 3.5%. Words by Ovidio Reyes Effectively. We would expect economic growth between 2.5 and 3.5%, it is above the range of the world economy that grows only 1.3%, and it is in the range of the economy of Central America and the Dominican Republic, of the economies of this Region, and we are also aligned in the protections of the International Ethnd. That is in terms of economic growth. As for inflation, we expect lower inflation than last year, growing between 6 and 7%; and employment we would expect it to be between 3 and 3.5%, at this time a point estimate of 3.2%. Journalist Erving Vega Does the investment look good? Words by Ovidio Reyes Foreign investment could be similar to last year; remittances will continue to grow, last year 3,300 million, we think that this year with the trend it could be between 3,800, 4,000 million dollars; exports 3,800; 4,000 million for goods; and another 3,800; 4,000 million exports from the Free Trade Zone. Journalist Erving Vega Thank you very much for joining us, Ovidio Reyes, President of the Central Bank.

Palabras de Ovidio Reyes la ocnsolidacin significa que, los choques que sufri la eccncma en el pasado perturbaren la inversin, el eipleo, perturbaren el capi- tal, pero esa perturbacin ya no se ve en las cifras, por lo tanto se ha estabilizado el expleo, se ha estabilizado la inversin, se ha estabilizado el capital, como resultado se estabiliza la produccin y va en crecimiento. Tambin se estabiliz el Comercio y la demanda, la oferta y la dsnanda; entonces, al estar todos en equilibrio, la eccr- nenia ya solo va en tendencia de crecimiento. 7 Periodista Erving Vega Y los factores qje inddai en esto sen faworsbles, tanto internos como externos? Palabras de Ovidio Reyes los factores externos am cuando el Mido pareciera que est sometido a mucho estrs y van a tener una desaceleracin las economas industriales para el 2023, nuestra particularidad de ser una economa pequea y muy abierta al comercio internacional nos ha facilitado a que continuemos con el crecimiento de nuestras exportaciones y participando activamente en el comercio. Eso nos ha dejado con una perspectiva de crecimiento mejor que el resto del Mundo, 1.3% se perfila el crecimiento en el Mundo y alrededor de un 3, 3.5% en Centroamrica y Rep- blica Dominicana. Nosotros, en estimaciones, en clculos tcnicos nos alineamos y nos coordinamos tcnicamente con los Organismos Financie- ros y coincidimos ahora en estimacin. Por eso es que nues- tro rango meta es entre 2.5 y 3.5. El 3.5% creemos que es lo ms factible, pero tambin tenemos un rango hada abajo porque el Mundo en trminos de crecimiento no est tan bien; de he- cho, algunas Naciones industriales estn reflejando problemas financieros, por eso es importante hablar ahora tambin de estabilidad finandera. Hay algunas Nadcnes industriales que han tenido quidsras bancadas, cosa que no est ocurriendo en nuestro Pais, pero estamos po- niendo ese rango de 2.5% tambin como una posibilidad; en- tonces, en ese rango, entre 2.5 y 3.5% cranos que va a crecer nuestra Economa con ms tendencia a lo positivo, hacia el lado positivo de la estimadn. 8 Periodista Erving Vega Ese es el factor, esas sen las variables externas. A lo interno cmo se vislumbra la situacin? Palabras de Ovidio Reyes Y tambin la variable externa de exportaciones no ha estado tan mal, porque los precios continan siendo atractivos. Esto es al- go que sealamos anteriormente, que a pesar de que los pre- cios estaban cediendo a nivel internacional pero continan siendo mucho mejores que lo eran antes, por lo tanto nues- tras exportaciones tienen salida. A nivel interno, las Polticas que se han implementado han sido muy importantes, es decir, todo el trabajo que se viene realizando desde las distintas Instituciones del Estado para apoyar y facilitar la produccin ha tenido el resultado esperado. Y la Poltica Fiscal ha sido realmente destacada, ha habido un equilibrio y una ccnsolidacicn fiscal importante, el Sector P- blico el ao pasado tuvo un supervit fiscal. Mientras muchos Pases tenan dficit y desequili- brios en sus cuentas y aumentaban su deuda pblica, Nicara- gua pudo consolidarse, reducir la deuda pblica como porcen- taje del PIB y terminar el ao con un supervit fiscal. Lo que va del Primer Trimestre se observa lo mismo, la recaudacin creciendo un 14% y los egresos contenidos. Eso constituye uno de los pilares fundamentales de la estabilidad macroeconmica. El otro es, que por el lado del Banco Central ha habido una Poltica Monetaria consistente para que la estabilidad finan- ciera y los flujos financieros continen, y eso nos ha per- mitido a nosotros una importante acumulacin de re- servas internacionales de ms de 4,800 millones de dla- res. De hecho en estos das que estaremos publicando los da- 9 tos, ya nos estamos acercando ms a los 4,900 millones de d- lares. El ao, pensamos, que si estas Polticas continan, lo finalizaramos alrededor de los 5,000 millones de dlares en acumulacin de reservas internacionales. Y la estabilidad cambiara refleja tambin todo este com- portamiento, ya que el tipo de cambio est bien estable; no- sotros en el Primer Trimestre, en Febrero hemos reducido el deslizamiento cambiario al 1% y creemos que poco a poco vamos a ir dando pasos y avanzando hacia la estabilizacin defi- nitiva del crdoba. Entonces, tenemos esa ccnbinacin de Pol- ticas, Monetarias, Fiscales, Institucionales, para promover la produccin y este es el resultado que hemos tenido. Periodista Erving Vega Y en la economa de a pie, en la economa de la calle, co- mo se refleja esto? Hablemos del IMAE precisamente. Palabras de Ovidio Reyes Bueno, siempre hemos mencionado que lo ms importante es ver el empleo cuando hablamos de la economa. El empleo es- t estabilizado, en una tasa alrededor del 3.2%, un mes 3.4, otro mes 3.1, pero la tasa del empleo est en 3.2%. Hoy que contamos ya Estadsticas Mensuales de Empleo nos permite ver y evaluar la evolucin de esta importante va- riable, que es quizs la ms importante para todos los ni- caragenses, y observamos que hay un incremento del empleo formal y una reduccin de lo que se conoce como empleo in- formal. Por ejemplo, el crecimiento de los Asegurados del Seguro Social permiti que el total de Asegurados ya llegara a los 800,000 Asegurados. Esa es una importantsima recuperacin des- pus de haber bajado a un poco menos de 700,000 Asegurados. 10 Y por otro lado vemos que tambin la afiliacin va mejoran- do. Y por el lado de la informalidad esta ha bajado hasta un 36% la tasa de suberpleo despus qje estuvo a ms de un 40%. En- tonces estamos viendo una recuperacin del empleo que es una ma- nifestacin tambin de la velocidad a la que se va moviendo la economa. Periodista Erving Vega Inversiones, cmo se perfila para este ao? Todava en las consideraciones para hacer la evaluacin y proyeccin del comportamiento de nuestra economa no se estima la va- riable China, por ejemplo, con el Acuerdo de Cosecha Tem- prana y la negociacin de un TLC que probablemente estar listo en 2024? Palabras de Ovidio Reyes La inversin ha tenido un componente de presin por el tema de los aumentos en los precios de los materiales de construc- cin, entonces la inversin para la construccin ha estado un poco deprimida por esa razn. Pero ya estamos observando nuevos Proyectos de Viviendas, estamos observando nuevos empujes en los Proyectos de Inversin ahora que la economa se ha estabilizado, y vanos tambin el empuje de los Proyec- tos de Infraestructura. Por el lado de la Inversin Extranjera Directa fue realmente destacada el ao pasado; nosotros esperbamos 1,200 millo- nes de dlares de Inversin Extrajera Directa, pero fi- naliz en 1,800 millones de dlares; es decir, hubo un ma- yor entusiasmo por reinvertir utilidades y por empezar nuevos Proyectos. Estn saliendo de la tubera todas esas cosas que estaban en ocmps de espera, y entonces pensaramos nosotros que durante 2023 se repita el fenmeno 2022, puesto que fue el arranque y ahora esto se consolida. 11 Es decir, la Inversin Extranjera Directa tiene esa parti- cularidad, que una vez que se estabiliza se mantiene, porque hay que escandir plantas, hay que reinvertir para dar- les mantenimiento a los equipos, y adems de eso para en- pujar nuevos proyectos de ventas, de productos. Entonces, por el lado de la inversin nosotros vanos que hay entusiasmo es- pecialmente en la Inversin Extranjera Directa y esperaramos que en las nuevas condiciones la nacional vuelva a los terrenos positivos. Luego, sobre los Tratados Comerciales es un xito indudable de que se haya logrado que un conjunto de bienes alcancen arancel cero con China, ese es un gran aliciente para todos los exportadores y puedan participar en estos mercados. Tambin es un hecho que una entrada de Nicaragua en los negocios ocn China va a generar crecimiento econmico, pero esos parmetros no los tenemos puestos en las estimaciones an, esperaramos a que se puedan perfilar bien los negocios, ver esas rutas comer- ciales que se van a abrir, ver productos que ya se estn colo- cando, para entonces poder trazar perspectivas y poderlas incorpo- rar en esta estimacin. Es decir, un empuje de la economa por ese lado va a ser positivo y generara mejores resulta- dos que los que estamos esperando. Periodista Erving Vega Hablaste de las exportaciones nicaragenses favorecidas tambin por buenos precios en el mercado internacional; a su vez, sin embargo, hay rna perspectiva de qoe desdarla la infla- cin para este ao? Palabras de Ovidio Reyes Los precios externos han bajado, los costos subieron mucho durante 2022 y eso se reflej en la inflacin interna: costos 12 de transporte, costos de los bienes y de los servicios que se importaron, incluyendo el petrleo, que luego baj. Ya para el 2023 lo que estamos observando es que los precios de los bienes que irrportamos estn descendiendo, los precios de las principales economas industriales estn bajando, ya la inflacin comenz a bajar en el Mundo y eso va a tener una consecuencia tambin en nuestra economa que estamos impor- tando inflacin, por eso esperamos una inflacin hacia la ba- ja, que se ubique en un rango entre un 6 y un 7% despus que el ao pasado finaliz en ms de un 11%; ya a Marzo ha bajado un 10% y Abril estamos seguros que va a continuar ba- jando, talvez a un 9%. Luego, Qu significa eso para los precios de nuestros produc- tos de exportacin? Bueno, tambin han bajado pero no mucho y no tanto como lo han hecho los otros productos, por eso contina siendo un factor positivo para los exportadores que lo estn aprovechando y se observa en las cifras que las exportaciones estn creciendo un 9%; es decir, vamos bien tambin por el lado de las exportaciones. Y por el lado de los precios internos ya la inflacin est cediendo y creemos que vamos a finalizar en ese rango, de entre 6 y 7% la infla- cin para este ao. Periodista Erving Vega Que el ao pasado super el 10%. Palabras de Ovidio Reyes Ee ms de un 10%. lo positivo es que la eocnonia ccmo estaba en recuperacin y en consolidacin, y como los flujos externos para la Nacin no pararen, crxitinuarcn todos los flujos, la actividad exportadora continu. No hubo una reduccin del consumo, eso fue algo llamativo; es decir, el consumo a nivel agregado creci entre 6 y 7%, el consumo real. Con aumento de pre- 13 cios uno deberla esperar que el consumo baje, pero no fue asi, ms bien el consumo creci y en buena medida esto se debe u obedeci a que el Sistema Financiero despunt, es decir, en el 2022 el Sistema Financiero volvi a presentar tasas positivas de crecimiento. Vino un poco como a la saga el Sistara Financiero, en cuanto a reactivacin econmica, pero ya se consolid y se est con- solidando fuerte. Lo que hemos observado es un crecimiento del crdito, que incluso al Primer Trimestre crece en un 20% el crdito. Entonces, cuando uno observa este fenmeno in- flacionario pero ve que hay crdito y que hay bastante para crdito de consumo, uno puede explicar entonces por qu el consumo no se deprime sino que contina creciendo, y eso es bueno, porque el consumo es la contracara de la produccin y, por lo tanto, una mayor demanda de consumo, de bienes de consumo, es tambin una mayor demanda por bienes de produc- cin. Entonces, teneros ese resultado de una inflacin que fue alta, se est estabilizando y que creemos que va a bajar. De hecho, des- de el Banco Central la baja del deslizamiento carbiario que generamos al 1%, que de hecho venimos desde el 5% y ya lo teneros en 1%, contribuye a bajar las presiones sobre los precios y con la estabili- dad carrbiaria existente no deberla ese componente estar ali- mentando para nada la inflacin. Periodista Erving Vega El resultado de cambiar la tasa cambiarla cul ha sido sobre el crdoba, se ha consolidado, se ha depreciado? Palabras de Ovidio Beyes El crdoba se ha consolidado. Hace 2 aos y medio el Banco Central venda dlares al Sistara Financiero, a los Agentes Econmi- cos en general. Por qu? Porque haba an un rezago de 14 inestabilidad, entonces el Banco Central intervena ven- diendo dlares, vendiendo sus divisas, pero ya este seria el tercer ao en que el Banco Central no interviene para nada en el mercado cambiarlo. Es decir, nosotros ya no inyectamos dlares a la economa, es todo lo contrario, ms bien nos demandan crdobas y a cambio nos ofrecen dlares; es cfecr, el Banco Central est adqii rien- do muchos dlares cano resultado de la consolidacin del crdoba, y eso va de la mano de la reduccin del deslizamiento cambiarlo, porque una moneda entre menos se deprecia es ms estable. Esa reduccin es del deslizamiento, pero sobre todo las Po- lticas que estn detrs, de consolidacin fiscal y de es- tabilidad monetaria, han permitido que el crdoba se afiance y que exista una mayor demanda por el mismo. El ao pasado, por ejeiplo, nosotros compramos alrededor de unos 380 millones de dlares; es decir, nos llegaron a vender al Banco Central el equivalente a 380 millones de dlares y nosotros entregamos cr- dobas a cambio. Ya este ao vamos por ms de 200 millones de dlares la venta de dlares que nos hacen los agentes pri- vados al Banco Central, y esperamos que eso contine. Periodista Erving Vega Es interesante preguntarse cmo se refleja esto, por ejeiplo, en la preferencia del nicaragense de tener sus ahorros en crdobas o en dlares, pero lo que uno aprecia en la calle es que ya el nica si le deben, te los voy a pagar en crdoba? fgamelos en cnha! Y no estn tan desesperados por tener dlares. Palabras de Ovidio Beyes Porque que la moneda est ms estable, ya la depreciacin de la moneda es mucho menor y esperamos, pronto, poder esta- bilizar totalmente la moneda, y eso va a ser un gran benefi- 15 ci para todos los nicaragenses, y que demanden ms crdo- bas. Efectivamente, antes con una devaluacin del 5% poda ser conveniente llevar de crdobas a dlares y despus de dlares a crdobas y tener una ganancia, pero ya con 1% como que po- des terminar perdiendo en los cambios, de estar llevando y trayendo. Y ya totalmente estabilizada sera realmente para otras razones, no para obtener una renta cambiara, pues no tendra sen- tido. Periodista Ervng Vega Mencionaste que se consolida la economa, me gustara pre- guntarte porque no s s nosotros hemos pecado de insistir con esto, pero cuando los Periodistas, cuando el nicaragense evala el ccnportamiento de la economa, de ccmo vamos, siempre tenemos como punto de partida de s ya superamos los facto- res que trastocaron severamente la economa, como fue el caso de la pandemia y como fue el intento fallido de Golpe de Estado. Siempre estamos comparndonos con antes del 2018, cmo venamos en el 2017. Ya eso es una historia superada totalmente? A partir de aqu es un nuevo hito? Palabras de Ovidio Reyes Efectivamente, la economa ya se consolid, la economa primero se estabiliz y luego se consolid y ahora est en tendencia, o sea, son tres momentos. Se estabiliz la eco- noma, durante la crisis se adoptaron acciones para estabi- lizarla; luego, el ao pasado se consolid la economa, puesto que venamos de mal memento a buen momento, extremo, ms de un 10%, ahora consolidamos al 3%, y ahora nos hemos montado en una tendencia. Entonces, ya la economa no est respondiendo a lo que pa- s, ahora ha hecho un corte, los Agentes Econmicos ms 16 bien estn, hoy para el futuro, preparndose para lo bueno que se observa en los movimientos de los factores, lo que se observa en los movimientos de los productos y las mer- cancas. Es decir, teneros que ahora adoptar una posicin hacia adelante, y creo que eso es lo que se observa en los resultados econ- micos de este Primer Trimestre, de que los Agentes Econmicos ya estn consolidados, se han montado en una nueva tenden- cia y van hacia adelante. Periodista Erving Vega Cules son, a manera de resumen que podra mencionar, los pilares que sostienen esa fortaleza ya de una economa consolidada en una tendencia sostenida de crecimiento? Palabras de Ovidio Reyes Creo que hay un sector econmico muy dinmico en nuestro Pas, un sector que ahora est observando el Mundo. Nuestro Pas ha dejado un poco atrs la historia de solo verse a si mismo, ahora nuestros mercados estn integrados en la regin y al resto del Mundo; es de- cir, estamos frente a una actitud hacia las cosas diferen- tes. Todos nuestros bienes los estn demandando, estn demandando todo lo que produce Nicaragua; el Pas se ha convertido en un productor neto de alimentos, fuerte, ya est reconocido eso, sernos productores de alimentos; el tema de Seguridad Alimentaria, que fue atacado, una prioridad en las Polti- cas del Gobierno, han tenido su impacto en trminos de produc- cin de alimentos y eso ha hecho que el Pas hoy tenga una reputacin en ese sentido. 17 Ese es un factor fundamental, que podamos producir toda nues- tra alimentacin, y no solamente producir para nosotros, poderle vender al resto del Lindo, es m activo qje ha estado detrs. Lo otro es el gran concurso de todos los Pequeos y Medianos Pro- ductores. Es un hecho que esta economa, que para m inde- bidamente se le llama informal, ya lo he dicho varias veces en este Programa, sencillamente es una economa de emprendedo- res, de gente que comercia, de gente que trabaja, representa un gran porcentaje en la Produccin Nacional, se mueve alrededor del 85% de actividad econmica y de servicio en ese sector, y ese sector est respondiendo y va hacia adelante. Y las Polticas, las Polticas son claves para generar este re- sultado, porque malas Polticas cendjoen a una mala economa, y buenas Polticas conducen a una buena economa. Eso as es. Tambin eso lo han reconocido los Organismos Internaciona- les, las buenas Polticas, las evaluaciones que hizo el Fondo Monetario indican que aqu hay buenas Polticas, y las evaluaciones del resto de Organismos tambin. Y en cuanto al componente financiero, este Pas tiene una estabilidad financiera destacada, pasamos todas estas crisis y el Sistsna Financiero est estable, pudo superar todos los pro- blemas, los estreses que vivi, y se consolida y avanza; es de- cir, tenemos una economa real y una economa financiera esta- ble, que sen el resultado del concurso de todos los nicaragen- ses y de las Polticas que ha implementado el Gobierno. Periodista Erving Vega Muchsimas gracias por habernos acompaado. Solo a manera de comentario de cierre recapitular algunos datos. Entonces la perspectiva es de crecer en un rango del 2.5 al 3.5%. 18 Palabras de Ovidio Reyes Efectivamente. Esperaramos un crecimiento econmico entre 2.5 y 3.5%, est sobre el rango de la economa mundial que crece apenas a 1.3%, y est en el rango de la economa de Centroamrica y Repblica Dominicana, de las economas de esta Regin, y estamos tambin alineados en las protecciones del Etndo Nfcnetario Internacional. Eso en cuanto a crecimiento econmico. En cuanto a inflacin, pues esperamos una menor inflacin que el ao pasado, creciendo entre 6 y 7%; y el empleo espe- raramos que se ubique entre 3 y 3.5%, en este momento una esti- macin puntual de 3.2%. Periodista Erving Vega La inversin pinta bien? Palabras de Ovidio Reyes La inversin extranjera podra ser similar a la del ao pa- sado; las remesas van a continuar creciendo, el ao pasado 3,300 millones, pensamos que este ao con la tendencia podra estar entre 3,800, 4,000 millones de dlares; las exportaciones 3,800; 4,000 mi- llones las de bienes; y otros 3,800; 4,000 millones las ex- portaciones de Zona Franca. Title: Report on the Results of the Meeting of the National System of Production, Consumption and Trade, President of the BCN, Ovidio Reyes R.
text: TRANSCRIPTION TRANSCRIPTION Issuing confidence and stability Issuing confidence and stability Press Conference Report on the Results of the National System of Production, Consumption and Trade Meeting President of the BCN, Ovidio Reyes R. October 06, 2023 President of the BCN: Good morning. We are going to present the result of the meeting that we hold every week with the National System of Production, Consumption and Trade to evaluate the progress of production, alerts, perspectives. Well, in general terms, we must say that we observed a good advance in production in the areas that we have analyzed this week, such as the production of beans, the production of chicken meat. And, we also made an evaluation of the prices of imported inputs and the progress of the reforestation of the "Green That I Love You Green" campaign. In general terms, we observe good behavior. In fact, as a result of what we have been analyzing during the first half of the year and so far in the second quarter, the Central Bank will present a report on the 2023 macroeconomic outlook today and we have proceeded to make an upward estimate of our outlook for the year. After we had expected growth between 2.5% and 3.5%, well, now we are expecting growth between 3% and 4% of the Gross Domestic Product, inflation we are expecting to end between 6% and 7%, and employment we would be expecting the unemployment rate to be between 3% and 3.5%. This, in light of the good results we have seen in agricultural production, in the service sector and in the recovery that is being observed in hotel and restaurant production. The economy is dynamic. We must point out and declare that the economy is already growing again. This growth is seen in all sectors, even as the world is showing signs of weakness as a result of the TRANSCRIPTION TRANSCRIPTION Issuing confidence and stability Issuing confidence and stability On the other hand, we saw that in the Production, Consumption and Trade System, we also evaluated it there, and well, I also mentioned that we had seen the progress of the bean harvest and poultry production. In the case of beans, a total of 80,523 apples were achieved in this first harvest, producing beans throughout the country. This was reported by the Ministry of Agriculture, and a total of 1,177,821 quintals of red beans were reached, which is the most consumed. Distributed 27% in Jinotega in production, 26% in Nueva Segovia, 22% in Matagalpa, 12% in Esteli and in the rest of the departments in 13%. What we also observed is that there was a yield of 14.5 quintals per apple and an increase in total production compared to last year's first harvest of 7%. In other words, we have a good harvest result, despite the fact that this year was not a rainy year because El Nino is already present. We would say that it was a moderate winter. It was not like last year, but, nevertheless, the results are positive, a 7% increase in the harvest of our beans, which has also become a good in demand internationally. In other words, there is a high demand and a good price for beans that other Central American countries and outside Central America demand. However, we have this good result. On the side of chicken and egg production, the accompaniment of farms and small producers continued. The industrial sector has its own dynamics, but a lot of emphasis has been placed on attention to enterprises and in this sense, 1,606 poultry enterprises were attended to boost chicken production. In total, these enterprises reached 97,552 pounds in 62 Creole hen production units. It has been working and with a production capacity of 1,650 boxes of eggs and 18,600 pounds of meat. Technical courses have also been held to support 359 entrepreneurs, 257 marketing spaces for these products in which 773 have participated TRANSCRIPTION TRANSCRIPTION Issuing confidence and stability Issuing confidence and stability As far as national production is concerned, it is noteworthy how the evolution of chicken meat production has been giving strong results in terms of production. For example, in 2022 the national consumption of chicken was 357.54 million pounds and in 2021 it was 339.91 million pounds. That is, there is a substantial growth of 5.32% in consumption and there are production volumes that guarantee it, in the same way. There is a strong expansion in the national consumption of this product and the policies that are being developed are for this effort to continue. So far in January-June 2023, progress has been made in a production of 133.9 million pounds of poultry meat. In other words, we also observe that the poultry sector is in a good moment of production. On the other hand, the Strategy for the Promotion, Production and Monitoring of Animal Feed was also evaluated. The IPSA colleagues presented different trainings to small producers for the production of their own animal feed that result in a cost reduction of up to 40% compared to the sale or purchase of food already produced, imported or by companies. In this case, we invite all interested parties to attend these trainings carried out by INTA to learn techniques on how to produce (their) own animal feed, which will substantially reduce costs. In this sense, the IPSA carried out 132 trainings for producers and technical personnel and also carried out, for example, in the case of the pork sector, training was attended to 1,881 protagonists on issues of food ration preparation. In the poultry sector, 4,411 protagonists, also in the production of concentrates for laying hens, broilers and backyard hens. In the cattle sector, 5,667 protagonists were trained in the production of concentrates, silage production and the production of nutritional blocks. In the sheep and goat sector, 2,132 protagonists on the handling and production of concentrates. Likewise, 62 fairs were held to promote them, in which 900 protagonists were additionally trained. In other words, the effort is also made not only TRANSCRIPTION TRANSCRIPTION Issuing confidence and stability Issuing confidence and stability On the other hand, the progress of the National Commission for the Transformation and Development of Coffee Farming was presented. Coffee at this time, however, is observing a lower price compared to the prices obtained the previous year. The reference price is US145, although we remember that the price of Nicaraguan coffee has an average premium of US20 of the international reference price, but it is a lower price than the high prices observed in previous years. This has been influenced by low international demand due to the global slowdown. However, it is a price that still allows the activity to continue. CONATRADEC has promoted specialized workshops on preparation and roasting methods, a total of 16 workshops to train producers. The advantage is that this increases the producer's ability to earn more income. Meetings have also been held with protagonists of the value chain on roasting, grinding and roasting curves in 5 roasteries, 8 cooperatives, 3 mills, 5 enterprises, fundamentally, and likewise, this type of training in all the departments of Nicaragua where coffee is produced. Also recently, CONATRADEC participated in the Japan International Fair SCAJ, which has already been held for several editions, in which Nicaraguan coffee has been promoted, mainly. We saw the theme of the campaign "Verde Que Te Quiero Verde", which consists of national reforestation. 13 million new plants have been planted, excuse the redundancy. There are 2,000 active nurseries to carry out this activity. The goal is to reach 24 million plants. To date, we have a little more than 50%. Institutions and municipalities, as well as organizations, are working to continue in this campaign that is progressing at a good pace. Finally, during the meeting we looked at imports and costs of agricultural inputs. There is good news and that is that many of the prices of imported goods have begun to fall. For example, in the case of herbicides, which in June had been observing a certain price, they have been falling since September. The case of urea has also been showing price reductions, and yellow corn. So, we have formed a working commission to evaluate TRANSCRIPTION TRANSCRIPTION Issuing confidence and stability Issuing confidence and stability This downward trend in international prices has also allowed inflation to go at a more moderate pace so far this year. In other words, we have been observing reductions in a few months and even very moderate growth in inflation. So far in September, the monitoring we have also carried out of prices is that prices are very stable. We would not expect to see positive inflation at the end of September, on the contrary, we believe that it will be close to 0%. This is excellent news. However, we are not going to be careless and we are going to continue evaluating how these prices or this improvement in international prices in inputs are transferred to domestic prices and in the end to consumer prices. That is what we saw in today's meeting. In summary, we are seeing a good evolution of all production items. Those of us we analyzed, we have a good bean harvest, we have a very good poultry production, CONATRADEC training programs are advancing, and training in animal feed production is advancing, as well as national reforestation. This is the positive thing about our results. And well, we invite you to look on the Central Bank's website in a few moments, the Economic Outlook for the year 2023, which as we have mentioned, we have revised upwards. Thanks a lot.

Title: Interview with the President of BCN Ovidio Reyes 15 Minutos Program, Channel 13
text: TRANSCRIPTION TRANSCRIPTION Interview with the President of BCN Ovidio Reyes15 Minutos Program, Channel 13 January 08, 2023 Journalist Roberto Zuniga 2023, together we move forward! in this blessed and always free homeland, because here there is a homeland, there is peace! Welcome, I am Roberto Zuniga, thank you for joining us. This is the 189th 15-minute broadcast, the first of this newly inaugurated year 2023. Today we talk about the economy, how the year closed economically speaking and what the prospects are for 2023. We spoke with the president of the Central Bank of Nicaragua, Ovidio Reyes, he is here with us. Welcome Ovid. President of the BCN: Thank you very much for inviting me again to your program. Journalist Roberto Zuniga Thank you. Happy new year! President of the BCN: Happy New Year, also of course. Journalist Roberto Zuniga Facebook Tuuitter Facebook Tuuitter Tube Tube TRANSCRIPTION TRANSCRIPTION President of the BCN: President of the BCN: *Explanatory note: The year is 2022. *Explanatory note: The year is 2022. And we also think that it was a good year for our country because export activity continued, there was also a rebound in foreign investment and the hotel and tourism sector and the service sector that was greatly affected in 2020 with the pandemic has also been recovering. So we saw a positive year with an external sector that was favorable in price for our exports and that the agricultural and primary sector of our economy knew how to take advantage of very well. INSS employment grew to almost 790,000 insured and we see a trend towards recovery, as well as formal employment. And we ended the year with a good year in terms of trade and transport activity. So, in a big nutshell, 2022 was a second year of economic growth and one that strengthened the trend towards a recovery in the medium term. TRANSCRIPTION TRANSCRIPTION Journalist Roberto Zuniga Journalist Roberto Zuniga President of the BCN President of the BCN Journalist Roberto Zuniga Journalist Roberto Zuniga President of the BCN President of the BCN Journalist Roberto Zuniga Journalist Roberto Zuniga They ended at 4,400 million dollars, a record number in our economic history, which shows the financial strength of our country and the ability to accumulate savings. In general, in growth processes there is a lot of spending, but our case has been unique because in the midst of the global savings that have been shown in the midst of the fiscal consolidation that the Government has been presenting and the improvement in the savings and deposits of the public, the Central Bank also shows that and economic growth is guaranteed. Deposits. Is it a subject with a high grade? It is highly rated. In fact, deposits have been growing steadily at rates of more than double digits, it has been the main source of funding for the financial system. It is a healthy source because it is with its own resources and has allowed and increased the capacity of the financial system to deliver and grant credits. In fact, credit, which had been timidly showing rates until the middle of the year, accelerated in the second part of the year and we are now in a credit dynamic that corroborates the fact that economic activity has been consolidating and strongly. Now, how was the year in foreign investment during 2022? President of the BCN TRANSCRIPTION TRANSCRIPTION Journalist Roberto Zuniga Journalist Roberto Zuniga President of the BCN President of the BCN Journalist Roberto Zuniga Journalist Roberto Zuniga There are those who say that this country is a country of remittances. Well, all of Central America, from Mexico, through Guatemala, El Salvador, Honduras, Nicaragua and even the Dominican Republic, we are recipients of remittances for a very obvious reason, right? We are very close to the north and so many people are looking for work and decide to emigrate and that makes our countries prone to that large flow of remittances. And indeed, during 2022 there was a significant increase in the flow of remittances, to the point that in the last month we have recorded - which is the month of October - remittances reached almost 320 million dollars. We believe that we could end the year with a little more than 3 billion dollars and if that trend continues next year we would be, without a problem, reaching much higher figures. Next year, by the way, what are the economic prospects for the country in 2023? TRANSCRIPTION TRANSCRIPTION President of the BCN President of the BCN Journalist Roberto Zuniga Journalist Roberto Zuniga Our economy is a very open economy, we export a little more than 7 billion dollars, but we import 10 billion dollars. And if we consider that the GDP is 14 billion dollars, you can see the size of the opening of the economy, only in trade there are more than 17 billion dollars, that is, trade goes beyond GDP. So, what happens in the world affects Nicaragua. World prices are reflected in our economy and economic activity as well. The world recovered and Nicaragua took advantage of the global recovery and took advantage of it. Central America too. Next year, international organizations indicate that there could be a global slowdown and put the world's GDP growing around 1%. Well, our estimate (for Nicaragua) is a minimum of 3% and a maximum of 4%. In other words, we see a slowdown in global growth that could affect our country, but we don't think that much, because a small country like ours takes a lot of advantage of trade and we believe that this will continue even when international prices have fallen, but the drop still leaves us in a higher price position than that observed before the pandemic. So we are fine and the export process will continue. How much will our Gross Domestic Product vary during the year? President of the BCN TRANSCRIPTION TRANSCRIPTION Journalist Roberto Zuniga Journalist Roberto Zuniga And in terms of inflation? And in terms of inflation? President of the BCN President of the BCN Journalist Roberto Zuniga Journalist Roberto Zuniga President of the BCN President of the BCN We believe inflation will end between 5% and 6% by next year. International prices of food goods have already begun to decrease worldwide, the price of oil has stabilized and is even at a much better price than it was last year, which was very high. And so these are indicators that show that the spiral that was observed during 2021 and 2022 has been contained, and that therefore 2023 is going to have more moderate inflation. He spoke to us a little about the issue of credits, both national and international bank financing. During 2022 you told us that there was an increase, especially in the last stage of the year. What does 2023 have in store for us in this regard? Continue, because credit is the main source of income for financial institutions. It had been stopped due to a risk issue, but since these risks have been reduced or mitigated, then, now the banks are active with the delivery of credit and it is what generates the most profitability. And well, like any business, the bank also seeks income, so this is a good time to make rents. So, we have no doubt that credit activity will continue to expand as it did this year, it could perfectly reach double-digit rates for next year, credit growth. Journalist Roberto Zuniga Journalist Roberto Zuniga Does this mean? More than 10% Does this mean? More than 10% President of the BCN President of the BCN Growth in credit. Growth in credit. Journalist Roberto Zuniga Journalist Roberto Zuniga President of the BCN President of the BCN Journalist Roberto Zuniga Journalist Roberto Zuniga President of the BCN President of the BCN TRANSCRIPTION TRANSCRIPTION Credit is positive because it finances productive activity, input activity, business operations activity, but it also finances consumption, the purchase of housing, the purchase of vehicles, the purchase of motorcycles and purchases in supermarkets also with credit cards. The issue of employment, such a sensitive issue. How do we close 2022? What does 2023 have in store for us? 2022 closed with an average unemployment rate of 3%, it is a very low rate in the sense that what we measure is whether people are active or working or not working. That is to say, for us a job is one that either employs you as an employee or is activated personally because you want to be employed and are engaged in various activities, not necessarily company activities or that have an owner or employer. So the one who is employed - which could perhaps be a broader definition - still represents 97%, that is, 3% is the one who is unemployed TRANSCRIPTION TRANSCRIPTION Journalist Roberto Zuniga Journalist Roberto Zuniga President of the BCN President of the BCN Journalist Roberto Zuniga Journalist Roberto Zuniga Our exports? Our exports? President of the BCN President of the BCN Journalist Roberto Zuniga Journalist Roberto Zuniga One One One beauty of the of the Was there a lot of tourist movement in the country during 2022 and how much? There was an improvement because in 2021, there was very little income from tourism, but already in 2022 we would expect it to end up at about 500 million dollars and by 2023 we believe that due to the tourism promotion that is being implemented and the greater flow of airlines, it will improve even more. Exports would end, those of goods at about 3,800 million dollars, the same as those of the Free Trade Zone, that would leave us a little more than 7 billion dollars of export revenues. Now, how do we translate all this, positive numbers that you have told us about during this conversation, to the citizen, to the family. What does it translate into, how can the economy of the family interpret it? TRANSCRIPTION TRANSCRIPTION President of the BCN President of the BCN Journalist Roberto Zuniga Journalist Roberto Zuniga Well, let's remember that during the pandemic consumption slowed down a lot, people stopped shopping, the acquisition of goods, especially assets, was postponed and when we get out of that phenomenon and people all start working, then that increases consumption capacity, imports increase. In fact, imports in our country grew a lot last year, the acquisition of vehicles increases, the acquisition of motorcycles increases, the acquisition of televisions, cell phones increases. And what we observe is that our economy, all this has expanded at significant rates of up to 17% and 18% in real terms and in nominal terms it is greater. Well, there is a price effect, but even isolating the price effect, because prices in the world have grown, quantities have increased. So, employment is what activates, more consumption, more dynamics. In fact, in our recent festive activities, you can feel the dynamism that commerce had, the Christmas activity, the end-of-year activity, in fact, they pushed commerce a lot and that is because there is employment. If there were no employment, all that would not occur, the same in the sales activities of entrepreneurs, because there was also a reactivation. In other words, GDP and the growth of all the other indicators is precisely to generate employment and for employment to generate more well-being. What does 2023 have in store for the country in general? TRANSCRIPTION TRANSCRIPTION President of the BCN President of the BCN Journalist Roberto Zuniga Journalist Roberto Zuniga So, monetary policy and fiscal policy, economic policy in general is aimed at guaranteeing the financial and monetary conditions for this to happen. Thanks to Ovidio Reyes, President of the Central Bank, here today in 15 minutes, in the First Division.

Title: President of the BCN presents progress of the National Plan for Production, Consumption and Trade
text: TRANSCRIPTION TRANSCRIPTION Issuing confidence and stability Issuing confidence and stability Press Conference Report on the Results of the National System of Production, Consumption and Trade Meeting President of the BCN, Ovidio Reyes R. July 07, 2023 President of the BCN: Good morning. As every Friday, we are going to summarize the topics discussed at the meeting of the National System of Production, Consumption and Trade, which the set of public sector institutions that serve this important sector for the national economy carried out to evaluate the goals and progress of the National Plan for Production, Consumption and Trade. In this case, we discussed five topics: The first was the Promotion and Monitoring Strategy for Chicken and Egg Production, which is important for Nicaraguan families. We also discussed the Production and Marketing Strategy of Honey, which is another important product in the family basket. Also, we saw the progress of the Strategy for the Safety and Health of All Crops and Animal Production, this is carried out by the Institute of Agricultural Protection and Health (IPSA), and in addition to that, all the events: fairs, visits and contests that are carried out by the Ministry of Family Economy. We also saw the monitoring of the Weather and the alerts in terms of prices. So, looking at the points: In the case of the Strategy for the Promotion and Monitoring of Egg and Chicken Production, well, the progress we observed between January and May 2023 is that 139.5 million pounds of chicken meat have been produced, this compared to the previous year represents an increase of 2.1 percent. On the other hand, 14.2 million boxes of eggs have been produced, this represents 4 percent compared to January-May of the previous year, that is, we see a good evolution based on the goal in chicken production and egg production. This is done by providing technical support to more than 246,000 poultry-producing families in TRANSCRIPTION TRANSCRIPTION Issuing confidence and stability Issuing confidence and stability On the other hand, work has been done with five cooperatives made up of 94 members to strengthen them through specialized support in production, value addition and transformation. The annual production capacity is 240,000 pounds of meat in the case of these cooperatives and 204,000 boxes of eggs. In the national market, 1,742 commercial spaces have been created, this constitutes production promotion fairs, an average participation of 3,480 entrepreneurs and 30.9 million cordobas of sales revenue, with respect to the poultry area, mainly. On the other hand, in the case of honey production served in this case by the IPSA, 30 technified and installed apiaries have been served, with 30 registered producers, around 325 hives in Leon, Boaco, Jinotega and Matagalpa. A total of 642 tons of honey have been exported to Germany, Belgium, Costa Rica, the Netherlands, Spain and the United States. National production continues to advance and the IPSA also advances in training honey producers; 7,954 beekeepers trained in identifying flora of interest, food processing, and beekeeping. That is in terms of honey production, which is also advancing at a good pace. On the other hand, as I mentioned, we dealt with the issues of the Safety and Health Strategy in all animal and general crops. In training, 393 talks have been given to 4,054 protagonists in agricultural practices, seed production, pest and disease control; also 961 technical talks to 12,041 protagonists on prevention and control of diseases in poultry, pigs, cattle, bees and good use of medicines; 42 talks to 475 protagonists on food safety, beef, pork and poultry meat; TRANSCRIPTION TRANSCRIPTION Issuing confidence and stability Issuing confidence and stability The IPSA has also carried out 405 biosecurity inspections, 20,403 visits to farms nationwide and 446 inspections in veterinary pharmacies. On the other hand, vaccination days have been carried out, 333 vaccination days, which involved attention to 125,824 birds from behind the yard in 3,061 protagonists, 39 days of vampire capture in 37 protagonist points and 10,675 inspections of agricultural processing establishments of dairy, meat, fruit, beekeeping honey. In traceability registration, which is an important activity, 6,768 farms registered in 6,768 protagonists, 973 visits to these establishments, 698,296 cattle identified in traceability in 36,682 producers and have been carried out  160 visits to these establishments and 194 identification and registration days for 1,483 producers. In total, the phytosanitary inspections carried out by the IPSA amount to 39,541 inspections. The MEFCCA (Ministry of Family, Community, Cooperative and Associative Economy) also informed us about the promotion of commercial and recreational spaces for the enjoyment of families. In this case, last year a total of 262 million cordobas of sales were made in these spaces in various spaces in promotion especially of small, medium and micro enterprises. In 2023, as of June, 6,870 events have been held with the participation of  000 protagonists and sales have been made for 166.8 million cordobas. The goal is to reach 300 million cordobas in sales, that is, to go from 262 million sales at these fairs to 300 million cordobas in the current year. To this end, the MEFCCA has been carrying out a set of additional marketing and recreation actions such as the municipal production carnival of the opening of the agricultural cycle that was held in 70 municipalities, 370 producers participated, such as the carnival of the Flowers: "Nicaragua in permanent flowering" in May in Catarina, Masaya with 137 entrepreneurs participating; the first fine cocoa festival in Matagalpa, in which 400 producers participated; sport fishing tournament in 24 events where 600 producers have participated; the national beekeeping festival in Sauce Leon with 100 entrepreneurs; and agricultural fairs, 476 events where 4,000 producers participated and so far this year what we mentioned in total sales. TRANSCRIPTION TRANSCRIPTION Issuing confidence and stability Issuing confidence and stability Finally, the behavior of the climate. INETER reported that on its website it has made an update on the rainfall regime and how the moisture is in the soils, which we invite everyone to visit, as well as the perspectives on the rains and the monitoring that is being done to the phenomenon of "El Nino", as well as the tropical waves that are about to enter our country that will continue to irrigate the national territory. That is what we discussed at the System meeting. We see that production continues to advance to what we expect. In the case of chicken meat and eggs we see good progress and in the case of fairs there is also commercial promotion. Thanks a lot

Title: Report on the Results of the Meeting of the National System of Production, Consumption and Trade President of the BCN, Ovidio Reyes R.
text: TRANSCRIPTION TRANSCRIPTION Issuing confidence and stability Issuing confidence and stability Press Conference Report on the Results of the National System of Production, Consumption and Trade Meeting President of the BCN, Ovidio Reyes R. May 12, 2023 President of the BCN: Good morning. This morning I am going to present a summary of what was addressed in the ordinary meeting of the National System of Production, Consumption and Trade that has just been held in a hybrid form. In this meeting, which is held every Friday, we evaluated the progress of the National Plan for Production, Consumption and Trade and also how all the sectors of production of goods served by the production system are advancing. The issues that we addressed in this meeting had to do with national exports and agricultural goods, imports. Also how progress is going. How from the education centers and the countryside the training plans in the technical field schools are advancing, or from the technical field schools to bring more knowledge to our working population, and we also addressed the issues of the National Strategy for the Promotion, Production and Monitoring of Vegetables, Vegetables and Tree Crops. On the subject of the evolution of exports and imports, we observe that during the January-April period of 2023 the export impulse in our country continues. Preliminary information indicates that in 2023 a total of 2,578.1 million dollars was exported, which means an increase of 3.5 percent in exports. And, imports reached a figure of 3,329.7 million dollars. Here there is a reduction in the total amount of imports of 8.5 percent. In principle, this is a global economic result. There are generally good prices for our products, but lower than those observed in previous years. And on the other hand, the prices of imported goods TRANSCRIPTION TRANSCRIPTION Issuing confidence and stability Issuing confidence and stability In any case, in general, trade continues to be dynamic and we hope that it will continue to do so for the rest of the year. When we look at the main export items of those 2,578 million dollars exported, both by the general regime and by the free zone regime, which are the ones that stand out the most? Clothing and accessories; the figure is 543 million dollars exported; raw gold, 348 million dollars; automotive harnesses, 292 million dollars; gold coffee, 290 million dollars; beef, 216 million dollars; cane sugar, 143 million dollars; cigars and cigarillos, 136 million dollars; cheeses, 78 million dollars; red beans, 56 million dollars; peanuts, 46 million dollars; farmed shrimp, 42 million dollars; and crude oil, 26 million dollars, among the products that are leading exports. Then many come. As you can see, if we take aside what the free zone regime is, the rest of the export products are basically those that are served by the National System of Production, Consumption and Trade, hence the importance of these meetings to see and design policies that encourage exports and the production of these goods. Then, when we look at agricultural goods, of that total, more than 2,500 million dollars exported, the agricultural sector exported 1,162 million dollars. And let's see in agricultural exports, now, what are the main export groups and components: coffee and yerva de mate, 291 million dollars; meat and offal, 225 million dollars; sugars, 155 million dollars; tobacco and substitutes, 146 million dollars; dairy, eggs and honey, 95 million dollars; vegetables and legumes, 64 million dollars; oilseeds, 52 million dollars; beverages, 30 million dollars; edible fruits, 30 million dollars; fats and oils, 29 million dollars; preparation of various foods, 9 million dollars, and then the rest of the products. This is the group of products that are already leading exports in the case of agricultural goods and that have become a fundamental pillar of economic activity and job creation in our country, they already were, but over time this has been consolidated and continued. TRANSCRIPTION TRANSCRIPTION Issuing confidence and stability Issuing confidence and stability The other topic that we saw within the meeting was the training provided by the INATEC (National Technological Institute) and the training centers coordinated with universities and municipalities. It is important to note that training and technical education in the countryside has played a key role in improving productivity and even improving the incomes of people who are engaged in professional activity and work in the countryside, and the advances are also important here. To date, what we observe is that there are 12,019 protagonists already enrolled and training within the field schools, the goal is to reach 23,593, this is an advance of 51 percent of the goal. This is month by month, in March there were 5,486, in April 7,312 and we are already in May at 12,019 protagonists trained to reach the goal.
