Title: President of the BCN speaks on "Economy 2023 and Prospects 2024" on Channel 13.
text: TRANSCRIPTION TRANSCRIPTION Issuing confidence and stability Issuing confidence and stability Interview with the President of BCN Ovidio Reyes15 Minutes Program, Channel 13Topic: Economy 2023 and Outlook 2024 November 12, 2023 Journalist Roberto Zuniga This is 15 Minutos in its 228th broadcast. I am Roberto Zuniga and thank you for joining us. Today we talk about the economy, the national economy, with the President of the Central Bank of Nicaragua. Ovidio Reyes is here with us. Welcome Ovid, thank you. President of the BCN: Thank you very much for inviting me to your program. Journalist Roberto Zuniga Well, we are about to conclude 2023, what do the numbers say? President of the BCN: The economy throughout 2023 has been showing an economic recovery, but, above all, it has now been in a position of economic expansion that is more important. In other words, we are coming from economic cycles that affected production and employment and the economy has already stabilized. In 2023 it ended up consolidating and now what awaits us is a moment of economic expansion. So, now we are in an expansive cycle, as if we are taking advantage of the moments for economic activity to rebound and grow. So, we had a scenario in 2023 that is ending better than expected, we have a moment of economic expansion, financial strength, credit recovery and also the reactivation of private investment that is generating this additional boost that is being observed in the economy. TRANSCRIPTION TRANSCRIPTION Issuing confidence and stability Issuing confidence and stability If we look back and look at what we set out to do at the beginning of the year, did it come true? President of the BCN: Not only is it being fulfilled, but it will be above expectations. For example, when we made our first economic estimate for 2023, we thought that, due to the international environment, which has not been so favorable and that they have rather reduced the demand for many exported goods, mainly from the free zone, well, we believed that the economy was also going to have a certain effect on a somewhat moderate growth rate. And so we proposed a growth, or estimate a growth, of between 2.5% and 3.5%. Well, just a little more than a month ago, we already reviewed, in the light of the first numbers, that we could end up better than that rate. And then we revise our estimate to a rate of between 3 and 4%. But at this point, what we have been observing in terms of economic activity, there is a third quarter in which the Monthly Index of Economic Activity during the month of August and September is reflecting a growth of 6% in those two months. And we also think that October had the same fate. In other words, that is what we mean when we are in economic expansion. With this better result, even the Central Bank revises the estimate again and we already believe that we are in a position to indicate that the economy is going to be between 3.5 and 4.5%, that is, we would improve our estimate by half a percent more. Answering your question, then, we are finishing much better than we were proposing at the beginning of the year. Journalist Roberto Zuniga The external sector. How was your behavior during the year? President of the BCN The external sector struggled because demand for many goods declined, especially those produced in the free zone. The sector Tube . . TRANSCRIPTION TRANSCRIPTION Issuing confidence and stability Issuing confidence and stability For example, the hotel and restaurant sector grew at 20%, a highly dynamic rate; the trade sector, 13%; in the cumulative we have, for example, that mines and quarries grow at 7%; agriculture growing at 2.2%; the manufacturing industry sector, 2.3%; construction, 5.9%, excellent dynamics; energy and water, 9.5%; commerce, 6.3%; transportation, 5% and financial intermediation, 5.9%. As you can see, these are really important rates. And then the sum of all this allowed more than compensated. And it is reflecting an economy that is growing 4.3% in the aggregate. So, we are in an excellent position even referring to what we had proposed. In terms of exportable products, then, even though we had a drop in the free zone, we did have a good result in the rest of domestic goods, especially in food production. Our country has positioned itself as a country that produces food and what we have as a result, true, is that total exports of goods reached 3,563 million (dollars) in the first half of the year. In other words, we are aiming for a little more than 7 billion dollars in exports. We estimate about 7,500 million dollars, because exports towards the end of the year begin to be made, especially of coffee and other export goods, sugar, etc. On the other hand, we see that in the external sector that the tourism revenue sector has been growing at rates of 10% and that we would end this year about 640 million dollars, approximately, in tourism revenues. Last year it was 598 million dollars, that is, there is an increase in tourism revenues. On the other hand, remittances, which are also monitored by our institution, in the first half of the year accumulated 2,200 million dollars. That means that by the end of the year we are going to get some TRANSCRIPTION TRANSCRIPTION Issuing confidence and stability Issuing confidence and stability Journalist Roberto Zuniga And this is good, is it bad? That is, you talk to me about so many millions, this compared to previous years, is it higher, is it less? President of the BCN It is higher than last year, it is greater. As I mentioned, in the case of tourism, for example, we went from 598 to 640 million, which is an increase, and in the case of remittances, last year we ended with about 3,900 million and we are going to end up at 4,500 million. Even exports are going to end up growing by around 5% in nominal terms. And another relevant variable for the economy that also reflects confidence and reflects commitments to entrepreneurship and investments is foreign direct investment, and this reflected a substantial increase to 1,447 million dollars in the first half of the year. Last year, foreign investment was 1,800 million dollars throughout the year, but in this first half of the year alone, 1,400 million dollars. Without a problem we are going to exceed, I think, the figure of 2,000 million dollars. Journalist Roberto Zuniga How do you interpret this particular fact? How should the country interpret it? President of the BCN It is a result of greater economic dynamism, because investment, or foreign companies that have investments in Nicaragua, are observing a business environment, they are observing an economy that is dynamic, and since it is dynamic, well, the existing (investment) reinvests in profits, expands plants, buys inputs, buys machinery and equipment and the result is this. This information is provided to us, through surveys, by companies based in Nicaragua that kindly provide the information to the Central Bank. TRANSCRIPTION TRANSCRIPTION Issuing confidence and stability Issuing confidence and stability And in some way also confidence for the country. In other words, I am not going to invest in a country that I do not trust. President of the BCN Of course. When the economy gets depressed and when confidence disappears, people stop doing business. If he does not see future profitability, he does not invest. So, it is a good indicator of business to see that people are investing in plants, in equipment, in machinery and in fixed investment as well, in both. And another important element that, in addition to all this, as I mentioned, construction 20% and private investment the same, which had been quite a lot, let's call it that, in decrease, because the rate was negative until last year and that was due to the fact that construction materials, prices, grew a lot internationally and that was reflected here that growth. There was an impasse due to this stagnation of prices, but the projects have already settled and have already been reactivated. Journalist Roberto Zuniga How does this translate into these good numbers, these positive results in the family economy, in the small economy? President of the BCN Well, in the statistics that we also collect from surveys and in the work carried out by the National Institute of Development Information, INIDE, they measure the unemployment rate, they measure employment in general and what is observed there is that the unemployment rate is low and stable, around 3% - 3.3% and sometimes 3.5%. It is an excellent indicator for any country. In other words, it is reflected in the fact that there are employment dynamics and it is also reflected in the fact that what is known here as the informal sector, the participation rate in the informal sector has also been decreasing. That is to say, we have the virtue that greater growth generates more employment and that is reflected in the income of families as well, and that is palpable because you see it in commerce, TRANSCRIPTION TRANSCRIPTION Issuing confidence and stability Issuing confidence and stability Journalist Roberto Zuniga We are now entering the final stage of the year, November-December. There is a lot of economic movement in the country. What can we Nicaraguans expect economically speaking of these two [months]? President of the BCN These last two months are going to be positive. We believe that this growth dynamic will continue. In fact, these are months of a lot of commercial activity, because people are dedicated to consumption, recreational activities, Christmas activities, family activities, there are even many marriages in these months, which is nice. And what does commerce tell us? That if commerce has been growing at 6.3%, it will also be two months of the end of the year around a 6% growth in commercial activity, which in human terms means that the holidays will continue, that there will be for shouting, that there will be for Christmas gifts and that there will be to celebrate it [with] this dynamic and this positive behavior, And that is what I believe that all Nicaraguans want for our citizens. Journalist Roberto Zuniga And speaking of this, of what one expects or what is expected, what does 2024 have in store for us? President of the BCN We believe that this growth rate will be repeated in 2024. In other words, if we are already at a rate of between 3.5 and 4.5, the least we expect is that it will be repeated. That is, if you take an average, 4% growth, well, next year we would also expect a similar rate. Inflation, if we see it downwards, for example, we are going to publish tomorrow the result of inflation and what is shown is a year-on-year rate of 6% inflation, remember that in December it was 11%. Already TRANSCRIPTION TRANSCRIPTION Issuing confidence and stability Issuing confidence and stability Journalist Roberto Zuniga Thank you, Ovid. President of the BCN Of course. Journalist Roberto Zuniga President of the Central Bank with us here today in 15 minutes. Thank you also, of course, for the attention you have given. Let's continue as a family.

Title: Interview with the President of the Central Bank of Nicaragua in Estudio TN8
text: INTERVIEW WITH THE PRESIDENT OF THE CENTRAL BANK OF NICARAGUA IN TN8 STUDY 13/07/2022 Journalist Erving Vega Thank you for joining us, it is always a pleasure to be with you through your TN8 Studio Program, broadcast for this Tuesday, July 12. We are exactly 7 or 8 days away from one more Anniversary of the Sandinista Popular Revolution, next Tuesday, July 19, 43/19. How are we as we arrive at the 43rd Anniversary of the Sandinista Popular Revolution in terms of Security, Social Peace, Stability, Economic Growth? Today we are going to specifically address the economic part, what is the behavior, what the economic indicators reflect in this First Half of 2022, and based on that compartment, what is the outlook for the end of that year 2022 and for the coming years. Our guest, Ovidio Reyes, President of the Central Bank. Good morning. Welcome, Ovidio, thank you for joining us. I start from something that I heard you mention and highlight at the Coexistence Business Forum, talking about perspectives. We are already coming and we are already in a position of economic recovery, we have returned to the path of growth in a range of 4 or 5%. That's right? In other words, have we already overcome the shock of the pandemic, the 2018 political destabilization, hurricanes Eta and Iota? Words by Ovidio Reyes That's right. And we ensure this because the level of production has already exceeded all these events, on average, and in the aggregate, the economy is already placing more value on all products; perhaps some goods are still lacking, but on average the country has advanced. On the other hand, we also observe that the unemployment rate has already been located in the places that have historically been located, in a stable condition, around 4%, that is the rate, let's call it that, natural or stationary of our Economy. And on the other hand, we observe a significant recovery in Social Security employment indicators; exports, thriving, and the Financial System with deposits and credit growing at significant rates, the case of deposits at rates around 20% and the case of credit already growing at more than 10%. So, when one adds up all these things, we say that we have already recovered that negative space that we had and now we are already in the field of looking for that path of natural growth for our Economy, which, we believe, this year can be between 4 and 5%. Journalist Erving Vega 43/19, 43rd Anniversary of the Sandinista Popular Revolution, in that context Nicaragua in Stability, Social Peace and Growth. By way of introduction, you shared at the beginning, Ovidio, the data, how we are, with a behavior of the Economy in this First Semester already underpinning what had been projected at the beginning: A growth between 4 and 5%. Words of Ovidio Reyes That's right. In the First Half of the Year we believe that the Economy is already growing at 5 or 5.5%... in the First Half of the Year! We have not yet published the activity information for the Second Quarter, but with the preliminary information we are obtaining on agricultural production outputs, exports, everything makes us think that we are going down that route. Journalist Erving Vega That is, closing a First Semester above 5%? Words by Ovidio Reyes That's right, above 5%. For example, we are seeing the continuity of the dynamics of exports, and preliminary information on exports indicates that both the Agricultural Sector and the Livestock Sector are growing by more than 5%; for example, the Agricultural Sector, in volume, grew 4.1%, and the Livestock Sector by 7.9%. These are leading Sectors, they are ahead of the Economy, and behind them come another set of Sectors that support it. Journalist Erving Vega In volume; To this should we add the price? Words of Ovidio Reyes In the price effect, total exports are growing 18.6%, because prices this year have been significantly higher than those of the previous year. This has supported and motivated the greater delivery of products from Nicaragua to International Markets. And on the other hand, the indicators we have for Trade continue to be very dynamic, with a growth of more than 10%; in addition, that in the Financial System a trend towards the recovery of credit has begun to be observed, and strongly. Until the month of May he had already been growing by 10%, which he was timid last year. Journalist Erving Vega The credit. The deposits had already shown a good signal for a long time. Words by Ovidio Reyes That's right. Deposits were already recovering, and credit did so firmly from this semester onwards. So, with credit reactivating and exports growing, we can already see a good response in this First Quarter. Journalist Erving Vega: At what level has credit been recovered? Words of Ovidio Reyes 10% after last year ended timid, it hardly grew, and the year before last it was negative. So it is also observed that the dynamics of financial activity responded to this whole set of stimuli that have occurred in the economy, and we would expect, then, that this pattern that was observed in this First Half will be reproduced during the Second Semester. Sure, there are base effects... Last year the recovery was great and, therefore, we are now facing a higher level of activity to compare in the second half of the year, but we believe that the economy will remain in that positive territory. Journalist Erving Vega Between 4 and 5% is the estimate to close 2022? Words of Ovidio Reyes That's right. Then, as I told you, employment in the end is the objective, that is, how all this activity leads to a recovery of employment, and there we have also been observing positive signs of employment recovery in the Insured, but also of employment recovery in the different areas. Now, the Coronavirus has had a change in the structure of the Labor Market that has not made it as agile as economic activity, but the important thing is that employment continues to be added in the Economy; we would like it to be faster, but it goes forward, which is the most relevant thing. Journalist Erving Vega: Have the jobs lost due to the coup violence of 2018 been recovered? Words by Ovidio Reyes It is still missing, the level is still missing, and then the Coronavirus came to imprint an even slower dynamic on employment, for reasons that people changed work habits, work habits; today a lot of employment is offered via shipments of products to homes, many people stayed working from home; that is, there is a change in the structure, but as I mentioned, formal employment has been growing and the unemployment rate has already reached standard levels. So, all this indicates that we are on the path of replicating the economic activity that we have been observing. We don't see why it has to be relegated, that's another discussion. Because in the world dark clouds have arisen with these problems that have been occurring in the different regions; for example, the confinement in China made the markets nervous, the situation in Eastern Europe, the same, and that even caused many goods or the prices of raw materials in the International Markets, which had been growing at accelerated rates, to be contained in recent months. And so we observe, for example, that oil that reached more than 120 is now in a range between 100 and 108, that the price of gold that reached more than 2,000 is now around 1,800. And when one reviews the set of goods that are traded in these markets, they have all stabilized. That also leads us to believe that, even though expectations were created in the world that there could be a recession, and there is a lot of talk about this in international reports, nevertheless we believe that due to the nature of our economy, which is small and can place these products without major interruption, we can continue to take advantage of it. This First Semester is an example of this. Many countries slowed down their production by a lot, but Nicaragua, and I must tell you, Central America has also maintained these important growth rates. When one reviews the statistics of Central America, the Dominican Republic, one sees that our economies are maintaining a good rate of growth, and that is going to continue. Journalist Erving Vega Multilateral organizations such as the IMF and the World Bank are already projecting, however, a significant impact on the World Economy, as a result of all these events. Words of Ovidio Reyes That's right, indeed. But it is not a collapse either; if they were already seeing a growth of 3.8 before, now it is 3.4, that is, it is not something that is going to affect, that is why I tell you, because of the structure of our economy, our exports or our dynamics. Journalist Erving Vega What makes it possible, for example, that in that world growth projections are revised and are a little downward, what makes it possible for Nicaragua, however, to maintain a path and a projection of 4 or 5%? Words of Ovidio Reyes First, I would say that there is an economic structure that has maintained dynamism in all these years, regardless of the disturbances that are observed; that is, we have an Agricultural, Livestock and Export Sector that maintains its rhythm despite events. For example, the Free Trade Zone today is much more dynamic than in previous years, during the Coronavirus it had an impasse but now it is growing. So when you have an economy that has entered into dynamics, it is very difficult to stop it, and these sectors have been showing that factor; and on the other hand, behind it there are clear policies that have driven all these actions, the policies of support for production and technological transformation. There are also the Policies of incorporating more Protagonists in all Production activities and that facilitate Food Security and in addition to that exports. On the other hand, there have been facilities that have been undertaken by Public Institutions in terms of training, in terms of Productive Promotion, Tourism, etc. So, this set of elements together with the Global Policy of Financial Stability, Fiscal Stability in Public Finances and Monetary and Exchange Stability all add up, and that creates an environment for production. Our country also enjoys a good reputation in terms of Global Macroeconomic Stability, and that has been a remarkable fact during all these years, it is not new. That element creates the conditions for production to continue, for production to continue. It is noteworthy, for example, and we have said it on several occasions, the rebound in Foreign Direct Investment; after having gone through difficult years, foreign investment has already reached 1,200 million dollars and we do not see anything to indicate that it will be lower, only in this First Quarter we have already exceeded 500 million dollars of foreign investment; so for the rest of the year it looks good, and if we add to these elements the reactivation that is already being observed in the Tourism Sector, then that will give it greater dynamism. Finally, you also have the Remittance Sector that has continued its dynamics; this is a phenomenon that has been common to all countries that are large recipients of remittances, Central America, Mexico. These have had a boost during the last two years, and Nicaragua is no exception. All these elements become drivers, policies, conditions, facilities, and also the arrival of sector flows do not combine, and that guarantees that the economy responds positively. Journalist Erving Vega How decisive has been the measure or policy of freezing, subsidizing the price of fuels so that the increase in the price at the pump to the population, the impact of international oil prices, does not have an impact? I mention it and ask it, in the context of the news that one can read and see in other countries; here nearby in the Region, Panama with riots, with protests, with problems; Ecuador, in Europe, at least 6, 7 countries with strong complaints from the population in the streets, due to the increase in fuel prices and the high price of food. How decisive has it been for Nicaragua to decide to inject money, subsidize and keep the price of fuel frozen? Words of Ovidio Reyes I think that an important component when a lot of volatility arises and a lot of uncertainty arises and the leading prices of certain products such as oil reach unobservable levels. I think something that can create those expectations and that can maintain stability is relevant. On the other hand, being able to count on the resources, as Nicaragua has remained with healthy public finances, then there were resources that could face it. In this sense, the Government made a decision to support stability in hydrocarbon prices and to subsidize. That is key, because fuel has a transversal impact on the entire economy; therefore, by resorting to the Subsidy it is also being an element of national stability to prevent prices from having greater impacts on the population. It is a positive measure seen from the Economic and Social point of view, to maintain the social stability of the country; Of course, all this also depends on the moments and the amounts. So far the government has been able to cope and if now the price of oil has dropped to 108 dollars and if it manages to stabilize at 100 dollars, then it is something that I believe in general will add an element of important stability and even expectations, because that also allows spending and consumption to continue. Of course, if the price of oil has been allowed to be reflected in the prices of national fuel, that would also have slowed down consumption and investment. So it also has a positive component in national demand, preventing national demand from falling; In that sense, I think it has been an important measure. Now, what other things besides fuel can be done? Well, from the point of view of Public Policies, the most sensitive products can be supported, so that imports are facilitated, for example, at affordable prices in terms of fertilizers and agricultural inputs. These things have been done and have had a positive result, perhaps if they had not been done we would have a more difficult scenario. Journalist Erving Vega: How are we in the projection of the behavior of inflation, taking into account that the world has indeed experienced an increase in prices? Words of Ovidio Reyes All the countries in Central America and the Dominican Republic have experienced in this First Semester an increase in prices that was not caused by internal policies, it was not caused by increases in spending or monetary expansion. Last week we met with Central Bank Presidents, and we came to the conclusion that this is a phenomenon that is affecting all of us, and that it is very difficult to adopt national actions to contain them. Central Banks have begun to raise our interest rates little by little, in order to compensate for the increases in interest rates at the international level. If the world starts raising interest rates to contain inflation, lower spending and contain inflation, Nicaragua cannot do anything differently because we would have capital flight if we did not. That is why we have gradually and gradually raised interest rates, and we have been able to do this because we were at a very low rate. An interest rate hike doesn't feel that difficult, but there will come a point when it won't be able to take it anymore if these hikes continue. That is perhaps the main problem, How far the interest rate is going to rise without affecting economic activity to combat inflation. That is the global issue. Journalist Erving Vega: Is the increase in interest rates intended to contain inflation? Words of Ovidio Reyes Inflation, because when the interest rate rises throughout the world, spending is contained, consumption is down, investment is down, global demand is down. Journalist Erving Vega: But does it have a negative effect on credit or not? Words of Ovidio Reyes Of course. I want to tell you that first what is affected is demand, that is, when demand drops, prices are expected to also fall. We are not doing it for that reason, we are doing it because they are raising the interest rate and we cannot stay below, because if the interest rate is higher abroad, than the national rate, capital flows abroad and we do not want to lose it. So we raised the rate as well. Is that the measure that is going to solve the inflation problems? The truth is that in the world with the Coronavirus, problems arose that are hindering supply chains that are causing these types of problems in employment, as I mentioned. We do believe that the industrial nations are going to do the greatest job to contain international inflation, and that is going to lower the pressure on us. And how is inflation in particular in our countries? Until this First Semester it is higher than last year. When we compare June versus June of last year in Nicaragua, it is at 10.3%, that is, it is a high rate, but the important thing is that we are already seeing that comparing May and June it has already stabilized, because in the world it has also stabilized. As I mentioned, the price of oil, the price of corn, the price of cattle, and gold stabilized at high levels. All the goods that are exported in the last two months have been left without major movement. So, we would expect towards the Second Semester, that due to this and since what they are expecting, which is a recession, is not observed, or has not materialized, but that dynamism is observed in world trade. We would expect inflation towards the second half of the year to fall to 7%, between 7 and 8%. In other words, a rate quite similar to that of last year, that is what we expect in terms of inflation, and we believe that with the policies that are being implemented, but above all with the economic response, that will not have a major consequence on our economy. Journalist Erving Vega When one observes price increases, and we review how that is reflected in exports, we celebrate it, but when we import and consume what we import a little more expensive, we regret it. How is the balance between the good of the high price in the reflection of our exports, but the bad of the high prices in the products we import? Words by Ovidio Reyes So far we see that the balance is in favor of the prices of what we export, because the dynamics have been very strong; We are talking about growth of more than 20% in exports over two years. In the cumulative we are talking about a 40, 50% growth, of course some costs have also increased, but imported goods are part of the cost, it is not all the costs. No one can say that because the price of an input grew by 40%, 50% and its costs increased by 40, 50%. That is not the case, because there are national components that have not grown as much as imported goods. So, in the end, when one looks at the entire cost structure, in the end the price effect of what we sell abroad continues to be greater than what it is costing. In fact, the measure of economic activity is that, it is how much we sell versus how much it cost us to produce it, and it is positive, because it is clearly noticeable that growth is 5.8%; In other words, there is added value in the net that we are producing. Journalist Erving Vega We are going through a 2022 with good economic numbers and with a positive projection for the closing, between 4 and 5, as confirmed by the behavior in this First Semester. For the coming years, what could we expect in terms of economic performance, taking into account external and internal factors? Words of Ovidio Reyes Well, I have always said that it is very difficult to predict 1 year, and 3, 4 years is more difficult, what one does are scenarios. Journalist Erving Vega: I try to incorporate here that expectation that all Nicaraguans have now that we see the signing of an Early Harvest Agreement, and we hope in the coming years an FTA with China, and everyone aspires to have access to that giant market. Words by Ovidio Reyes When we make the Future scenarios, what we take into account is, first, the national capacity, that is, what we have in employment, what we have in investment, what we have in capital and what we have in infrastructure to sell abroad. Doing a purely internal exercise, we believe that we can maintain 4% growth without problems, going forward; In fact, our simulations indicate that we can grow by 4%. If we add to this environment that there are other considerations such as the Free Trade Agreement with China, such as new Trade Agreements, such as a global recovery and a way out of geopolitical conflicts, we are talking about the medium and long term. Journalist Erving Vega: But what will have to happen? Words by Ovidio Reyes In any case, it has to happen, and a stabilization of the economy in terms of the problems that arose with the pandemic. So we could expect higher growth and we could expect the economy to return to the 5% rate, and if it can overcome that trend, all the better. But in our scenarios we are seeing 4% that we incorporate into the information and we send it to the Ministry of Finance and Public Credit, so that it can be incorporated into its estimates of the medium and long term budget. And an inflation that we this year could end up between 7 and 8%, but that in the future could go down to 5% and then stabilize around between 3 and 4%. That is the medium-term expectation that we have. Journalist Erving Vega: Would one expect an interesting productive dynamic, based on the opportunities opened up by an FTA with China? I'm talking about the demand for products, one would expect that if someone has a pork processing plant, they would expand the operation, or if someone has the initiative to do a small project, they would think a little bigger. Words of Ovidio Reyes That's right. I think that there the expectation comes in two ways, first because of the products that China can demand, which is a huge market. If we are faced with a market, the Nicaraguan economy, such as that of the United States, which is an important and large market, of around 320 million inhabitants, the China market, we are talking about 1,400 million inhabitants, is extremely large, and that would allow the goods to be used in the United States. that Nicaragua has, comparative advantage that they are agricultural goods, can also be easily placed in China. One should expect an increase in trade dynamics opening up those routes; in fact, the Latin American countries that began their relationship with China early today export and have diversified their exports, thanks to that component that they were able to open in Free Trade Agreements. So, Nicaragua is going to take advantage of that, for that factor, first. And the other important factor is also Chinese investments, which usually occur in large projects and in important areas of the economy. So those two elements, the investments from China, added to the exports that Nicaragua can place in that market, the Minister of Finance spoke of 1,000 million dollars, which will undoubtedly give greater dynamism to our country. Journalist Erving Vega: And all this is employment? Words of Ovidio Reyes Indeed, all this translates into employment and opportunities and improvements in living conditions, because when economic activity is energized, then the well-being of the entire nation is improved. On the other hand, I believe that opportunities are also opening up not only for China but for the entire Asian market, which is immense. One sees China, but around it there are also other major players in trade and dynamism in that Asian region. For example, one sees Viet Nam, another huge market for products very close by; Korea, the same as the Thailand Market, Malaysia, Indonesia and even India, which are another 1,400 million people. Asia really is an important sector that must be observed for our products, we are not going to pretend to go there beyond what the country can, because this is a small country. But the important thing is that being a small country, we have more advantage to get, because we are not going to influence or hinder any other market, it is enough to place our products there. Well, for the next few years, right? Words of Ovidio Reyes Yes. Journalist Erving Vega By way of conclusions, let's go back to 2022, I would like to highlight in this part the main Economic Indicators that the Economy is showing this First Half of the Year and with which we hope to close 2022. Words by Ovidio Reyes First, we are seeing that the Agricultural Sector, Fishing and even Mining, especially Gold, continue their positive dynamics and add a lot of energy to the National Economy. We see that these sectors are going to end again in positive shape this year, we also see the sector that to everything we see being observed in terms of the real economy, the Financial Sector has now joined, and with the increase in credit this will allow the dynamics to continue towards the Second Semester. We see inflation that has been a little higher than last year but as a result of external factors, at the national level, there is nothing that is causing inflation, on the contrary, there is a lot of exchange rate stability in the exchange rate, in access to foreign currency we do not see any disturbance in the market. Even what we observe is a positive dynamic in terms of private investment and housing construction. Towards the second half of the year we see that this will continue, and we would expect to end the year with this positive growth rate and with the continuity of this policy. We would also see that inflation would stop growing and rather even instead of being at that rate of 10.3% it could, and it will go down to a more stable rate. Title: Report on the Results of the Meeting of the National System of Production, Consumption and Trade, President of the BCN, Ovidio Reyes R.
text: TRANSCRIPTION TRANSCRIPTION Issuing confidence and stability Issuing confidence and stability Press Conference Report on the Results of the National System of Production, Consumption and Trade Meeting President of the BCN, Ovidio Reyes R. July 14, 2023 President of the BCN: Good morning. As every Friday, the institutions involved in the work of national production hold meetings to evaluate the progress of production, and the progress and prospects of the activities that the institutions that participate in this National System of Production, Consumption and Trade attend. Today we evaluated five topics: The behavior of the export of agricultural products, MIFIC (Ministry of Development, Industry and Commerce) made its presentation; the report on the progress made in the Annual Plan of CONATRADEC, the National Commission for the Transformation and Development of Coffee Farming, which was carried out by CONATRADEC; the Strategy for the Promotion, Production and Monitoring of Animal Feed carried out by the IPSA (Institute of Agricultural Protection and Health); the advances in the Diploma in Technologies to Improve Agricultural Production and Productivity that is carried out by the National Agrarian University (UNA) and the CNU (National Council of Universities). In the case of exports of agricultural goods as of June 2023, we continue to observe that exports maintain a positive growth rate. For example, total exports as of June, or January-June 2023, already reach the figure of 1,907.9 million dollars. That means a growth of 1.7 percent. If we look at the general regime of exports, these amounted to 2,199.9 million dollars with a growth of 2.9 percent and free zones that grew by 1,708 million dollars; a growth of 0.2 percent. TRANSCRIPTION TRANSCRIPTION Issuing confidence and stability Issuing confidence and stability With regard to the main export products, in the case of non-agricultural goods, the main products were: clothing, exporting 847 million; raw gold, 530 million dollars; automotive harnesses, 454 million dollars; farmed shrimp, 57 million dollars; whole fish, 29 million dollars; cotton yarn, 21 million; fuel oils, 20 million dollars; lobsters, 16 million; artificial fiber fabrics, 14 million dollars; and raw silver, 13 million dollars. This by main products and then there are more products that are specified in the global report. The main destinations: United States, 2,045 million dollars; Central America, 662 million dollars; Mexico, 499 million dollars; European Union, 229 million dollars; Canada, 143 million dollars; United Kingdom, 36 million; Switzerland, 33 million; South Korea, 32 million; China, 29 million dollars; and Taipei China, 25 million. That is by main destinations. Then, we observe that when we look at agricultural products, they amounted to 1,735.1 million dollars. This represented a growth of 3.8 percent compared to the previous period. In the general regime, 1,475 million dollars were obtained in agricultural products for a growth of 4.3 percent, and in free zones 260.1 million dollars were obtained for a growth of 1.6 percent. And as for agricultural imports, these were 847.9 million dollars with a much smaller reduction than the global one, in this case it is 1.5 percent. The main agricultural products exported, what were they? In January-June compared to January-June of the previous year: Gold coffee, 460 million dollars; beef, 331 million dollars; cigars and cigarillos, 212 million dollars; cane sugar, 172 million dollars; cheeses, 113 million dollars; red beans, 88 million dollars; unroasted and uncooked peanuts, 69 million dollars; crude oil, 46 million dollars; raw tobacco, 16 million TRANSCRIPTION TRANSCRIPTION Issuing confidence and stability Issuing confidence and stability And the main destinations of agricultural exports were: United States, 700 million dollars; Central America, 433 million dollars; European Union, 213 million dollars; Mexico, 112 million dollars; Canada, 50 million; United Kingdom, 32 million; South Korea, 30 million; Peru, 17 million dollars; Taipei, China, 16 million; Mauritania, 14 million; Japan; 12 million dollars; Dominican Republic, 11 million dollars; and China, 11 million dollars. We observe that the prices of export products so far in 2023, many continue to grow, as is the case of cigars and cigarillos, cane sugar, cheeses, crude oil, uncooked peanuts, red beans, cane molasses, oranges. These products are growing. There are others that have lowered their price a little, such as gold coffee, beef, farmed shrimp, mollusks and bovine offal. However, all these prices are higher than the prices that existed in 2021, that is, we still have attractive prices for all our exports. That is in summary what we saw regarding the evolution that we evaluated of exports to the month of June, information that is preliminary and that will be endorsed with the definitive information from the General Directorate of Customs (DGA), in the following months. We see then that exports are going positive and that the tax is maintained. Then, with respect to CONATRADEC, he reported on the activities it has been carrying out in terms of the promotion of coffee and the activities of attention to coffee producers. Specifically, CONATRADEC this week held the Cup of Excellence, Nicaragua 2023 Contest. 28 municipalities participated in this contest, or there were representatives of 28 municipalities. 290 coffee samples were presented and 42 cooperatives representing some 6,000 producers participated, and a transnational and eight coffee exporting organizations participated. As we mentioned, the CONATRADEC Press Release has already been made public. The participation was very good. Nicaragua once again showed the quality of the coffee that our country has and we reached a price that has not been reached in any of the Central American countries of up to 80 dollars per pound of coffee. That is an excellent price for top quality coffee, and sales that exceeded 800 thousand dollars in that contest. The important thing is TRANSCRIPTION TRANSCRIPTION Issuing confidence and stability Issuing confidence and stability Also, CONATRADEC participated with a representation at the Expoferia in Portland, Oregon from April 21 to 23, for the promotion of Nicaraguan coffee, in which the main coffees of the world appear and are presented.  on the other hand, CONATRADEC provided technical support for the designations of origin. In the coffee sector, a great effort is being made in marketing, coffee quality, and certified designation of origin so that producers achieve better sales. In this case, there are already designations of origin for Dipilto coffee, which is a coffee that is produced in the municipalities of Dipilto, Macuelizo and Mozonte, and 1,810 coffee producers participated in these rounds.  also, for the Cuspire coffee designation of origin, from San Rafael del Norte, the municipality of San Rafael del Norte, San Sebastian de Yali and different cooperatives participate, the total amount produced by these coffees of origin is in the order of 130 thousand quintals. With these designations of origin, coffees are sold at a much better price and so far they are the coffees that are standing out in the fairs and in the cups of excellence as the best quality coffees in Nicaragua. CONATRADEC also participated and carried out training for the quality management of packaging, roasting and basic cupping to different protagonists, almost 100 protagonists in the different support programs they have and technical training for the promotion of coffee. On the other hand, the IPSA presented the progress in the Strategy for the Promotion, Production and Monitoring of Animal Feed. In this case, 54 inspections were carried out in animal feed plants and plants of animal by-products, both for self-consumption and commercial. On the other hand, they also carried out surveillance and samples in different plantations and the training in this case of 92 producers, technical personnel in the departments of Masaya, Leon, Managua and Juigalpa. On the other hand, training has been carried out in the pig sector for 167 protagonists, strengthened in topics on the preparation of feed rations for pigs, 289 protagonists strengthened in issues on the production of concentrates for hens TRANSCRIPTION TRANSCRIPTION Issuing confidence and stability Issuing confidence and stability Also, the National Agrarian University presented the advances in the diploma in technology to improve agricultural production and productivity in 2023. From January 26 to June 29, 47,500 protagonists have already been trained or are being trained in these diploma courses. This diploma is relevant since technologies are taught, a total of 45 technologies that are being taught from the university in 5 modules that are the following: The farm as a productive, agricultural, livestock and forestry unit, the first module; the second module in technology for the training of water, agricultural and livestock production; the third module in technology for animal size nutrition and reforestation; the fourth module in technology for fish farming, hydroponics, non-traditional crops and protein banks; and a fifth module in technology of family gardens, seed banks and post-harvests of grains and vegetables. As we mentioned, courses and training have already been given in this diploma - 47,500 protagonists - progress is already underway through the third module and only the fourth and fifth modules remain. In these courses, 24 virtual transmissions, 847 maximum connections, 24 documents in format, 24 videos have been made and all this technology is available to participants through the web and the different technological links that exist in the municipalities so that as many producers as possible can participate. We invite those interested to also visit the website of the National Agrarian University and participate in these trainings that are part of the university extension to increase the production and productivity of our country. That's what we had to report. The weather advances are also carried out throughout the week by the INETER (Nicaraguan Institute of Territorial Studies) and the summary can be found on their website. Thanks a lot

Title: Interview with Ovidio Reyes, President of the Central Bank, with Journalist Erving Vega TN8 Studio, Channel 8
text: Interview with Ovidio Reyes President of the Central Bank with Journalist Erving Vega TN8 Studio, Channel 8 August 10, 2023 Journalist Erving Vega How are you, good morning. Welcome. Thank you for joining us. A pleasure to be with you. Remember from 7:00 a.m. to 8:00 a.m. live Monday through Friday and a repeat at 1:00 p.m. TN8 studio broadcast for this Thursday, August 10. Today we have our guest on the central issue, the President of the Central Bank, Ovidio Reyes. Thank you Ovidio, for joining us. Welcome. Words by Ovidio Reyes Thank you, Erving, for inviting me to the show. Journalist Erving Vega We work today, August 10, already on the way to Santo Domingo, back to Las Sierritas, Managua Holiday today. But we want to inform you in a special way about important economic issues that the Central Bank has issued in recent days. The last announcement was yesterday, and I don't know, if I have a wrong perception and it seems to me that among the announcements of August it is like the most important. Could we say that the devaluation is over as of 2024? Because the slip rate is set at 0% as of 2024. Ovid, thank you for joining me. Words by Ovidio Reyes Thank you very much, Erving, for giving me the opportunity to explain this to the population. Since 1993, Nicaragua has followed a monetary policy of pre-announced daily devaluations, which is known as the Currency Exchange Slippage, which consists of announcing every day a different exchange rate, almost imperceptibious but causing the currency to lose a little value, it is the daily devaluation. Journalist Erving Vega: And the annual cumulative? In the Annual it has a percentage, when that policy began that devaluation was 12%, then with the passage of time it was reduced, when it began there was a lot of monetary and fiscal imbalance, and exports were very low. Since 2009 we began to make adjustments to this policy, and since 2007 we began to work on a scheme to see how we could graduate, and reduce the pace of devaluations until the currency stabilizes. That was a kind of Plan and Medium and even long-term, we are talking about many years that we have been implementing these actions step by step. 3 years ago we went from 5% to 3%; then to 2%, this year to 1% and for next year it will go to 0%. That is to say, effectively next year there will be no pre-announced daily devaluations, what will govern is an official exchange rate for the entire year. Journalist Erving Vega An important headline for all the media, we start with the announcement is: "The devaluations will end". In this sense, my question is: Are the devaluations over and is it something solid for the next few years from 2024, or is it for 2024 and is this subject to see if it can be sustained for the following years? Words of Ovidio Reyes Well, we have policy instructions for you, one instrument is slippage, we also announced something we call the Monetary Interest Reference Rate, which at the moment we have placed at 7%, that is another policy instrument. There is another policy instrument called The Reserve Reserve, it is 15% and they are instruments that absorb liquidity from depositors; when someone brings a deposit, we ask the banks to put 15% in the Central Bank, of all the deposits of the public. That is another instrument of monetary control. Then we have another one called "Open Market Operations"; that is, we buy and sell Securities of various kinds. These instruments are all still in force, only that the slip pass for the 24th is 0%. The intention is to have it there, but there are conditions in the world that change and we could adjust the policy. However, it is not in our interest to reactivate it. We would really prefer to use the interest rate, the Monetary Reference Rate; then we would leave that slip rate there at 0% and proceed more to Market; that is, to use operations of purchase and sale of Securities, to use the interest rate and any other mechanism that allows us to maintain the stability of the national currency. We believe that in Nicaragua exchange rate stability is highly valued, that is why we have taken this step, but we also have strengths that allow us to make this a reality. The first thing is that the official exchange rate is in practice an official reference exchange rate; This is important. Economic Agents use it to set their prices in cordobas; it is used for the maintenance of the value of the currency, which is continued, the value maintenance clause remains in force, that is maintained. That is to say, anyone who wants to make contracts in dollars payable in cordobas, uses the official exchange rate as a reference, will continue to do so, and people who make contracts of that nature in dollars, convert it with the value maintenance clause. Then, the exchange rate is used as a reference for these operations; this exchange rate is also used when banks want to sell dollars to the Central Bank because they need cordobas, the public dananda cordobas. So we use that exchange rate, and we also use it for debt payments, that's what it's used for, but for the sale of foreign currency it's totally free. The Central Bank does not intervene or force anyone to sell the currency at a price X, which economic agents use the Official Exchange rate as a reference. Journalist Erving Vega Which is how it works right now. I really go to the Bank with cordobas and I want to pay a fee in dollars, the Bank sells the dollars at a price, or if I take dollars he buys them at a different price than the one I buy from him. Words by Ovidio Reyes Of course, because he provides that service of ccnpra-sale of foreign currency, and everyone who engages in this activity knows that they will find a lower exchange rate than the selling rate. That's right, that's the same. In fact, what we have in Nicaragua is a system of free convertibility of the currency, it is totally free. The Central Bank does not intervene in the sale of foreign currency, in fact, when we had to intervene, when there were imbalances it was for the sale of foreign currency, the intervention was to sell foreign currency to the market to stabilize the market, but we have not sold a single dollar for 3 years, and this is determined in the market. Rather, the opposite has happened, they have come to sell dollars because they give codes. This year, for example, as of yesterday it is already worth more than 600 million dollars that have been sold to the Central Bank, and we have delivered the equivalent in cordobas. In such a way that the country is accumulating international reserves as a result of this greater demand for cordobas. Poder medir las condiciones de nuestras viviendas, poder medir la poblacin, los reque- rimientos y todo esto le va a servir al Pas, a la formula- cin de Polticas Pblicas y hasta los negocios, porque varos a saber dnde estn las ccnaaitcacicnes pblacionales, y dnde se mueven el producto, el empleo y otro montn de cosas.
