Title: Transcript: Interview with Ovidio Reyes, President of the Central Bank, with Journalist Erving Vega TN8 Studio, Channel 8
text: Interview with Ovidio Reyes President of the Central Bank with Journalist Erving Vega Estudio TN8, Channel 8 October 13, 2022 Journalist Erving Vega Hello, how are you doing. Good morning. Welcome. Thank you for joining us. It is always a pleasure to be with you through this program Estudio TN8, broadcast for this Thursday, October 13. Our central theme: We are going to talk about the economy, the economic projections, not only from the economic team of Nicaragua, how are the projections going, are the projections readjusted? There is a reestimation in the light of the behavior of the world economy that international financial organizations such as the International Monetary Fund, the World Bank, ECLAC, CABEI, among others, say. We can advance, the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank, which have made very, very conservative projections about Nicaragua's economic behavior for this year 2022, made their recalculation, their reestimates and are much closer in these new calculations to what the economic team of Nicaragua has projected in terms of economic performance for this year, The World Bank estimates 4.1% growth for Nicaragua this year and 4% the International Monetary Fund is almost in line with what the Central Bank, the Ministry of Finance and the Economic Team of Nicaragua as a whole, have projected since the beginning of the year, because at the beginning of the year they have projected I understand that it was in a range between 4% and 5%. Our guest, the President of the Central Bank, Ovidio Reyes. Good morning Ovidio, Welcome. Ovidio Reyes R., President of the BCN Good morning, indeed, we have been participating in the annual meetings of the Monetary Fund and the World Bank. In our case, virtually. We have held meetings with its main officials and there are meetings still pending and the IMF has managed to bring its estimate closer to ours. This phenomenon had not occurred in the last three, four years because they had moved away and had underestimated our projections, but this time they did have a number quite similar to ours. We had many talks, a lot of dialogue and we were able to explain the fundamentals of our economy and with firm statistics they proved that we are indeed on that path. Journalist Erving Vega We will expand on the topic later. What does this mean for Nicaragua? in a context where the main technicians of these organizations say  I am speaking in the global context  "the worst is yet to come", that is, the projection regarding the world's economic performance for this year 2022 is not at all flattering, in the midst of this turbulence, Nicaragua comes out quite well: 4% estimates the International Monetary Fund, 4.1% the World Bank, I repeat, almost in line with what was projected by the Economic Team of Nicaragua since the beginning of the year, was 4%-5% Ovidio? Ovidio Reyes R., President of the BCN Between 4% and 5%. 4.5% indeed. Journalist Erving Vega What are the keys precisely to this good performance of our economy? in this context of turbulence, of this context that is not at all flattering as the technicians of these organizations themselves say: Well, "the worst is yet to come" in terms of the performance of the economy for this year 2022 in the world. We will expand on the topic later. Thank you for sticking with us. The central theme this morning in Estudio TN8, "Growth Projections of the World Bank and the International Monetary Fund" are almost aligned with the projections made from the beginning by the Economic Team of Nicaragua. The International Monetary Fund in its reestimation or recalculation projects an economic performance for Nicaragua of 4%, and the World Bank of 4.1%. The Economic Team of Nicaragua had said from the beginning that we were going to grow between 4 and 5%. We're almost online, right? Words by Ovidio Reyes Yes, we will be in line, because there are always differences, and if those differences in estimates are not very distant, then we are fine. There is always a minimum range. So, in the conversation we had with them, we were able to explain to them that the economy has had an excellent response with its exports, that there has also been a good response from the Service Sector, a greater consumption dynamic, and that foreign direct investment continued. In addition to that, the Financial System began to reactivate credit during this year. These elements were decisive for the Nicaraguan economy to reach a growth rate of 5% during the first half of the year, and that is already a fact, there are already firm figures. So, towards the Second Semester we were also able to show that the dynamic was going to continue, with a slightly lower rate, but it was going to continue; therefore, they revised their estimates and aligned themselves with ours. Journalist Erving Vega I like to share with our viewers to move forward with the interview. "Growth Projections by Region" is graph number 1. United States 2021, 5.7, for 2022 they are projecting 1.6. Euro area for this year 3.1; the Middle East and Central Asia 5%; Emerging and developing Asia, 4.4; Latin America and the Caribbean 3.5; this is the whole, Latin America and the Caribbean. And Central America? By taking it aside. Words by Ovidio Reyes Central America is projecting, by the Monetary Fund, a 4.7% growth. In other words, Central America has a better response than the rest of Latin America and of course than the rest of the advanced economies. Then, they make their estimates for next year, and that's where they don't see a good picture for advanced economies. Journalist Erving Vega 1% for the United States; half a point for Europe. Words by Ovidio Reyes That's right. And in the case of Latin America, they are projecting 1.7% for next year. Central America, they are projecting growth of 3.6%; that is, they foresee a slowdown in 2023. Journalist Erving Vega But always better than the rest of the world? Words by Ovidio Reyes Central America is always better than Latin America, and also than the advanced economies and the rest of the world. It is a fact that Central America has been able to take advantage of its condition as a small economy and Nicaragua a lot, and it has been able to insert itself well into international markets and trade, as a result of the years of globalization. So, economies now have a quick response, and that's what we've been seeing. Journalist Ervin Vega Now, in Central America as a whole, there are better and worse performances. Words by Ovidio Reyes These are moments that happen and sometimes one country is further ahead, another country is behind; But there is really a lot of synchrony between the policy movements of our countries. Journalist Erving Vega Is this one correct? For example, Nicaragua, the bar in blue is 2022. Words by Ovidio Reyes Yes. what they are saying there in these stretches is that Nicaragua is going to grow during 2022, it is going to go down a little in 2023 and then it is going to grow again. They are not behaving in other countries, but well, that is what they are projecting, in our case. Journalist Erving Vega Is Nicaragua the country with the best projection in terms of its performance for next year? Words by Ovidio Reyes According to them, yes. In our case, we have always had a projection that Nicaragua's GDP is between 4 and 5% in the long term, but it can oscillate to 3.5% in certain periods. So, the medium-term forecast is in line with ours. Journalist Erving Vega These graphs are from the Monetary Fund. Let's move on to the World Bank's projection, more than a graphic one, it is a screenshot of their Summary Note. That's for Nicaragua, it's still a graph from the Monetary Fund, that's right, right? Words by Ovidio Reyes That's right. Journalist Erving Vega This is the World Bank's statement: In Nicaragua, growth is projected to moderate to 4.1%; we have already mentioned it, which was close to what the Economic Team of Nicaragua says. I would like to present this screenshot to you because it is more or less what was happening back in January, February, March. The doomsayers, and I'm talking about a negative approach from people who always say, no, we're not going to grow that, and they almost wish we didn't grow that. The World Bank, ECLAC and the International Monetary Fund said it was 3%; then, based on that figure, they tried to discredit the projection that Nicaragua was making of 5%. There it is, for example: "The World Bank and ECLAC deny Ortega's economic projection. While the Nicaragua regime forecasts growth at the end of the year of up to 5%, International Organizations calculate that it will barely touch 3%." That was the approach, what can I say today? In other words, the reality of economic development has said something different. Words by Ovidio Reyes That's right. In other words, it has corroborated that the Economy is indeed in a better position than was thought, or what they thought. We always maintained, and continue to do so, that the economy in 2022 was going to be a year of recovery. I think that in some of the programs we did, I mentioned it to you, it was going to be the year of economic recovery, and indeed it was, and that it was going to be sustained. Last year we came out of the Coronavirus with a rate of more than 10%, and this year we were going to grow a little more moderately, between 4 and 5%. And we believed, that's what I said a few months ago, and we believed that in the medium term we were going to keep growing also around 4%, and in the best case 5%, and maybe at some point 3.5%. Well, the data are corroborating that this was the route that our economy effectively brought and the International Organizations are accepting it, that is the positive thing. Journalist Erving Vega Journalists and I believe that people in general will exercise their imagination, how these dialogues, those talks, that exchange between the Economic Team of a Country with the Technicians of an Organization like these take place. I don't really know what the tone will be, if it will be tense, it will be a discussion, it will be very contradictory, but what I do have as a question Ovidio is, why the World Bank, why the International Monetary Fund always throw very, very low, why are they so pessimistic about Nicaragua? Words by Ovidio Reyes Well, there is a bias they have with small countries like ours not to put it in, even if they are convinced that it is going to be better, not to put it so well, perhaps for fear of making a mistake, to say that it is going to be good and in the end it is not right, and then the bureaucracy penalizes them. There is that. Journalist Erving Vega Let's see, for fear of making a mistake I am wrong, because they were wrong, now they had to readjust and recognize that they were wrong. Words by Ovidio Reyes But for them that is less expensive than the other; I've always seen it that way. And about the conversations. Well, it really is a dialogue, they are not discussions, nor are they lawsuits, because they are professional positions, that is, we arrive with numbers, they present, evaluate, and in the end we reach a point. When we disagree we tell them, and when they don't want to accept a figure they explain why, but sometimes we don't agree, sometimes we agree... This time we agree! Journalist Erving Vega I'm a bit of a fighter, maybe I would say to the Technicians: Hey, you made a mistake and I told you that you were going to make a mistake. Keep this in mind for next year when you make your estimates for Nicaragua. Words by Ovidio Reyes Indeed, what we asked was that they get closer to our positions, which were more realistic, and in the end it happened. In other words, that does indeed happen. Journalist Erving Vega The good thing is that we have a good projection in a difficult context, because what is being projected in terms of the performance of the World Economy is not at all flattering. Words by Ovidio Reyes It is not at all flattering because many events occurred that created problems and are manifesting themselves now. For example, Public Spending expanded too much, the amount of money in the entire world expanded too much, due to the effects of the pandemic, and when that happens the Economy suffers it. That is why prices skyrocketed. The prices today of imported products are really high, up to 40% in some goods and up to 70% in other goods, and that is an element that has and brings enormous costs for production, because today machinery, equipment, supplies and materials are imported expensive, and that includes Consumer Goods for the home, that includes even imported Medicines. And that is the high cost of an excessively expansive Fiscal and Monetary Policy worldwide. Nicaragua did not do that, we remained in balance, we did not expand the amount of money, nor did public spending expand, but inflation came from outside, totally from outside. It is dramatic and even unfair, because now we have to pay more for all the goods we import; For better or the other side is that exports have grown, and that has allowed the payment of the bill. That distortion that has been created plays against our countries, and it plays against the population that now has to pay higher prices, because in the world prices went up, things did not go well. So, we are at that crossroads of high global inflation, which is manifest in the documents of the IMF and the World Bank, and that we have to do a job that we did not have to do, because the Nicaraguan economy was balanced, and the work now is to adjust as well as they are doing; That's the cost. Journalist Erving Vega In the case of the official projection, does Nicaragua also readjust a little? Words by Ovidio Reyes We believe that the world is decisive for what happens in Nicaragua, and there are many statistics that support that when the world is doing well, when the nations with which we trade are doing well, we are doing well; and when the world is doing badly, and the nations with which we trade are doing well, we are not doing so well; I am not saying badly, because sometimes the growth rate drops a little and is not necessarily negative. But the last experience of that nature that occurred was back in 2010, when there was the global financial crisis. In the world there was a great restriction on the amount of money and that affected our economy, and the GDP was negative in Nicaragua. They are not talking about a global recession, they are talking about the fact that instead of the 3% that they had been growing, they are going to grow by a timid 1%. That can affect us, and we are acknowledging it. Now, in our next Report and Evaluation, we will most likely correct our growth rate, which we are expecting to be between 4 and 5% from the beginning of the year ; we will most likely adjust it by 3.5 and 4.5%. We do not think that we have to slow it down further, because the fundamentals and the statistics that we have been observing, indicate that we are indeed going to reach no less than 4%, but being prudent between 3.5 and 4.5%, that is our new estimate. And on the other hand, as I mentioned, inflation has been giving too much momentum, and we expected at the beginning of the year inflation that was going to be between 6 and 7%, then we corrected, between 7 and 8%, but now we also need to correct, because prices are not giving way worldwide, goods continue to be expensive. And we believe that we can end up between 8.5 and 9%. The good news Erving is that today, the INIDE published the Consumer Price Index for September, and in September prices basically did not increase, the index reflected 0.07%. So it seems that the adjustments that took place in international prices in the economy arrived, hit and now they are stabilizing. And that also makes us more optimistic in terms of our medium-term estimates, that inflation in the coming years is going to subside, it is going to subside. Of course, everything will depend on what happens in the world. If, as the IMF says, things are going to go badly for them, for Central America they don't say they're going to go so badly, they say they're going to go well, for Nicaragua they say they're going to go well. But if things go wrong in the world, and prices become unbalanced, then it will be something that we are going to have to evaluate. But in the perspectives what is observed is that inflation begins to ease this year and falls a little more in the following years, at least about 2 years of slightly higher inflation. Journalist Erving Vega We would always like to grow a little more, 5, 6, 7, 8, but Well, that's the reality, and that reality in this global context looks better than the rest. What are the determining keys to having a better performance than the rest of the world, and if we go to our Region, even than the rest of our own neighbors? Words by Ovidio Reyes I think that an important factor is politics. Nicaragua enjoys a good Iberian Economy, good Fiscal Policy, Macroeconomic Balance; that is, the Budget is balanced, there is a controlled deficit, a deficit of no more than 2% of GDP. For economists, this is an excellent deficit. Public debt is stable, and that has been a determining factor, because throughout the world public debts rose a lot with the pandemic. In the case of Nicaragua, the public debt remained stable, it did not grow. And on the other hand, Monetary Policy has also been balanced; that is, we did not inject money massively, nor did we do it as other countries did. We remained prudent, trying to ensure that the economy and the monetary balance supported the currency and the exchange rate; and the exchange rate is very stable, it is free on the street. So there is a Global Macroeconomic Policy that also focuses on spending on investment, Social and Productive; So those are key. The other thing is that Nicaragua has a large export base that has been able to take advantage of the moment. Exports have been in the last 4 years standing out at significant rates, and this year, without problems, 3,500 million dollars minimum, I am talking about a floor in exports of goods, another 3,500 million dollars in exports from Free Trade Zones; we are talking about more than 7,000 million dollars of exports. That is to say, we have solid foundations that generate a flow of foreign currency, economic activity and employment, which is what sustains our economy. Journalist Erving Vega There the palms are for the Producers, the synergy as well, Producers, Public Private Sector, support for the Small, because for there to be projections there have to be products. Words by Ovidio Reyes Well, our Economy is an Economy of Entrepreneurs, an Economy based on thousands of people competing, of Small, Medium Producers and Large Producers as well, and they all move freely, and that is what generates the great current of economic activity, with the State facilitating, delivering Training, promoting, delivering Technologies, facilitating things so that all Nicaraguans benefit from that growth. Journalist Erving Vega How good is it when reviewing its impact on the objective central What the has always stated the President, who is our main adversary says he is Poverty? How good is an economic performance of this level, and how much does it make us advance in this fight? Words by Ovidio Reyes Well, the statistics that have been collected on Poverty are good, in the sense that Poverty has been reduced in the last 10, 12 years. In other words, economic growth it generates wealth, true, of course, not yet the wealth of the large countries, but within the framework of our reality, poverty has been reducing. The INIDE I was seeing is preparing other Indicators where it is measured, for example, how many motorcycles there are in the country, how many cell phones there are in the country, how many televisions per home, and those Indicators notably continue to improve: How many people have brick floors in their homes, how many now have zinc, how many people now use blocks in construction, how many have access to drinking water, sewage service, electricity, how many people have access? And these are signs that the country is making progress in reducing poverty, and these indicators are positive. So, if there has been an impact of this economic growth on poverty reduction. Journalist Erving Vega Regarding "Julia", is it a phenomenon that could have an impact on our projections? Between 160 million and 200 million have just been calculated in damages. Words by Ovidio Reyes That is something that we are evaluating, we are collecting information to see what the impact could be, and there above all are the crops and infrastructure. We have to finish making all the impact; but all hurricanes in Nicaragua have had severe impacts because the country is vulnerable. This hurricane once again told everyone that Nicaragua is a transit area for hurricanes; the hurricane passed through Nicaragua almost in the middle of Nicaragua, and that moves everyone's contribution. That is to say, we have explained this in International Organizations, about how Climate Change is affecting our Economy. It is a Human issue, it is a Natural issue, but it is also an Economic issue due to the losses caused by these disasters, and we are going to make every effort to be able to mobilize resources from the International Community, which will mitigate all these impacts. Journalist Erving Vega I have a second pause. I will return to Ovid's conclusions. The topic we are developing today: "Growth Projections for Nicaragua by the World Bank and the International Monetary Fund" are assimilated to the official projections of the Government of Nicaragua and its Economic Team. The Fund made its reestimate calculating a 4% growth for Nicaragua, this year, the World Bank also made its reestimate and projects a 4.1% growth for Nicaragua. This year, in line, in tune, almost the same as what the economic team of Nicaragua projected at the beginning of the year, which was a range of 4 and 5%. But this year, Ovidio, the official reestimate would be between 3.5 and 4.5%? Words by Ovidio Reyes And 4.5% in light of the evaluation of the world economy, which they point out is evolving as we expected. Journalist Erving Vega Which continues to be much better than projected for the rest of the Central American Region, and in turn Central America as a whole, with a better projection than the performance of the global economy. Words by Ovidio Reyes Indeed, due to the open commercial nature of our economies, we have been able to make better use of it. Journalist Erving Vega What are the main factors that are holding the world back in its economic performance? The pandemic is no more, or does it still have? Words by Ovidio Reyes Well, the pandemic left aftermath, and one of the aftermath was that it broke what are known as supply chains, which have not yet normalized. The other result of the pandemic is that for some reason a lot of people left the workforce and haven't come back. That is also happening in Nicaragua. For some reason, families with the pandemic decided either to work from home or simply to stay at home doing household things and it has been difficult for them to return; That is the second element. And the third element that is affecting the world is financial risk, that is, after the pandaral, vulnerabilities appear that have left the financial system weak, a lot of money, a lot of demand and little supply, as a result prices skyrocketed and now the risk is that international interest rates rise. The United States is thinking of making a strong increase in its interest rate, and that is what puts the outlook and sees it as negative, why? Because global interest hikes such as the one in the United States cause a lot of capital to flow out of our countries to take advantage of the yield. As a result, economies cool, spending cools down, and then there is a downturn in the economy, and in the worst case, even a recession. So, these are the elements that have caused that there is now a panorama, according to them, discouraging in the perspective. In our case, we have the advantage that our country is not a country that is based on international financial integration as other countries in Latin America are. Our country is based on its productive capacity, that is, on its exports and its generation of foreign exchange; So a movement like this does generate outputs, it does generate expectations, but the most important thing is that our foundation, which is the export base, is not affected and that will continue. Journalist Erving Vega Now when we read the Considerations of the technicians in their Reports, I am talking about the World Bank and the International Monetary Fund, they say, Russia's war against Ukraine, although there it is like many Master's, Postgraduate and Doctorate degrees are faltering. Because then there is a hurricane of criticism from economists who perhaps studied with the same technicians who say, no, it is not the war brother, it is the energy crisis that they have created from the so-called sanctions. But hey, that's a political takeover, but it's a fact that it's having an effect. Words by Ovidio Reyes I believe that there are elements that occur around the cause and exacerbate it, that is my point of view. But the cause in Economics, the cause of inflation is usually monetary and fiscal imbalances, they are not other types of imbalances, there are supply imbalances as well, as economists say. That is, for example, if a drought comes, prices rise because food becomes more expensive, but that has not happened, what has happened is that the breakdown of supply chains has generated a supply problem. But the fact that inflation is growing so much is because there is a lot (... inaudible) with any investor. Today we already have it at 6%, the Federal Reserve, the European Central Bank, the United Kingdom and all the Central Banks of Latin America, have been adjusting their interest rates; if they adjust it, we are going to have to do it too, because if we don't, capital could flow and we don't want that, of course, with a limit we are going to continue doing it. And on the other hand, in some way our adjustment motivates a certain adjustment in our economy, since inflation comes from abroad we cannot control it all because the imported corponent is very high, but we can take actions to mitigate it and that is what we are going to do. Title: Report on the Results of the Meeting of the National System of Production, Consumption and Trade - President of the BCN, Ovidio Reyes R.
text: TRANSCRIPTION TRANSCRIPTION Issuing confidence and stability Issuing confidence and stability Press Conference Report on the Results of the National System of Production, Consumption and Trade Meeting President of the BCN, Ovidio Reyes R. June 16, 2023 President of the BCN: Good morning everyone. We are going to report the results of the weekly meeting of the National System of Production, Consumption and Trade that aims to evaluate and monitor the goals contained in the National Plan of Production, Consumption and Trade for the 2023-2024 agricultural cycle. On this occasion, we covered the issues of exports of agricultural products to the month of May, the progress for the strategy for the security and health of all crops and animal production, the presentation on the microcredit program for the field "Adelante", the report on the technological and technical centers, the follow-up and monitoring of the production and consumption of beans, and the behavior of the climate. So, we are going to explain the results of each of these issues that we address today. In the case of exports to the month of May, the evolution of global exports and agricultural exports, the preliminary monitoring that will later be confirmed with the information already registered by the General Directorate of Customs Services, the preliminary information indicates that exports to May are advancing at a good pace. growing at 3 percent, for a total exported amount of 3,247.3 million dollars. Of that total, 1,861 million dollars corresponded to exports of goods under the general regime and 1,385.8 million to exports from free zones. The former grew to 4.9 percent and the latter to 0.6 percent. Then, we have observed a reduction in imports of 7.9 percent, which totaled 4,244.9 million dollars. A good part of this reduction was caused by a drop in prices observed during the last months of the year, compared to the total amount exported. TRANSCRIPTION TRANSCRIPTION Issuing confidence and stability Issuing confidence and stability Then, when we look at agricultural exports, and those directly served by the National System of Production, Consumption and Trade, these grew in the accumulated January-May compared to January-May of the previous year by 5.6 percent, a total of 1,459.7 million dollars of exports of agricultural goods, 1,241.9 million correspond to the general regime and 217.9 million dollars to the free zone regime. Here, both agricultural exports of the general regime grew by 5.5 percent and those of the free zone by 6.2 percent. In agricultural goods, what are the main products that are being exported?: the coffee, grass and mate items, which are grouped together, amount to 382 million dollars; meat and offal, 287 million dollars; tobacco and substitutes, 188 million dollars; sugars, 166 million dollars; dairy, eggs and honey, 117 million dollars; vegetables and legumes, 83 million dollars; oilseeds, 64 million dollars; fats and oils, 43 million dollars; beverages, 37 million dollars; edible fruits, 35 million dollars; and preparation of various foods, 12 million dollars. These are the main export items in the agricultural sector. So, as we can see, there is a continuity of the export dynamic with upward movements of goods of exported products, and also with downward movements, but it is observed that in the case of edible oil, cane sugar, red beans, cattle, powdered milk, fluid milk, cane molasses, oranges, bananas, cheeses, waste for food, tobacco and bovine offal, offal, all of these have significant growth. All of them of more than 20 percent, that is, there is a good price position for these products in particular. And there are also others that have had reductions, especially those that have to do with lobsters, fish fillets, farmed shrimp, which those are having for the cyclical moment TRANSCRIPTION TRANSCRIPTION Issuing confidence and stability Issuing confidence and stability But, in the combined we have a good position with respect to international prices, which have to continue to be the main or one of the main incentives to always advance in the area of exports. That is on the export side. But, in this system we also integrate all the components that are relevant to ensure national production, and in this case the Institute of Agricultural Protection and Health (IPSA), made its presentation on the safety and health of all crops for animal production in general. What progress can be observed on the side of animal and plant health? Well, in the training, 3,089 protagonists have been trained in good agricultural practices, in the production of certified seeds, in pest and disease control at the national level. 10,703 protagonists have also received talks on prevention and control of diseases in cattle, pigs, poultry, bees, and good use of veterinary drugs at the national level. Other talks: 358 protagonists who have received training in the safety of bovine, pork and poultry feed, and talks to 2,349 producers in the implementation of good agricultural practices and traceability. Another work of the IPSA is its inspections, they have made 1,040 visits to seed establishments and marketers nationwide and 1,255 visits to agricultural input establishments, as well as 605 samples in various items of chayote, tobacco, potato, citrus, fruit trees, coffee and cocoa. There are also 34,500 visits to farms under pest surveillance, accompanying 1,685 producers, and 42,252 trapping services have been carried out to monitor the various pests monitored by IPSA. Also visits to agricultural farms: 343 biosecurity inspections, 18,049 visits to agricultural farms and 387 to veterinary pharmacies. This is part of the work they do to ensure quality and good practices. Also, they have taken 5,875 samples for disease detection, for epidemiological surveillance and to maintain the health statuses that our country already enjoys. Also health days: 324 vaccination days, 120 thousand 321 birds have been covered in these vaccination days. And days of vampire captures, 31 days of captures, which can be detrimental to TRANSCRIPTION TRANSCRIPTION Issuing confidence and stability Issuing confidence and stability Also, the IPSA has carried out and continued its work of bovine traceability records, 6,185 registered farms, new farms, new farm registrations and a total of 624,577 cattle identified among all producers nationwide, as well as another 167 days. In other words, the work of traceability in the livestock sector continues, does not stop and advances as established in the Plan. In addition to that, they have carried out 34,902 inspections to date of shipments and by-products of animal and plant origin abroad, all at the national level to ensure that Nicaraguan products maintain quality and their sanitary status. That is what IPSA informed us at today's meeting of the progress they have been making during their work plan. There was also a presentation of the Adelante Program, how it is advancing. This Adelante Program is the loan program, micro loans made by the Government. The complement of the Zero Usury Program that already exists for the city. The Adelante Program is for the countryside. To date, 5,368 protagonists have been served, of which 2,139 are women, 3,209 are men and the total credit that has already been granted through this program amounts to 351.4 million cordobas, with a low default rate of just 0.28 percent. It should be noted here that there are 18 delegations and also in 140 municipalities attention to attend to all those who request loans and require this financing that has a really low interest rate relative to other interest rates in this same market that is around 15 percent, it is low for micro financing. The interest rates for micro financing, the minimum are around 40 percent, however, in this program they are offered at 15 percent. Also, the average number of loans made in this program is 65,279 cordobas and the bulk of the loans are located between 12 months and 24 months. So, to all those interested in these programs, it is important that you visit the offices where these loans are made. For example, in the case of the primary sector, loans are covered for agriculture, livestock, manufacturing, construction and wholesale trade. In the case of the secondary sector, loans are covered for the processing of food products, TRANSCRIPTION TRANSCRIPTION Issuing confidence and stability Issuing confidence and stability On the other hand, another topic that we covered during the meeting was the issue related to the Nicaraguan Institute of Agricultural Technology (INTA), they are the centers and farms for the development of agricultural technology, currently 7 new centers and farms for the development of agricultural technology have been installed. Currently, INTA reported that it has 26 development farms and 15 agricultural development centers. A total of 299 experiments have been established, the experiments consist of varieties of different plants, varieties of hybrids and also native varieties and in addition to that in the incorporation of agricultural technology and practices. In research, 42 research experiments have been conducted in technologies out of an annual target of 101 experiments. In precious beans, coffee, for example, 21 experiments have already been carried out out out of a total of 25: in cocoa 17 research experiments out of a total of 22: vegetables and arbor crops to date there are 31 experiments out of a goal of 47, there is a goal of producing only in this case 400,000 healthy plants, with good genetic quality and that can be marketed nationally. In musaceae, roots and tubers, 30 experiments have already been carried out out of 45 that are planned. In the case of musaceae, for example, 10 experiments out of 18, and the goal is to reach 600,000 genetically healthy and resistant plants. In fruits, 39 experiments out of 66 experiments. In herbs and cooking and medicinal plants it has already carried out 92 established experiments out of 168; and in animal feed, 38 experiments have been carried out out out of a total of 61. So this is the progress that INTA is making, which is offering healthy products and genetically improved varieties, that is the progress in this area. TRANSCRIPTION TRANSCRIPTION Issuing confidence and stability Issuing confidence and stability The winter, we were also informed by the colleagues of the Nicaraguan Institute of Territorial Studies (INETER), which is already established around between 60 and 80 percent of humidity has been reached at the national level and is distributed, that is what the colleagues of INETER reported to us. On their website they have a weather report for all interested parties and also has a projection of the winter outlook that everyone can consult. There is all the specialized information. But the good news is that we were informed that it can already be said that it has already begun and the lands are suitable for crops already well distributed at the national level. So, that is in the information we have. Exports in advance. Institutions of IPSA and INTA working hard to ensure that there are good seeds, that there are genetics and in addition to that that there is corresponding animal and plant health. And on the other hand, the microcredit program is advancing at a good pace to reach 500 million cordobas, we are already at 357. And a good availability in the case of beans, there is a stable supply and we would also hope to meet the production and consumption goal for this year and for half of the next, which is what covers the production, consumption and trade cycle. Thanks a lot

Title: Interview with Comrade Ovidio Reyes, President of the Central Bank of Nicaragua, with Journalist Alberto Mora, Live Magazine, Channel 4
text: Interview with Comrade Ovidio Reyes, President of the Central Bank of Nicaragua, with Journalist Alberto Mora Live Magazine, Channel 4 August 15, 2023 Journalist Alberto Mora Welcome, my viewers. Thank you for being with us this morning of Tuesday, August 15, 2023. As always a pleasure to be with you through the screen of your televisions. We hope you have a good Tuesday. Well, this morning we will have in the studio the President of the Central Bank of Nicaragua, Companero Ovidio Reyes. With him we will talk about different aspects that have to do with the behavior, with the good performance of the national economy, economic indicators, statistics, projected growth, the growth that has been occurring during these months that have already passed of the year - we are already about the eighth month of the year 2023 - and we will also talk about the measures that the Central Bank has taken. Zero rate in terms of the sliding of the cordoba in relation to the dollar from 2024, and throughout the year. Also the issue of the truncation of checks, which he is also going to explain a little more. And all the topics of interest about the national economy, exports and others. Well, we welcome the President of the Central Bank, comrade Ovidio Reyes. Thank you for being with us. Mr. President, thank you for joining us this morning and we wanted to talk about different aspects that have to do with economic behavior, the projections you have for this year, which we have already more or less known, and also specific aspects such as the zero rate of sliding of the cordoba in relation to the dollar for next year. Also the issue of checks, the truncation of them and that I understand that it is a situation that has been developing in various countries. not only in Nicaragua and I would like you to start please, if you will allow us to give us a general overview of what the behavior of the economy is up to this moment. I understand that they have not closed August, but you can already have as you always do, and you are with your reports. Where are we going, what direction are we going? And welcome Ovid, this morning. Words by Ovidio Reyes Yes, thank you very much Alberto for inviting me to your Program and being able to explain these issues to the population. The economy, according to the information we have been collecting, continues with a positive growth trend. The latest Report of the Monthly Index of Economic Activity reflects a cumulative growth of 3.9%. We have a growth goal for this year 2023, which is between 2.5 and 3.5%. We believe that we are going to reach this goal closer to 3.5 than to 2.5 because of the results we have been observing. In recent months, there has been a momentum that is being generated by Commercial, Services, Transportation, Communications and Financial Services activity, which are giving the economy a new component, which at the time we made the estimates did not exist; however, we will maintain the estimate target for this year at growth between 2.5 and 3.5%. On the other hand, we have observed that international price pressures have begun to have their effect on the national economy; that is, international prices that throughout 2022 and at the beginning of 2023 were very high have begun to fall. In the world this is happening because the Central Banks of the main individual economies are playing shares, the main Traite raising the interest rate; making general credit and access to money more expensive. That has had a consequence and inflation in the rest of the world has fallen. How has this been reflected in Nicaragua? Well, already in the month of July inflation was -0.25, that is, it was already negative. We believe that in the remainder of the year this effect of the global inflation will be reflected in our economy and we would expect inflation to be around 6% this year, from what has already been accumulated, it will go down. In other words, the international effect that the Nicaraguan economy had due to inflation is already giving way for the same reason, and that is that the world economy is deflating. So, that is what happens on the price side. On the side of the workforce, we are expecting an unemployment rate of 3.2, 3.3% for this year. Journalist Alberto Mora Words by Ovidio Reyes It is the open unemployment rate, it is the one that we have been monitoring all this time and that we would hope will be maintained, it is a stable rate, it is not high. We have also seen in the Indicators published by INIDE, that what is known here as underemployment, has also been decreasing; So they are elements that we have taken into consideration for the projections, and vain that we are in correspondence with the goals that we set at the beginning of the year. Journalist Alberto Mora Now, talking a little about the behavior of exports, which are foreign exchange earnings; also talking about the issue of remittances, which is very important for the country's economy. Where are we? Some data have been given and despite some decreases in the prices of commodities, there is still a tendency to maintain these indicators in some cases increased, right? Words by Ovidio Reyes Yes, the international prices of Nicaragua Spartan products are in good shape; that is, that is an element that should motivate the boost in exports that we have been observing in recent years to continue; that is, there are good prices for coffee, there are good prices for livestock, good prices for sugar, good prices for gold, good prices for all the products that Nicaragua exports. Except for the problems that are occurring due to the reduction in demand that has affected the Free Trade Zones, not only in Nicaragua, but throughout Central America, the rest of exports of Goods and Services are growing well. Journalist Alberto Mora Not like in a moment since some prices were higher, the case of coffee, I think. Words of Ovidio Reyes What there was was a great increase, there was a reaction; So they were much higher than they should have been, but they have good prices, coffee is averaging about 170 dollars a quintal, it has always been a good price for coffee that level and we would hope that it will remain there. So, on the export side, believe us that we have secured about 8,000 million dollars of export revenues, that is an important amount for our economy. We are also seeing that Tourism has rebounded, statistics show that Tourism is reactivating and that affects Hotels and Restaurants and the commercial chain, which is also in a momentum. And we would expect no less than 600 million dollars of income from Turisno. In fact, last year we went for that amount, and this year it will be higher; but in our estimates we have it like this, about 600 million dollars. The other thing is that the statistics of foreign investment also show a positive result, last year 1,800 million, this year it could be about 1,600 million dollars in foreign investment. And well, what you mentioned, Remittances, which are having an accelerating dynamic in all Central American countries, in Mexico and the Dominican Republic. In other words, remittances are constituting an important source of income for all these economies, and the amounts in other countries are much larger. Nicaragua is having a boost but even the rebates of Nicaragua are lower with the other countries of the Region that are much larger, the dcble efe what we collect; however, the amount this year is going to be important. That is to say that we expect about 4,800 million dollars in income from remittances during 2023 and for next year an even higher amount, but this year 4,800. So, if you see, Alberto, we have 8,000 million dollars in export revenues, we have 600 million dollars in income from tourism, 4,800 million dollars in income from remittances, and 1,600 million dollars in income from foreign investment; that is, there are sufficient funds in the economy to energize it. This also shows that Nicaragua has greatly reduced its exposure and its risks. Because if you look at it, in all aspects it is diversified and is generating foreign exchange, the country has opened up, our economy has become very open, quite open. That has many advantages, that is, it allows us to mobilize resources, it allows us to boost the economy. Although it also has the disadvantage that if something bad happens outside, it affects us, but the truth is that we have been able to take advantage of the commercial spaces, the service spaces, the location spaces of our products, and Vamos Adelante. Journalist Alberto Mora Now, in the case of remittances there is an impact on domestic consumption, right? Words by Ovidio Reyes Remittances are perceived, at least by the surveys we have conducted, by low-income people, many low-income people. So, it has a spillover component, right, because they receive it and it helps the consumption of the Families, and if they are helping in the dynamics of consumption. However, we have also known of people who have made ventures with these Remittances, which is also positive, you not only have to receive to spend, but to invest. Journalist Alberto Mora And there are also stories that can be told. Now, as for the 8,000 or so million dollars in exports, are you including the Free Trade Zone and Goods? Words of Ovidio Reyes They are almost half and half. In other words, we have been able to capitalize on all the activities and plans that have been developed from the National System of Production, Consumption and Commerce to generate agricultural, livestock, forestry and forestry activity, which allows the economy to be maintained at a good pace. And the most important thing is that this sector, the Primary Sector of our economy, has not only shown dynamism but strength; that is, in all the episodes we have had, of cycles, this sector is the one that has presented the fewest situations. Journalist Alberto Mora Now, talking a little about the aspects that have to do with decisions that have been made, I am going to start with the "Truncation of Checks", a word that you use, and that has to do with checks drawn in favor of a company that is going to deposit it in a bank that is not the same as the one where the check was issued. What happens there? What is the mechanism? Because since they talk about electronic references, then people believe, some, that the chequeo.to is going to disappear, that it is no longer going to do it; that is, there is some information there that could be perfectly clarified and it is appropriate, I think, despite the fact that you have been doing it, for people to know more, and how it mainly benefits them. Words by Ovidio Reyes That's right. The physical checks, the ones you know, the checkbook, those continue. The State also issues checks for payroll payments, those continue to work. What is sought is to speed up its payment, to make the payment effective. Why? Because we have had problems with customers, for example, who arrive at a bank and can wait up to 3, 4 days for the payment to be made. Journalist Alberto Mora I want to explain it, well, in my own way. If you are paid with a check from Bank X and you have your account in Bank Y, you are going to deposit it in Bank Y, and since it is not a check from Bank Y, which is not identical, then you wait 3, 4 days for them to cash you, even if the cashier has already received the check. That's right? Words by Ovidio Reyes Like this. Because they cannot verify whether or not it has a fund; so, for the verification of funds, it must be sent to the Central Office, it must be sent to the administrative aspect. Journalist Alberto Mora The old-fashioned way, as we say. Words by Ovidio Reyes Everything is mechanical, and that is a delay. And then, for the payment, there is another round, because then it has to be sent to the Central Bank, there the checks are cleared, so it is a very long process for those who require their money now. Because if you have a check you want to get to the window and get paid immediately. But it doesn't work that way in all cases; unless the check is from the Bank itself, then they will attend to the payment, because they verify it. On the other hand, if it is not from the Institution itself, it must be verified. The verification process took time, because as of yesterday we began to accelerate payments, how? Using electronic means, in what way? Well, cano does a lot of people with documents: You take a document, and he says go, he takes out his cell phone and I'm afraid of a photo, he scans it and he can send it to other people whatever the document is. Well, in this case we are doing the same with this procedure: The physical check is taken and what the Bank does is that it immediately scans it, it goes to the scanner; then, the scanner becomes the check, that's why it's called "Truncamiento", that is, the check is truncated, he says, this is my physical form, once he makes the digital capture, the guy can even grab the check and put it aside, the digital one is the one that becomes valid, from that point on. We do that within the Bank. Journalist Alberto Mora Now, the customer who has deposited has nothing to do with that; that is, that is an internal matter among the Banks. Words of Ovidio Reyes That's right. It is a mechanism that we have established from the Central Bank to speed up payment, the digital capture of the check, no longer needs the physical, bureaucratic procedure, but is sent electronically to change. Journalist Alberto Mora Or immediately you know: "there is no bottom". Words by Ovidio Reyes That's there lullabies, in the memento. Now, problems can arise, that is why we have given ourselves no less than 24 hours for the check to be cashed, because in the end it is also a mechanism for validating the check, numbering and searching, the signature, it is cleared, etc. So we have managed to reduce the cost, that is, up to 4 days that the payment of a check could return, now it has to be paid in 24 hours; that is, if you take it in the afternoon, at the end of the afternoon, well, you will have to wait the next day, if you take it early you will receive it the same day. That's a benefit for all check users who require it to be cashed as soon as possible. Journalist Alberto Mora And the streamlining of part of the banking processes, right? Words by Ovidio Reyes Of course, because then we will be able to settle all the financial processes that are in the air, on the same day. Journalist Alberto Mora Now, I have read, I have seen that in other countries they were moving forward. What's going on? Why hadn't we done it? Well, others haven't started either, but why wait this time to do so? Words by Ovidio Reyes That's right. Well, things arrive at the time they have to arrive, that is, we have a whole process of national ecology that is increasingly entering the digital world, the world of the Web, the massive use of mobile telephony. Nicaragua has its degree of progress in the issues of Banking, it is called that, and Banking Digitalization; So, this is one more step in that process; But not only this plan, there are many other plans that you are making known at the time, to use digital and electronic media, and that speeds up payments. Journalist Alberto Mora This digital thing is also a "goat", I'm going to talk about it as they say in good Nicaraguan; he puts it "chiva" because of the scam issue, Ovid. Words of Ovidio Reyes That's right. You have to be careful! I call on all those who are listening to us on television not to give any information, to call or ask them in the name of the Truncation and in the name of the Central Bank. We do not call anyone on the phone to ask for anything, neither their account, nor their phone number, nor data verification, absolutely nothing!, nor by WhatsApp, nor by email, nor by phone calls, nor personal. I want to make that clear, that someone introduces himself saying that he is an official of the Central Bank and wants to ask them for information. .. No! Banks do not have this practice either, because we all agree to avoid bank scams. So, any scammer who approaches and is serious, and who believes that he is a banker and who sends him and asks for personal information, I invite him not to hand over anything, absolutely nothing! If you want to manage your accounts, go to the Bank, it is the best. No giving anything, absolutely nothing! Not the ID, not the account number, not his name, not his surname, not his address, not where he lives, not his relatives, not anything! Because by doing that they expose themselves. No matter how seriously it is seen, it does not matter, they must deliver absolutely nothing. You have to be careful of these people because they really are a plague; People are able to extract information and extract their account numbers and keywords, so they are subject to scams. You have to be very careful. Journalist Alberto Mora: We have a couple of other issues that we want to address with the President of the Central Bank. When checks were issued by an institution, an express institution or a private person, at the end of the month the checks that had been sent, those that had been paid, returned. Later, the banks began to say, we are going to send those to each other, unless you make a request and make a payment of so much. Will that not happen now? Words of Ovidio Reyes Now what happens is that, the one who issued the check and wants to validate them, what he will receive is an electronic copy because it has already been truncated. That is, it has a physical component when it was issued, and once the Bank captures it digitally, that is the one that counts, the other is left out, that is, the electronic one; Customers will receive electronic copies of their checks, that is the mechanism and regulation that we have established. Journalist Alberto Mora Why were they established? Taking advantage, returning to the tena, why was an amount of up to 2,000 dollars or its equivalent in cordobas established? Words of Ovidio Reyes For your security, already an amount of 2,000 dollars and an amount of 70,000 cordobas is an amount that is better verified physically. There the same mechanism is maintained, super- rior checks are made by physical means, it is not truncated, but it goes to verification. That is the reason and this is how it is done in all countries. Pasque you will understand that there are express checks of millions, thousands and tens of thousands of dollars; that is, those checks are not going to go to truncation but are going to go to physical verification. Journalist Alberto Mora That is, at this time they are not thinking of changing. Words by Ovidio Reyes There it is maintained, with the higher amounts there is the physical mechanism, in the rest of the smaller denominations, of the 70,000 cordobas and the 2,000 dollars there goes the truncation, the electronics, which are the vast majority. Journalist Alberto Mora Now, talking a little about the other decision that the Central Bank has feared, the Zero Slip Rate in relation to the cordoba against the dollar. By 2024 what does this allow? You have said the strengthening of the currency, everything else, what about the issue... He has said that inflation is now one point less, .25 less, he has said a data that is going down, that there is also a positive impact of RDOJA on the external side. But, what allows us to do this and what do people gain, what do we all gain with a strengthened currency that maintains its price, remains unchanged? Words by Ovidio Reyes Let's start from the conditions in which this decision is being made. First, we have had, as I mentioned in the external funding package, important foreign exchange income in the country, they are generated for multiple reasons, there is not just one. I mentioned exports to you, tourism, foreign investment, and remittances, which are the main sources of external funding. The Exchange Rate is very stable, quite stable, in fact the Central Bank announces the exchange rate, we call it the Official Exchange Rate, but it is really a Reference, why? Because we do not participate, we do not intervene and we let the exchange rate flow by itself. In fact, in the sale we do not determine the exchange rate, what we give is a reference with the Official Officer; the sale rate is freely determined in the Market. Purchase and sale of foreign currency by Banks, Financial Institutions, Institutions authorized for the purchase and sale of foreign currency. Money changers and everybody, so it flows very well. For 3 years the Central Bank has not sold a single dollar to the economy, that the Central Banks are supposed to be active, buying and selling; even, in some countries of the Region, banks sell foreign currency for imports. But well, in our country that does not happen, we do not sell foreign currency to carriers or sell foreign currency to anyone. We have not sold you a single dollar for 3 years, the opposite has happened, rather, as there is a greater demand for cordobas they lead us to sell dollars to the Central Bank, and since we have the power to enisicn, then we deliver corctics to CBnbdo. That has allowed the aoxrulation of healthy reserves, because it goes with an asset, in this case the dollars, and an equal, healthy monetary scansion; that is, it is not with debt, it is not with any liabilities for the Central Bank. Journalist Alberto Mora: So that people understand, what do the Reserves have to do with the money supply? Words of Ovidio Reyes It has to do with the fact that we expand money if we have dollars. Journalist Alberto Mora If you allow that? Words by Ovidio Reyes If we have an asset. Journalist Alberto Mora: The machine is not used because then it would be unsupported money. Words by Ovidio Reyes What we have are assets, with assets we support the issuance of the currency; that is the way we do it; It is not that we are expanding money for the sake of expanding, it does not happen that way. I mean, this is not a wonder that we are going to get 100 aorctfcas, and with what? You need the asset; so we have been accumulating important Reserves, more than 5,100 million dollars we have in International Reserves. In 2019, when we had to confront all the imbalances, we reached 2 billion; that is, on the way we were at 3,000 when imbalances occurred, we lost a billion at that time, we had to sell a billion dollars at that time. Well, from that moment to date we are already at 5,100, that is, we have recovered 3,100 million dollars. Journalist Alberto Mora 100% more, approximately. Words of Ovidio Reyes So far this year, more than 500 million dollars have been sold to us and we have bought them, and our purchase is freely made by those who want to sell them. We are not doing or forcing or telling anyone that this should happen; so, since there is a good foreign exchange market, man, we saw that there was no longer any need to continue devaluing the currency. Because the currency is devalued when the opposite is happening. The exchange rate goes up if people want a lot of dollars, when people are looking for dollars then there is pressure in the market for the exchange rate to rise, but if they are looking for cordobas and they are sending us dollars, it no longer makes sense to continue devaluing. It's dacar, you're not going to be at the center of the aartiaite; however, we had already committed our Exchange Policy in 2023 with a devaluation of 1% per year, irreceptibie, until December 31 of this year. So, that commitment that we already had published in the Bank's Vfeb we are going to maintain, because many Agents were also programmed with that slippage; So we maintain the slippage rate of 1% and we would expect that by the end of the year the exchange rate will reach an amount as of December 31, we say we would expect the exchange rate to be 36.6243, with that day-to-day slippage that we are having. As the devaluation rate is 0 in 2024, then 36.6243 will be the exchange rate that will govern for the entire year 2024, as a reference for operations. We use that exchange rate to buy the foreign currency, the dollars that they sell us, that is the exchange rate we use. We use it for the payments of the foreign debt of the Gcbiemo because the Gcbiemo delivers corcdbas, we sell us the dollars, we convert it into dollars and pay the public debt; we are the State Fiscal Agent and then we do that function. And that exchange rate is also used for the value maintenance clause, which is maintained, that has not changed, it is the same clause that is going to be established and now that same exchange rate is going to be used. From now until December 31, the exchange rate table that is published by the Central Bank, and from January I 2024 to December 31, 2024, this exchange rate that I mentioned to you and that I want to repeat again to make it clear will apply: It is 36.6243, that is the exchange rate that will govern for all of 2024. Journalist Alberto Mora He explained why this can be done. Now I would like you to explain a little, what do we gain, what does the State, the National Economy, earn, what does the one who has dollars earn, what does he earn, what does he earn? Words of Ovidio Reyes Exchange rate stability is the greatest of all gains, no one is favored by having an exchange rate that is changing, excuse the redundancy, no one wants it, what they want is a stable and predictable exchange rate, of predictability. If we already know that this is the exchange rate, one can project everything, everything is projected, it is projected calmly. The principle is that when it is moving there is uncertainty, you even know what people's minds are like, what if it is more? That is the mind and they are right, a thing that is unstable, that is moving in price, has its uncertainty. At the time when it began in 1993, that policy was justified and that the devaluation rate was 12%, and it was considered at that time that it was the best option because it was a non-abrupt rate, to suddenly take the exchange rate from one amount to a high amount, but it was something that happened every day as almost imperceptible. The same thing happens with what we did this year, which was, to lower the slide to 1% and it becomes imperceptible, but it is still moving and that generates uncertainty. But well, in this case we are looking for certainty and using other instruments that we have now incorporated in the Central Bank and that we are going to favor the use of those instruments better, than to be using devaluations. For example, we now use and indicate a monetary reference rate that is around 7%; with that interest rate we use it for our banking operations. That is, purchase of financial instruments, deposits of banks in the Central Bank, sale of Securities value- res, Ccnpra-sale of Securities. That is what we call in technical language, Open Market Revenues, but it is nothing more than injection of liquidity and withdrawal of liquidity in the economy, and we use our cano reference rate so that all banks can be oriented to where the economic conditions are going. So, we are going to use the interest rate more than devaluation, it is the modern thing, it is the right thing to do, and we are going to depend more on the market in determining things, as well as on the Exchange Market, which in fact already depends on the froffence. The Currency Exchange is not controlled by the Central Bank, there is what we know as Free Currency Conversion, Free Convertibility, and that is maintained. Journalist Alberto Mora: But people can make their payments according to that rate of the Central Bank, as has always happened, right? Words by Ovidio Reyes Guide cuckold. Journalist Alberto Mora: But can you tell me that, I accept it more expensively. Words by Ovidio Reyes But we leave that to be negotiated between the one who is buying and selling it; it is impossible for us to come and impose an exchange rate by practice. Journalist Alberto Mora If you had to calculate the Canbiaria Tax for your liquidity operations and everything else that has been explained, how do you explain it to people who do not know about Economics? Words by Ovidio Reyes Well, suddenly we need to inject cordcas into the economy because we see that there is not much liquidity; so with our financial instruments that are Securities that we enit, we enter the market, we buy and sell, for what? To maintain the cordobas that people need for their activity. Journalist Alberto Mora For example, when there is a lot of money without backing, they raise the interest rate, they hoard the bill so that people come to leave the rials, and then you have the cordobas. Words by Ovidio Reyes Or we make it cheaper so that they take the money and maintain monetary balance. These are operations that, first, aim to make the exchange market stable, and second, aim to ensure that the economy has liquidity to function. Because if there is more economic activity, more money is required, yes. So, to the extent that economic activity is growing the Agents van Requiring more cordobas, then, we carry out these monetary operations to ensure that there is sufficient liquidity and the economy works. Journalist Alberto Mora To conclude, the economy is moving forward positively and it is very possible that we will approach 3.5; You were talking about 2.5, 3.5. Can this be exceeded, because right now it is going more or less well, it is going for the highest rate that you have proposed. Words by Ovidio Reyes That's right, we would hope that if we reach our goal, and well, and if a better rate can be achieved, then it would be excellent. Journalist Alberto Mora It can happen, right? Words of Ovidio Reyes Of course it can happen, but at this moment our estimate is 3.5. Journalist Alberto Mora Correct, you always try to be a little cautious with projections, but well, you have always been closer than the International Financial Organizations, because they sometimes bet very low, and then it turns out that the numbers are closer to what you have projected. Words by Ovidio Reyes We have had a good accumulation of experience making these estimates and we have been correct with a fair amount of objectivity. Journalist Alberto Mora Hypothetically speaking, what could alter that 0 Rate? Words by Ovidio Reyes I believe that this will give the country and the economy more stability, prices, it will help prices a lot, because it is clear that an already stable exchange rate all imported goods are priced at that price, and therefore it should not be moving, unless it happens that the other wants to make more money; that's something else. But because of the exchange rate there should be stability, and also because of economic strength more stability. In other words, we should expect prices to stabilize, and that in that sense, we all win. Journalist Alberto Mora I thank you for coming, thanks to Companero Ovidio Reyes, President of the Central Bank, I hope that this information will be very useful to those who have heard and seen us this morning. I thank Ovid again.
text_original: 1 Entrevista al Compaero Ovidio Reyes Presidente del Banco Central de Nicaragua con el Periodista Alberto Mora Revista En Vivo, Canal 4 15 de Agosto del 2023 2 Periodista Alberto Mora Bienvenidos, amigos televidentes. Gracias por estar con nosotros esta maana de martes 15 de agosto del ao 2023. Como siempre un placer estar con ustedes a travs de la pantalla de sus televisores. Espera- mos que tengan un buen dia martes. Bien, esta maana tendremos en el estudio al Presi- dente del Banco Central de Nicaragua, Compaero Ovi- dio Reyes. Con l conversaremos sobre diferentes as- pectos que tienen que ver con el comportamiento, con el buen comportamiento de la economa nacional, los indicadores econmicos, las estadsticas, el creci- miento proyectado, el crecimiento que ha venido ocu- rriendo durante estos meses que ya transcurren del ao - ya vamos sobre el octavo mes del ao 2023 - y tambin conversaremos sobre las medidas que ha toma- do el Banco Central. Tasa cero en cuanto al desliza- miento del crdoba en relacin al dlar a partir del 2024, y durante todo el ao. Tambin el tema del truncamiento de los cheques, que tambin nos va a explicar un poco ms. Y todos los temas de inters acerca de la economa nacional, exportaciones y de- ms . Bien, le damos la bienvenida al Presidente del Banco Central, al compaero Ovidio Reyes.
