Title: Interview with Ovidio Reyes, President of the Central Bank, with Journalist Erving Vega TN8 Studio, Channel 8
text: Interview with Ovidio Reyes, President of the Central Bank, with Journalist Erving Vega TN8 Studio, Channel 8 November 15, 2022 Journalist Erving Vega Hello how are you, good morning, welcome, thank you for joining us. We are in TN 8 studio from Monday to Friday from 7:00 to 08:00 in the morning live and in replay from 1:00 to 2:00 in the afternoon. So for those who watch us on the replay, good afternoon and good morning to those who are with us live, on the live broadcast from 7:00 to 8:00 in the morning. Central theme today, we are going to talk about the economy. As we are closing, there are 16 days left to end the year. How we are closing this year 2022 from the point of view of the behavior of our economy and what are the projections for next year 2023 as well. We are going to expand on the subject with the President of the Central Bank, Ovidio Reyes, who is already with us in the study and we thank you. Words by Ovidio Reyes Good morning. Journalist Erving Vega Good morning Ovid. We appreciate that you allow us this interview to make this year-end balance, although there are still no closing figures, but there are 16 days and 16 intense days to go, moreover, from the point of view of economic activity. Words by Ovidio Reyes That's right, even though we don't have the closing information because the year hasn't ended, but there is a lot of information already accumulated up to the month of November that indicates the trend that we have been observing for economic recovery and the maintenance of growth and the recovery of employment. So we are going to have two consecutive years of economic expansion and we believe that next year will also be the case. Journalist Erving Vega Is Nicaragua back on the path of economic growth? Words by Ovidio Reyes Effectively. Journalist Erving Vega With two consecutive years, is this already considered consolidated and with less risk of returning to decline? Words by Ovidio Reyes Not only because of the inherited growth, but because all sectors are showing expansion. So we believe that we are already assured of a continuation of the economic expansion next year as well. Journalist Erving Vega And the behavior so far is going according to projections, or better, or a little. Words by Ovidio Reyes Everything is being fulfilled as we expect. It is excellent news because since the year before last when we saw that the economy was emerging from the economic difficulties generated by the pandemic, we saw that the force that was coming was strong, that is why we forecast a positive 2021 at the time and then a 2022 with a lower growth rate, but consolidated. Let's remember that in 2021 it was more than 10%. This year we would expect it to continue expanding, but already at a moderate rate. Journalist Erving Vega Do we remain at a projection of 3.5% - 4.5%? Words by Ovidio Reyes 3.5% - 4.5%, that's our estimate. Journalist Erving Vega We expand on the topic later with the President of the Central Bank, Ovidio Reyes. Thank you for sticking with us. Central theme today closing How does our economy close? Precisely by evaluating the behavior of our economy at the end of the year. Our Guest the President of the Central Bank, Ovidio Reyes, again Ovidio, thank you for joining us and welcome. The first question we started with and by way of introduction, well, is the behavior of our economy in line with what has been projected since the beginning of the year in the country? Words by Ovidio Reyes That's right. Journalist Erving Vega 3.5%, 4.5% Words by Ovidio Reyes That's right, that's the rate we're expecting to close for 2022, between 3.5. and 4.5% growth; The series that we monitor monthly, indicate that global activity is expanding, and this year it is led by Hotels and Restaurants, Commerce, Transportation and Communications, Manufacturing Industries. It is interesting how Hotels and Restaurants was the one that suffered the most in the pandemic and is now the one that is ahead in growth rate, 21.9% as of September, and if it is Commerce 8.2% and Transportation and Communications 7%. Statistics also show a recovery in the arrival of tourists, which has not yet reached pre-pandemic levels, but there is already an interesting movement in these sectors. And the other thing is that all sectors: Fishing, Financial Intermediation, Mines and Quarries, Energy, Agriculture and other Public Administration Services, have all been growing, and that gives us a certain guarantee that December is going to behave in a similar way. Journalist Erving Vega Now, how good is 3.5%, 4.5% growth? Words by Ovidio Reyes Well, when we compare it with the rest of the world, it's good growth, because the rest of the world is struggling for reasons of its own, and growth is going to be around 3%. So if we end this year at the average of our estimate, which is 4%, then we will be 1 point above what is happening in the rest of the world. Journalist Erving Vega Is that the global projection? Words by Ovidio Reyes That's right, that's the global projection. Journalist Erving Vega And at the regional level, Latin America and even smaller? Words by Ovidio Reyes We are at 4%. Central America has always had an outstanding economic movement relative to the rest of Latin America, perhaps it is the Region that has best taken advantage of the Free Trade Agreements and the one that best took advantage of the moment of Globalization, and was able to insert itself in international markets; so that is allowing the entire Region to have a good economic performance. In the Economic Indicators of the Secretariat of the Central American Monetary Council, of which Nicaragua is a member, it can be seen how all the countries of the Region are synchronously recovering; We suffered from the pandemic and now we are recovering. And the same happens with many of the economic variables as a sign of the interrelation and commercial integration that exists in these countries. Journalist Erving Vega 3.5, 4.5, is then the economy's performance maintained in the direction of what was projected. Words by Ovidio Reyes Effectively. Journalist Erving Vega The issue of inflation? Words by Ovidio Reyes Well, inflation is the variable that has been affecting the entire world and that has Industrial Countries concerned in the first place, because the origin has the pandemic as its origin, which motivated monetary expansion and the expansion of public spending. Nicaragua did not do that, Nicaragua remained with fiscal balances and monetary balances; As a result of this great monetary expansion and the high public deficits, a demand was created, which was more than correct to create, otherwise the recession Had been more acute. But the greater demand also generated inflation and that is what we are observing; inflation that was exacerbated by the confinements because it paralyzed trade, and in addition to that, bankrupted certain suppliers or large suppliers that later had a hard time relocating their products. So as a consequence the costs increased a lot, the cost of all the goods, of the inputs, of the Consumer Goods, Home Appliances, Vehicles worldwide, and the price of oil increased disproportionately at the time. The good thing for our Eais, or healthy exporters of Primary Goods, is that the prices of Coffee, Livestock, Gold, Meat, Peanuts, and Sugar also rose, and that also helped the country to compensate with greater exports. Now a phenomenon is happening a little in reverse, after prices rose a lot, what is observed now is that at the international level they are already going down. They are still high before the pandemic; In other words, they are still attractive prices for our exporters, but they are already moderating. Coffee has dropped in price; Gold fell but in recent weeks it rose again, and the price of world food has also been contained. So, this year we are going to see the effect of the rise in international prices, and we would expect inflation to be between 10 and 11% as a result of those international prices. But since the entire price chain has already been contained and is moderating its growth, we would expect that next year these prices in Nicaragua will also moderate and be contained, and we would be projecting inflation for 2023 that could be between 5 and 6%; The world also expects price moderation. On the production side, we believe that even though there are no positive things in the world, they believe, for example, that global growth will be more timid, and Industrial Economies will grow around 1% in 2023; then we would also make a kind of comparison and we would be growing between 3 and 4% in our estimate. I would think that if the world does indeed slow down, that would also be a much better rate than the rest, and that it leaves us in a position to continue with the economic expansion that we have been observing. But now, the Producers, the Export Sector must try to have more gains in production volume to compensate for the moderation of prices. We see, however, that economic growth continues and that we will reach a third year of growth by 2023. Journalist Erving Vega Between 3% and 4%, 4.5%, would be good in terms, well, we have come from 3 years, 2018, 2019, 2020 with decrease, we are back on the path of growth. But what expectation can we generate with 3%, 4%, 4.5% growth for the Nicaragua's great objective, to continue advancing in the fight against poverty. Words by Ovidio Reyes Tccb positive growth translates into poverty reduction and if growth is greater than population growth, it will undoubtedly follow. There has not been a study of Poverty for a few years, but from the Social Indicators that we observe, the improvement in telephone coverage, the improvement of roofs in homes, the laying of bricks in houses, the acquisition of motor vehicles, both cars and motorcycles, and other indicators that measure the ability of people to improve their standard of living, we are observing that the standard of living is indeed improving, little by little as it happens, they are not great leaps, and we would hope that this rate also contributes to the reduction of poverty. Employment is the other key variable, employment in recent months has been recovering, the Informal Sector is shrinking and formality is improving. Social Security is already reaching the figure of 800,000 Insured Persons, and that is excellent news, because it indicates that the Economy is indeed supporting the creation of employment, that this was an issue that we have been addressing at the time, since the pandemic left new work habits, and it could have affected at the time when the search for jobs occurred. and indeed it did. And that is why indicators such as the labor participation rate were reduced, but with the new dynamic, we are returning to hiring jobs, and we believe that this will continue and will place the unemployment rate around 3% for next year, as will also happen during the present. Journalist Erving Vega How has the international scenario been, favorable, unfavorable this year for the economy, and how do you project yourself for next year? Words by Ovidio Reyes As the goods of the products that we export remained very high, the scenario was favorable; It was not so favorable in terms of expectations because there was a lot of noise about trade problems, geopolitical problems, and especially about the policies of interest rate hikes that tightened financial conditions. This also motivated us, the Central Bank, to continue adjusting interest rates in response to interest rate hikes worldwide. Yesterday there was also another movement in the interest rate, and most likely we will too, we cannot be far from that reality. But despite this complicated scenario that was glimpsed during this year, our products found an outlet, the Regional Market demanded more Nicaraguan food products. I could say without a doubt that we are repositioning ourselves as a regional food supplier with a lot of capacity to carry grains and products such as meat and sugar cane and other goods, which in the current conditions we have seen is a great strength, since not all countries have that capacity to produce their own food. Nicaragua has managed to generate a lot of capacity, and the most important thing is that it continues to expand. So even though that scenario was a bit complicated, the country did respond positively because our goods had good prices and found an outlet. That is why we insisted, when this improvement in international prices began, that it was going to be an opportunity to capitalize on the Primary Sector, and to be able to generate technological improvements and improvements in production methods, so that productivity increases are the ones that determine Nicaragua's production going forward. And I believe that the country is achieving it in that. Journalist Erving Vega For next year the scenario looks good, or does it represent a certain threat to the country? Words by Ovidio Reyes It seems that for next year economic activity is going to be lower than this year that is ending, at least that is what the International Financial Organizations say, that we follow them. But again, not even in the pandemic when there was a breakdown in international trade did our exports stop growing, and there was a global recession, and yet our exports advanced. Because it is a reality, the need for food will always exist and Nicaragua that is its specialty, to produce food, and the Free Trade Zone to produce Industrial Goods, but Nicaraguans, what they have the capacity is to produce food. So we believe that we are going to be well positioned and that we are going to move forward, we do not see in this international scenario something that is going to limit us. Because again, even though prices have fallen in recent months, for international goods, they are still higher than in the pandemic. So there is an incentive to produce. Journalist Erving Vega From the point of view of the scaffolding, the supports of our internal economy, how are we doing in that sense? Words by Ovidio Reyes Well, what is happening in the Financial Sector is good news, the expansion of credit that we have been observing. The pandemic had the disadvantage that it generated a lot of uncertainty, and banks showed a lot of caution in the delivery of loans. But now that uncertainty has diminished considerably, there has been excellent news that has once again mobilized enthusiasm in the Financial Sector, such as the latest evaluation by the Monetary Fund, the improvement of the international rating for Nicaragua by Standard & Poor's; the removal of Nicaragua from the Grey List, from the OXEE, and all these oosas mobilize expectations and financing, and that has also caused credit to be reactivated. We expect that the expansion that we are observing in credit will continue stronger during 2023, and that it will also be a factor that contributes internally to guarantee the growth expectation we have. The other thing that we have been observing is that national foreign investment is taking a good position, and therefore is reinvesting a lot of profit, and is also expanding plants. That is another foundation that we believe will give dynamism as well as the recovery that we are expecting in the Tourism Sector, it will also add new momentum. So, we see that in general there is not a single sector that shows us weakness; on the contrary, the entire economy has been strengthened and is developing with full normality. Journalist Erving Vega Let's say the variables that determine the health, the solidity or not of an economy, how it is; We are talking about reservations, for example, how are they, what does it reflect on us? Words by Ovidio Reyes Well, deposits have been growing positively, it is a structural issue that Nicaraguans have already taken a liking to saving; In other words, that is very good, because our own financing is even healthier than international financing. Journalist Erving Vega Are savings growing? Words by Ovidio Reyes Yes, savings are growing, but it is interesting that savings did not stop growing during the pandemic, rather it was consolidated, and now it is expanding, it has not stopped doing so; And as I said, it is healthier even than international financing, loans and everything else, because it is from its own source. So the national savings base continues to expand, it is an excellent indicator even of confidence of depositors and of all the Companies and Institutions that put their money and resources in the Financial System. The other important indicator is the expansion of the monetary base, the monetary base continues to grow and when it grows, it grows because the Financial Sector either sells dollars to the Central Bank, or the Public Sector also increases its deposits, and that means that there is more capacity or more demand for money; When there is demand for money, then the indicator expands. There is a continuity that is basically determined by demand, and as a result of this greater monetary requirement and the greater savings in consolidated International Reserves around this month, yesterday were at 4,260 million dollars. The Central Bank buying dollars in the economy, it is a very interesting phenomenon, because about 3 years ago the Central Bank always sold dollars to the economy, but for almost two and a half years, the Central Bank does not buy a single dollar in the economy, it does not place a single dollar in the economy. We do not sell a single dollar, on the contrary, we have only bought dollars, that is why we are accumulating many Reserves; that is, we have a good supply of foreign currency that no longer requires the Central Bank to intervene. That is very positive, that is an excellent sign that there are conditions for even greater exchange rate stability. So we see that the foreign exchange market is in balance and well funded, with resources from exports, foreign investment, remittances, tourism, which keep commercial activity lubricated. And on the other hand, we see a stable fiscal balance, Public Finances with great collection, more than 2 digits in collection; Rates that reached 30% of collection, are now moderating by around 20%. And that, as savings are healthy for the Financial System, the collection is also healthy for public finances because it is not indebtedness, they are Nicaraguans' own resources that are relocated and that also show signs of strengthening the movement of economic activity. So we see public finances with stable public debt and a controlled deficit between 2 and 3%, which in any country in the world is enviable. These two conditions, monetary balance and exchange rate with consolidating international reserves, and a public deficit with controlled public debt, even reducing as a percentage of GDP, and strong revenue, give us elements to think that economic activity is on good financial foundations, and therefore will continue to expand during 2023. Journalist Erving Vega I have a second pause, we are going to return with the conclusions of Ovidio Reyes, President of the Central Bank, we are back. We are talking this morning with the president of the Central Bank, Ovidio Reyes. Scbre the state of the Economy, the behavior of the Economy at the end of this year 2022, there are still 16 days left in December, 16 intense days from the point of view of Trade mainly. Trade and Tourism, right? But well, the data that Ovidio has shared with us is that we are closing in line with what was projected between 3.5% and 4.5% growth. We are back to the growth path of 2021 with 10.3% and this year with 3.5, 4.5%, and the projection for next year of 3%. Words by Ovidio Reyes Between 3 and 4%. Journalist Erving Vega This is good considering that we are growing more than most of the rest of the world. How solid is it to keep us on that growth path for the coming years? Words by Ovidio Reyes When commercial activity and productive activity already find their way it is very difficult to stop it, this is like when you want to move a large object with wheels, it is very difficult to push it, but once you push it to stop it is a little difficult. The same thing happens with the Economy, it took time to push it, it was difficult; together we pushed the economy and now it has taken flight. Then there is not going to be a deterioration overnight, in addition, there is no such element of risk so pronounced that it indicates it. The risks that we have been seeing at the macro-economic level are of a financial nature, for example, the latest interest rate hike could at the time, and if they become very pronounced, affect global economic activity. But in Nicaragua it does not represent a serious threat, we raised the interest rate in Nicaragua, to also prevent capital flight. Because if the whole world is raising the interest rate and we don't, money can go abroad. Journalist Erving Vega But it also has a negative impact on credit, doesn't it? Words by Ovidio Reyes Well. So far it hasn't been so strong, it's small and I understand the banking position, because after coming from a crisis in which you lost a lot of customers and you start to affect the interest rate a lot, you can lose customers again, and nobody wants that. So there is a lot of prudence in the Banks, not to transfer international costs to credit, but the last word has not been said; However, there is a global effort to contain inflation, yes, and movements in interest rates moderate monetary expansion. Journalist Erving Vega The inflation that you probably look at is perhaps the only note there in the negative, right? Because going to double digits means a blow, I would say a significant blow to the domestic economy. Words by Ovidio Reyes Price adjustments are always not welcome, but let's also remember that production needs prices, when one sees it from the producer's side, better prices encourage more production; If you see it from the consumer's side, it is negative, it affects your pocket. In fact, there is lime and sand in what is happening, just as exporters were incentivized, consumers resent the rise in prices a little. But, nevertheless, what we see is that they are moderating, that international prices have stopped growing, they are stabilizing, and we would see a decrease in that growth next year. Perhaps, I think, in this year that happens more than the consumer, I think that here the one who was most affected by the rise in prices is construction materials, the rise is very strong, and it is that many materials are also imported, electric switches, electricity things, goods to produce materials are also imported, luminaires, etc. And construction is also suffering from the increases, and it can be seen in the statistics that the Construction sector is being a little more prudent. We believe that this stops Projects; for example, if the price of construction material rises a lot and a Project was expecting a certain profitability, the rise in prices is no longer the same profitability. What has happened a bit is that, postponement of projects waiting for better conditions, but after that sector that is particularly affected by the rise in prices, we see that the rest of the sectors are growing. For example, it is true, prices are rising, but trade is growing in real terms by 8%, in nominal terms the growth is almost 18%, that is, the rest is prices. So, even so there is trade, even so there is movement of Infrastructure, of Transportation, and we believe that in that sense the price increases, although it is true that they have affected the pocketbook, but they have not paralyzed economic activity, that is, it continues. Because there is this other factor, there are good prices, we have to earn more on the side of the Producers. So, leaving aside the issue of prices but seeing that they have not been an impediment to productive expansion, we see that the rest of the activities are going to continue as we are observing here in the Monthly Index of Economic Activity, they will continue to expand and they will continue to generate employment. Journalist Erving Vega To close, by way of your conclusions, we are once again on the path of growth, there are economic policies, there is social behavior that is decisive. What would be the recommendations we should make, so that effectively once we push the cart, not only does it not stop but we can make it go faster? Words by Ovidio Reyes I believe that there is an important element in all this, the Economists, and many call it expectations, and depending on how one forms the expectation of the future, the cart continues. And the truth is that, for what has happened this year, positive expectations have been created; that is, people got to work, the sector moved, all sectors moved, and when there is activity that expectation is created, and the expectation leads you to make consumption and investment decisions. So this element of generating economic policies that pay off good expectations, I think it is an important element that has been done. We have been promoting this from our sphere, the Government Institutions from their branch from the National Sisters of Production, Consumption and Commerce have been generating training, training, programs to generate this productive environment, this work environment that all Nicaraguans need to continue moving forward and achieve the main objective, which is the reduction of poverty. Journalist Erving Vega Thank you very much for joining us. Ovidio Reyes, President of the Central Bank.

Vamos a ampliar el tema con el Presidente del Banco Central, Ovidio Reyes, quien ya nos acompaa en el es- tudio y agradecemos. Palabras de Ovidio Reyes Buenos das. Periodista Erving Vega Buenos das Ovidio. Agradecemos que nos permitas esta entrevista para hacer este balance de cierre de ao, aunque no hay todava cifras de cierre, pero faltan 16 das y 16 das intensos, adems, desde el punto de vis- ta de la actividad econmica. Palabras de Ovidio Reyes As es, aun cuando no tenemos la informacin de cierre porque no ha terminado el ao, pero s hay mucha infor- macin ya acumulada hasta el mes de noviembre que nos 3 indica la tendencia que hablamos venido observando a la recuperacin econmica y al mantenimiento del creci- miento y de la recuperacin del empleo.
