Title: President of the BCN presents results of the meeting of the National System of Production, Consumption and Trade
text: TRANSCRIPTION TRANSCRIPTION Issuing confidence and stability Issuing confidence and stability Press Conference President of the BCN presents the results of the meeting of the National System of Production, Consumption and Trade March 17, 2023 President of the BCN: Good morning. Today, the ordinary meeting of the National System of Production, Consumption and Trade was held with all the institutions that participate in this important working mechanism to evaluate the progress of national production, and also to design actions and policies to ensure that there is sufficient capacity of our economy to produce food and products for export. which is the sector served by the system. Particularly, at this meeting we saw how the progress of agricultural statistics, fisheries and forestry statistics was with respect to the goals that had originally been proposed. We also reviewed compliance and progress on the precious grains strategy; in this case they are coffee and cocoa. And about how the training that is produced by the National Technological Institute (INATEC) and the technical field schools to raise the capacities of our workers and agricultural producers is going. What did we review in this working session? Well, we saw that the agricultural sector in the cycle, the cycle remember that it begins in May and ends in April, the agricultural cycle, coinciding with the rains that start in May, is not a calendar year, but it is a year that overlaps between one year and the other. So, we already have a production progress report that began in May 2022 and ends in February 2023. So what are we observing? We observe that the agricultural sector, fundamentally, the agro-export sector, continues to grow in production by 5.2%, the agro-export sector. We still do not have all the statistics of the completion of the coffee harvest, there is a degree of progress, but in due course they will be announced, last year there were 3.7 million quintals, this year we were expecting a similar amount. TRANSCRIPTION TRANSCRIPTION Issuing confidence and stability Issuing confidence and stability Regarding musaceae, the generation of products such as bananas has been relevant; it grows 9.8%. For example, bananas in units of 940 million units that were produced in the 2021 cycle, at this point it is already over one million 32 thousand units. In other words, we have an activity there that is picking up and that is also emerging as a good sector of dynamism for all farmers. A bit of a reduction in bananas for export, but international market conditions have had an effect. Then we have that in the roots and tubers sector, production grows by 2.8%, mainly due to cassava production, which grew from 5.8 million quintals to 6 million quintals, a little less taro, which fell by 13%, but cassava production is the one that has been dominating the dynamics of this sector. which is also composed of the quequisque and in the end grows by 2.8%. In basic grains, which is the main activity, because this is the one that guarantees us food security, we have very positive statistics. For example, we have that beans grew, went from 4.7 million quintals to 4.8 million quintals, this exceeds national consumption and that is a good reason for a positive signal for all producers, in the sense that the surplus is exported and therefore generates income for production. And then we have white sorghum growing by 29% from 517 thousand to 668 thousand quintals. Rice, both rainfed and irrigated, also expanded. Rainfed rice grew by 2.7, from 753 thousand quintals to 773 thousand quintals. For its part, irrigated rice went from 5.2 million quintals to 5.3 million quintals for a growth of 2.5%. So, if we look at the statistics: there is more rice, there are more beans, there are more grains, there is more sorghum. There are more grains in Nicaragua! I want to emphasize that this is a dynamic that we have been observing, a constant throughout this period, Nicaragua has been emerging as a food-producing nation and, in fact, in difficult situations, countries come to our country to buy it, because we have that high national capacity to produce it, it has to do with the very idiosyncrasy of the Nicaraguan. that there is no small plantation in the countryside that does not explode to its maximum capacity, with small trees, with everything. And well, and with business too. Even in TRANSCRIPTION TRANSCRIPTION Issuing confidence and stability Issuing confidence and stability Well, the result of the policies that have been implemented of the effective coordination of the National Production System is that basic grains continue to expand, they grow by 2.3%, let's remember that the population is already growing a little more than 1%, in other words, we are growing more (in food) than the growth of the population and that is positive. And a good part of this, as I mentioned in the case of beans, is also destined for export. Then, the fishing sector has been outstanding in terms of its performance. The production of scales, which is the production of fish, is basically growing by 39.7%, that is, it went from 22.1 million pounds to 30.9 million pounds. Trawl shrimp has also performed well, growing by 77.4%. It went from 3 million to 5.4 million, that's a significant increase. Farmed shrimp grew 1.5% from 68.2 to 69.3 million pounds and sea cucumber went from 12.2 to 14.2 million pounds for a growth of 16.1%. The growth of the capture and export of tuna from 37 million to 42.4 million pounds, a growth of 14.7%, was also positive, and in other seafood products, the same, they went from 44 thousand pounds to 125 thousand to 784 thousand pounds. As a result of all this, fishing grew 8.7%. There were also some products that presented reductions, but they were more than offset by these products that are showing excellent dynamics and a good use of international prices. Then, with respect to the fulfillment of export goals, we have already mentioned on different occasions, and also the institutions or representatives of the institutions that are in charge, have explained that the volume of exports is also growing. In this case, the total value of 2,955 million dollars, 10.7% higher than the previous year, which was 2,670 million dollars. And it is noteworthy that exportable agricultural production grew by 21.5%, that is, we went from 1,397 million last year to 1,698 million dollars. This is what I told you, or we said, that Nicaragua is gradually becoming a great food producer, with respect to the rest of the countries in our region. Of course, we are not comparing ourselves with other countries, but with countries (in the region), ours has an excellent dynamic in food production, which was a fundamental problem when the pandemic occurred: Where to get food? Well, Nicaragua didn't have that TRANSCRIPTION TRANSCRIPTION Issuing confidence and stability Issuing confidence and stability It is important that export prices grew a lot in 2022, in 2023 it has moderated growth. However, in the case of agricultural products, they have been growing by 1.2%. In fishery products they grew 25% and in forest products they grew by 13.9%. Although livestock products did drop in price by 10.3%, and that to some extent also had some impact on what corresponds to the production and generation of meat, in the case of livestock. For example, we have that, in the case of the livestock sector, the cattle slaughter had a reduction of 12.5%, it went from 910 thousand head to 796 thousand head, and it has to do with both external prices, and the fact that in 2021 the significant increase that there was was taken advantage of, and there was a lot of extraction. So, it is also an issue that has to do with the cycles that occur in livestock production, when there is a lot of extraction, well, there is a period of adjustment and then when the cattle are fattened again and there are more cattle (inventory) to export, inventories increase and expansion continues. But the country is producing more pork, pigs, from 282 thousand head we went to 300 thousand head, and after poultry slaughter we went from 62.5 million slaughtered birds to 67.3 million slaughtered birds, that is, a growth of 7.6%. And here there is an almost substitution effect, as there was an improvement in international meat prices that were transferred domestically, so there is a greater consumption, by substitution, of poultry and pigs and also, consequently, an increase in their production. In other words, this substitution has also allowed the family to guarantee access to this type of product. The collection of milk, as a result of the lower activity in that sector, was also slightly reduced, but not so that of raw milk, which remained at 389 million gallons, grew slightly and is now 391 million gallons. That is, milk and meat in the aggregate, incorporating pork and poultry, are maintained. On the other hand, we observe that egg production has increased by 7% from 20.8 million boxes already in 2022 and so far in 2023: 22.3 million boxes. So, there is also a positive effect of the dynamics that we are observing in trade at the aggregate level, because when there is more production, there is also a greater dynamism of consumption activities. TRANSCRIPTION TRANSCRIPTION Issuing confidence and stability Issuing confidence and stability And on the other hand, in education in the countryside, well, the progress of all activities that have a lot to do with the results of productive activity was also evaluated, because a more skilled, more trained, better trained population, better trained workers, also lead to an increase and a good practice of production in general. In summary, this is what we wanted to report on this occasion and greet our population, and guarantee that in our country enough food is being produced for the national supply and even the international supply of the (countries that) demand our products. Thanks a lot

Title: President of the BCN, Ovidio Reyes R.  Exhibition "Challenges of Agricultural Higher Education in the Fight against Poverty"
text: fiaenfadde Issuing confidence and stability WORDS OF THE AUTHORITIES Monday, May 22, 2023 President of the BCN, Ovidio Reyes R. Exhibition "Challenges of Agricultural Higher Education in the Fight against Poverty" Good afternoon. I would like to thank you for the invitation to participate in this great event and to greet the Rector of the National Agrarian University, Master Engineer Alberto Sediles Jaen, as well as the rest of the authorities, teachers, researchers and students of this prestigious University. Thank you all very much for your presence. The training of professionals in the field of agriculture, livestock, forestry and other professions that accompany it is of great interest to our nation. The work in national universities is to address these fields with an academic sense, but above all practical, as it corresponds to engineering, since its application is directly linked to production, management, marketing and research in crops, which includes by extension the rational use of forests, land, water and materials for agricultural production. Generating technologies that incorporate our way of doing things helps reduce technological and economic dependence, which benefits all farmers and even consumers. Addressing these issues with scientific rigor is a key task of the National Agrarian University, to provide solutions to the great agricultural challenges that our country presents. I am not going to delve into these concepts that are well mastered by you, I am going to refer rather to the agricultural policies that you illustrate in your work in order to train professionals who contribute to the great objective of achieving greater production that generates jobs and income that contribute to the reduction of poverty. Agricultural Policies. The agricultural sector has been making significant progress over the last fifteen years. Progress has been observed in crop yields, in the increase of national production, new technologies have been incorporated in the field, new production methods have been adopted, national consumption and agricultural exports have grown, to mention the most remarkable facts. The details of these advances are incorporated in a recent presentation of the National Plan for Production, Consumption and Trade 2023, where the details for each activity and items are presented, and which I invite you to consult. The main agricultural policies that are being implemented and are outlined for the immediate future in the Plan are the following:  Food security and sovereignty, in order to achieve greater production that ensures food in domestic and export markets;  Productivity and competitiveness, which increases the performance of the main items and guarantees a nutritious and healthy diet;  Education and training for production, to promote the development of the human talent of producer families, through training, training and knowledge transfer;  Research, innovation and productive technologies, to generate new technologies and agricultural practices that contribute to genetic improvement, sustainable management of crops and animals, which facilitate their adaptation to climatic variety;  Protection and conservation of Mother Earth, for the strengthening of the national system of protected areas and the establishment of biological corridors; or Forestry, which seeks to promote the conservation and sustainable use of forests;  Commercial, to promote the development of the productive sectors and national and foreign supply;  Financing and investments, promoting socio-productive investment projects to increase the national production of goods and services;  Agro-industrialization, to strengthen the integration of value chains with agricultural production; and  Security in the field, in order to strengthen the surveillance system in the productive areas. This set of policies constitutes the guidelines on which all agricultural action revolves. The actions have made it possible to reach thousands of producers and companies, who have benefited from the different services, training and information provided by the public institutions that participate in this contest. Agricultural Development. The development of the agricultural sector has been achieved with firm steps, with some sectors advancing more than others, but in the end all generating more value and, with it, improving the income and standard of living of families in the countryside. Together, the agricultural, livestock and forestry sectors represent 1 6.5% of national production, measured through the gross domestic product. What is relevant is that, from this participation, a stream of subsequent activities in agribusiness, marketing, transportation, financial services and exports is derived that energize the economic flow to meet the consumption needs of the population and external demanders. It is an outstanding fact that Nicaragua has made great leaps in food production. In aggregate, the country produces more food than it consumes domestically, which is reflected in the fact that food exports exceed food imports twice as much. This presents us as a net food producing country, a fact that is growing over time. Many of the goods that were previously produced exclusively for domestic consumption are now traded internationally. Examples of these goods are those derived from milk and red beans, among many others. This new reality, which is added to the traditional production of goods for agro-export, induces our producers, financiers and marketers to have a more far-reaching vision and to monitor both national and international markets, as well as their prices. It also promotes the absorption of new technologies of greater productivity and quality, to increase competitiveness that ensures the success of its goods. The order of magnitude of our exports is also relevant. Agricultural exports drive the rest of total exports by representing 35% of the total exported in the country, while the country's total exported represents 49% of the Gross Domestic Product. Never before in its history has Nicaragua had so much significance in terms of external trade dynamics, which motivates us to ensure that we have already founded a continuous process of export capacity. It is well known that an export process that begins is very difficult to reverse, due to the virtuous dynamics that occur in investment, production, marketing and consumption. The improvement in the quality of goods occurs with the emergence of a country brand that is gaining more and more reputation, thus increasing the demand for the rest of the goods in the economy. It is to be expected, then, that in the future Nicaragua will deepen its export model and consolidate itself as an economy that is increasingly inserted in international markets. Another structural characteristic of the agricultural sector is that it has proven to be resilient in the face of all kinds of shocks. Climate change is its greatest challenge, because climate changes affect crops, varieties and even inputs. The volatile international environment and domestic problems may affect agricultural production. However, even though the above seems to have its foundations, the truth is that the agricultural sector has been able to resist all kinds of disturbances. It has stood firm and has not presented significant setbacks. On the contrary, in the face of adversity, the agricultural sector has not stopped growing and generating wealth. In this sense, the agricultural sector has become an economic pillar of our country of great resilience. Because of this demonstrated particularity, Nicaragua must continue to bet on the development of its agriculture, livestock and forestry, focusing its policies and actions to deepen its growth. Poverty Reduction. The development literature has amply explained the reasons why the rural sector, although it is a dynamic sector that employs a large population, presents disadvantages in terms of exchange with respect to other sectors. Farmworkers receive lower wages than city workers. Something similar happens with rents. This leads to poverty in the countryside being higher than in the city. In Nicaragua, surveys measuring living standards show positive results in terms of reducing poverty in general and extreme poverty. However, when looking at the sectors, overall poverty, even though it has been reduced, is three times higher in the rural sector than in the urban area. The same happens with employment and other socioeconomic indicators that show that the standard of living in the countryside is lower than in the city. One way to attack this structural problem is to increase the capacities of rural workers to improve their productivity and thus improve their income. Hence, the set of public policies includes a lot of technical and professional training for the countryside. It also includes the use of information technology and field visits that facilitate the improvement of knowledge. The provision of information in the field is key. The massive dissemination of knowledge, prices, production volumes, marketing, demands for goods and climatic conditions supports and facilitates markets and the correct decisions of employees and employers. Investment in infrastructure, development of agricultural projects, and access to financing are conditions to facilitate production and generate greater added value. This will lead to improved wages, increased consumption and satisfaction of families in the countryside that will continue to support poverty reduction. This development approach to reduce poverty requires a lot of professional, technical and research training, hence the academic training at the National Agrarian University will be essential to deliver the professionals and technicians who will be in charge of these production, marketing and distribution chains both in the countryside and in the city. Conclusion Nicaragua has an agricultural potential that is being exploited by all its protagonists, which has improved the standard of living and promoted the country's growth and development. Agriculture, livestock and forestry are a resilient pillar of our economy and as such must continue to be promoted by the State, to continue advancing in achieving total food security in all areas and promote exports. The National Agrarian University has a great responsibility in training future professionals who will meet the main challenges in the field, but mainly to increase production through the incorporation of agricultural technologies and solutions. We are convinced that with the help of all Nicaraguans we will be able to achieve the expected results in the plans and policies implemented, because we have already been making successful progress in the production of food for national consumption and exports, which will ensure that we continue to increase income and further reduce poverty. Thank you all very much for your attention.

Title: Award Ceremony "Economy, Finance and Development Award Contest 2023" Remarks by the President of the Central Bank of Nicaragua, Ovidio Reyes
text: fiaenfadde Issuing confidence and stability WORDS OF THE AUTHORITIES Thursday, November 23, 2023 Award Ceremony "Economics, Finance and Development Award Contest 2023" Remarks by the President of the Central Bank of Nicaragua, Ovidio Reyes Good morning. I would like to extend a warm welcome to the award ceremony of the "Economy, Finance and Development Award 2023", held by the Central Bank of Nicaragua. For the Central Bank of Nicaragua, it is very gratifying to have the presence today of researchers, special guests, students of the Economics and Business Engineering career of the National University of Engineering, officials of the Central Bank and the media. The Central Bank carries out various activities year after year to promote economic research, recognizing the importance of empirical studies that support a better understanding of the economy that allow the development of policies, mainly of a monetary, exchange and financial nature. This is an ongoing process, not only because of the diversity of issues that affect the economic well-being of Nicaraguan society, but also because of the changing environment facing our economy. One of the most outstanding activities of our institution, in this effort to contribute to knowledge, is the Economy, Finance and Development Award. Through this contest, the Central Bank of Nicaragua summons students, teachers and professionals in general, to contribute to economic research for decision-making and, in this way, contribute to the development of our country. This year, in response to the call of the Central Bank of Nicaragua, eight research projects were submitted to the contest, of which seven were carried out by national researchers, and one by a foreigner. The proposed research dealt with the monetary, financial, exchange, productivity, food security, infrastructure and public policy fields. We thank all the researchers for attending our call and for the contributions made. For the 2023 Economy, Finance and Development Award, the qualifying jury decided to award two prizes and a special mention. The criteria used for the selection of the papers included the strength of the methodological approach used in the research, the contribution to empirical research and the relevance of the results in terms of the application of economic policies, among others. Thus, two prizes and a special mention were selected, corresponding to the following:  The first place prize was awarded to the study "Optimal Size of Government: The Case of Nicaragua" by the authors Matilde Guadalupe Cerda Ruiz and Axel Ornar Canales Garcia, both economists, and who are here, I ask you to stand up, please, we give a round of applause to the winners. Thanks a lot.  The second place was awarded to the work "Macroeconomic Fundamentals of the BCN Exchange Table", by the author William Alberto Mendieta Alvarado, economist, I also ask William to please stand up. Thanks a lot. The special mention went to the study "Vulnerabilities of the Nicaraguan microfinance sector", which corresponds to the authors David Ernesto Miranda Largaespada, Jaimie Vivian Gonzalez Jarquin and Jennyfer Beatriz Flores Cerrato, all of them economists, can you stand up, please also so that we give them recognition. Thanks a lot. I congratulate the winners for their effort and dedication, and for their contribution to research. In closing, I would like to thank all those present for their participation in this event. The Central Bank of Nicaragua will continue with its commitment to promote research, especially those studies that contribute to the design and analysis of economic policies aimed at promoting growth and sustainable and inclusive economic development in our country. Thanks a lot

text: TRANSCRIPTION TRANSCRIPTION Issuing confidence and stability Issuing confidence and stability Presentation of the President of the BCN, Ovidio Reyes R., at a meeting of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs with Non-Governmental Organizations January 18, 2023 Good morning. It should be noted that in our country last year a second year of economic growth ended after the pandemic, and that we are heading for a third year of continuity of that economic growth. There are elements of recovery that come with any shock. Just like when you get sick, after you get sick, you recover and then you see an improvement. The question is whether he is going to get sick again and if he is going to go back again. And what we have seen from our economy is that we have recovered, and there is no way that we will get "sick" again, and that we have all the conditions to continue growing. That is important because there is always a doubt about whether after recovery we will have the ability to continue. But the truth is that Nicaragua has very solid foundations, an important strength in the export sector, which has been the spearhead of the recovery, the funding of the economy, and the incorporation of best practices, good production technologies and radiates to the rest of the economy. The Minister of Finance and Public Credit (MHCP) has already highlighted that there are more than 7 billion dollars (in exports) and I believe that the numbers are already closing for about 8 billion dollars in exports, 4 billion from the free zones and another 4 billion from exports of goods and services from our country. These are huge numbers. If we think that in 1991 the country barely exported about 300; 400 million dollars, then, the leap is very important, it is big, it is enormous. We have become a country with an export and open economy. Wide open! Our GDP is around 14 billion dollars. So, 8 billion in TRANSCRIPTION TRANSCRIPTION Issuing confidence and stability Issuing confidence and stability  not only exports, but also foreign investment, which will be about 1,500 million dollars. In other words, we are talking about exports and investment alone, the country is funding itself with 9,500 million dollars. These are large numbers. And if we see tourism that is going to end with about 500 million dollars, then we are already talking about 10 billion dollars in those product groups alone.  if, as the Minister (MHCP) mentioned, we add the remittances that are 3 billion dollars, we are talking about 13 billion dollars of income for our country against a GDP of 14 billion dollars. We are talking about the fact that the funding of our economy is the size of our economy. And if we add imports, which are 10 billion dollars, then we are talking about the country being eminently commercial. It went from being a timidly closed economy to being a broadly open economy. And the success story in the world is that countries that manage to reach this state are not stopped by anything, that is, they only continue because the country is not seeing itself. The problem is no longer what we are going to eat, but the problem is what we are going to supply the world. And that has radically changed Nicaragua, which in the countryside is thinking about what it produces abroad, in addition to what it produces inside. That has pros and cons, but there are more pros than cons. It has the downside, that prices are balanced at the global level and then export products become more expensive domestically, but it generates foreign currency and the generation of foreign currency generates income and by generating income it generates other flows of goods and services that compensate. So, this productive base that we have today is a sufficient condition to ensure the continuity of growth. So 2023 is also going to be a good year, that's for sure. We have been told: you are optimistic. We have been saying for two years that we are going to grow and we are growing, and that is not being optimistic, it is being realistic. That is the reality, there is no other, any other is hidden, it is not true. TRANSCRIPTION TRANSCRIPTION Issuing confidence and stability Issuing confidence and stability If it is on the employment side, the INSS indicators show a recovery in jobs. We closed last year (2022) with almost 800,000 formal Social Security jobs. After the pandemic, many people decided not to return to the labor market for multiple reasons and that has limited the expansion of employment. In other words, people are working with less employment, companies are working with less employment. That increases efficiency, but it also increases entrepreneurs, since, if companies do not employ, then people seek and find other ways. But we have a very low unemployment rate that is around 3%. In this rate, what we collect is all the employed, both those who are self-employed and those who are employed by an employer.  What we see is that there was a reduction in underemployment and an improvement in formal employment after the recovery. But it needs it and that is good news, because if it needs it it means that there is employment to continue growing more. That is to say, we do not have a deficiency in the workforce, there it is, exceeding and waiting for new opportunities. So, employment is also advancing hand in hand with the recovery. (Internal) inflation is international and public finances are balanced. In Nicaragua, the public deficit went down and the public debt (is) under control, very low. In fact, with respect to what happened to countries in general that became heavily indebted, that increased their public deficits, Nicaragua was the opposite, we did not get into debt, we kept the deficit under control and there are no conditions for internal inflation to arise.  the Central Bank, on the other hand, kept its monetary policy stable, the exchange rate stable and we did not expand the money supply, quite the opposite; quite the opposite. Rather, they came to sell dollars to the Central Bank, a very clear sign of stability. The problem is when they ask the Central Bank for dollars, that is a problem. That means that there is a shortage of foreign currency and then people are "thirsty" for dollars. TRANSCRIPTION TRANSCRIPTION Issuing confidence and stability Issuing confidence and stability Everything comes (inflation) from outside because, as I mentioned, the economy is so open, the openness is so great that any "sneeze" outside, we feel it inside. And in terms of prices, it has been. When we look at the price statistics of imports, they grew by more than 40%, up to 60% certain groups of imported goods. And that was reflected in the domestic economy: all international inflation. I mentioned 10 billion dollars of imports with a GDP of 14 billion, all prices are reflected internally. But this international inflation, as there is growth, is not affecting consumption, which becomes a bit contradictory, because when one hears the effect of inflation on poverty, and it is true, inflation affects the poorest, but consumption is growing 8% in real terms: it is an inflation that does not affect consumption. Why can this happen? Because there are diverse sources of financing, there are remittances for 3 billion dollars, there is the financial system that reactivated credit. So, if inflation comes, then the public goes into debt, and continues to consume. The Director of Customs gives us a figure: 70,000 motorcycles entered in October. Consumption does not stop, people continue to acquire goods, they continue to acquire household appliances, they continue to acquire assets, cars. So it has been an inflation that has not affected consumption in our country. So, the flow of spending continues and we see commercial establishments full, businesses full, hotels and restaurants in recovery and that is why we trust that it is difficult for there to be anything to stop it because the "engine is on". And in the economy, when the "engine is on," just something extraordinary comes along that stops it, but it doesn't stop. That's right, because people's entrepreneurial enthusiasm and business enthusiasm is what prevails in the end and everyone is (thinking): "No, this is the time to work, it's not to be resting". So, we have booming consumption. TRANSCRIPTION TRANSCRIPTION Issuing confidence and stability Issuing confidence and stability So, the effect of inflation has been on private investment. Fortunately, at the aggregate level, public investment has continued, that has compensated. And aggregate investment is maintained, it maintains its pace. That is what we were talking about too and the Minister of Finance explained to us that investment spending was going to have to be activated more in order to compensate for the decline that has been observed in the private sector. And so, the economy continues to move forward. But prices are something that we believe, it is already starting to fall globally. There is already talk of two consecutive months of price stability, including falling prices in some industrial countries. The prices of raw materials and main goods have already been contained, food prices have begun to fall worldwide and then we would expect that by this semester prices will stabilize more. So, the main macroeconomic parameters have to do with: growing economic activity, stable employment and low unemployment rate, high inflation, it was more than 11%, but we see it in a downward perspective, and an expanding export sector, are what characterize our economy at this time. I think it is an opportunity for all those who are doing business, to make business proposals, it is the best time to do it. Not years ago, because there was a lot of uncertainty, the coronavirus generated a lot of uncertainty. I couldn't say to someone: "yes, this is a good time to do business", I'm going to ruin them rather, we did tell them to do business at that time, but there were those who did. Those who do take risks and do well, not necessarily badly. There were others who did badly, that's how it is. But at this time that there is recovery, that there is TRANSCRIPTION TRANSCRIPTION Issuing confidence and stability Issuing confidence and stability Finally, I am going to refer to the financial issue. The financial economy is also evolving positively. Deposits growing by double digits, more than 10%. I believe that the strong savings capacity of our economy, companies, and businesses has been a fundamental element. We carry out indicators to monitor families at an aggregate level and it was clearly seen that after the pandemic or during the pandemic, families greatly increased their savings, a lot, and got out of debt. I think there is already a change in the Nicaraguan mentality that debts must be honored. This is already becoming more and more entrenched and can be seen in the data. The default rate in financial institutions is very low, a default rate of 3% and in microfinance institutions that historically had delinquencies of up to 20%, they are at 6%, 5%, in arrears. And during the pandemic, families got out of debt. It's an incredible thing how it looks like people saved a lot, got out of debt. A lot of savings is also bad. Look how incredible for macroeconomics. At the private level it is good to have a lot of savings, but at the aggregate level in the macroeconomy, since a lot was saved and that lowered spending, aggregate spending goes down, and when spending goes down there is no one to buy because everyone is saving. Well, that happened with the Coronavirus, you can see how savings increased strongly and that also helped financial institutions a lot and they were in need of money and had families saving and a lot of liquidity accumulated. In fact, the Central Bank also accumulated a lot of liquidity because no one wanted to spend with the pandemic, everyone tightened, it was an automatic adjustment. There was no need to tighten the public treasury, there was no need to tighten monetary policy. Families were squeezed and that funded the financial system and now the financial system already has a very strong, national savings base. They also lowered the debt with the foreign banks, they worked hard. That is good for the country because it leaves you less exposed to external financing. And now they are expanding credit with their own source based on national savings, and that has allowed them to keep interest rates stable, even though they are not able to pay the right to pay for them. TRANSCRIPTION TRANSCRIPTION Issuing confidence and stability Issuing confidence and stability So we also have a healthy financial system at this time, a financial system that is generating its own resources for credit activity and that will also contribute to expansion. So, when you add up all that I just told you, there is no one to stop growth, it comes. That is an element that we have shared with international organizations. The Minister (MHCP) told them about the good grades we had last year with these organizations and the positive evaluation we had from Standard & Poor's. The removal of Nicaragua from the FATF gray list and return to the fold of the countries, without that problem. We also had the positive evaluation of the International Monetary Fund. In fact, now, at the end of next week, we are already going to the evaluation of the IMF Board and it is going positively. We have already seen the documents, we are doing well. Thanks a lot. Thanks a lot.

Title: President of the BCN presents results of the meeting of the National System of Production, Consumption and Trade
text: TRANSCRIPTION TRANSCRIPTION Issuing confidence and stability Issuing confidence and stability Press Conference President of the BCN presents the results of the meeting of the National System of Production, Consumption and Trade May 26, 2023 President of the BCN: Good morning everyone. Today we ended the weekly meeting of the National System of Production, Consumption and Trade to evaluate the progress of the different strategies in the field of production, marketing and training and technologies that are developed from the different institutions and universities that participate in this contest in order to achieve the goals of our plan and to be able to meet the requirements. both of the production in general and of the consumption of food of our population. In particular, we deal with the issues of agricultural technologies that are developed by the CNU (National Council of Universities), to support production, the activities carried out by CONATRADEC (National Commission for the Transformation and Development of Coffee Farming), the technologies incorporated by INTA (National Institute of Agricultural Technology), in terms of the production of herbs, medicinal and cooking plants. The strategy for the production of basic grains that is key for our people, and also the collection of this information that is linked to global economic activity. I will briefly explain each one: In the case of universities, the National Agrarian University (UNA), presented the reports on agricultural technology that have been carried out by the training carried out by the University, in the open university that the UNA has, for the training of thousands of producers. In particular, 17 courses have been developed that are carried out with technological means to 390 points in which different protagonists, producers and entrepreneurs are trained in topics related to pest combat, technologies for fumigation, fertilization and treatment of storage, and another set of trainings that are carried out by the university to increase the quality of the population. TRANSCRIPTION TRANSCRIPTION Issuing confidence and stability Issuing confidence and stability On the other hand, CONATRADEC promotes its coffee promotion activity, in the case of the coffee exhibitions held in the United States and Japan for the participation of producers who promote the consumption of good Nicaraguan coffee, the country brand and in addition to that business in that sense. And on the other hand, the promotion of the Cup of Excellence, they have already been doing work regarding the selection of coffee samples that are going to be taken to this contest. There are already 38 evaluated, classified samples that come from different cooperatives and coffee producers that produce good coffee. The intention of participation of international companies has already been expressed, more than 30, and 15 international tasters have already been selected to come in relation to this activity. And on the other hand, CONATRADEC is also promoting the promotion of origin coffees, Dipilto coffee and other types of coffee that are being promoted from that office and also promoting all the general financing activity and its work plan for this year. Then INTA presented what refers to the Strategy for the Promotion and Production of Herbs, Cooking and Medicinal Plants. The production plan deals with the production of foods such as grains, meats, poultry, but it also goes down to the level of fruits. In this case, the explanation of herbs, medicinal and cooking plants corresponded: INTA has developed 120 types of herbs, through research, it has carried out 138 investigations for reproduction and 8,765 producers have participated in the demonstrations, 89,912 plants have been developed in different types of herbs such as oregano, lemon grass, chives, coriander, etc., which are basically of high consumption in the population for food preparation. All this dissemination has also been promoted through diversified gardens in the MEFCCA (Ministry of Family, Community, Cooperative and Associative Economy) and also through the demonstrations that will be held in the Ministry of Agriculture. TRANSCRIPTION TRANSCRIPTION Issuing confidence and stability Issuing confidence and stability The other is about the Strategy for the Promotion and Production of Basic Grains. In this case, the production of rice, sorghum, corn, fundamentally. In this case, the training has also been intense. 52,582 producers already served for a goal of 150,000 services that are within the production plan, 931 fairs and farmers' markets promoted, 10,960 producers have participated in these fairs, and, on the other hand, sales of a little more than 19 million cordobas have been made in them. On the other hand, INTA has been experimenting with 35 experimental varieties of seed. For example, they presented us with varieties of red beans that can even reach yields of 32 quintals per manzana, of yellow corn, yields that can reach 75 to 80 quintals per manzana. They already have these varieties. In hybrid, white hybrid corn, 120 quintals per manzana; white sorghum, varieties that reach 65 quintals per apple; sesame between 15 and 20 quintals per apple; and soybeans 70 quintals per apple. They promote these technologies through different breeding centers and all the technical information is on their website, and this is a good way to invite all producers to adopt them and be able to use these yields. They require effort, they require training. The institutions of the production system provide it. INTA in particular also has a training system in coordination with MEFCCA and INATEC so that everyone can adopt these technologies. It is a great challenge for the production system to increase productivity. In fact, the last presentation of the production plan shows how the country has been increasing productivity. But since we already have these technologies, we invite everyone to adopt them, it is a slow process, but it must be promoted and disseminated. They also talked about the different fairs that are held through the Ministry of Family Economy for the promotion of family production. There are fairs, technical assistance, events, competitions, farmers' markets that are promoted. A total of 5,439 events have been promoted through the MEFCCA. 9,820 protagonists and entrepreneurs have participated in these events and 132 million cordobas have been marketed. This includes all kinds of promotion of activities of small and medium-sized enterprises, entrepreneurs and also products that come from the countryside. We invite all producers and TRANSCRIPTION TRANSCRIPTION Issuing confidence and stability Issuing confidence and stability  Finally, we also address the issue of global production. The Central Bank presented the summary of what is the Monthly Report of Economic Activity, which is being published today on its website. As of March, we have been observing the continuity of economic growth in our country. Between January and March of this year, economic activity grew 3.2 percent. The result of all the actions we carry out within the National System of Production, Consumption and Trade, also has consequences on aggregate activities. Title: President of the BCN, Ovidio Reyes R. Presentation of recent economic developments and perspectives before the National Assembly of Nicaragua
text: fiaenfadde Issuing confidence and stability Tuesday, January 31, 2023 Tuesday, January 31, 2023 WORDS OF THE AUTHORITIES President of the BCN, Ovidio Reyes R.Presentation of recent economic developments and prospects before the National Assembly of Nicaragua Good morning comrade Gustavo Porras, President of the honorable National Assembly, members of the board of directors, deputies and greetings to all those present. Thank you very much for inviting me to this plenary session to explain the recent economic evolution and the prospects that we envision from the Central Bank of Nicaragua for the year 2023. Our economy, for the second consecutive year, continued to register a positive economic evolution, with growth in economic activity and employment, stable financial indicators and a public sector with healthy finances. We can safely affirm that the fundamentals of the economy have been preserved and, therefore, the continuity of the previous economic well-being has been consolidated, which was temporarily interrupted by internal and external disturbances such as the one generated by the COVID-1 pandemic 9 and the impact of hurricanes. The country was put to the test as a result of these tensions and Nicaragua was able to come out ahead, highlighting its strength, which mainly rests on the high resilience of the primary sector of our economy: agriculture, livestock, fishing, mining and forestry, which today has a strengthened export base that has been encouraged by the good prices and markets that our products have found. Today, our country has gone from being a semi-closed economy to an economy that is widely open to trade and inserted in the international competition that generates sufficient resources for the funding of our economic activity and global stability. This element is distinctive and is a guarantee to ensure that economic growth continues in the present and in the coming years. In 2022, economic activity maintained a growth trajectory that was reflected in all sectors. Thus, the evolution of the Gross Domestic Product (GDP) as of the third quarter of 2022 shows that all economic activities are on the path of growth, regardless of whether, due to periods or seasonalities, one or another activity may show a reduction z in their performance. Likewise, according to data from the Monthly Index of Economic Activity (IMAE) for November 2022, it is confirmed that the economy is on track to end the year as expected, with growth in a range of between 3.5 - 4.5 percent, led by the primary and secondary sectors, with activities highlighted by their export orientation. such as agriculture, fishing and manufacturing. It is also noted that service activities have entered a phase of greater dynamism, with high year-on-year growth rates in the activities of hotels and restaurants, transport and communications, financial intermediation and trade. On the expenditure side, exports and private consumption led the economic momentum in 2022, with exports being a factor in the strength of the economy, in a context of good demand and high international prices of exportable products. Employment continued to recover, formal employment increased and underemployment decreased. This is manifested in the fact that the open unemployment rate continues to decrease, although the labor participation rate remains below the levels of the first quarter of 2020, prior to the pandemic, which is due to a global phenomenon associated with the effects of the COVID-19 pandemic, which is manifested in the fact that there is a lower proportion of people of working age who are active in the workforce. The formal employment rate stood at 24 percent of the employed population, increasing, while the underemployment rate fell to 38.3 percent. On the side of affiliation to the Nicaraguan Social Security Institute (INSS), the number of affiliates reached 783,384 in December 2022. Domestic prices, meanwhile, continued to be pressured upwards by external factors. In the midst of a set of positive economic results at the domestic level, the country has had to face the global inflationary phenomenon, which has been transferred to national prices, making national inflation mainly imported in nature. The world's main economies presented high prices in 2022 as a result of the COVID-19 pandemic and central banks have reacted by raising interest rates to moderate aggregate spending, including in our country. Thus, as a result of the increase in the prices of imported products, among which capital and intermediate goods for production stand out, in 2022 the national year-on-year inflation stood at 1 1.59 percent. The pass-through of international inflation was reflected in a greater contribution from the food and transport divisions, which have been the divisions most affected by international prices. On the other hand, the behavior of prices at the global level has been reflected in an increase in production costs, mainly in the divisions associated with food production. However, policy measures have eased inflationary pressures, in particular, the Government's policy of implementing a generalized subsidy on the prices of gasoline, diesel, and butane gas for home use. Likewise, the price increase has been limited by the decrease in 2022, in the variation of the exchange rate, as a result of the policy of reducing the exchange rate slippage implemented since 2019. However, despite these price increases, aggregate consumption has not been reduced and commercial sales in the economy are growing by 8 percent in real terms, which is explained by the greater economic dynamics, the reactivation of credit and the various sources of funding from the private sector. Monetary variables continue to perform well, creating room for growth. In this sense, all monetary aggregates grew in year-on-year terms at the end of 2022, in particular, the monetary base, deposits and the broader monetary aggregate (M3A) grew at double-digit rates. On the other hand, the good performance of external flows and the position in cordobas of the banks and the Government has led to net purchases of foreign currency on the exchange desk of the Central Bank of Nicaragua, favoring the stability of the foreign exchange market, reflected in an exchange rate gap that has not exceeded 0.5 percent. which indicates sufficient funding of foreign currency. Thus, the Central Bank has not had a demand for the sale of foreign currency, but rather has bought foreign currency to maintain monetary balance and meet the greater demand for cordobas. This change in behavior in the market is relevant, because it indicates that the economy is demanding more cordobas and inducing a lower and not a higher exchange rate. For this reason, the Central Bank in January adopted an additional reduction of one percentage point in the exchange rate slippage. This is now 1% per year, a policy that we will continue to implement gradually to continue advancing in the strengthening of the cordoba. The monetary and fiscal performance has favored the strengthening of the Central Bank's Gross International Reserves (RIB). In this way, during 2022 gross reserves increased by 357.9 million dollars, ending with a historical balance of 4,404.4 million dollars and a coverage of 2.8 times the monetary base and 7 months of imports excluding free zones, allowing to reach a reserve position that further enhances the capacity to safeguard the current exchange regime. Financial intermediation showed a positive evolution, consolidating credit growth. The dynamism of economic activity is having a positive impact on the expectations of economic agents and the ability of households and companies to pay. The Nicaraguan financial system continues to show a solid and resilient position, with capital and liquidity levels above regulatory minimums. This year, the consolidation of the credit recovery stood out, reflected in increases in the portfolio, leveraged mainly by higher deposits from the public. Thus, as of December 2022, deposits grew 12.9 percent, while credit grew 15.3 percent in year-on-year terms. The greater delivery of credit was accompanied by improvements in the quality of the portfolio and an increase in the profitability of the banking and financial system. Thus, reductions were observed in the portfolio in non-performing loans and at risk, which favored an improvement in profitability. External flows continue to increase, favored by the international context. This increase is due both to the situation of high international prices and to the permanence of a strengthened export base, which continues to take advantage of foreign trade opportunities. Thus, the value of total exports of goods and free zones grew by 15.5 percent in the period of January-November 2022 compared to 2021. Remittances also increased and stood at an amount of 3,225 million dollars in 2022. Foreign Investment amounted to 1,160.6 million dollars in the third quarter and tourism stood at 41.1 million dollars in the same period. We expect the positive dynamics observed in 2022 to continue during 2023 as well as in the medium term. For 2023, GDP growth is estimated in a range of between 3.0 and 4.0 percent. We expect inflation to be reduced and end in a range of between 5.0 and 6.0 percent. The prices of the main international products have already begun to fall, including oil, as well as food, so we expect national inflation to moderate from the first half of 2022. It is important to note that the country's economic recovery has been recognized by international organizations. The International Monetary Fund's Article IV assessment just last week notes Nicaragua's strong economic recovery and favorable prospects. For its part, the sovereign rating agency Standard & Poor's upgraded the country's long-term ratings, considering among other things the low fiscal deficit, stable debt levels and a resilient financial sector. The FATF also recognized Nicaragua's progress in improving the elements of its Anti-Money Laundering and Countering the Financing of Terrorism (AML/CFT) regime, removing Nicaragua from the gray list. Even though downside risks are present at the international level, Nicaragua's economy has its strengths to mitigate them. The main strength is the high degree of openness that has been achieved, highlighting the export sector and foreign investment. In addition, the financial system has shown a good capacity to recover its stability and will continue to facilitate the reactivation of financial intermediation. The entrepreneurial and business economy has been able to absorb the shocks and is a great shock absorber of employment, greatly contributing to economic recovery and growth. While fiscal policy has generated resources to support economic growth and create fiscal margins, which, together with monetary policy, have resulted in greater national savings, strengthening the economy's capacity to deal with potential adverse impacts. With these economic strengths, the country is practically shielded against future adverse events and they are a sufficient condition to guarantee the continuity of economic growth and macro-financial stability. I thank you very much for your attention and wish you all a good morning.
text_original: fiaenfadde Emitiendo confianza y estabilidad Martes, 31 de enero de 2023 PALABRAS DE LAS AUTORIDADES Presidente del BCN, Ovidio Reyes R. Presentacin de evolucin econmica reciente y perspectivas ante Asamblea Nacional de Nicaragua Buenos das compaero Gustavo Porras, Presidente de la honorable Asamblea Nacional, miembros de la unta directiva, diputados y saludos a todos los presentes. Muchas gracias por invitarme a esta sesin plenaria para explicar la evolucin econmica reciente y las perspectivas que visualizamos desde el Banco Central de Nicaragua para el ao 2023. Nuestra economa, por segundo ao consecutivo continu registrando una evolucin econmica positiva, con crecimiento de la actividad econmica y del empleo, indicadores financieros estables y un sector pblico con finanzas sanas. Podemos afirmar con seguridad que los fundamentos de la economa se han podido preservar y, por lo tanto, se ha afianzado la continuidad de la bienandanza econmica precedente que se vio interrumpida transitoriamente por perturbaciones internas y externas como la generada por la pandemia del COVID-1 9 y el impacto de los huracanes. El pas se puso a prueba a raz de estas tensiones y Nicaragua pudo salir al frente, destacndose su fortaleza, que principalmente descansa en la alta resiliencia del sector primario de nuestra economa: agricultura, ganadera, pesca, minera y silvicultura, que hoy presenta una base exportadora fortalecida que se ha visto incentivada por los buenos precios y mercados que han encontrado nuestros productos. Hoy por hoy, nuestro pas pas de ser una economa semi cerrada a una economa ampliamente abierta al comercio e insertada en el concurso internacional que genera recursos suficientes para el fondeo de nuestra actividad econmica y la estabilidad global. Este elemento es distintivo y es una garanta para asegurar que el crecimiento econmico contine en el presente y en los prximos aos. En 2022 la actividad econmica mantuvo una trayectoria de crecimiento que se reflej en todos los sectores. As, la evolucin del Producto Interno Bruto (PIB) al tercer trimestre de 2022 muestra que todas las actividades econmicas estn en la senda de crecimiento, independientemente que, por perodos o estacionalidades, una u otra actividad pueda mostrar reduccin z en su desempeo. Asimismo, de acuerdo con datos del Indice Mensual de la Actividad Econmica (IMAE) de noviembre de 2022, se confirma que la economa est en curso a terminar el ao conforme a lo previsto, con un crecimiento en un rango de entre 3.5 - 4.5 por ciento, liderado por los sectores primario y secundario, con actividades destacadas por su orientacin exportadora, como la agropecuaria, pesca y manufactura. Asimismo, se constata que las actividades de servicios han entrado en una fase de mayor dinamismo, con altas tasas de crecimiento interanual en las actividades de hoteles y restaurantes, transporte y comunicaciones, intermediacin financiera y el comercio. Por el lado del gasto, las exportaciones y el consumo privado lideraron el impulso econmico en 2022, siendo las exportaciones un factor de fortaleza de la economa, en un contexto de buena demanda y altos precios internacionales de los productos exportables. El empleo se continu recuperando, el empleo formal aument y se redujo el sub empleo. Esto se manifiesta en que la tasa de desempleo abierto contina disminuyendo, aunque la tasa de participacin laboral permanece por debajo de los niveles del primer trimestre de 2020, previo a la pandemia, lo que obedece a un fenmeno global asociado a los efectos de la pandemia del COVID-19, el cual se manifiesta en que hay una menor proporcin de personas en edad de trabajar que se encuentran activas laboralmente. La tasa de empleo formal se ubic en 24 por ciento de la poblacin ocupada, aumentndose, mientras que la tasa de subempleo se redujo al 38.3 por ciento. Por el lado de la afiliacin al Instituto Nicaragense de Seguridad Social (INSS), el nmero de afiliados alcanz 783,384 en diciembre de 2022. Los precios domsticos, por su parte, continuaron presionados al alza por factores externos. En medio de un conjunto de resultados econmicos positivos a nivel domstico, el pas ha tenido que enfrentar el fenmeno inflacionario global, el cual se ha traspasado a los precios nacionales, haciendo que la inflacin nacional sea principalmente de naturaleza importada. Las principales economas del mundo presentaron en 2022 elevados precios derivados de la pandemia del COVID-19 y los bancos centrales han reaccionado subiendo las tasas de inters para moderar el gasto agregado, incluyendo a nuestro pas. As, como resultado del aumento de los precios de los productos importados, entre los que se destacan los bienes de capital e intermedios para la produccin, en 2022 la inflacin interanual nacional se ubic en 1 1.59 por ciento. El traspaso de la inflacin internacional se reflej en una mayor contribucin de la divisin de alimentos y transporte, que han sido las divisiones ms afectadas por los precios internacionales. Por otra parte, el comportamiento de los precios a nivel global se ha reflejado en aumento de los costos de produccin, principalmente en las divisiones asociadas a la produccin de alimentos. No obstante, las medidas de poltica han atenuado las presiones inflacionarias, en particular, la poltica del Gobierno de implementar un subsidio generalizado a los precios de la gasolina, disel y gas butano de uso domiciliar. Asimismo, el incremento de precios ha sido limitado por la baja en 2022, en la variacin del tipo de cambio, producto de la poltica de reduccin de la tasa de deslizamiento cambiario implementada desde 201 9. Sin embargo, a pesar de estos aumentos de precios, el consumo agregado no se ha reducido y las ventas comerciales en la economa estn creciendo en 8 por ciento en trminos reales lo que se explica por la mayor dinmica econmica, la reactivacin del crdito y las diversas fuentes de fondeo del sector privado. Las variables monetarias mantienen un buen desempeo, generando espacio para el crecimiento. En este sentido, todos los agregados monetarios crecieron en trminos interanuales al cierre de 2022, en particular, la base monetaria, los depsitos y el agregado monetario ms amplio (M3A) crecieron a tasas de dos dgitos. Por otra parte, el buen desempeo de los flujos externos y la posicin en crdobas de los bancos y el Gobierno ha propiciado que se registren compras netas de divisas en la mesa de cambio del Banco Central de Nicaragua, favoreciendo la estabilidad del mercado cambiario, reflejada en una brecha cambiara que no ha excedido el 0.5 por ciento, lo que indica suficiente fondeo de divisas. As, el Banco Central no ha tenido demanda de venta de divisas, sino ms bien ha comprado divisas para mantener el equilibrio monetario y satisfacer la mayor demanda por crdobas. Este cambio de comportamiento en el mercado es relevante, porque indica que la economa est demandando ms crdobas e induciendo a un menor y no a un mayor tipo de cambio. Por esa razn es que el Banco Central en enero adopt una reduccin adicional de un punto porcentual del deslizamiento cambiario. El que ahora se ubica en 1% anual, poltica que continuaremos implementando gradualmente para continuar avanzando en el fortalecimiento del crdoba. El desempeo monetario y fiscal ha favorecido el fortalecimiento de las Reservas Internacionales Brutas (RIB) del Banco Central. De esta forma, durante 2022 las reservas brutas se incrementaron en 357.9 millones de dlares, finalizando con un saldo histrico de 4,404.4 millones de dlares y una cobertura de 2.8 veces la base monetaria y de 7 meses de importaciones excluyendo las zonas francas, permitiendo alcanzar una posicin de reservas que potencia an ms la capacidad para resguardar el rgimen cambiario vigente. La intermediacin financiera mostr una evolucin positiva, consolidndose el crecimiento del crdito. El dinamismo de la actividad econmica est incidiendo positivamente sobre las expectativas de los agentes econmicos y la capacidad de pago de los hogares y de las empresas. El sistema financiero nicaragense contina mostrando una posicin slida y de resiliencia, con niveles de capital y liquidez superiores a los mnimos regulatorios. En este ao, destac la consolidacin de la recuperacin crediticia, reflejada en aumentos de la cartera, apalancados principalmente por los mayores depsitos del pblico. As, a diciembre de 2022, los depsitos crecieron 12.9 por ciento, mientras que el crdito creci 15.3 por ciento en trminos interanuales. La mayor entrega de crdito se vio acompaada de mejoras en la calidad de la cartera e incremento en la rentabilidad del sistema bancario y financieras. As, se observ reducciones en la cartera en mora y en riesgo, lo que favoreci una mejora en la rentabilidad. Los flujos externos siguen aumentando, favorecidos por el contexto internacional. Este aumento se produce tanto por la coyuntura de altos precios internacionales como por la permanencia de una base exportadora fortalecida, que sigue aprovechando las oportunidades del comercio exterior. As, el valor de las exportaciones totales de mercancas y zonas francas crecieron en 15.5 por ciento en el perodo de enero-noviembre 2022 respecto a 2021. Tambin las remesas se incrementaron y se ubicaron en un monto de 3,225 millones de dlares en 2022. La Inversin Extranjera ascendi a 1,160.6 millones de dlares al tercer trimestre y el turismo se ubic en 41 1 millones de dlares en el mismo perodo. Esperamos que la dinmica positiva observada en el ao 2022 se mantenga durante el ao 2023 as como en el mediano plazo. Para el 2023 se estima un crecimiento del PIB en un rango de entre un 3.0 y 4.0 por ciento. La inflacin esperamos que se reduzca y finalice en un rango de entre 5.0 y 6.0 por ciento. Ya los precios de los principales productos internacionales han comenzado a descender, entre ellos el petrleo, as como de los alimentos, por lo que esperamos que la inflacin nacional se modere a partir del primer semestre de 2022. Es importante destacar que la recuperacin econmica del pas ha sido reconocida por organismos internacionales. En la evaluacin del artculo IV del Fondo Monetario Internacional recin realizada la semana pasada se seala la slida recuperacin econmica y las perspectivas favorables de Nicaragua. Por su parte, la agencia de calificacin soberana Standard & Poor's mejor las calificaciones de largo plazo del pas, considerando entre otras cosas al bajo dficit fiscal, los niveles de deuda estables y un sector financiero resiliente. Asimismo, el GAFI reconoci el progreso de Nicaragua en la mejora de los elementos de su rgimen Anti Lavado de Dinero y Contra el Financiamiento del Terrorismo (ALD/CFT), sacando a Nicaragua de la lista gris. An cuando a nivel internacional estn presentes riesgos a la baja, la economa de Nicaragua cuenta con sus fortalezas para mitigarlos. La principal fortaleza es el alto grado de apertura que se ha alcanzado, destacndose al sector exportador y la inversin extranjera. Adicionalmente, el sistema financiero ha presentado una buena capacidad para recuperar su estabilidad y continuar facilitando la reactivacin de la intermediacin financiera. La economa emprendedora y de negocios ha podido absorber las perturbaciones y es una gran amortiguadora de empleo, colaborando en gran medida en la recuperacin econmica y el crecimiento. Mientras que la poltica fiscal ha generado recursos para apoyar el crecimiento econmico y crear mrgenes fiscales, los que, aunado a la poltica monetaria, han resultado en mayores ahorros nacionales, fortaleciendo la capacidad de la economa para hacer frente a potenciales impactos adversos. Con estas fortalezas econmicas, el pas est prcticamente blindado frente a futuros acontecimientos adversos y son una condicin suficiente que garantizan la continuidad del crecimiento econmico y la estabilidad macrofinanciera. Agradezco mucho su atencin y les deseo a todos que pasen una buena maana.

Title: Presentation of the pre-census study on housing and families in conditions of extreme poverty, President of the BCN, Ovidio Reyes R.
text: TRANSCRIPTION TRANSCRIPTION Presentation Pre-census study on housing and families in conditions of extreme poverty President of the BCN, Ovidio Reyes R. July 31, 2023 Ovidio Reyes President of the BCN: Good morning to all those present, to the authorities who are with us at this event. For the year 2024 we have scheduled the Population and Housing Census, and that implies carrying out pre-census activity, organizing the census together with the public institutions of their competence, in this case with the Mayors' Offices, with the Housing Institute, the National Institute of Development Information (INIDE), which is responsible for this activity, and the Central Bank, which we are going to support with all our technology, with our knowledge and our work, to be able to carry out this important task of measuring the population and housing infrastructure, both family and housing or the infrastructure that is dedicated to production activities. i i TRANSCRIPTION TRANSCRIPTION On this occasion, a pre-census study was carried out in which houses were counted and also a preliminary population count was made, which is not a census, but a pre-census activity, and the INIDE is going to present us with the results of this activity, which as we indicated is preliminary, it is not conclusive. The conclusion will be given by the census itself, but we believe it is important to share with you, especially with the measurement of a relevant indicator for our country such as the poverty indicator, since at the national level the central objective of the policies that are implemented is the reduction of poverty. Therefore, this first approximation of the measurement will be carried out by the Director of Censuses and Surveys of the National Institute of Development Information, INIDE, Irene alvarez, with the aim of sharing them with our population and as a preliminary of what we are going to do during the year 2024. So we want to thank INIFOM, the Mayors' Offices, and INIDE also for having devoted their best efforts. In two months this activity was carried out and well, we are sure that with everyone's participation we will successfully complete this great task of the National Population and Housing Census of 2024, which we will carry out and carry out in April of next year. Irene alvarez Director of Censuses and Surveys of INIDE: The pre-census study on Housing and Families in Conditions of Extreme Poverty was carried out with the participation of INIDE, BCN and mayors' offices, with the participation of 14,496 enumerators, of which 8,670 were women and 5,826 were men. General Information:  At the national level, an average of 4.3 people per household was found.  2 2 TRANSCRIPTION TRANSCRIPTION  In relation to extreme poverty, it was detected that 6.4% of the population lives in housing with conditions of extreme poverty. The percentage of homes in this condition is 6.9%. This measure of poverty, based on housing conditions, is lower than that estimated in the last 2016 Living Standard Measurement Survey when it showed a figure of 6.9% of extreme poverty, measured from consumption. Facts about families:  Of the people living in extreme poverty, 48.8% are men and 51.2% are women.  The total number of people registered is distributed in the following age ranges: From 1 to 5 years old: 10.9% From 6 to 12 years old: 16.4% From 13 to 18 years old: 12.3% From 19 to 30 years old: 20.3% From 31 to 60 years old: 29.8% Age 61 and older: 8.5%  The population pyramid structure that resulted from this survey is very similar to that estimated by INIDE, indicating robustness in the measurement, and constitutes a basis for the survey of the Population and Housing Census in April 2024.  Regarding the data on heads of households, the report concludes that the heads of households in conditions of extreme poverty are mostly women, with 62.3% and only 37.7% of the households, the heads of families are men. * Housing facts:  Houses in conditions of extreme poverty are generally built of the following materials: TRANSCRIPTION TRANSCRIPTION Zinc: 28.2% Scrap: 9.9% Adobe or Taquezal: 9.2% - Concrete or concrete block: 2.8% Bamboo, barul, reed or palm: 2% Others: 15.1%  Regarding property ownership, of the homes surveyed, 88% are owned homes.  In relation to access to basic services such as water and electricity:  50.3% of the dwellings are connected to the public drinking water network  72.7% of the dwellings have an electricity network  Of the registered dwellings:  58.3% have cell phones  30.5% use tube TV  11.5% have a refrigerator  5.6% have cable TV  4.6% have plasma TVs  3.1% have motorcycles for home use  2.5% have internet service Thanks a lot * Errata: During the presentation, the figures 74.4% and 45.1% were given, which were not correct. 4

Title: Exchange of Academic Collaboration Agreement between the Central Bank of Nicaragua and the National University of Engineering Remarks by the President of BCN, Ovidio Reyes R.
text: fioenfaa/de Issuing confidence and stability WORDS OF THE AUTHORITIES Tuesday, April 11, 2023 Exchange of Academic Collaboration Agreement between the Central Bank of Nicaragua and the National University of Engineering Remarks by the President of the BCN, Ovidio Reyes R. Good morning! It is a pleasure to greet you and extend a cordial welcome to this exchange ceremony of the Academic Collaboration Agreement between the Central Bank of Nicaragua and the National University of Engineering:  Mrs. Glenda Marcia Velasquez Vargas, Rector of the National University of Engineering.  Authorities and teachers of the National University of Engineering,  Professors of the Central Bank of Nicaragua who collaborate with the Career of Engineering in Economics and Business,  New students of this career, and  Media present. The collaboration between the Central Bank of Nicaragua and the National University of Engineering for the development of the Career of Engineering in Economics and Business began in 2014 as an initiative to train professionals in economics and business with a focus on engineering, that is, with an emphasis on mathematical, statistical and systems tools for economic analysis. Throughout these years of agreement, 7 annual calls have been made from which a total of 189 students of high academic performance were selected to whom scholarships and facilities are granted to study the career of Economics and Business Engineering, of which 100 students have graduated and 89 are active and who we hope will finish their studies from 2023 to 2026. Students are prepared in the areas of: macroeconomics, microeconomics, mathematics, statistics, econometrics, business administration, accounting and finance, among other subjects. This solid training has allowed graduates to have a broad job placement, such as the central bank, the government, teaching centers, research centers and businesses, as well as to opt for academic continuity in higher education programs at prestigious universities. Currently, 10 students have graduated in master's degrees with specialties in economics, data analysis, economic and quantitative models, as well as finance and fintech. Another 5 students are finishing master's studies in economics, economic and quantitative models. In this new stage of the Economics and Business Engineering Career, led by the National University of Engineering, the Central Bank of Nicaragua has decided to continue providing its support, for which this Academic Collaboration Agreement has been signed in order to guarantee by the Central Bank the teachers in the subjects of economic profile for the years 2023, 2024 and 2025. In addition, the Central Bank of Nicaragua will be supporting students who enter the career of Engineering in Economics and Business with the delivery of computers, training in a second language, economic research and internships at the BCN, as well as in the public activities of an economic nature promoted by the Central Bank. We thank the authorities of the National University of Engineering, its rector, professors and other authorities, for always being in collaboration with our monetary institution. We also hope that this new stage of collaboration will be as successful as the previous stage and will continue to result in benefits for students and for the socioeconomic development of our country.
